5) Take the printed pages and combine it with a piece of leather in an assembling machine filled with at least 20 mb of refined glue.

[note]TADA![/note] Now you have a book with detailed info about the chunks you scanned. Visual Prospecting adds the information to your map the moment you make the book.

§2Data Sticks are not easy (or possible) to make right now, so do not lose them.§r You can put it in a crafting table to erase it when done.

Ore locations are given as the center of the chunk. Ores that are marginal in that chunk may not be found in the center but on an edge. Look at where ores are located and determine the center of the vein. At higher tiers, it scans more chunks for ores. If you just want to know about fluids, use the lower tier version so the book isn't as long.

Each underground fluid field is 8x8 chunks. This starts at 0,0 and continues for 8 chunks east and south, containing 64 chunks. Not all fields have anything in them though. Within the field the amount can vary +/- 25 percent. The amount reported in the book is the minimum and maximum per field across all chunks in the field. The prospector reports on 3x3 fields (as in, 9 fields of 8x8 chunks) at all tiers with the center field where the seismic prospector is located. Fluid extraction rate depends on many factors, check the wiki for details. In general, anything above 300 is really good. The total amount in the chunk is complicated.
Mercury can be centrifuged out of redstone. If you find some cinnabar ore in a redstone vein or one of the infused stone veins you can use that too.

Combining sulfur trioxide and water in the chemical reactor will give you sulfuric acid for your single use acid batteries. You'll need to make sulfur dioxide first.

On the other hand if you've made some light fuel you'll have some spare hydrogen sulfide you can also turn into sulfuric acid (after a couple steps), and if you've automated it, you'll be drowning in it honestly. Once you can make an LCR, you can skip directly from HS to SA in one step. Keep in mind that you'll need all that acid for making stuff instead of for single use batteries by then.

Batteries work pretty much the same in a battery buffer as in a regular machine's battery slot. Battery buffers are used to buffer power to stabilize output.

They come in different sizes: 1, 4, 9(!) and 16 slots. They can draw 2A and output 1A per battery inserted - watch your wire amperage! Cables come in 1x, 2x, 4x, 8x, 12x, and 16x, with tin transferring 1A per size. Make sure not to mess up, or your cable will melt, becoming a fire, and possibly an explosion.

Remember that there's loss when outputting EU from any GT machine, so putting 4 4-slot ones in a row loses 8 power compared to 2 from 1 16-slot one. And this is for every amp too.

[note]You can import batteries into one, but ONLY empty acid batteries can be exported from one. No, you can't get around this.[/note]
A few recipes require IC2 batteries. Fill your small battery hull with some molten redstone and you'll get an RE-Battery.

A second source for sodium is glauconite ore or glauconite sand. This type of ore vein can be found at Y level 20-50.

Soapstone and talc can be used for lubricant.

Salt ore mixes can be found in the Overworld between Y 50-70.

Salt isn't only used to get sodium, it's an important ingredient in many Pam's HarvestCraft food recipes.

Lepidolite and spodumene are good sources of lithium for your batteries. Later on you can get a lot more in different ways.

You can get Cadmium from Sphalerite (centrifuge or thermal centrifuge). Later on you can use GT++ Ore processing chains to get Cadmium from Rare Earths. I don't care how you get it, just get some Cadmium.

The canning machine is used to fill batteries, fill or empty containers with fluids or occasionally dusts, or to fill tin cans with any kind of food (HV+).

At LV-HV tier you can make batteries with sodium, cadmium, or lithium.

Want to move your chests and barrels without spilling all the things (buildcraft™)? No problem! Make a dolly and you can carry your full chests, barrels or storage drawers anywhere you want. But be warned, you will get a slowness debuff so hopefully you don't have to travel very far. You can also move non-portable buildcraft and iron tanks without losing fluids, and worktables without losing stored recipes.

Shift-right-click an empty dolly to collapse it. It won't carry anything until you unfold it, but it will stack and can go in your backpack.

§3PS: Later on you can fly or make a traveller's belt to get around the debuff.§r

Do you want to move a spawner around and build a cool mob farm? That will be no problem if you get the diamond dolly. You can move 6 spawners before the durability runs out, which is probably more than you'll need right now.
Crafting some nice grain bait for your animal trap.
Crafting some tasty fruit bait for your animal trap.
Crafting some veggie bait for your animal trap.
Crafting some fish bait for your fish trap.
Tired of hunting for cows, zombies or sheep? You can build a trap and hope some animal or monster drops will be caught by the netting inside.

Have you ever tried to catch a fish with your bare hands? It's time to craft a fishing rod and get some fish the easy way. Cast your fishing rod in some water and wait until the bobber dips below the surface. Then reel back in your line and hopefully you caught yourself something nice.
Fishing can be very boring. Why not automate it with a fish trap?
It's time to plant some wheat to make some bread or to prepare grain bait for your animal traps.

The first step in making bread is to macerate your wheat into flour with a mortar or a macerator.

Flour can be used in many food recipes for different Pam's HarvestCraft foods.
Baking your dough in a Furnace makes some tasty bread. Your first bread!

Water and flour makes a dough or two... Dough can be used in many different food recipes from Pam's HarvestCraft.

Don't use the terrible NEI recipe, instead drop a stack of flour into a cauldron full of water. Celiacs beware!
Smelt your bread again and you get some toast! It gives you more nutrition points, and unlocks more culinary potential!
Another distillate you can make out of oil is Sulfuric Naphtha which has a burn value of 40,000 EU per cell in the gas turbine.
Centrifuging Butane or Propane gives you LPG with a burn value of 320,000 EU.

You can process Sulfuric Naphtha to fluid Naphtha which has a burn value of 220,000 EU in the Gas Turbine. Naphtha can be used to get Ethylene for Polyethylene, but it shares this use with Refinery Gas and Light Fuel, so decide for yourself which one you want to use.

If you choose to make High-Octane Gasoline in EV and onwards, it will need a lot of Naphtha. You can also make Polycaprolactam (Nylon), which doesn't have any useful purpose yet, but it might get some in the near future.
Another distillate for your gas turbine you can make out of oil is Sulfuric Gas which has a burn value of 25,000 EU per cell.

Refine your gas in a chemical reactor with Hydrogen gas to give it a better burn value of 160,000 EU. It used to be the least useful fraction of oil, but it's now possible to distill it into large amounts of Ethylene if you steam-crack the Refinery Gas beforehand.

This early, you will have to use a Chemical Reactor to crack it, but later on there's a dedicated multiblock for this purpose, the Oil Cracker. For best Ethylene results, you should severely steam-crack it, and you will get lots of Methane as well.

Distilling some "refinery gases" gives you some methane gas. There are many more (and probably better) ways to get methane.

You will need this in later tiers, for PTFE as an example.

If for some reason you want to be able to jump down a cliff without getting the message "Player X fell from a high place", a great idea would be to find a way to slow your fall. The store was out of feather falling potions, so make a hang glider instead.
The electrotine battery is exclusively used in project red machines and the jetpack. Electrotine is made by mixing redstone and electrum dust in a mixer, or mined from the Nether.

Your glider gets you to the ground safely but it does not have any method to get up. After you researched electrotine you discovered that it is powerful enough for your first jetpack.

A diamond chestplate surrounded with 4 electrotine batteries is powerful enough to bring you up into the air.

It does not have a hover mode so you better take your glider with you.

Hint: This jetpack can't fly higher than Y-128.

GREAT.... you now have an empty jetpack. You need 25 electrotine dust to completely fill it. Let's craft an electrotine generator and a charging bench to use the power of electrotine.

You will very quickly discover that, while it is fast and cheap, it's empty in the blink of an eye. Despite this, it is useful in combination with the hang glider to get into the air and to get away from hairy situations.

Your coal jetpack needs coal and water to produce steam. After a short warm-up period you can go and take it for a ride. Keep in mind you will need your glider to make a soft landing.

Put your jetpack on your back and hit Shift and the adventure backpack's action-key to start it.

Max flying height for this jetpack is Y-185.

Vertical velocity decreases linearly with height after overcoming optimal height - 135 for jetpack and 100 for copter.

The copterpack is the first jetpack with a hover mode. It uses several different types of fuels to power it.

Buckets of creosote, lava, oil, diesel, cetane, ethanol, and fuel will work.

Equip your copterpack, then hold the sneak key and press the Adventure Backpack action key. You can also switch between hover and normal mode.

Max flying height is limited to Y-200.

Vertical velocity decreases linearly with height after overcoming optimal height - 135 for jetpack and 100 for copter.

[note]Dropped items will be pushed away from you, just like a helicopter pushes things away, so be careful in the End, or by cliffsides.[/note]

Your first electrical jetpack, It can be charged in any LV machine. You need to hit the IC2 mode-switch key to toggle between normal mode and hover mode while holding down the jump key. When descending, remember to shut off hover mode or else you'll drain your jetpack.

The only limitation is that you can't fly higher than Y-185.

For charging on the go, you can craft a charging crystal from ic2 charging components. You have to take the backpack out of the armor slot and put it in your hotbar and activate the charger by sneak-clicking.

Later on GT++ charge packs are belts that can charge everything in your inventory including armor. Check NEI for the recipe.

Finally, the GT++ wireless charger will charge everything in your inventory, including the jetpack, from your base at long ranges. A quest is unlocked once you finish your nanosuit. Just remember when you are off world or in the Nether that your jetpack isn't charging!

This jetpack uses IC2 biogas and can fly up to Y-245. You can switch between hover and normal mode using the IC2 mode-switch key.

An empty jetpack can be (re-)fueled in a fluid tank filled with biogas.

The advanced electric jetpack is an upgraded version of the electric jetpack.
While worn in the chest armor slot and charged with EU, it allows the player to fly. It provides no armor protection, but will charge tools being used in the same manner as the advanced lappack from its 3,000,000 EU internal storage.

The advanced electric jetpack is limited to a maximum flying height of Y-256.

[note]To turn it on, hit the fly key listed under gravisuite. You can then use space to fly up. To activate hover, hit the IC2 mode key while holding space. Will also recharge tools.[/note]

Combining the advanced electric jetpack and nanosuit yields you the advanced nano chestplate. Now you have the protection of the chestplate combined with the freedom of movement of the jetpack.

[note]Works like the AEJ.[/note]

The GraviChestPlate is the ultimate quantum armor combined with a high powered jetpack. Some notable features include:

- 30M EU Capacity
- Spacesuit Capability
- Hazmat Protection
- Gravitation Engines (Creative Flight)
- Levitation Mode
- Quantum Shield (Invincibility, requires full Quantum Armor)

[note]KEYBINDS
HUD: Gravi HUD Key
Gravitation Engines: Gravi Fly Key
Levitation Mode: Spacebar + IC2 Mode Switch Key
Quantum Shield: Sneak + IC2 Mode Switch Key[/note]
You've been using your hide shield long enough. After you make your first tools, grab a bit of iron ore and make a nice iron shield.

Upgrade your wooden spear with a stone arrowhead and iron screws to a stone spear.
This spear has better durability than the wooden one.

Upgrade your wooden spear with an iron arrowhead and two steel screws to an iron spear.

The iron spear has better durability than the stone variant.

At MV Tier you can upgrade your iron spear to a diamond one. Get a diamond arrowhead, two stainless steel screws and a wooden spear.

This spear has superior durability.
Your iron shield is old and worn out. With a shield made from diamond plates you can maintain block for up to 5 seconds.

Wow, your first handmade §oehm§r machine made bow. Now it's time to make a quiver and maybe some arrows.

To place arrows in the quiver, put the quiver and the stack of arrows in a crafting grid. Make sure the Gameplay key Special doesn't conflict with other keybinds. By default, it is Z. When you have the bow selected, use Z to swap arrow slots in the quiver.

While it seems like these might be worthless, these arrows do have special uses. You really want to share a cookie with friends, don't you?

Let's go hunt a bit.

The arc furnace is an alternative to macerating stuff back into dusts and for making Cast Iron, Annealed Copper, and Glass (in MV). You get ingots, and sometimes different materials back from recycling than with a Macerator. You also have both slots at LV.

[note]You can also use certain gases to boost your Arc Furnace processing speed.[/note]

A faster alternative to Steel production is to use the Arc Furnace and smelt Iron Ingots (or Iron Dust) into Cast Iron Ingots. Then macerate them into dust and smelt the dust into Steel very quickly in the EBF.

Of course, you'll need enough Carbon/Coal/Charcoal dust to do so.

Upgrade your battery buffer to hold 16 batteries for primary storage.

You can use different buffers - probably with fewer batteries - for your EBF, Thermal Centrifuge, and so on.

To cook some healthy food you need a few tools crafted first.
Saucepan,
pot,
rolling pin,
mortar,
mixing bowl,
soft mallet,
skillet,
knife...

You live close to the water and don't have a boat? Man, get it together.

You need wooden planks, slabs and a knife to craft one. (This is also quest id 666, be careful, something is going on.)

[note]We here at QuestBook, Inc. do not guarantee the usefulness of boats. The standard worldgen does not include oceans, so their usefulness is heavily curtailed. There are lots of rivers, but horses might be more useful if not on a server.[/note]

The wooden tracks can be made without any machine, though always check NEI for assembler recipes for discounts. Functionally equivalent to normal rails, but with a lower maximum speed (for safety reasons).

[note]Hint: You can use your wooden rails for Steve's Carts farms.[/note]

The rubber dinghy requires only a few rubber plates. Like the vanilla wooden boat, it will break and dismantle whenever it hits a surface, however instead of returning sticks and planks, it will return a damaged rubber dinghy, which can be re-crafted with two pieces of rubber back into a usable rubber dinghy!
I meant to say boat... The inflatable boat is the first boat that doesn't break on impact with a solid block.

Unlike all other boats, this amazing carbon fiber canoe is COMPLETELY INDESTRUCTIBLE!* This means that you can smash it into as many beaches, lily pads and alligators as you like, the carbon fiber canoe won't take a scratch!

Warning: We are not held responsible for any damage caused by riding the carbon fiber canoe into a lava lake or the Void.

*Therefore, warranty is NOT included.

The electric boat works mostly like a vanilla boat, chugging through the water at a decent pace. It will hopefully drop itself once you crash, which is slightly nicer than the usual sticks. That's all well and good, but what if we utilize the electric engine? Wearing an energy storage device in your chestplate slot, like a batpack or energypack, will cause the boat to drain energy from it and propel you forward at supersonic speed! Doing this will consume about 100 EU per block traveled, so even a decent batpack won't last long!

Really? Yes for the more advanced boats you need a new shape form.

You need to make an Extruder first to progress further.
The extruder is not very useful in LV. But it will extrude your next tier of boat, get you extra fluid cells, or make §osome§r Tinkers Construct tool parts.

The wooden junction, wye and switch tracks need an assembling machine to craft. They allow you to join and switch to tracks going to different locations.

NEI doesn't show the right recipe on the first page. Go through the recipes a bit to find the right one.

The switch lever is the manual version of the switch motor, requiring a player to operate it instead of a redstone signal.

It is used in various signaling systems, mainly to change the way switch tracks and wye tracks work.

The crowbar comes in a Railcraft (and thaumcraft versions of RC) and a gregtech variant. It is used to manipulate machines from railcraft, remove plates and any other covers (pumps, conveyor modules, etc.) from gregtech pipes and machines as well as breaking certain objects faster, such as tracks. This tool is also used to access certain inventories from Railcraft.

Hold a crowbar and shift-right-click to attach carts. Click the starting cart then continue to click to add more carts to the link. Carts will act slower the more connections are made.

The crowbar can be used as a weapon, though it costs twice as much durability on attack (just like any other non weapon tool...).

After you craft your first cart the journey can begin...

Well, not really. You will need some kind of tracks first.

[note]We here at QuestBook, Inc. do not guarantee the usefulness of minecarts or trains in any way. Especially since you can mine out a vein in a single session once you have a hammer and backpacks.[/note]

[warn]WARNING: Unprotected carts can be knocked off their rails by lightning. Cover the area with blocks to prevent carts from disappearing.[/warn]

[warn]Also, make sure to keep your cart in one chunk, or use chunkloaders covering the whole area the cart works within. Loading/unloading chunks may cause carts to disappear or duplicate.[/warn]

[note]You should only make these if you want to have fun with them, as anything they can do is better done by other methods, including the Long Distance Fluid Pipeline. Excessive minecart and train use on servers may cause lag and you may be asked to switch later anyway.[/note]
If you don't have any armor, "mud armor" is better than nothing. Mud can be found in some wet biomes, or crafted from dirt and water.
If you can't find mud you can make very poor armor out of wood. Cutting down a few trees to make a set should do. You will need a soft mallet too, so save a few logs for that.
Iron armor is much better than the leather armor. Especially when you have to go outside during the night.

Killing some cows will give you enough leather to craft a complete set of leather armor.

Hint: You are able to dye this armor.
Bronze armor has the same abilities as iron armor. Same durability, same protection and same enchantment capability.
The gold armor is a "nice to have" armor. The durability is very low but you look expensive when you wear it.
Diamond armor is the best armor in Vanilla Minecraft, but over here there are much better armors available.
Not really better but fancier. The chain mail armor is made out of steel rings.
The steel armor has more durability than the iron/bronze or chainmail armor.
Combining the strength of advanced alloy plates with the steel chestplate makes your vest very hard. Now you have double the durability and increased armor points by 1.5.

You may have noticed big meteors everywhere, and maybe wondered if they're useful somehow? Well, they are, but not just yet. I'll give you a reward for collecting some now.

Inside the meteor you can find a skystone chest containing some processor press plates. Save them for later, you can't do AE2 without them. Though you can also just make them yourself in EV. Plus the chest is nice, and can be placed underneath blocks and still opened.

If all surface meteors have been raided, put some skystone in your Ore Finder to find underground ones, or wait until you can make a Meteorite Compass to find them.

With your brand-new Compressor you are able to make some metal blocks for your new anvil. You're required to craft at least one for the Forge Hammer.

§3With the anvil you can repair, rename and enchant armor and some types of tools (non-GT).§r

Do you want to automate your smeltery because you're planning to make stacks and stacks of glass blocks?

No problem, craft a large bronze pipe and place it under the faucet. Make sure to connect the pipe to the faucet using a wrench. Now the molten fluid will flow inside the pipe. Under or next to the pipe you have to place the casting basins or tables.

A hopper and a chest underneath will auto-output products from the casting blocks.

NOTE: Faucets will output precisely 144L each activation if you toggle it off immediately. That's going to have some uses later on...

You want a better automation than using pipes? Sure, craft a comparator and link it with redstone dust placed on the ground. The redstone needs to be adjacent to the faucet to activate the crafting process.

Steel production is so slow. If you got enough bricks and clay, build a second BBF. Build it attached to the first one, so they can share a wall and you will save some bricks, clay and concrete.

[warn]Note that this will generate twice as much pollution in total - consider moving them further away.[/warn]

Not even two BBFs are fast enough...Can you figure out how to save the most bricks making 4?

[note]PS: If you can't, this pack may not be for you.[/note]

[warn]Note that this will generate massive amounts of pollution - have you considered the Nether?[/warn]

Your Bricked Blast Furnace uses coal like hell and your steam boilers do too? Well it's time to make more coke ovens and automate them a bit. The Coke Oven Hatch, Wooden Fluid Pipes, and Tin Item Pipes will help you reach your goal.

Since this is a GT multiblock, it can wallshare bricks and hatches. The amount of bricks required for this quest is the minimum for creating 10 wallshared Coke Ovens.

Remember that tin item pipes require a steel wrench to dismantle them.

[note]Search NEI for a more efficient way to make coke oven bricks.[/note]

[warn]The whole coke-oven process generates a lot of pollution, so consider putting it further away.[/warn]
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lWhy One Coke Oven When You Can Have Ten?

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Seriously, how dark can one be? You're sure the face in that crystal was nothing but imagination...
You feel empowered, light, almost like a ghost.
1023 Buckets of blood in one slate! How much more I can store, oh I wish I would know. Then I add one and check if it works. 1024 buckets of blood in one slate! ... ...
The demons summoned are rather strong, but their souls contain immense power!
Tier 4 slates: Getting close.
As you might've discovered by now, plants grow very slowly. So why don't you try to speed that up a little? A watering can will come in handy.
Top tier chalk, for fancy wall paintings?
Your tier 5 orb.
Your tier 4 orb.
Enhanced elemental chalk, to write "darker" runes than you're used to...

Runes of Superior Capacity increase the Altar's size by 14% multiplicatively.

Runes of the Orb increase the soul network size by 4% each. You'll need them later on.

The final frontier: There are not many runes available. The acceleration rune reduces the tick time until the next buffer I/O interaction. It starts at 20, and is reduced by 1 for each rune, with the minimum being 1.
More powerful rituals require dusk runes. With your new dusk chalk, you can enhance your ritual diviner to place those. Allowing you to perform a lot more rituals.
The last diviner so far, used for the most powerful rituals.

Time to open a portal to the Demonic Realm. What could possibly go wrong? (It's recommended to do this ritual in a space dimension, as the demon city spreads up to 1000x1000 blocks)

[note]You should also be starting the ritual from the ground rather than in the air for the best results![/note]

Requirements:
- 15M LP (Archmage Blood Orb and >= 13 Runes of the Orb)
- 8 Crystal Belljars (one filled with each of: magicales, potentia, incendium, terrae, tenebrae, sanctus, aether, and aquasalus)
- 1 Sacrifice (Bottle a lesser demon/elemental in a soul vial)
- 1 Master Ritual Stone, 128 Ritual Stones, and 1 Blood Altar
- 1 Awakened Activation Crystal

Steps to the Ritual:
1. Use a Ritual Diviner to place all the Ritual Stones.
2. Place the Belljars atop the 8 pillars surrounding the center.
3. Link the Belljars to the Master Ritual Stone.
4. Place the Blood Altar on top of the Master Ritual Stone.
5. Start the ritual with the Awakened Activation Crystal.
6. The Belljars are drained of their reagents.
7. Kill the lesser demon/elemental with a Dagger of Sacrifice.
8. The Demon Portal is opened.

For more details and images, visit [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Convocation_of_the_Damned[/url]

[warn]The OW is now blacklisted for the portal. Too many people did not follow the recommendation and servers suffered for it. It also does not work well in the Personal Dimension.[/warn]
With these new shards you're able to craft the most powerful spell components. Maybe it's time to upgrade your mining spell?
For the emitter and the sensor you'll need to get some certus quartz.

Good circuits are an improvement on basic circuits. They're an MV-tier circuit, which is a component of all MV gregtech machines.

To open MV, you still need to make an EBF and do the Aluminium quest if you haven't already, since §oeverything§r needs aluminium.

This quest also opens the Project Red quests - one of the early automation options.

Now that you've made some tools, you can start getting into some real agriculture. Get ready to craft many more iron saws...

Welcome to CropsNH, the premier passive resource production mo... wait sorry I'm hearing just now that Bees do in fact still exist.

Anyways, if you want to learn how to till your way to the Stargate, with the passive resources needed throughout much of your progression, this is the place to be.

The first step will be obtaining a stock of basic crops which you can breed from. If you don't already have them go steal some from those villagers, or that witch down the hill.

[warn]CropsNH crops do not behave the same as IC2 Crops. These quests will walk you through how they work, it's recommended that you give them a read if it's your first time using them.[/warn]

This is the start of the first 4-circuit circuit line. This one doesn't really have a consistent naming scheme unlike the later ones, but it still works the same way, aside from the fact that you get your first EV §oand§r IV circuits from it, all the rest only have 1 new tier of circuit. Because of this you'll need to make 2 new CAs to finish it.

The first one is the Integrated Processor, the final type of MV circuits. You also don't need to craft any other circuits to make it, so it's the cheapest. This repeats each circuit tier.

[note]This and all circuits past it need a cleanroom.[/note]
This is the second step to making EV and IV circuits.
Integrated Processors need central processing units. You can get these by cutting a central processing unit wafer.

The Processor Assembly circuit needs some small coils. You can make these a couple different ways.

[note]If you somehow got SMD Inductors already, you may hold 64 in your hand to skip this quest.[/note]
They shoot you with explosive fireballs but they are weak when you hit them or knock the fireballs back with a weapon. Better upgrade your armor with fire and blast protection.

You investigated the pearls, and managed to reactivate them to become eyes. This has shown you that the source of the disturbance seems to be coming out of the portal frames inside the strongholds, deep underground. They seem strangely drawn towards its mysterious depths. Perhaps they can be used to reactivate it?

Hint: Throwing Ender Eyes in the air in the Overworld will guide you to the nearest stronghold. From time to time Ender Eyes are destroyed in this process, so make extras. Try to do so in a place without obstructions so you can see where it went.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Is This the End? No, it's the END Dimension

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Capacitor Banks are upgraded RF batteries which can store the RF power you generate.

BTW, you can also use capacitors to upgrade your EnderIO machines. They'll use more power, but also work faster.
The Vibrant Capacitor Bank is the largest non-creative RF Battery from EIO. It can store 25 million RF in a single block.
Vibrant alloy is a high tier EnderIO alloy made out of ender eye, energetic alloy and chrome dust.

Energetic alloy is a new alloy from EnderIO made out of gold, conductive iron and black steel dust. Double-layer capacitors need it, as does the HV energy hatch.

[note]The direct mixer recipe has 7 ingredients, so you need an EV mixer or a multiblock to use it. You have to use the other one for now.[/note]

In order to upgrade one armor item with basic upgrades, you need a vibrant crystal and 10 XP levels. Some upgrades can be applied directly, but more advanced ones will require empowering the armor first.

Next you'll need to find some tropical bees. The hives can be found in Jungle biomes. Be careful as these bees are very aggressive and can poison you. Collect the silky combs and extract some silk wisp from those in order to make some Apiarist's clothes. Try to get pristine bees. If you're having trouble finding them, you can use Nature's Compass to search for a specific biome.

Collect silky combs and extract some silk wisp out of it in order to make some Apiarist's clothes.

This can take a very long time, so parallelize!

Use a GregTech or Forestry Centrifuge to get Silky Propoli. For higher tier (and useful) combs you need a GT centrifuge.

The Forestry Centrifuge is able to centrifuge up to 9 items out of bee combs. It uses RF energy.

Latter bee combs need the GT one though, so keep that in mind.

Centrifuge your silky propoli to get some silk wisp at a chance of 60 percent. Put 9 silk wisp in the Forestry carpenter or GregTech assembler to get woven silk.

This fine fabric can be used for crafting Apiarist's Clothes or to upgrade a Forestry Backpacks to 45 slots.

If you have collected 24 woven silk you can make a complete Apiarist's suit to be protected from bee stings and other bad bee effects. You can also use the suit parts to upgrade your EnderIO Dark Steel Armor to have the same effect.

Your Dark Steel armor can be upgraded in various ways by combining it with various other items. You will need an anvil and a lot of XP.

Make sure when making the potions to only do three at a time, so the NBT data matches.
In order to upgrade a Dark Steel weapon or tool, you need a vibrant crystal, 10 XP levels, and your trusty anvil.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §5§lDark Steel Tool and Weapon Basic Upgrades

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Your weapons and tools can be upgraded even more by adding capacitors and various other items.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §5§lDark Steel Tool and Weapon Advanced Upgrades

betterquesting:10.desc:8: It's possible to power RF machines with a solar panel. It outputs 10 RF/t. Perfect for low use RF machines.
The upgraded RF solar panel is much better. It outputs 40 RF/t.

Enchanted Earth makes saplings and seeds planted on it grow faster. When stacked on top of each other it has a chance to add ticks to the block above accumulating all the way to the top. This will randomly speed up growth a bit.
The next solar panel you can make is the MV one. It gives 128 EU/t. You'll need to make some sunnarium first though.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §a§lPower of the Sun at MV Level

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Put those 128 EU panels on a block to make them placeable in the world.

At EV you're able to make Indium. Indium cannot be found in Ore form [note](except in super small amounts on Ross)[/note].

First you need to make Indium concentrate out of purified galena and sphalerite ore, then mix in some aluminium to get Indium. Indium is used in large amounts later on, automate this ASAP.

You also get lead, zinc, silver, sulfur, and water back from the lead-zinc solution. So it's not like you don't get the materials from the ores at all, just less of them.
The next solar panel you can make is the HV one. It generates 512 EU/t. First you need to produce enriched sunnarium by mixing irradiated uranium and sunnarium.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §9§lPower of the Sun at HV Level

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Put those 512 EU panels on a block to make them placeable in the world.

Books can be found easily enough in villages or in the roguelike dungeons surface brick house. I'm sure they have a recipe too.

Now glue on the other hand...or should I say horse? Try and get a horse inside a smeltery and feed it hay to keep it alive.

Or you can wait until after you go to the Nether and get some sulfur. Either way.

Fishing can be very boring. Why not automate it with a fish trap?

This is fish trap 2.0.

Many cooking recipes need milk and water. Crafting it in the crafting table can be very tedious.

It is much easier using a Forestry worktable. Move all your buckets into the worktable, and shift-click to craft them all at once.

The Bauxite vein contains two ores that get you Titanium, Bauxite and Ilmenite. Bauxite also contains Aluminium, as does (obviously) the Aluminium ore. You want tons of Titanium, so collect a bunch.

When you're mining you'll surely pick up some Meteoric Iron from small ores, enough to make your rocket. But if it's not enough, or you want more, you can also mine the meteors that fall out of the sky.

You've gotten some Rutile as a byproduct by now, right? Or EBF'd some Ilmenite?

Rutile, Chlorine and Carbon makes Titaniumtetrachloride, and some CO. You can recycle this for Carbon if you want to. Best use a Large Chemical Reactor in that case to get the full recipe.

Combining TiCl4 with Magnesium in an HV EBF will give you a Hot Titanium ingot, and Magnesiumchloride. You can recycle this as well to get all the Magnesium and Chlorine back using some Sodium.
With Platinum in hand, you consider making some SMD diodes. Eventually, in EV, they will be required. But for now it is up to you if you have enough Gallium and Platinum to use them.

Your first EV circuit is the Workstation.

You can make Blue Alloy with Silver and Electrotine in an Alloy Smelter. If you don't have Electrotine, you can make it from Redstone and Electrum in a Mixer. Have fun!

Plastic circuit boards require a plastic plate with Sulfuric Acid to make an Empty Board. By adding copper foil and Iron(III) Chloride or Sodium Persulfate you can craft a plastic circuit board. Later on you can make them more efficiently.

[note]PCBs are used in the circuits in HV tier.[/note]

This bad boy will tremendously boost the byproducts of your cracked fuel or pyrolyse oven. This way you can make industrial TNT, polyethylene, polytetrafluoroethylene and other plastics more efficiently. You'll also need this for the platline.

You'll need to make EV circuits in a cleanroom to build this machine.

For hatches, you can choose your own tier. 1 MV energy hatch is enough for most of the useful recipes. 2 MV energy hatches or 1 HV energy hatch will cover almost all the rest. You will also need 1 input hatch, and at least 5 output hatches. An output bus will capture any solid outputs.

NEI is not great for determining which cracked fuel option is the best. Instead, visit the Oil Cracking Unit wiki page linked below for a complete list of all the fractions in a nice, convenient format!

[url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Oil_Cracking_Unit[/url]
This machine will help you turn dust into crystals which you will need for high tier recipes.
You know what this does. :D
Use the autoclave to crystallize your dust. You can also make Raw Carbon Fiber out of Carbon Dust, and do other things.

You'll use this a lot to make high tier circuits, and for other recipes.

[note]You'll soon find that everything you use the PLE on needs a cleanroom, so make sure you start on that.[/note]
This way of making carbon plates requires autoclaving carbon dust. There are 4 different fluids you can use, check NEI to see which gives how much.

If you want to save the environment you can autoclave 16 plantballs to get raw bio fiber with the following liquids:

Biomass        33% chance
Methanol       50% chance
Fuel            90% chance
Nitro-diesel 100% chance

§rHowever, making carbon plates this way will require an electric blast furnace.

These are the first parts you will need for your beloved nano armor.

[note]To actually complete the nano armor, you will need EV circuits and nano crystals (see Storing and Transforming EU).[/note]

[warn]IC2 is slowly being removed from the modpack! Check out the nearby quest "Modular Meddling" for the replacement.[/warn]

The nano helmet is a bit special. It will provide you with night vision as long as you have energy!

[note]If you got these from a lootbag, hold these in your hand after completing the "Carbon Parts" quest to skip this quest.[/note]

Don't burn yourself.

[note]It's also possible to get Firestone from the Sulfur Bee, though it has a notably smaller comb output.[/note]
Carbon plates are used for a bunch of stuff, including eventually the nanosuit. Go check out the armor chapter.

You can stop worrying about some mobs for now. This will help you survive a bit and will give you some of that SWAG. Your journey doesn't stop here traveller, as quantum armor awaits you!

[note]PS: The nano suit also acts as hazmat gear.[/note]
Bio carbon plates are made out of raw carbon mesh. Put it in the electric blast furnace to make carbon plates.

This oven is the best way to get charcoal and creosote (x50 faster than the Coke Oven) and other byproducts. You will need tons of bronze, iron and steel to build it, but it's worth it. Finally, it will be possible to dismantle the charcoal pit.

With Cupronickel coils the oven is a bit slower. Each coil tier speeds up the charcoal production.

To make wafers, you need to make monocrystalline silicon boules first. The process takes 450 seconds and requires solar grade silicon dust and a small gallium arsenide crystal in the electric blast furnace. You can make 16 wafers out of every boule.

All your little turbines take up too much space? Are you running out of water? It's time to solve these problems. This Large Steam Turbine can help you produce a tremendous amount of energy. It will also distill water for you, so you can use the same water again inside your Large Boiler. Don't forget to make a rotor for the turbine and put inside the controller, otherwise this multiblock won't do anything.

Each turbine has a specific optimal flow, the Steam flow that gives the highest fuel efficiency, the value shown on the turbine's tooltip. This is the flow you want to match, and you can use a Fluid Regulator as a cover to make it exactly what you want, but you can go beyond this flow to get an even higher EU/t value, at a loss of fuel efficiency. You can make turbines in 4 different sizes, with larger turbines producing more EU/t, but with varying amounts of fuel efficiency. Generally, Large is the best due to having the highest fuel efficiency and a good optimal flow rate

When using turbines, be careful of flow rates. To find the optimal flow rate, you divide the optimal energy flow rate listed on the turbine, by the energy value for the plasma. You can also use the Large Turbine Calculator (there's a link on the main spreadsheet, which is linked to in discord), or scan the multiblock's controller while feeding it a minimal amount of plasma to see what the optimal flow is. Make sure to use a Fluid Regulator set to this flow rate for highest fuel efficiency, or go beyond it to get more EU/t at a cost to efficiency, with Steam Turbines being the worst at retaining efficiency beyond the optimal flow.

If you go beyond the optimal flow, you will get a higher EU/t value, but less fuel efficiency, and the maximum EU/t value depends on the turbine type and its Overflow Efficiency tier. For this type of turbine, tier 1 reaches the max at 150% of optimal flow to produce 112% of the EU/t, tier 2 reaches the max at 200% of optimal flow to produce 133% of the EU/t and tier 3 reaches the max at 250% of optimal flow to produce 156% of the EU/t. The closer you get to this maximum, the more fuel efficiency you're throwing away. Don't exceed your dynamo hatch's maximum EU/t output, though, or you will have problems!

Use NEI with the appropriate long rod to find assembler recipes that will work for you. Or the spreadsheet. Long magnalium for small turbines, long titanium for normal turbines, etc.

Pre-moon, the best rotors are Shadow Metal or Vibrant Alloy.

Post-moon, the best HV rotors are Shadow Metal or Oriharukon (this is IV-tier). Luckily, turbines are now fully functional with multi-amp dynamos, so give those a try if you need extra amps!

For additional choices, see the spreadsheet and Large Turbine Calculator.

As soon as you have the ability to store energy in large quantities, it would be necessary to have a way to generate energy in large quantities. You need a large bronze boiler. But in order to make this boiler, you will need a mountain of bronze. This boiler produces 800L of steam per tick. This is enough to run 10 basic steam turbines.

The large boiler can use either water or distilled water. Water is consumed at a rate of 1L of water per 160L of steam.

To make a large boiler you must make a 3x3x6 structure with Bronze Pipe Casings in the center of the middle 3 levels. The lowest level must contain at least 1 input hatch, 1 output hatch, 5 fireboxes, 1 muffler, and one maintenance hatch. The lowest level can not contain any plated bricks.

§cWarning: Different from other boilers, Large Boilers must contain water at all times while active. If at any point the Boiler runs out of water while it is active, it will explode.
For the next tier we need advanced circuits. To make advanced circuits, you need transistors.

Now you can make Advanced Circuits, which means it's time to build a Large Steel Boiler. Each one of these produces 1000 EU/t in Steam, which means you will need several Steam Turbines to convert it all to power! Keep in mind that the MV ones are less efficient, so calculate your losses when building your setup.

The Titanium Large Boiler is a distant cousin to the Bronze and Steel Boilers, and it has a significant difference. Instead of accepting just about any burnable fuel, it will only accept specific ones and reject all others. You can see which ones are accepted by looking at the appropriate NEI tab, but the Solid Super Fuels are guaranteed to work.

This is a big downside, but the upside is that these boilers output respectable power even in these tiers. Without any other inputs, this boiler produces Superheated Steam at a flow rate matching 4000 EU/t, on turbines running at 100% fuel efficiency. If this becomes 150%, then the steam output will produce 6000 EU/t, almost the same as a boosted Large Combustion Engine!

To get all the power from this, though, you will need an HP Steam Turbine, followed by a regular Steam Turbine, or more than one of each if the flow rate is too big for the turbine material you've chosen. Make sure to send the Distilled Water back to the boilers!

The Large Tungstensteel Boiler is the biggest and baddest of the four. Like the Titanium one, it is a specialized boiler that only accepts specific fuels, mainly the Solid Super Fuels, but it will produce Superheated Steam at a rate equivalent to 16000 EU/t, at 100% fuel efficiency. If you have good Steam Turbines, especially Oriharukon ones, you will get much more power than that, around 24000 EU/t or more.

Depending on how many of these you build, you might need a huge amount of turbines. To solve that problem, consider going a bit above the optimal flow on each turbine, or even switching to Loose mode, although this is only a good choice if you can match the optimal flow in that mode.
Make energium out of ruby and redstone dusts in the MV mixer. Then use the autoclave to make Energy Crystals. Energy crystals can store 1 million EU and work as an HV battery.
Nano crystals are used for making the nano armor.
Advanced circuits need an MV precision laser engraver. Let's craft one.

To create some silicon wafers, put the monocrystalline silicon boule in a cutting machine. It would be best to make the MV version because you'll need it soon for ILCs, RAM, and other chips.

You can also use wafers to make diodes more efficiently if you have polyethylene as well.

By the way, did you ever try looking at the oredict for circuits? You can tell what tier they are from that. They go: Primitive (ULV), Basic (LV), Good (MV), Advanced (HV), etc. Now make your Good Integrated Circuits.

In order to make HV machines, you need HV circuits. The first one you can make is the Advanced Circuit from IC2. You'll need to make LV circuits to make MV circuits to make the HV circuits. Yay for recursive crafting! Start with the LV Integrated Logic Circuit. And no, you can't use the IC2 Electronic Circuits.

Advanced (HV) circuits require an LV circuit assembling machine. Basic (LV) and Good (MV) ones can also be made much more efficiently with this machine.

However, all circuit assemblers need higher tier circuits than the other machines of their tier. This means you have to use MV circuits instead of the LV ones you've been using until now. I know you want it, so make it already!
The night vision goggles need special sensor lenses to work.
The night vision goggles need advanced heat exchangers to work.

Making a gold capped greatwood wand requires 30 vis, but your old wand's limit is 25. So first create an iron or copper capped greatwood wand reload it with 50 vis and then later on in the next quest create a gold capped greatwood wand.

§3You can always press the NEI 'U' command on the caps, the core, or the boss ingredient to find the correct GT:NH recipe for the wands.

Combining a scuba helmet with a nano helmet in an assembling machine will give you a nano scuba helmet. You'd better not try to dive with it because you can't. It is a part of the new quantum suit helmet.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Don't Try to Dive With It

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Combining stainless steel platings with some nano leggings in the assembler gives you nano plated leggings. Better not try to wear them because you can't. They are part of the new quantum suit leggings.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Plated Leggings - Better Not Try to Wear It

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Combining some rubber boots with nano boots in the Assembler gives you Nano Rubber Boots. Better not try to put them on because you can't. They are part of the new quantum suit boots.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Don't Try to Walk With It

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Plating all your armor parts with iridium alloy casings gives them a better durability. Before you can wear these quantum armor parts you need to activate them with some quantum crystals.
The quantum armor is a high tier and very durable armor with a lot of features like night vision, fall damage reduction and running very fast.
Ideal for your Implosion Compressor.

Lapotron crystals require you to mix your energium dust with some lapis dust. You should check out the Storing and Transforming EU tab for the lapotron crystal and the Lapotronic Supercapacitor Multiblock.

With your new HV mixer you can make lapotron dust. Place it in an autoclave to make some raw lapotron crystals. With an EV assembler and advanced circuits you can make lapotron crystals which store up to 10 million EU.
For your quantum armor you need some quantum crystals. Place a lapotron crystal in your precision laser to get a quantum crystal. You'll still need to be in IV to make it though.
Mixing better alloys needs a better Mixer.

The Avaritia 9x9 dire crafting table...is no longer used to make rockets :(. But you can still make it, if you want solars, kinetics, or whatnot. First of all you need 81 crafting tables to make a double compressed crafting table, a few HV components, wafers and a crystal matrix. And yes, you do need that many nether stars.

After hours of hard work and a few stacks of TNT your first rocket is finally ready. But before you can go to the Moon you need to actually craft it.

[note]If you've crafted the rocket with a chest, there's a crafting table recipe that will turn it into the normal rocket that completes this quest. Check NEI.[/note]

[note]Holding the rocket in your hand will unlock all pre-requisite quests in addition to this one. This also works for all of the following rockets.[/note]
Each rocket needs a Control Computer, appropriate to the tier of the rocket.
Rockets require heavy duty plates for the main hull. Let's craft 37 of these plates out of compressed aluminium plates, compressed bronze plates and compressed steel plates.
Every rocket needs a nose cone.
Every rocket needs a few rocket fins.
Every rocket needs a rocket engine. Better craft two, because the Moon lander also needs one.
The Moon lander is required for a soft landing. You will need an additional frequency module for hearing things on planets, and a second seat for a Moon buggy you may build later.
The buggy seat is part of the Moon lander.

The frequency Module will help you hear sounds properly while in space (it's also used with the telemetry unit so that your buddies can keep track of you from your base, if you are playing with friends). You need it in your inventory and in the Moon lander.
Every rocket needs fuel storage canisters. For the tier 1 rocket you need to craft two of them.

Every rocket needs a launch pad. Build a 3x3 launch pad and place your rocket on top of it.

Storms and other events that affect entities can knock your rocket off (but not lightning warp anymore), so make sure to not leave it alone.

[warn]Before liftoff, make sure you clear the airspace above you![/warn]

Be sure to check out [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Moon_Travel_Checklist[/url] for a Departure Checklist!

[note]Also note that they emit pollution, lots of it. So either put it far from your base, or use a scrubber while launching. You probably won't have to worry until T4 or so though.[/note]

To pump fuel into your rocket you need a fuel loader. Place it next to any side of the launch pad. The green side is for energy, while the yellow is for fuel. Pipe it in if you don't want to lose your cells.

You can also power it with batteries, if you're worried about it draining your power, or don't want to set up the infrastructure.

[note]Rockets keep their fuel in them on landing now, so you don't need to take this with you anymore unless you want to go to multiple places in one trip. Or you didn't fill it all the way or something.[/note]
Oxygen gear is used to attach oxygen tanks to the oxygen mask. This is absolutely vital for any astronaut.
The oxygen mask is part of the system used to breathe on planets without oxygen, the others being oxygen gear and oxygen tanks.

The Light oxygen tank is an oxygen storage tank that can hold up to 1000 units of air. It is used to provide a portable source of oxygen while in areas that do not have an oxygen source of their own.

Usage:
Up to two oxygen tanks can be worn at a time. To wear any type of oxygen tank, open your inventory and click on the Galacticraft tab at the top of the menu. Here you will see the available spots for your various types of equipment. Simply place your tank(s) in one of the slots with a gray picture of an oxygen tank. Other types of oxygen tanks include the medium oxygen tank, which holds twice the amount of oxygen as a light tank, and the heavy oxygen tank, which holds three times the amount of a light tank.

Can be found between Y 5-60 either as "Copper Ore" or "Chalcopyrite". Most of the time you'll find it together with "Iron" and "Pyrite".

To see where an ore can be found, click the raw ore in NEI, and it will show you more details. Works with small ores too.

With iron tools, you are able to mine most of the Overworld ores. You've probably already found iron or magnetite, given how common it is. So bring me some ores and make some iron ingots out of them.

To see where an ore can be found, click the raw ore in NEI, and it will show you more details. Works with small ores too.

For every flight the rocket needs some fuel. So refine some fuel for your rocket.
This quest chain will guide you through the progression of rocket fuels.

For your T1 & T2 rockets you have 2 options. You can either use Cetane-Boosted Diesel or make RP-1 rocket fuel.

For the moon, a full rocket leaving from the Overworld should have enough fuel left to make it back, but you might want to take extra just in case.

[note]Rocket Fuel usage is not based on the destination nor the type of fuel used. Rather, it is based on the tier of the rocket, with higher tiers both storing more fuel, and consuming less. Also, the gravity of the planet affects how much fuel is used, with lower gravity locations using less fuel to launch.[/note]

The oxygen collector is a block that gathers oxygen from leaves and farm plants to use in an oxygen bubble distributor, oxygen sealer, oxygen compressor, and other oxygen-reliant machines. If you plan to build a Moon base, which needs a continuous oxygen supply, you will need to build one.

The oxygen compressor is used to fill empty or depleted oxygen tanks. Connect an oxygen pipe to the blue ring input side and a power source to the gray square input side. Place an oxygen tank in the bottom right slot and it will take oxygen from the input and place it into the tank.

A parachute is used to prevent death upon re-entry into the Overworld's atmosphere. The parachute is an essential part of your journey to space. You should never journey into space without it. There will even be a warning if you try to launch without one on you.

Use the assembler to save materials.
The advanced wafer is used for more advanced machines such as the advanced solar panel or the Avaritia dire crafting table. It is also used in the creation of a space station.
The basic wafer is used for creating basic machines such as the basic solar panel, the fuel loader, the energy storage module and the compressor.

The warp you have accumulated over time is starting to become a problem. Making bath salts to clean off the warp is only a temporary solution. To truly get rid of it, you need something more powerful, a pure tear. If you collect a few things for me, I will give you one. Think wisely about using it, since it's a very long journey to unlock it through research.

§3PS: You need an LuV-powered EBF for the osmiridium.
For every circuit you need a circuit board. Craft a coated circuit board and use copper wire to finish it.

Every basic circuit needs two resistors to work.

There are better versions you can make later.

[note]You can also use slime, blood, or glue instead of Sticky Resin![/note]

The diode requires gallium arsenide, and you may be wondering how to get gallium or arsenic this early in the game.

Sphalerite and zinc are the primary sources of gallium at this tier.

You can find sphalerite in sulfur veins at Y 5-20, and the small zinc ores in the Overworld or the Nether at Y 80-210. You won't find much on the Overworld because of obvious reasons. To get additional zinc crushed ore drops, use a Tinker's Construct tool with the Luck (Fortune) enchant on it, probably the best use for all that lapis you got while looking for calcite. Or use a miner, if you don't mind how slow it is.

- Sphalerite can be electrolyzed for a small chance of a gallium dust. Better put in a lot or you might get unlucky.
- Zinc crushed ore can be washed and then thermal centrifuged or forge hammered and then centrifuged. But you don't always get the crushed ore as a drop, the impure dust doesn't give gallium.

You can get arsenic from realgar small ores in the Nether at Y 15-85. Centrifuge the dusts in a centrifuge.

Other sources are Tinker's Construct cobalt ore in the nether and cobaltite ore in the Twilight Forest. You can use your EBF for that. You also need to level up your pickaxe to ardite or make an Ironwood Pickaxe or LV Miner to harvest cobalt ore.

Another way to get gallium and arsenic is with XP buckets in a crafting grid if you're really desperate.

With your EBF you can combine these two dusts to make a Gallium Arsenide Crystal.

Advanced circuits need integrated logic circuits and random access memory chips.
You can get those by cutting the ILC and RAM wafers.

Finally, the HV circuit! To make it, you need good integrated circuits, RAM, an integrated logic circuit, and transistors.

By the way, circuits get cheaper to make as you go along, but not till HV.

Don't you hate having to manually compress all those tiny piles? Well, let me show you how to automate that. A combination of type filter, chest buffer (or super buffer in HV) and packager frees you from that annoying task. The chest buffer can hold up to 9 stacks of tiny piles and the super buffer can hold 256 stacks of tiny dusts, which is more than enough. You can set its mode with a screwdriver on the output side. Set it to 9 to export 9 tiny piles at a time and let the packager compress these into regular dusts.

[note]When you unlock them, Super buffers can be lag sources, so be careful to keep them as empty as possible. If you end up using a multiblock packager, be sure to change the buffer from Stocking mode to Transfer Size mode.[/note]

You can crack and distill a lot of different fluids out of your already distilled products, such as Butane, Butene, Butadiene, Benzene, Ethane, Ethylene, Helium, Hydrogen, Methane, Octane, Propane, Propene, Toluene, and even more Light Fuel, Heavy Fuel, or Naphtha. You can then crack them down even further too sometimes. Many of these are only used for power. Go check out the spreadsheet for more details than this quest can encompass.

For now, get some Butane and Propane.
Bio diesel and diesel can be boosted using tetranitromethane. Ethenone and nitric acid are required to make tetranitromethane in a chemical reactor.
Methane gas has a burn value of 104,000 EU per cell and can be burned in the Gas Turbine.
Methanol has a burn value of 84,000 EU per cell and can be used to make Bio Diesel and other fluids. It's also used to make certain rocket fuels.
Ethanol has a burn value of 192,000 EU per cell can be used to make Bio Diesel and other fluids.

With Ethanol or Methanol and Seed Oil or Fish Oil you can make Bio Diesel. Its burn value is 320,000 EU per cell, less than regular Diesel, but more renewable. Diesel or Bio Diesel are needed for Cetane-Boosted Diesel.

Oxygen can be made in lots of different ways. Most commonly you'll either electrolyze it out of cassiterite sand, sugar from sugar canes or sugar beets, water, or various other oxygen-rich dusts, or centrifuge it from brown or yellow limonite dust.

Later on, water electrolyzing or air centrifuging is probably going to be your main source.

You can make ethylene several different ways

- Ethanol and sulfuric acid in an MV Chemical Reactor
- Ethanol in a Chemical Dehydrator
- Distilling various gases (i.e. wood gas) in a Distillery
- Obtain it from Oil in the Working with Oil tab

[note]You will need much more than 12 cells later on so keep that in mind.[/note]

Pam's peanuts are a good seed oil source, and can be sped up with sprinklers. Or you can use CropsNH Canola (the best option). Another option is Forestry tree nuts such as Hazelnuts, Butternuts, or the King of nuts, coconuts. Or you can be lame and get them from regular seeds like wheat seeds.

Sodium hydroxide is needed for bio diesel. You can make it out of sodium and water, or out of salt water.

Sodium hydroxide is also used in advanced aluminium production.

Hopefully you saved some sulfuric acid. If not, make some more. Together with acetic acid you can make ethenone.

Save the ethenone for HV, you'll need it to make tetranitromethane for cetane boosted diesel.
Nitric acid can be made out of water, oxygen and nitrogen dioxide.

Acetic acid can be made out of Oxygen and Ethylene. Alternatively, it can be made out of Biomass, Wood Vinegar or Vinegar. It is an important part of making Ethenone on your way to Cetane-Boosted Diesel.
To make nitrogen dioxide you need to combine oxygen gas and nitric oxide in a chemical reactor.
Nitrogen and hydrogen... Ammonia.
To make nitric oxide you need to combine oxygen and ammonia in a chemical reactor.
Use your Formaldehyde to make 1,1-Dimethylhydrazine. You need to combine it with some Hydrazine and Hydrogen along with a Formaldehyde Catalyst in a Chemical Plant.
Combining Oxygen and Methanol along with a Formaldehyde Catalyst in a Chemical Plant produces some Formaldehyde.

I need some ingredients to help me train since they don't grow well where I am, could you provide some? I'll give you the results in return.

[note]You only need to turn in one set each time you complete the quest.[/note]
You'll need this for epichlorohydrin.
You just need to cool down those ingots in your Vacuum Freezer and you'll get your first Titanium.
Tungstensteel is needed in all machines for the next tier. Can you get enough to advance?

Since vanilla bows are only craftable in the assembling machine and mobs don't drop them very often you should make a Tinkers bow.

Wood would be the best material for now. Craft the bow limbs out of wood and the bow string out of strings. The arrow that has the most durability is bone, so craft the stick out of bone. It is much lighter but less durable than a regular arrow. Use a flint tip to make it repairable with flint.

You can repair your bow the same way as all the other Tinkers tools. The arrows can be regained by repairing them or picking them up from the floor. The arrows should be in your inventory if you want to pick up the ones you fired.
The bronze javelin is a bit expensive and has only 7 throws, yet it is a good mid-range weapon. With one bronze ingot you can replenish your stack of javelins.

Is the bone bow too expensive for your taste? Then make a flint throwing knife instead. You need flint and a stick to get 12 knives. The durability and the attack damage are very low but it still helps with killing mobs from a safe distance.

The knives should be in your inventory if you want to pick up the ones you fired.

If you're lucky enough to spawn near a sand- or rainforest biome, you can find some quicksand.

Collect a stack of it, dig a small ditch, and fill it with the quicksand to protect your "dirt base" home. Just don't fall in!

All the different mining veins that have been found seem to be really far apart. One way to shorten the travel time is to create a railroad from your base to the different mines. Sadly this requires a large amount of both iron and creosote. Let's not forget to place the last symbolic rivet on one of your new train lines.

In order to make your bricked blast furnace you need to find a lapis vein containing calcite.

You can find the vein in the overworld at Y 20-50.

To make bricks for the blast furnace you need concrete and gypsum. Gypsum can be found in a vein together with basaltic and granitic mineral sand, and fullers earth. Y 50-60 and only in the overworld.

Do you need flawless or exquisite diamonds, emeralds, rubies or other gems? Or, interested in getting more flint, coal, or whatnot out of your ore? Well then it's time for you to make a Sifting Machine.

You can find small Zinc ores (look in NEI) or you can search the Nether for Sphalerite.

The Sifter only takes Purified ores, but you can get these easily by throwing Crushed ores into a Cauldron with water.

[note]Note that you need Polyethylene to make this machine![/note]

Smelting up to eight items at once sounds nice? With a bit of bronze & steel you can make a §5§lSteam Hearth§r for all your furnace needs!

Aside from having §2§l8x§r the parallels and §2§l25%§r more speed, it's also significantly less steam intensive (per parallel) than the High Pressure Steam Furnace. Not only that, but depending on your input you can further increase your speed bonus by taking advantage of two special modes: §cBlasting§r and §9Smoking§r.

In §cBlast Mode§r, the Steam Hearth will smelt at §2§l2x§r speed & use §4§l2x§r steam for all §nmetals§r, just like with the §5EFR Blast Furnace§r. 

In §9Smoke Mode§r, the Steam Hearth will smelt at §2§l2x§r speed & use §4§l2x§r steam for all §nfood-based recipes§r, just like with the §5EFR Smoker§r.

Upgrading this multiblock to its §6High Pressure§r variant also gives §2§l2x§r speed & §4§l2x§r steam usage.

[note]You can use a screwdriver to quickly swap between modes on the machine![/note]

After you can make steel and have a tinkers smelter you can make molds. Molds can be used in the alloy smelter and the fluid solidifier. You need them to make vacuum tubes, ingots, gears and more.

[note]PS: The 'shapes' are for the Extruder.[/note]

Iron (III) Chloride can be made by first making hydrochloric acid out of hydrogen and chlorine. Then combine this with some iron dust to make Iron(III) Chloride.
You can etch your board with it.
Sodium Persulfate can be made in the electrolyzer out of sodium bisulfate dust. Sodium bisulfate is made out of sulfuric acid and salt in the chemical reactor. You can etch your board with it.
Do you like flying? Ok then, make a slimy bouncepad and enjoy the view.

Rubber trees are not the only source for raw rubber. Go and find a slime island high in the sky. Slime balls and slime leaves give raw rubber too.
Make some slime tree farms beside your rubber farm.

§3Liquid slime is not allowed to be placed down, as it acts as a spawner, and can cause lag.

Tired of using small cells to process chemicals? Build a Large Chemical Reactor and you can just pipe in and out fluids. Or use the glorious large fluid cells to deliver and remove fluids from the hatches.

You can decide if the reactor should void any extra products when the outputs are full or not by toggling the void mode in the GUI!

There are also recipes specific to only the LCR, sometimes even allowing you to skip a step, so keep your eyes open for that.

Additionally, as a multiblock, LCR also counts as a cleanroom for any cleanroom recipes.

You will also need:
1 Maintenance Hatch
1-2 Energy Hatches
0+ Input Bus (if a recipe has an item input. For full automation, you should probably use 1 for each material)
0-1 Output Bus (if a recipe has an item output)
2+ Input Hatch (use 1 for every fluid)
1+ Output Hatch (same as above)

You can use a screwdriver on an output hatch to cycle through its modes. Use shift-right-click to go directly to specific fluid mode, then lock the fluid with a cell for easier automation. This works on more than just the LCR.

[note]You can use any type of coil to form the structure, but there is no benefit accrued from using higher tiers.[/note]

A scepter is crafted from a wand core, a primal charm, three wand caps, a twilight forest monster mob drop, and some screws. Any sort of core or cap may be used, but the caps must match each other. A scepter cannot hold a focus, but holds 150 percent as much vis as a wand with the same core, and gives an additional 10 percent discount for costs, beyond any discounts from its caps or the user's worn equipment.

This is ideal for all your crafting needs and to progress further!

[note]There are multiple ways to get enough vis capacity to craft the scepter. If you are not yet able to make it, maybe first work on Fusion and make yourself some boots with better discounts.[/note]

A staff requires an extra step for crafting: Two (matching) wand cores must be combined with a primal charm, and crystal clusters to produce a staff core. (While the recipes are all similar, each type of staff core requires a separate research topic to be learned.)

With your new 50 vis wand you are able to make a Scepter which holds up to 75 vis.
First you need some primal charms which cost 50 vis to craft.

Join the core with two wand caps, a twilight forest mob drop, and screws just as for making a wand. A staff cannot be used for crafting, but holds 2.5x as much vis as a corresponding wand. It can even serve as a backup weapon for melee. While it cannot receive weapon enchantments, its damage is decent, and it does not take damage with use (no durability bar).
betterquesting:10.name:8: A Wizard's Staff Has a Knob on the End

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
This is the first GT-type tank. It stores 32 buckets or 32,000L, and can be used to I/O cells. The ULV Tank from GT++ needs steel plates, iron plates, tin plates, a clay pipe, and a water bucket.

GT tanks do not auto-output. If you want to move fluids out of the tank, use a GT pump, conduit, or something similar.
The next version of GT tanks stores 64,000L in a tank. It actually requires a pump this time, so it's a little expensive. Consider staying with your ULV ones if you only need basic I/O.
These store 128,000L. The dark steel plates and LV pump make it a little annoying to make, since it needs an EBF.
The second item you'll need a lot of in MV tier. When you want to get fluid out of tanks you'll want one, though you don't necessarily need an MV one.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lYou're Gonna Hate This in MV Too #2

betterquesting:10.desc:8: This one stores 256,000L. The ULV circuits make it annoying to craft, so make them only if you need them. This is the last of the Voltage Tier ones, after this is the Super Tanks, which you can actually make right now.
The first item you'll need a lot of in MV too. If you want to pull items out of chests or barrels you'll need one. Way faster than the LV one, so it's actually useful.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lYou're Gonna Hate This in MV Too #1

betterquesting:10.desc:8: An electric piston for your MV machines. The third item you're going to craft a lot of in the future.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lYou're Gonna Hate This in MV Too #3

betterquesting:10.desc:8: The fourth item you'll need a lot of in MV, which is still a pain to craft.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lYou're Gonna Hate This in MV Too #4

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Too lazy to make an ore washer, yet bored with your non-automatable cauldron? Then the simple washer is the machine for you! It works much faster than a normal ore washer. Of course, you don't get any byproducts, but who cares!

There are simple washers for every tier up to UV, but the speed doesn't increase much past the HV version.
Bad things may happen if this creature is allowed to stay alive. The ores in its cave being valuable have nothing to do with why you need to kill it. Seriously.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Don't Look it in the Eyes!

betterquesting:10.desc:8: OK so there is this maze. And there are... minotaurs. But what in the world is a minoshroom?

Required for your first wand, and in general, an ugly creature.

[note]To progress in TF, you need to follow the achievements. They can be finicky, so make sure to check if you got the achievement each time. If not, try to drop and pickup everything that dropped from the bosses.[/note]

[note]If you have problems completing the quest, you can also use the Spawn Eggs from the Vending Machine to try again.[/note]
Stop him before he makes his wish at Prismo's!
Phantom Busters! Or wait... Ah whatever. They drop good armor by the way.
It flies, it makes funny sounds, and... IT'S SO FLUFFY! Well, kill it.

It seems the cold doesn't bother her. Committed crimes: None. But... you know... you have to progress somehow...

[note]PS: Keep going.[/note]

Wanted: Alpha Yeti, Dead.
Committed crimes: Violently throwing ice at people, for no reason.

Hey, you! I want that lamp. I have something for you in return. You don't need it anyways, do you?

[note]If you want the TF achievement, get that first.[/note]

Who hasn't experienced this...? You're just minding your own business, mining a few diamonds, and suddenly, you wake up in your bed, all your items gone.

Time to strike back!
"Zombie Pigman"? What the hell is going on with you zombies?! Maybe you should encase your animals better at night...
Eeeek! Wall climbing monsters, gross! Slay them. Quickly! Watch out for the witch spiders, they can give as good as they get.

Arrows are nice, if you shoot them. If one hits you, well, bad things happen.

Hint: Arrows are an excellent source of telum.
You should be careful with this task. Fire protection is highly recommended.
Nobody knows who they are, or where they came from. They're just annoying at night, and too stupid to make a crafting table.

Uh, fancy teleport pearls. You need them. All of them. Now!

[note]PS: Top is regular enderman, bottom is special mob's version. Complete one set. Blame SM for their method of creating new endermen types for this. HEE ones like angry don't count.[/note]

After collecting a couple of those wither skeleton heads, you feel like you could use some more action. So why not kill a wither? You'll need a ton of nether stars anyway...

Kill it twice for something nice.
You have been busy my friend. I have something for you. Give me your hearts, and I will magically enhance them so you can actually use them.

In order to advance to a higher tier and reach Mars, Deimos and Phobos, you need to make yourself a better rocket. There are rumors that an Evolved Skeleton hiding out on the Moon has the schematics of such a device.

Not that regular creepers are nasty enough, no. There is an evolved creeper boss! He is your key (Well he HAS a key...) to reach the next tier of planets (Asteroid Belt, Ceres, Io, Europa, Ganymede, Callisto).
In order to proceed to Tier 4 Planets, the blaze boss needs to be killed. Find him in one of the dungeons on Ceres.
Fluffy, fluffier, ghasts! And also big crybabies. This one hides in a dungeon on IO, and holds the key for Tier 5 planets.
Seriously, a crystal boss? Anyway, it's your key to Tier 6 planets, and he lurks around on Enceladus.
Totally looks like a thaumic slime to me. Don't you think so? Find this dude on Proteus.
The final frontier... A... wolf that is not even an Iron Maiden fan?... What did you expect, a super boss? Heh. No. The budget was too tight...
I guess you're good at killing things, huh? And if you got this far, maybe making things too?

To make your altar more powerful you need to upgrade it. Add another ring of Blood Runes with a two-high pillar of blood-soaked thaumium blocks at each corner. Top each of the pillars with a block of glowstone.

View the structure preview in NEI or visit [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Blood_Altar[/url] for images on how it should look.

If you want to make tier 4 slates you need a Tier 4 altar. This can be made like the tier 3 altar with pillars out of void-blood-soaked stones four blocks high and a blood brick on top of the pillars.

If you want to make tier 5 slates you need a Tier 5 altar. This can be made with 4 beacons. Beacons have thaumcraft recipes and can be found in the thaumcraft book on the GTNH page. The quest is most of the way through adept thaumaturgy.
The highest tier of the blood altar is tier 6. You need pillars of blood-soaked ichorium 7 blocks high and on top the crystal cluster blocks made out of demon soul shards.

Automatic mining in LV tier? Wow! This nifty machine will collect ores for you, which can be helpful especially in the Nether, as it won't anger pigmen.

Place up to two stacks of mining pipes in the right slots. Each pipe can go 1 block, and allow the miner to dig 1 block further. If you're above Y64, you may need to pipe more in.

This machine only needs 8 EU/t to work, so LV batteries in a batbuff work OK if you don't want to make another generator.

The miner searches for ores in a 17x17 block work area (adjustable with a screwdriver), and comes with a level 1 fortune bonus! Great for gathering additional small ores!

Don't forget to cover it up! These are GT machines, so remember to protect them (and their power sources!) from rain on all sides. And set a waypoint with JourneyMap so you don't forget where you placed it if you place it far away! You'll need to chunkload the miner if you want it to keep working when you're not there.

The MV miner will find ores for you faster than the LV miner, and in a larger range. It also has a larger fortune bonus, great for gathering small ores in the Nether. Plus it's faster, but I'm sure you figured that.

The HV miner is faster, has longer range, and has more fortune than the previous two. If you want a better one, look in the multiblock tab. It's recommended to take one with you to the Moon to gather meteoric iron.

Now it's time to invest in some renewable energy. Let's start with solar panels. The basic one only gives 1 EU/t. Most GT machines can use them as covers, and receive power, but only so long as it can see the sun (the top). Be sure to put a glass layer above them in case it rains while you swap panels. You'll still want to keep rain off the sides of the machine hull too.

[note]The Aluminium Iron plate needs an MV Forming Press.[/note]
The next solar panel you can make is the ULV one. It generates 8 EU/t.
Put those single EU panels on a block to make them placeable in the world. Use an MV assembler to combine the panel with a ULV hull.
The next solar panel you can make is the LV one. It generates 32 EU/t.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lPower of the Sun at LV Level

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Put those 32 EU panels on a block to make them placeable in the world. Use an MV assembler to combine the panel with an LV hull, a battery, and a robot arm. Now this panel will clean itself!

If you're tired of crafting tons of tree taps, how about a machine that uses power but never breaks? Let's craft an electric tree tap!

If you're looking for better ways to get Sticky Resin, you might want to consider the Sticky Cane crop. For more information, check the crop quests.
Your hoe must be getting worn out by now. Why not craft an electric one which never breaks?

If you want to make more advanced (and cheaper!) circuits, you will need a Cleanroom. The Cleanroom is an interesting multiblock, because you will be placing other machines §oinside§r of the room!

The cleanroom is a hollow multiblock between 3x4x3 and 15x15x15 (WxHxL) blocks. The base does not need to be a square; a rectangular shape is fine. The top layer is built out of Filter Machine Casings, except for the edges, which are Plascrete Blocks. The controller needs to be in the center of the top layer. If the width or length of the room are even, then it can be any one of the two (or four) middle blocks. The rest of the structure is built out of Plascrete Blocks.
