Up to 30% of those Plascrete Blocks can be replaced by other valid blocks or materials:

A Reinforced Door lets you get in and out of the cleanroom. Make sure to keep the doors closed, or the cleanroom will rapidly lose efficiency. Travel Anchors and Elevators also work, you can even embed them in the floor if you want to. You can also use Ineffable Glass as a "door" if you'd prefer.

In order to automate power and item transport through the walls, you can use Cable Diodes or Machine Hulls. Just be really careful when upgrading your machines to a higher voltage. Be sure to remove the machine hulls and diodes and replace them with the new power tier, or else you will be very sad. You don't need to do this for ones you only use to pass items through.

If you want to see inside, you can use any EV+ tier glass (for example, Reinforced Glass, Managlass, or Ineffable Glass). If the Cleanroom does not form, mind the 30% limit: often the problem is that you added too much glass.

Finally, the Cleanroom itself will need a Maintenance and Energy Hatch to run. The power usage of this multiblock is a bit unusual. It starts out at 40 EU/t and then gradually goes down. But even when it uses 40 EU/t - which is usually MV - a single LV energy hatch suffices, because it accepts two amps of LV power. Just keep in mind that this makes the Cleanroom an exception, not the rule.

Let's build a 5x5x5 room for now. You can expand it later as needed. Give it power and let it run until it reaches 100% efficiency. Below 100% efficiency, machines inside the cleanroom have a chance to void outputs, so you want to keep the cleanroom running at all times!

Any maintenance issue reduces the maximum efficiency by 10%. Monitor your cleanroom manually with Waila or automatically with either an Industrial Information Panel or a Needs Maintenance Cover connected to a Redstone Powered Light or Howler Alarm.

[note]Multiblocks such as the Large Chemical Reactor or Hyper-Intensity Laser Engraver don't need to be in a cleanroom. However, you will still need the cleanroom later on for other machines, like Bio Labs.[/note]

[note]Other helpful hints: you can use an AE Wireless Connector or a Transvector Interface for item transport to avoid machine hulls, and use a higher tier energy hatch to reach 100% efficiency faster.[/note]

[warn]Keep in mind that you can not use anything in the cleanroom that causes pollution, or the cleanroom will stop working.[/warn]

The portable scanner is a tool capable of showing advanced information about almost every block in the game. In order to function, the tool needs to be charged first. It can hold up to 400k EU and accept 128 EU/t or less. This is MV tier.

It can scan crops by right-clicking them.

It can scan machines from GregTech, giving information about current progress, the stored energy, efficiency, problems and CPU-load - be sure to check the full chat window for additional details.

For any block in the game it scans, it gives information about its ID, Metadata, position in the world and hardness value. It also gives information about pollution level in the chunk the scanned block belongs to.

In addition it shows when the cleanroom has reached its 100 percent efficiency level.

The Plunger is used to clear liquids from pipes. It can also be used on a machine to remove up to 1000mb of fluid from its internal buffer. So you don't have to wrench your machine and re-place it. It can be crafted from a rod of the desired material and rubber sheets.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §c§lIt's a Dirty Job, and You're Going to Do It

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
There are a number of chemical recipes that are unlocked with an §5HV Chemical Reactor§r; you will finally be able to make Ender Eyes, Ammonia, Gelled Toluene, and plenty of other useful components. 

Alternatively, if you're up for it, you can head over to the Mass Processing tab and build yourself a §5Large Chemical Reactor§r (LCR) instead! In addition to having a more efficient overclock, the LCR can input multiple liquids so you won't need to mess with those pesky cells any longer. 

[note]If you choose to go the LCR route, be sure to take a look at the PTFE questline just ahead of this one, starting with "Teflon Don".[/note]

[note]P.S. You can skip any of the following rubber/plastic questlines by holding 128 of the respective sheets in your hand![/note]

This tank works the same as the smaller GT tanks, but holds way more. Specifically, 4,000,000L. Only make this for things you need tons of, LV circuits are expensive after all.

Now you can store the same amount of fluids a steel 5x5 Railcraft tank contains in a single block.

[note]A lot of nice functionality has been added to Super and Quantum tanks. You can now pick them up with a wrench without voiding the fluids! Super tanks (but not Quantum) will give you heavy debuffs though, so better prepare some milk.

If you actually want to void the fluids you can crouch while using the wrench.

They now also have optional automatic fluid output, fluid locking, overflow void mode, or full void mode. And all that with a nice and simple GUI. Quite the IMPACTful change I would say.[/note]

Making paper out of wood pulp and water can be tedious and difficult. Why not use a mortar to grind the sugar cane into chad and press it with two stone slabs to paper? Later on you can use the chemical bath for an even better ratio.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §a§lChad - A Better Way to Make Paper

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Maybe you're lucky and started in a bamboo forest. Bamboo is a very useful tree since it grows really fast and when you break the bottom-most block, the whole thing comes apart.

You can use them as sticks, or you can place the bamboo sticks to grow and make a three-block-tall wall to protect your base. You can also use Berry Bushes for that, assuming you don't want to spend materials on fences.

An early game protection moat can be made out of punji sticks. It hurts all mobs/players and additionally gives a slowness II potion effect. Make a trench around your base and put the punji sticks inside.

But not as good as steel. Mostly, this is used in machine hulls, or in tools if you don't want to use steel up for that.

To make Cast Iron, you either need to use a Tinkers' Smeltery to melt some Iron Ingots down and cast them into Iron Nuggets, or use an Iron Ingot and a saw to craft Iron Nuggets. Then put these in a furnace to get Cast Iron Nuggets. With the Compressor, you can compress the nuggets into ingots.

§3Hint: Crushed or purified iron ore (not a mixed version like pyrite; look for Iron Ore in Chalcopyrite veins) can be smelted directly into iron nuggets. 

You can optionally use an Alloy Smelter to turn iron ingots into nuggets faster than a smeltery. 

Later on, you can use an Arc Furnace to make Cast Iron Ingots directly.

Use molds to make plates, sticks, bolts and many more item parts in the fluid solidifier.

Molds are != to Extruder shapes. You're gonna need 2 sets. If they're too expensive, just make the most important ones for now.

Keeping a base spread apart for pollution or explosion prevention can really wear you out, so why not make some concrete to get around faster?

Harvest some Marble and centrifuge it into Calcite, and mix up some concrete in your Mixer. Next output it into a Fluid Solidifier with a block mold to make concrete blocks.

You'll move faster on top of these blocks. They can even be turned into bricks to prevent unwanted spawns! Hint: 10 buckets of wet mix converts to exactly 160 blocks. These blocks can also be Chiseled into different varieties.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §2§lBase Too Big? I've Got a Fix For You!

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Dark steel pipes are much better than the bronze, steel, or potin pipes you might have been using. Make sure your wrench can handle mining level 3 or you can't deconstruct them.

[note]If you don't need these, just recycle them to get the materials back. Not everything needs ginormous pipes or high heat tolerance.[/note]
After entering the HV age you've found a way of making a water reservoir which solves the finite water problem. Craft it with some fused quartz glass, HV pumps, and cauldrons.

Tired of standing around to collect all the drops and XP from your diamond spikes?

Make yourself a vacuum hopper to suck up all the drops and XP. Feed the XP into a tank to store it.
The first step to brew beer or other alcoholic fluids is wheaty juice.

If you want brews or alcohol, I recommend you to build one of these. You might have noticed that you cannot build a brewing stand without Thaumcraft. But fear not, you can still find them in secret rooms on the first floor of some roguelike dungeons or ur-ghast towers. Better get searching...
What's better than lame brews? Alcoholic brews! Get one of these to make beer, rum or even vodka.
Jägermeister is a common drink in Germany, why don't you grab a bottle? This one seems to be a cheap fake tho...
Some machines need Emitters and Sensors, like the Scanner or the Circuit Assembler.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §5§lYou're Gonna Hate This 5 and 6 in HV

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Ender eyes are available at HV in the chemical reactor. Combine some ender pearls with blaze powder.

Epoxid circuit boards require an epoxid plate, gold foil and sulfuric acid to make an empty board. By adding electrum foil and Iron(III) Chloride or Sodium Persulfate you can craft an Advanced Circuit Board.

[note]If you used IC2 Scrap Boxes to obtain the empty boards instead of using epoxy, hold 64 Advanced Circuit Boards in your hand to unlock this quest.[/note]

The Microprocessor is the highest tier version of the LV circuit, getting you 2 per recipe.

In addition to what's listed, you'll need 2 Resistors, Transistors, and Capacitors, SMD or non-SMD.

This advanced circuit type needs a cleanroom.

NOR, NAND and other high tier chips require an HV cutting machine.

[note]You'll soon find that everything you cut needs a cleanroom, so make sure you start on that.[/note]

To make more advanced wafers, you need to make phosphorus doped monocrystalline silicon first. The process takes a while, so make sure you have stable power.

You can also get more wafers, and thus more chips out of higher tier boules. You still need to make the lower tier ones sometimes though.

There are many different ways to source Phosphorus, you can process ores like Apatite or Tricalcium Phosphate. You may also consider centrifuging ashes if you use a benzene setup, extracting it from combs if you use bees, or obtaining it from the Fertilia crop. Remember to be prudent when searching through NEI!
To create some phosphorus doped silicon wafers, cut them in a cutting machine. An HV version of the cutting machine is needed for future wafers and chips.

NAND is used for data sticks, data orbs, and UV circuits. NOR chips are needed for data orbs and LuV circuits. You can get these by cutting NAND and NOR wafers. Just worry about the data sticks for now.
Data sticks are very important for seismic prospecting and for the assembly line in the LuV age. Go and craft a few data sticks.

Radon is needed for EV emitters and sensors.

If you can get some Plutonium 239 and Uranium 238, you can use the chemical reactor recipe and keep cycling the Plutonium around to get more.

Using the LCR recipe is recommended, as it is more efficient and faster due to the LCR being able to perform 4/4 OC.

An EV chemical reactor is required to get some indium or make your radon production much faster. If you already made a large chemical reactor use that instead.

[note]Either reactor will complete the quest.[/note]
For impure radioactive ores for your nuclear reactor, you can look for pitchblende and uraninite. You can find them on Mars and Phobos at Y 30-60.

You can find several other ores on these planets (some of which actually don't have a use, honestly), but the most useful right now are probably the ones on the right. There's also Draconium, Jade, Mirabilite, Tanzanite, Vinteum, and Vyroxes.
Pumps, pistons, conveyor modules and robot arms are the most needed machine parts in EV. Go and craft one of each.
Some machines need Emitters and Sensors, like the Scanner or the Circuit Assembler.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §8§lYou're Gonna Hate This 5 and 6 in EV

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Quantum eyes are required in EV emitters and sensors. Just infuse your ender eye with radon to get one.
This is the Nano Processor circuit line. Similar to the previous circuit line, these are four circuits. The §onano§r circuits go all the way to the LuV-tier Nano Mainframe.
The NanoCPU Wafer is made out of a CPU Wafer with raw carbon fiber and molten glowstone in an EV chemical reactor. Cut it for nano CPU chips.
The Nano Assembly is an EV circuit.
The Nano Supercomputer is an IV circuit.
An HV chemical bath or better is needed for the quantum eye. If you make an EV one you can also process Ilmenite better.

Second largest vanilla storage component, used to make 16k ME storage cells, or can be upgraded to make 64k ME storage components. Can be recovered from a crafted 16k ME storage cell by fully emptying the storage cell, and shift-clicking it in your hand.
Component of the crafting CPU which provides 16,384 bytes of storage for crafting.

Highest tier storage cell, which can contain 65,536 bytes of storage. 65,536 bytes of storage can hold 8,128 stacks of a single item, or 4,160 stacks, while holding 63 different items. The 64k storage cell uses 512 bytes of data to store a single type.

When placed inside a drive or chest will consume 2.0 ae/t.
Largest vanilla storage component, used to make 64k ME storage cells. Can be recovered from a crafted 64k ME storage cell by fully emptying the storage cell, and shift-clicking it in your hand.
Component of the crafting CPU which provides 65,536 bytes of storage for crafting.
Export bus for fluids only.
Component of the crafting CPU which displays the top level job and its current progress so you can monitor at a glance how your crafting jobs are progressing.

The Nano Mainframe is the first LuV Circuit, and the end of this circuit line produced in EV. To craft the Tier 2 Rocket and reach Mars, Phobos and Deimos, you need to reach this circuit and make 8 of it.

After that, you will be able to progress into IV much more easily, but you will need two more circuits to make the IV Circuit Assembling Machine.

It's EV, OK?

[note]Make one of these.[/note]
Sunnarium batteries are made out of blue steel: a mixture of steel, black steel, brass and rose gold.
Small Sunnarium batteries are EV tier. Some might think they're cheaper than Lapotrons, but it depends on Sunnarium. And they hold less energy.
Want cheaper EV batteries? Mash your old ones together, and somehow it works!

It is possible to run MV machines while still in LV - build a transformer and use 4 power sources 32 EU/t to power one 128 EU/t machine.

It transforms power up or down, depending on the mode, which you can switch with a soft mallet. Step-up means 4A LV in, 1A MV out, while step-down means the reverse.

Make sure you understand the following if you prefer your base not being a crater:
A step-down mode is the default one. In this mode, the large dot is the input. In a step-up mode, it's the output. Do not mix it up. LV machines that receive MV power will explode.

If the transformer is connected to power, or was in the past, then do not change the mode with stuff connected. It's better to break and place it again to get rid of the stored power rather than rotate it with the wrench and blow things up. Make sure to also disconnect the nearby wires with a wire cutter.

As a reminder, machines don't blow up if they are given more amps than they can consume. They blow up from higher voltage tier.
These work the same as the LV ones, but 1 tier higher.

If you need a transformer with more than 4A you need a high amp transformer. You can input 4A MV and output 16A LV. Useful for running lots of LV machines. Its mode can be changed with a soft mallet, just like before.
If you need even more amps then craft a power transformer. This one is 16A -> 64A. The soft mallet is still how you change modes.

This tool is a combined Trowel, Hoe, and Shovel. The basic spade will allow you to easily clear weeds from your sticks, till soil, and potentially obtain bonus seeds from simply harvesting the crops (right-click) without breaking them. Each point of resistance increases the chance of getting a seed when harvesting with the basic spade as follows:

1 Resist = 3%
10 Resist = 32%
31 Resist = 100%

[note]If you're removing a crop with your spade, sneaking will let you remove the crop without having to worry about the spade breaking the crop stick.[/note]
betterquesting:10.name:8: Tools of the Trade 1 - Less Dirty Hands

betterquesting:10.desc:8: The HV Extruder is needed to extrude tough metals like Tungstensteel and HSS.

Want to use all that delicious XP to raise your levels? Move the tank with XP above you and attach this convenient shower head to take the XP from the tank.

This thing can be laggy, so be careful about letting too many XP orbs out of the tank. Apply a redstone signal to turn it off.

After a few forbidden researches your warp level has increased a bit. Do you want to know how much warp you have?

Craft some litmus paper to print out the warp level.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Did You Want to Know Your Warp Level?

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
You can build a space station if you want. You can add up to four spin thrusters to your station to rotate it.

Days on space stations last longer than on the overworld, so you can generate more solar power.

§oYou can build space stations here:§r
§21§r. Moon - §9T1
§22§r. Mars - §9T2
§23§r. Jupiter - §9T3
§24§r. Venus - §9T4
§25§r. Saturn - §9T5
§26§r. Uranus - §9T5
§27§r. Neptune - §9T6§r

Each §2Retrieval Task§r in this quest corresponds (in order) to the resources you will need in order to §2build a space station§r at one of the planets listed above. The "§9T#§r" afterwards refers to the §9tier of rocket§r you will need to get there.

[note]You will need to complete at least one task to complete this quest![/note]

[warn]It is likely that you will lose your rocket when flying back to Earth or another space station. Make sure you have an alternative way to return (some form of teleportation) or use another planet/moon as proxy (if you get an error while doing so, you spawn on the planet/moon and can launch your rocket again).[/warn]

Are you prepared for the Moon?

If you die on the moon you will be returned to earth without your stuff. A Soulbind enchantment will keep an item with you when you die.

In order to understand where you are, and where you §owant§r to be, you'll need a map. This is a magical place, so why not a magical map? The main part is a Magic Map Focus.

First, go find some Raven feathers. You can get them by killing Ravens. They like to hang out near the obsidian pillars.

Then you need some Torchberries (found underground) and some Glowstone dust.

For the magic map you need the magic map focus and a paper stack, made from a stack of paper.

It will fill in the area near you, and reveal boss locations. You need to kill these to get access to the rest of the Twilight Forest. Start with the Naga.

You can see what to do next in the TF achievement tab. There's also quests for the boss kills on the kill all the things tab. You can only get one map every 24 hours, so be careful with it.

§4Only use the map in the Twilight Forest, using the map in any other dimension will lag the server!

I have a small present for you: a Talisman of Remedium which is very useful to persevere during the dark nights with all these monsters.

First you have to prove you can survive on the moon by yourself. After mining some moon turf, dirt, and rock, you can have it.

Make sure you check back in the HV questline for necessary ores you should gather while here.

This Plate Bending Machine allows you to directly make double, triple or more compressed plates, which might be useful for your first rocket in HV Tier.

It also allows you to make dense plates at all.

You'll probably want MV battery buffers as well.

[note]You only need to make one of these battery buffers.[/note]

Better machines need some better batteries. Lithium is the best material to use when making batteries.

[note]You only need four batteries of one listed type.[/note]

Using lubricant instead of water or distilled water in your cutting machines will increase their speed.

You can make lubricant out of oil, seed oil, fish oil or creosote in a distillery (or distillation tower later on). If you're able to craft a brewery you can use talc or soapstone to get much more lubricant each cycle.

Lube cells are required to make low tier energy hatches, so stockpile a few cells and use the rest to make your cutting machine faster.

Now that you are starting to find more and more iron, you feel your copper chests are too small to hold all the stuff.

[note]Do you have copper chests that are too small? You can also upgrade with a fitting upgrade item.[/note]
Most of your berries can be extracted to juice form. This is a chance to get more food variants and the nutritional value is higher than eating the fruit directly.
Potatoes, onions, butter and a skillet make very tasty potato cakes.
So easy, skillet and an egg.... fried egg.

Now let's combine all the things together and make a healthy and delicious breakfast.

Some cooked meat, potato cakes, toast, fried egg and a tasty juice provide you with a very nourishing meal.

You can use any cooked meat and any fruit juice here.

Pumps can do more than pump oil and water. You can go to the nether and pump lava from the huge lava lakes too.

Once you reach HV, lava can be centrifuged for Silicon Dioxide, Magnesia, Quicklime, Gold, Sapphire, and Tantalite. You can get Silicon, Magnesium, Calcium, Gold, Aluminium, Manganese, Tantalum, and Oxygen out of them.

This is a good use for your LV pumps once you upgrade to MV pumps for oil. If you get into Thaumcraft or Blood Magic, there are ways to produce lava with magic unlimitedly and easily too.

[note]You'll want either ULV tanks and cells, or BC tanks and a dolly to transport your lava.[/note]
After you build a cutting machine you can make some diamond plates for your new 64,000L single block tank.

Find some Glow Flowers in the Nether and plant them in the Overworld. You will never need to go to the Nether and harvest Glowstone again.

[note]These must be planted on Soul Sand in order to grow![/note]

Did you run low on redstone and/or gold? It's no problem with a glowstone flower farm. You can centrifuge glowstone dust to redstone and gold dust. Redstone is also a good source of chrome. You'll need tons of gold for HV, so it's a good idea to set this up before then.

[note]There are actually a couple plants that produce glowstone, pick the one you like![/note]
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lDid You Run Low On Gold or Redstone?

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
After you build a cutting machine you can make some diamond plates for your new, even bigger diamond chests.

[note]Just as with the previous chests you can also upgrade with a fitting upgrade item.[/note]

If you found enough gold, you can upgrade your chest to make it an even bigger inventory of 9x9.

[note]Do you have iron chests that are too small? You can also upgrade with a fitting upgrade item.[/note]

To unlock research you need a scribing tool and paper. To do the research, you need a scribing tool and the research note you made in the research table, so you should probably make two tools.

Note: Thaumcraft Research Tweaks has reworked the research table GUI. Aspects are now combined with drag & drop between aspects in the GUI. You can also right-click while dragging the aspect instead of dropping; the same works with the hexes. All the new features are described in your Thaumonomicon, make sure to check out the 'Research', 'Research Expertise', 'Research Mastery' and 'Research Duplication' pages.

Litmus paper will tell you how high your warp level is, but how can you get rid of the nasty warp effects? Bath salt will help you by prohibiting warp effects for a short period. Just throw the salt into a 1x1 water hole and jump inside. You will feel relieved a bit after bathing.

[note]Note: The more permanent warp you have, the shorter the duration.[/note]
Bathing in a spa will automate the process of temporarily removing warp effects. Take the bath salt with you into the spa.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Bathing in a Spa. Automated Warp Removal

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
This soap is very special. It will remove temporary warp and has a small chance to also remove some normal warp, if you are lucky. Taking a bath first increases your chances.

This can later be upgraded to remove your permanent warp.

[note]Hint: You need to chisel your tallow block for the recipe to work.[/note]
Finally, with your new wand with 50 stored vis you're able to build your own enchantment table. The recipe can be found on the GTNH Tab in the Thaumonomicon.

Find a sigil in a chest? Get one from the Wither? You've heard about a ritual to activate it.

You need an enchantment table, 8 redstone dust, a weapon, and an animal you want to sacrifice. Catching and holding it with a Golden Lasso would be the easiest way. Check in LV for the Golden Lasso quest if you haven't completed it yet.

Place your enchantment table on a grass field and surround it with redstone dust. At midnight, place the animal on or near the table and kill it. You can check with the sigil if it's time yet by right-clicking it on the enchantment table. Of course you also need to have your sigil on you.

Beware! Your actions will have consequences.
With your ascension to adept thaumaturge you are ready to fusion craft beacons. The beacon recipe is found on the GTNH Thaumcraft Page. Activate it in your base to gain various positive effects.

You can kill the powered-up monsters that spawn on the cursed earth, or just sleep and despawn them. Use a shovel with the silk touch enchantment to dig up the cursed earth blocks. You can use these blocks to make a mob spawner, or place one under a vanilla spawner to let it run even when you're not around.

When setting up a mob spawner in the Nether using Cursed Earth, poor design can cause huge TPS issues.

Make sure the Cursed Earth is not attached to anything from the Nether. For example, you can place it on top of marble, but the marble cannot touch anything in the nether (netherrack, brick, etc.), and must be floating in the air. Also, limit the Cursed Earth to 1 chunk max, with 2 block buffer to the chunk edge, including a wall.

Silky jewels add silk touch to your tinkers tool, making them useful for collecting GT ores intact. You can also use them for other purposes, like obtaining cursed earth or grass blocks if needed.

The recipe can be found on the GTNH page after researching the enchantment table.

The second ritual will not be as easy as the first one. After this ritual your sigil will be stable enough to make stable unstable ingots which will not explode, and will no longer take durability damage.

This ritual needs to be performed in The End dimension. The ritual is performed by placing a Beacon in the center of a flat area of at least 11x11, not necessarily End Stone. Then place a chest in each of the cardinal directions leaving 4 spaces empty between the chest and the Beacon. In each chest insert these specific contents:

North: iron ingot, gold ingot and the other things listed in the task.
South: The different Ore Blocks and the other things listed in the task.
East: The potions.
West: The Music disks.

A spiral pattern of Redstone and String is then laid out around the beacon. At any time, shift-right-clicking the Beacon with an Activated Division Sigil in hand will show the building progress of the ritual.

Finally, kill an Iron Golem while it stands within the ritual area to activate the process. If it works, there will be an explosion that destroys the beacon and chests, while every Enderman in the End vanishes. During the ritual, throngs of aggressive mobs imbued with Haste will begin spawning and attacking the Player who needs to kill 100 of them to complete the ritual. If the Player dies or leaves the dimension, the ritual will fail and will have to be started over. Once enough mobs have been killed, the first activated Sigil in the inventory will stabilize. The Pseudo-Inversion Sigil can be used an unlimited number of times, and dividing an Iron Ingot by Diamond will produce Mobius "Unstable-Stable" Ingot which does not explode, can be produced in any crafting interface and will stack up to 64.

The brewing stand is really important for brewing the various potions like night vision, healing, haste and jump. Toxic potions or splash potions can be created too. You'll also need it to make a brewery.

With your basic wand you can finally create one. The recipes can be found on the GTNH page in the Thaumonomicon.

Do you feel lonely? Need some extra protection in your base? Want to keep the pigmen off your back in the Nether? Craft some Iron Golems and the monster problem inside your base will be gone.

They can do good amounts of damage and aggro enemies like the pigmen away from you. They can even take care of that pesky Vampire Pigman.
Feeling lonely? Located far away from a snow biome? Craft a Snow Golem, and perhaps challenge him to a snow ball fight.

After many, many, hours of doing Thaumcraft research you've found a way to craft pure tears. Ichorium purifies the nether star which sucks all the warp away. Be careful, as this may have a deadly end.

Did you ever have a dream where you could purge all your warp with no bad side effects? This purification talisman will let your dreams come true. It gets rid of it a little at a time, so no effects!

Don't forget to wear it.
A chest for bees only. It can hold up to 125 different bees in one chest.

Untreated frames are the simplest frames. They do not work in bee houses, only in apiaries or alvearies. You will need them to craft bee houses.

They increase the bee's performance. Each untreated frame will double a bee's productivity.

Impregnated Frames are even better than untreated Frames.
Each frame doubles the bee's productivity. It has a longer durability than the untreated frame, but a shorter one compared to the proven frame.

You can make proven frames or purchase them from a villager. If you can't find a beekeeper, there are a couple of different options to get one. Rescue a zombie villager, add doors to a village to get them to make kids, or perhaps use a cupid's bow and arrow...

About magic frames:
They're the core of magically endowed frames. They also have a special ability - no maximum production chance. Normal frames are ineffective to get above 16x production (4 frames) but with magic frames you can keep going - just watch out, above 16x you'll be working your bees so hard they have a chance to degenerate into ignoble ones. This can happen any bee tick, not just when they die. Frames to lower genetic decay will lower the chances of this happening.

Of course, with very long lifespans, high production genes, swarmers, and tons of frames, you may think this is worth it.

Note that normal products have a cap of 200% produced, and specialties 100%.

Forestry trees have a variety of attributes. Once you get a tree with a useful attribute, you can breed that attribute into other tree species. This way you can get an ultimate tree that combines all the attributes you want - including the type of fruit! You can also extract the genes with Gendustry if you can make the machines.

[warn]Please do your Forestry tree-breeding indoors or underground because butterflies cause lag.[/warn]

Keep in mind that for quests, you will need to breed the species "pure", not a hybrid. You should probably save the crossbreeding until after you get all the good ones.

For faster tree breeding, enclose your trees so that butterflies cannot escape, and breed bees with better traits for area and pollination speed. There's also frames too if you can afford it. The sieve may also help if you want to do it more exactly if you can make an alveary. You need either bees or butterflies, trees won't pollinate each other.

Trees have the following characteristics:
§2Saplings/Fertility§r: chance of getting a sapling from a destroyed leaf. Good for making into biomass or other uses. Balsa, Gooseberry and Sweetgum are what you want.

Allele     Drop Chance
Lowest   1%
Lower    2.5%
Low       3.5%
Average 5%
High      10%

[warn]Maturation/Matures[/warn]: the growth speed of a sapling into a tree. Important if you plan to cut it down right away for logs. Golden Raspberry is the fastest.

The sapling in the NW corner determines the stats of the new tree, and is where bone meal must be applied to mature the tree. The Giant Sequoia is best here too.

Each game tick, a leaf block with fruit has a probability of ripening by one step, and higher sappiness values correspond to a higher ripening chance. You can boost the Fermenter's output by using honey or fruit juice. Blue Mahoe and Red Maple are the best. NEI doesn't show recipes for analyzed saplings, and probably hybrids too, in the fermenter.

Below is more information on some other parameters:

§2Growth§r: Sipiri trees have Tropical instead of Light, can only be bred in a Biome with temperature 90%-190% and humidity 90%-200%, and can only grow in 120%-190% temp and 90%-200% humidity. All other trees just need light to grow.

§3Tolerates§r: if it can be planted on sand or not. Only Desert Acacia and Grandidier's Baobab have this. The trait is either Plains or Plains, Desert.

§5Supports§r: what kind of fruits it can theoretically have. Determined by Species. Only fruits from families listed under this trait can be produced by the tree, regardless of what appears under the tree's Fruits trait. There are a number of trees from the Extra Trees mod that support all 4 types, but none from Forestry itself.

§aFruit§r: determines what fruit or nut it produces. Each fruit/nut provides different advantages:
Plum and Cherry Plum only produces 100L Fruit Juice, but have a 60% chance of producing Mulch in the Fluid Extractor or Squeezer.
Papaya produces 600L Fruit Juice, but only has a 10% chance to produce Mulch.
Coconuts produce 300L Seed Oil, but only have a 25% chance to produce Mulch.
Use a Forestry Multifarm so you don't have to break the leaf block to get the fruit/nut. Set it to Manual Orchard, and place everything first.

§bFamily§r: Tells you what family of the fruit listed under the Fruits trait is: Pomes, Prunes, Nuts or Jungle.

Common Princess and Forest Drone can be bred to cultivated bees.

Cultivated bees have the shortest lifespan - this means they make great princesses to breed with your newly bred drones. The queen will die quickly, quickly giving genetic material to work with. Make sure the traits you want are kept!

They are also a Fast production bee, which means lots of honey combs for powering your Beealyzer or Treealyzer.

Cultivated Bees produce Honey Combs every 0.9 minutes. Note that production times are an approximation based on the bee's base production speed and the product's rarity. They do not reflect actual production time.

Make sure your cultivated bees are pure with a Beealyzer or GT scanner.

The main bee breeding quests will require pure bees but you can use Ignoble or Pristine princesses.

To cross breed bees you need two different species of bees. One drone and one princess from different naturally-generating hives (Meadows and Forest as an example).

Bee Houses do not allow crossbreeding. You need an Apiary to cross-breed them to a new species. Certain frames will help this process. Shortening their lifespan means faster crosses. Increasing the mutation rate means getting mutations and thus rare bees quicker.

Common Bees produce Honey Combs every 2.2 minutes. Note that production times are an approximation based on the bee's base production speed and the product's rarity. They do not reflect actual production time.

Make sure your bees are pure by checking their genetics with a Beealyzer or GT scanner.

[note]Breeder's Notes:

Riiiight from the start, they have a trick for you. The Common bee is bred from most mundane species smashed into each other. The problem is the Cultivated species, which is next in line, is bred with most mundane species along with Common. Noble and Diligent then are crossed from Common and Cultivated. You could start with two mundane bees, have the results loop back unattended, and run that whole progression. Here's an example active:inactive mix you could get on a princess over time:

Meadows:Forest
Meadows:Common (Yay!)
Common:Meadows (Double yay! Active trait!)
Cultivated:Common (Boo!)
. . . some time passes . . .
Diligent:Noble (Wait, what?!)

Meanwhile, this quest would still be sitting there, waiting for you to submit Common bees. Whoops!

If Cultivated starts to show up, just stuff any princesses and drones involved into a chest and act like that didn't happen for now. You can use them when you complete this quest to jumpstart the Cultivated species.

Now, if you don't have any way to speed up breeding and don't want to stand around to micromanage, you can try filtering, or just checking on the result from time to time. Either way, maybe don't leave it going overnight if you're on a server.[/note]

Cross breeding common and cultivated bees can result in noble bees.

Noble bees produce dripping combs every 3.8 minutes and honeydew. Note that production times are an approximation based on the bee's base production speed and the product's rarity. They do not reflect actual production time.

You've heard of a drunk beekeeper saying he has perfected a method of creating proven frames using Honeydew and a little magic. It might be worth your time to try experimenting yourself.

Your noble bees produce some dripping combs.
A good source for honey, and if you have a magical mind, honeydew for proven frames.

Cross breeding noble and cultivated bees can result in majestic bees.

If you didn't get it from Wintry bees already, Majestic bees have a very important attribute - high fertility. They will leave 4 drones when they die. This means lots of genetic material for the next generation to work with.

Majestic bees produce dripping combs every 1.5 minutes. Note that production times are an approximation based on the bee's base production speed and the product's rarity. They do not reflect actual production time.

Cross breeding noble and majestic bees can result in imperial bees.

These bees produce a Regeneration buff in their active area. You can probably find a use for this in case of...accidents.

Imperial bees produce dripping combs every 3.8 minutes and royal jelly every 5.1 minutes. Note that production times are an approximation based on the bee's base production speed and the product's rarity. They do not reflect actual production time.

Royal jelly is needed in making scented paneling for an Alveary - the third tier bee housing.

You can now start working towards the Master Registry in the How to Be(e) tab.

Royal jelly is a honey bee secretion that is used in the nutrition of larvae, as well as adult queens. It is only produced by the imperial bee. Its production can be increased with proven frames or any other kind of frames except for the soul frame. Royal jelly is also useful because it can craft ambrosia, which fills 8 hunger points (4 full food icons) and gives Regeneration I for 40 seconds. Royal jelly is used to craft scented paneling which are required in the creation of alveary blocks.

The alveary is an advanced variant of the apiary. The alveary allows for combs to be produced faster due to its natural speed increase to production (as well as the ability to add up to six frames via the Extra Bees frame housings) and due to its ability to be modified by other blocks.

It is possible to adjust the internal temperature of the alveary using the alveary heater or alveary fan in order to accommodate bees that require hotter or colder climates.

Certain bees will not produce their specialty items unless they are Jubilant. This requires matching their preferred Temperature/Humidity, without any genetic modifiers. Some bees also need a block of something beneath them as well.

It is also possible to use mutators to increase chances of mutation, alveary lighting and alveary rain shield to allow bees without the nocturnal and tolerant flyer traits to work during the night and rain, respectively, and the swarmer to use excess royal jelly to create princesses that last for a limited number of generations.

[note]If you're mutating bees that need a specific block in it, you need to place the required block under the middle bottom, and have the one directly above be a normal alveary block.[/note]
Are your cobblestone or dirt barrels filled to the brim? No problem, upgrade them!
Are your upgraded cobblestone or dirt barrels full again? No problem, upgrade them some more!

It's upgrade time again. You can make Obzinite by mixing obsidian, steel, and zinc in the smeltery. Obzinite pickaxes are able to mine ardite in the Nether.

Leave the rest of your Obzinite as liquid in your smeltery; you'll want it to make the Tool Forge. You need 16 ingots in the smeltery to make 2 Large Plates.

[note]Later in LV you can get a better yield by using a Mixer.[/note]

With your steel tool you are able to mine obsidian. You can make the Reinforcement which gives a reinforced modifier which increases the durability of your tool. Reinforced level X makes a tool unbreakable.

§3PS: In many cases this is not worth it, since the tools don't degrade that fast, it doesn't cost much to repair, and you get better materials (with higher durability) to make them out of reasonably fast. Plus, by the time you got it to unbreakable, you'd be auto-mining everything with a miner anyway. Just use redstone, or maybe luck/silky. However, there are a few very nice use cases like lumber axes and tools for automation setups.
Korn is german for wheat. That's why this special alcoholic brew is named like this. Doppelkorn means double-wheat.
Sugarcanes are a source of sugar, and therefore alcohol. If you want some rum or sugar, you'll need these.
Vodka is Russian for "small water". It is a rather high proof alcoholic fluid.

Firestone ore is used to make some BC machines like the filler, and some other stuff. Unfortunately, it's in the nether...at the bottom of the lava ocean!

Here are some tips for finding it:

-Firestone only spawns in deep lava, at least 6 deep. It will only replace netherrack, so a fjord filled with soulsand won't have any. Can you think of ways to check the lava depth, and what's down there?
-Alternatively, if you keep your head at just the correct height above the lava and at the correct angle, you'll be able to see underneath it - surely there must be a hovering jetpack?
-...or just look for the biome when your cursor is over the JM map. Hell is the default one that has netherrack.

Firestone can be mined with the GT miners, if you place it within horizontal range. Firestone ore and products will cause random fires to start nearby, so get it into a backpack quickly!

[warn]Please click the checkbox below to confirm that you are ready to handle being given the reward for this quest, and to deal with any fires that it may cause.[/warn]

Maybe you were lucky and received the luck modifier on your pickaxe. If not, you may still have an unused modifier on your pick so you can add some lapis lazuli. Or you can perhaps add another modifier by adding a diamond and a gold block to your pick and then add some lapis.

You can put the lapis lazuli in more than one slot in the tool station, use blocks to raise the luck level faster, and even use lapis blocks in the crafting station with your tool for maximum luck gain.
Mining and digging can be soooo slow. Get some redstone on your pick, shovel, or axe to make it faster. You can use a Tool Station or a Crafting Station to upgrade your tools.

If you don't have an extra modifier on your tool you can easily add one. A gold block and a diamond are all you need.

You can add two more modifiers, but you'll need to read the tinkers book yourself to know what to use.

If you have some time you can look for cobalt and ardite in the Nether.

You've heard rumors of a special wood only found in another land, a forest of Twilight, that can make tools strong enough to mine them.

Remember, you need an electric blast furnace to process these materials before you can make tools with them.

Your sword is too dull? Get some nether quartz to sharpen it.

If you have lots of Certus quartz, 1 piece of Certus is equal to 4 Nether quartz.

The LV GT++ Steam Boiler is the next machine you can build to produce steam more efficiently than with the previous single block boilers. It won't use fuel unless it cools below 100 degrees and gains a higher efficiency with longer burning fuels.

[note]Fortunately, it won't explode if you let it run dry but it §nwill waste fuel§r if there is no water present.[/note]

How about lossless 32 EU cables? Redstone alloy is a superconductor and will transfer your energy without any loss.

Redstone Alloy is a new alloy which requires an EBF. Mix redstone, silicon and coal by hand, or in the mixer for a better result.

[note]Remember not to mix it up with Red Alloy, that's the ULV one.[/note]

The Kinetic Generator will transform mechanical energy into electricity. The EU output depends on the KU input. It is most commonly used together with a Kinetic Wind Generator or Kinetic Water Generator. The Kinetic Steam Generator only has one tier, so you should probably use a Steam Turbine instead.

When placing a kinetic generator, any time, the "input" side is the side facing you. So you will place the kinetic generator, then the wind/water/steam gen, and then place a rotor inside. Power can be drawn from any side of the kinetic generator, up to the rated amount per side.

WARNING: Breaking a kinetic generator improperly will not return the generator. Use a GT wrench, and right-click it. It should drop immediately. Try again if it just changed directions.

The Kinetic Wind Generator generates energy from wind power which varies randomly, although certain factors can change this.

Unlike the Windmill, the Kinetic Wind Generator will require maintenance in the form of Rotors. These are needed to run the Kinetic Wind Generator.
Once a Rotor is placed inside the GUI, the block is given sufficient space, and the current wind level is adequate for the current rotor, the Kinetic Wind Generator will begin to generate Kinetic Energy.

This can be converted into EU by using a Kinetic Generator attached to the correct face (the black circle).

About Wind
First off, the wind strength of a particular area is affected by 3 factors: Height, Weather, and Chance. The higher up in the world you are, the higher the wind level. Below y64, there is never enough wind to be used, and KWG's will not function at all. Weather will also give boosts; Rainy weather will give a 20% boost to normal wind levels, and stormy weather will give a 50% boost. The final factor of chance makes the wind strength vary randomly, however there is a limited range of variation.

The easiest way to check the current wind level in an area is by using a Windmeter. Wind is strongest at around Y160, towards the build limit of Y255 there is very little wind, hence no point attempting to run Windmills that high. While inconvenient, the Wind Generator can run anywhere.

The Kinetic Water Generator allows Kinetic Units to be produced via the movement of water in river and ocean biomes. As with the Kinetic Wind Generator, it requires either Gearbox Rotor. Search NEI for appropriate options.

If the Kinetic Water Generator's Rotor isn't entirely submerged in water, it will alert you there is "no room for the rotor". If the Kinetic Water Generator isn't placed in a river, ocean or deep ocean biome, it will alert you it "must be placed in a river or ocean biome". Check the Game Mechanics spreadsheet on Discord for a list of biomes and their tags.

While inconvenient, the Water Generator runs more consistently.

[warn]You can use Witchery (for example) to convert biomes.[/warn]

The Kinetic Wind and Water Generators need Gearbox Rotors to function. They can be added and removed with standard automation. Higher tier rotors will last longer. In addition, the iridium ones don't break. The IC2 ones might bug out for durability loss though. Energetic is probably the best for now, since it can give out a full amp, and more is wasted.

[note]You only need to make one rotor to complete this quest.[/note]
The Windmeter measures wind strength. It shows you on which height you can place your Wind Generator.

You'll probably want HV battery buffers as well.

[note]You only need to make one of these.[/note]

Better machines need better batteries. Let's make some HV battery hulls for new batteries.

It's up to you what kind of battery to make, but realistically you'll probably make Sodium or Lithium.

Better machines need some better batteries. Lithium is the best material to use when making batteries, at least for LV-HV.

[note]You only need four batteries of one listed type.[/note]

Kinetic generator compatibility has been improved so that you no longer need transformers, you can connect directly with a cable. But why not use your transformer to send the power back to base more efficiently, it's a loss of about 97EU per HV amp just going from 160 straight down to 63 without it. If you transform up (after going through 1 block of cable to transform it to GT power), you only lose about 97EU per EV amp, which saves 4x the energy in regard to cable loss.

[warn]IC2 machines don't care about rain, but remember to cover your transformer.[/warn]

Wondering why new pipes don't always auto-connect? This was changed to make the pipes smarter. You can now use a wrench to connect only the pipes you want. You don't need a plate or a foil to prevent pipes from connecting anymore. The pipes will still autoconnect if you build one onto the other.

Pipes transferring anything hotter than a certain amount, like steam, will cause damage to a player touching them. You might want to cover hot pipes to prevent getting hurt. Also, if the heat level is higher than the pipe's heat capacity, it will melt.

Pressing RMB on a pipe in the center of the 'grid' will enable or disable a connection. It will have an X through it if the connection is enabled. You can do the same to any of the 4 corners to adjust the opposite side. You can similarly connect each of the 4 sides by clicking on the closest box in the grid.

Pipes have a free built-in shutter to reduce sloshing. Shift-RMB with a wrench on the side you want to prevent input.

Pipes attempt to transfer half of their capacity twice per second, so the full capacity per second in total.

Large or Huge fluid pipes can be a poor man's storage tank, holding large amounts on their own.

For machine outputs, including the boilers and Railcraft water tanks - the one made of Water Tank Siding - you will not need pumps. Other tanks will need pumps or Tinker's Construct faucets to move fluids.

You can put covers such as GT oak planks or plates on a pipe as well. Normally this prevents connections in that direction, but you can use a screwdriver to enable connections. This lets you make pipes that look nice going through walls. Use a crowbar to remove covers.

They work basically the same as pipes, but you need wire cutters (or a soldering iron) instead of a wrench. Additionally, you take damage if they're not insulated (wire) but not if they are (cable).

Hint: If you click one wire or cable on the other it will auto-connect. Cables and pipes can be painted to make sure you do not cross your MV line with your EV line, or dump hot lava into your plastic water pipes. No boom today.

Ha ha just kidding there is always a boom today!

The MV Machine Hull needs aluminium. You're also gonna need aluminium for every MV machine part, so keep that EBF truckin'.

Here are some tips on where to start:
- MV Electrolyzer makes getting aluminium easier.
- MV Extruder makes parts cheaper.
- MV Miner saves your time.

Have you read the quest Safety First for details about mixing tiers?
Sending MV to an LV machine causes it to explode.
Sending MV voltage over LV cables causes them to melt, which causes fire that will likely cause the machines to blow up.
Additionally, recipes done in a tier higher than the original one (not ULV, ULV counts as LV) are overclocked (OC'd). The OC'd recipes use 4x power but complete 2x faster.

Wondering why you need magnalium now? It's not for GT machines but for a material update for your crossbow.

Getting Aluminium will become easier once you get an EBF or MV electrolyzer.
If you can't find any aluminium, search for chests in the Twilight Forest or kill a few monsters. 

Combine Aluminium and Magnesium in your alloy smelter to get Magnalium.
It's time to craft a Crossbow Limb and the Crossbow Body to upgrade your old Wooden Crossbow.

Now you are able to make a better long range weapon - a crossbow. Use wood for the crossbow limb and the body and use obsidian (Reinforced III) for the tough binding. Normal strings for the bowstrings would be enough for now.

Assemble the bow yourself on your tool forge.

[warn]For upgrades:[/warn]
[note]Redstone - Speed on the draw
Lapis - Fortune on kills
Moss - Self-repair[/note]

§6NOTE: Some mobs require damage from specific tools. IF YOU ARE SHOOTING AT SOMETHING AND IT IS NOT GETTING HURT, *RUN*. And then figure out what weapon might be best to kill it.
Why not upgrade your bowstring too? You got some from the last quest, but will need to find some more in the Nether by killing spiders. Craft some fiery bowstring with it.

To make your crossbow even better, craft an ardite crossbow body. You received a few ardite ingots as reward before but will need to find ore in the Nether and process it in an Electric Blast Furnace.

With redstone you can make your bow faster. This requires a free modifier slot on your crossbow.

Don't bother putting Nether Quartz on the crossbow, it only improves damage from whacking mobs over the head with it. Put the Nether Quartz on your bolts instead.

Magnalium bolts are much better than your old wooden bolts.

You can use nether quartz on the bolts to make them even better. This requires a free modifier slot.

Experiment with NEI to find other good bolt materials.

To make these bolts, you must use a Fluid Solidifier instead of the Tinker's casting table. It's important that you get the molten iron out of the smeltery and into the Fluid Solidifier, the GT molten iron won't work.

The bolts should be in your inventory or in a bauble slot if you want to pick up the ones you fired.

To get your molten fluids back to a solid state you need a fluid solidifier. This is handy for processing molten rubber directly from the chemical reactor. It's used for crossbow bolts as well.

Keep in mind that GT fluids are different from Tinker's Construct. You will mainly work with GT fluids going forward.

Your crossbow need some ammo to shoot with. Let's craft some wooden bolts. For now, you can put either iron, obzinite, or steel on the tip of your bolts using the Smeltery. For higher tier bolts and tips you will need to pump metals into a Fluid Solidifier with the correct tool rod inserted.

[warn]For upgrades:[/warn]
§lNether Quartz§r - More damage
§lMoss§r - Self-Repair (unlock in GTNH Thaumcraft tab)

[note]You can store these in a bauble slot to save on inventory space![/note]

Your wooden soft mallet breaks after a few uses. Now you can make a rubber mallet which is much more durable.

§3You can create much higher durability mallets using Steeleaf or Ironwood, both easily attainable once you get access to the Twilight Forest.

Ironwood is much harder and more durable than rubber. Ideal for a soft mallet. Collect some liveroot underground from some roots, macerate it and mix the powder with iron and gold to create a new magical material.

You can make some unique armor with this material.
If you locate a labyrinth you may find steeleaf in chests inside. This is the best material for a soft mallet for now, however a unique armor out of steeleaf can be made too.
With your plate bender you're able to make empty cells. The circuit needs to be configured to 12 otherwise you will make foils. Once you have an LV Extruder, you can make cells directly from ingots.

One of the most important machines in HV is the Universal Macerator. It has an additional output slot to get more materials when macerating ores. You want this, really, really, badly. If you get it, you can say goodbye to your Gallium worries!

The Nether is full of different kinds of quartz. Go and find a quartzite vein. They're located between Y 80-120. It might be hard to find one, because that area is usually air, you'll just have to keep looking.

Lithium can be washed out of Lepidolite Ore or centrifuged out of either Lepidolite Ore or Spodumene Ore. At MV you can electrolyze clay dust for it. Look for canyons to find hardened clay and macerate it for dust.
Sodium can be washed out of Glauconite Ore and Sand. It can also be electrolyzed out of salt.

It's both cheaper and faster to make Annealed Copper in the Arc Furnace as opposed to the Electric Blast Furnace. 

You may find this to be quite useful as an MV cable material since it only loses 1 EU per block.
Now it's time to 'cook' your first thaumium ingots. After first researching it, you need iron ingots and praecantatio essentia to make it.

Forget everything you know about food and values. With your new canning machine you are able to fill tin cans with very nourishing food. This food can be consumed in milliseconds and makes you full and happy. And you can eat as much as you want without getting tired of the food.

Eating before you are starving restores saturation and conserves cans.

You can use a scanner to manually check how your EBF works, or you can make an information panel from nuclear control and always see the status. Make a GT sensor kit and use it on the EBF controller. Place the sensor card in your info panel. Enable it with a redstone signal.

The GregTech sensor card can monitor GregTech machines like the EBF, Turbines, and Pyrolyse ovens. This is handy for keeping an eye on maintenance issues for multiblocks.

If you want to put the panels far from the machines they are monitoring, you will need range upgrades.

[note]There's also a more advanced version.[/note]

Using the MV bender you can finally press dense plates. So let's craft a passive chunkloader. It will also load a 3x3 chunk area. You need ender pearls or coins to power the chunkloader.

Passive anchors will run for 1 hour off of an ender pearl, and a varying amount depending on the coin used.

§aPersonal Anchors§r are loaded once the owner visits, and stay loaded while the player is logged in.

§9Passive Anchors§r are loaded once the owner visits, and stay loaded until the server resets.

[warn]World Anchors[/warn] are always loaded, even after a server reset.
Want to transport oil or other fluids, have a portable crafting table or a portable chest? Then you need to craft some minecarts with tanks, chests or crafting tables.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Minecart with Tank, Workbench or Furnace

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
If you plan to automate the oil transport from your oil field far away, you need a fluid loader and unloader. A locking track will stop the train as long as oil is loaded or unloaded.

[note]PS: You should probably use the Long Distance Fluid Pipeline once you can make it in LV unless you really love trains.[/note]

Full details on how to use these may require online research (GTNH changes the recipes, not normal Railcraft functionality), but here is a simple list of things to do:

1. Make a loop of track from your base to the oil well.
2. Place a locking track near the well, and put a fluid loader two blocks above it. The track should be in Locking Mode - use a crowbar to change it.
3. Use the tank car on the filter in the loader and set it to Immediate mode.
4. Connect the well to the loader as normal.
5. Put a fluid unloader under a locking track at your base, and set it the same as the loader.
6. Automate the locomotive similarly - a fluid loader above a steam locomotive set to manual and filtered to the locomotive.

Either you got it working, you need to do more research, you realized it moves 32 buckets a trip and decided to just walk, or you can go to Discord and ask why anyone would build a train.

Item loaders also exist, but the main use for them may be to refuel your locomotive.

The furnace cart is a cheap locomotive. Click with coal or charcoal on the cart and it will start moving.

This is a curiosity, and probably you will use the steam locomotive from the next quest for an actual train.

The steam locomotive is much better than the furnace cart. You can control the speed and the direction the locomotive will move. You need to put water and coal inside to make steam to power the locomotive.

You can use a water tank or other water source to refill this locomotive by placing a Fluid Loader above it at a stop. The loader can be placed either directly above the track, or a block higher to give you clearance when riding the train. (You can't actually ride a train unless you sit in a normal minecart.)

This locomotive runs on any fuel you can burn in a steam boiler, perhaps you will want to use compressed coal blocks or similar. You can use an Item Loader to refuel it.

Once you have stable electricity in MV, you will likely move to the Electric Locomotive.
Electric Locomotives are much better than steam ones. You need electric rail for it.

If you decide to not use a locomotive and drive with one or two carts only, you can use some booster tracks. Activate them with a lever or a redstone torch. You can also use them to slow down, especially when doing corners!

Did you ever dream of driving in a railcart at high speeds? Well your dreams can come true with the high speed tracks. Be careful though; you need to lower the speed when your rails change direction or when the track ends.

Railroads in the nether are dangerous. The reinforced tracks are blast proof. Hopefully you're blast proof too?

You can move 25% faster than with normal tracks.

NEI doesn't show the right recipe on the first page. Go through the recipes a bit to find the right one.

Electrical tracks are used together with your electric locomotive. You need to power the rails with energy.

NEI doesn't show the right recipe on the first page. Go through the recipes a bit to find the right one.

[note]Alternatively you can use the search bar to search for a specific name, in this case electric tracks![/note]
To get your tracks electrified you need an electric feeding unit, shunting wires and some support frames. You can use an MFE or a transformer to get GT energy into the feeder unit.

It is also possible to create a bizarre hybrid of staff and scepter (sometimes called a "staffter"), by using a staff core instead of a wand core in the scepter recipe. The resulting device can neither hold a focus nor be placed in a crafting table, but it can still be used to activate constructs, or as a "vis battery" for Repair-enchanted equipment or Runic shielding.

Now that you have some Europium, put it to use by making a MK II reactor.

This one requires the same block placement, but replaces the LuV casings with fusion machine casings and the superconducting coil blocks with fusion coil blocks. The energy hatches must now be at least ZPM too.

Each energy hatch has an energy capacity of 20M EU and draws up to 8192 EU/t. That means it can handle start costs up to 320M EU and power consumption up to 131072 EU/t. Furthermore, MK I recipes in a MK II reactor are granted 2/2 OC which doubles the speed and power consumption.

A MK II is nice, but why not make a MK III? This time you need UV+ energy hatches, as well as the Fusion Machine Casing MK II.

Each energy hatch has an energy capacity of 40M EU and draws up to 32768 EU/t. That means it can handle start costs up to 640M EU and power consumption up to 524288 EU/t.

The MK III reactor also grants 2/2 OC for every machine tier above the minimum recipe tier.

To upgrade your reactor further and to make UV motors, you will need to get some americium. The recipe is pretty expensive, but once you made the next tier of reactor, you will unlock a simpler and cheaper one. However, to get there you will need a lot of americium already, so better make sure you are producing enough lutetium.

Let's start with just 48 ingots. Enough for a single UV motor.

Now that you have a reactor, it's time to utilize it to create power.

The simplest plasma you can make for power is Helium plasma, but it also provides a lot of power. Deuterium is renewable from water, and you can get Helium-3 from Endstone.

However, you will need a way to convert the plasma into EU. To do this you will need a large plasma turbine. This will also need a dynamo hatch that can handle the power you're outputting. For Helium plasma, you will want a 4A LuV Dynamo or above.

Your fancy new Large Plasma Turbine will need a rotor to go inside of it. You can make it out of any GT material, but the best right now is NORMAL Draconium.

[warn]Always test in creative or the GTNH Power Planner (linked below) first![/warn]
[url]https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1FTFdfmY_UWbTbFOyNzARKeI90pbHvPBH6M3JHJmaC-E/edit?usp=dsharing[/url]

When using turbines, be careful of flow rates. To find the optimal flow rate manually, divide the optimal energy flow rate listed on the turbine, by the plasma's energy density (EU/L). You can also scan the multiblock's controller while feeding it a minimal amount of plasma to see what the optimal flow is. Make sure to use a Fluid Regulator set to this flow rate for highest fuel efficiency, or go beyond it to get more EU/t at a lower efficiency. Plasma Turbines are the best at retaining efficiency beyond the optimal flow.

If you go beyond the optimal flow, you will get a higher EU/t value, but less fuel efficiency, and the maximum EU/t value depends on the turbine type and its Overflow Efficiency tier. For this type of turbine, tier 1 reaches the max at 250% of optimal flow to produce 158% of the EU/t, tier 2 reaches the max at 400% of optimal flow to produce 214% of the EU/t and tier 3 reaches the max at 550% of optimal flow to produce 301% of the EU/t. The closer you get to this maximum, the more fuel efficiency you're throwing away. The choice is yours!

[note]For a lot of extra information on fusion, check out the new quest line called Powerful Nuclear Physics.[/note]

To make Oganesson, you'll need to make Californium. To make that, you'll need Beryllium and Plutonium 239, all in the Fusion Reactor. After the two fusion chains, you'll have the best noble gas in the pack, which is used in several places.

In this tier, you can send it to Void Miners, to increase their ore production speed, or EBFs, to make them run faster. Later on, Oganesson will be used in other places, like the optical circuit line, or to produce Metastable Oganesson, which is needed in much larger quantities later on.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §2§l§nI Put Fusion in Your Fusion so you Can Fusion While You Fusion

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
While one reactor is nice and all, why not make another? This time you can use the MK3 americium recipe to make it easier.

Costing just 1 ingot of Plutonium, and 2 cells of hydrogen, this recipe is much easier and faster than the MK2 version. By making americium plasma, then putting it through a turbine, you will get americium in the liquid state. You will need at least 132 plates for the controller and the fusion machine casings.

Plus, free power!
It's time to get yourself a 3x3 crafting area. Use your flint and some wood to build one!

Hoppers come in handy when you want to automate your machines. You can input items via hoppers directly into GT pipes and you don't have to use a conveyor module. However, the input rate is much slower, and the hopper must be beneath its source inventory.
Your cart needs power, obviously. A cart can be powered via coal, solar or lava. If you are able to make solar panels you can power your cart with the sun.
Want to automate digging for ores? A drill head made out of iron is the cheapest alternative.
Your cart needs power, obviously. A cart can be powered via coal, solar or lava. Why not power your cart with lava?
After you craft side chests you can add more different chests to the cart. Some sides are reserved for tools so no chest can be placed there.

Nuclear fusion is the next major step in your progression, and to accomplish it you will need a Fusion Reactor Mark I. You will unlock new materials across the next few tiers with fusion, making this a required multiblock. Europium is what you will need first to make it to ZPM.

At the same time, fusion can generate power for you, primarily via Helium Plasma in this first tier. The speed of the reactor can make for significant EU/t, but actually consuming this plasma fast enough at this early stage is difficult. You will have Large Plasma Turbines, which can run a buffered dynamo for 4 output amps. This might require a lot of spam compared to powergen setups you might be using, such as UCFE, vac nukes or other options. Later, you will unlock XL turbines and a fusion line for them. 

For your first reactor, you will need a controller, 1-16 fluid input hatches, 1-16 fluid output hatches, and 16 LuV+ energy hatches. Each energy hatch has an energy capacity of 10M EU and draws up to 2048 EU/t.

That means you can do any fusion recipe with a start cost of 160M EU or less, and takes 32768 EU/t or less. Using more fluid hatches means you need less fusion casings. While this doesn't matter as much for the mk1 reactor, this principle helps tremendously with the higher reactor tiers.

[note]You'll notice that there is an option to create a Compact Fusion Reactor MKI instead of the normal size. This is available as an option for every tier of Fusion Reactor. They are not required by any means, but they are demonstrably quicker if you're willing to spend extra resources.[/note]

To make a mk2 reactor, ender quarry, T5 rocket, unlock ZPM, or other things, you will need europium. Once you make a t5 rocket you will be able to find this as part of a very rare ore. Until then you need to produce it in the reactor. But it's probably not worth it to look for the ore anyway.

[note]Now that you have produced europium, you can process the Europium III Oxide from your Monaline if you built one.[/note]
Producing RF Power by hand is a good idea for making one or two recipes in the Forestry machines. The turrets can be charged with it too.

Producing RF power with lava is possible with the help of the biogas engine. You need water, fruit juice, liquid honey, milk, seed oil, or forestry biomass in the other slot. After a brief warmup time, the engine outputs up to 50 RF/t depending on the fluid used.

The possible fluids give the following power:

Water: 10 RF/t for 1k ticks
Fruit juice: 10 RF/t for 2.5k ticks
Liquid honey: 20 RF/t for 2.5k ticks
Milk: 10 RF/t for 10k ticks
Seed oil: 30 RF/t for 2.5k ticks
Biomass: 50 RF/t for 2.5k ticks

Peat fired engines use Peat or Bituminous Peat to run. Peat burns for 5000 ticks and produces 10 RF every tick, 1 peat makes 0.66 Ash, so you get 2 Ash for burning 3 peat. Bituminous Peat burns for 6000 ticks and produces 20 RF/tick.

Peat Farms can be set up by using a managed farm with tin electron tubes. It is possible with a manual farm too.

Electron tubes are used to set farms to a special kind of crop and can be used in engines, alvearies and some crafting recipes.

Use a soldering iron to attach an electron tube to a circuit board.

Electron tubes are used to set farms to a special kind of crop and can be used in engines, alvearies and some crafting recipes.

Use a soldering iron to attach an electron tube to a circuit board.

Use a soldering iron to attach an electron tube to a circuit board.

Electron tubes are used to set farms to a special kind of crop and can be used in engines, alvearies and some crafting recipes.

Use a soldering iron to attach an electron tube to a circuit board.

EV circuits need an MV Circuit Assembler, so make one.

[note]Shortly after this, all circuit recipes will need a cleanroom, so get started on it![/note]
With your workstation circuits you can craft an HV circuit assembler. This is needed for IV circuits.
An EV circuit assembler requires IV Circuits to craft. With this assembler you can make higher tier circuits.

Epoxid is needed for Advanced Circuits boards. You need Sodium Hydroxide, Epichlorohydrin and Bisphenol A to make it.

You can also use the molten form for some other things you might want to check out.

[note]Using a Large Chemical Reactor? You might be able to skip some steps, look around NEI to find out more.[/note]
Mainframes are the first IV Circuits you can make. It's used for a few EV machines, and basically all IV machines and components.

Glycerol is a byproduct of making bio diesel, but it's really useful too. It's used to make epoxid in EV, and for making dynamite, I guess. Both TNT and iTNT are better though.

[note]PS: You don't actually need dynamite, and epoxid can be made another way, if you don't want to make bio diesel forever/at all.[/note]

More than just a byproduct of your Sodium Persulfate production. HCl becomes important for Epoxid in HV/EV tier. You can also use it to process bee combs.

You can also make it directly from Hydrogen and Chlorine.
Epichlorohydrin is another product needed in your epoxid production. By now you should be experienced enough to figure out which path is best for your setup using NEI.

The next circuit line requires Epoxid. To start, let's get some Phenol.

The easiest way is to get phenol out of heavy fuel. There are other ways, like getting it out of wood tar from a pyrolyse oven, isopropylbenzene and oxygen, or chlorobenzene and water.

§3Already automated Epoxid? Hold 128 sheets to skip this questline.
The next step towards Epoxid is to get Bisphenol A. You will need to combine Phenol, Acetone and HCl in a chemical reactor.
Pumps, pistons, conveyor modules and robot arms are the most needed machine parts in HV. Go and craft one of each.

Let's craft a personal chunkloader. It will load a 3x3 chunk area. You need ender fragments, ender pearls, or coins to power the chunkloader.

Personal anchors can be powered with ender fragments for 1h, ender pearls for 4 hours, and a varying amount depending on the coin used.

Personal Anchors§r are loaded once the owner visits, and stays loaded while the player is logged in.

Passive Anchors§r are loaded once the owner visits, and stays loaded until the server resets.

World Anchors§r are always loaded, even after a server reset.

With your HV assembler you can craft a world anchor. So let's make one. It will again load a 3x3 chunk area.

You need coins to power the world anchor, it will run a varying amount depending on the coin used.

§aPersonal Anchors§r are loaded once the owner visits, and stay loaded while the player is logged in.

§9Passive Anchors§r are loaded once the owner visits, and stay loaded until the server resets.

[warn]World Anchors[/warn] are always loaded, even after a server reset.

[note]Check with server operators in case world anchors are disabled. On the official servers, world anchors are currently disabled to keep TPS high.[/note]

Go get the schematics for tier 4 rockets.

This will open the Planets Venus and Mercury and the Jupiter Moon Io.
Each rocket needs a Control Computer, appropriate to the tier of the rocket.

In the last step you need to infuse your Marshmallow with some epic food in the Thaumcraft infusion altar. Before you can do it you need to unlock the research.

Is this worth it? Is there any enemy worthy of using the buffs this gives on? That's up to you.
Pumps, pistons, conveyor modules and robot arms are the most needed machine parts in LuV. Go and craft one of each with your new Assembly Line.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §d§lNow You're Really Gonna Hate This 1-4 in LuV

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Some machines need Emitters and Sensors, like the Scanner or the Circuit Assembler.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §d§lNow You're Really Gonna Hate This 5 and 6 in LuV

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
After you craft an IV assembler, upgrade your Electric Blast Furnace with new Coils out of HSS-G Ingots. This ingot becomes even more important in LuV tier. But right now both of these are still far away. Just make a bit that you need for the next rocket.

To find a Molybdenum Vein, you probably want to make a high quality Prospector's Scanner with a good range.

Keep the hydrogen and continue in a second chemical reactor to obtain the purified Solar Grade Silicon. You get all the Hydrochloric Acid back!

Maybe you can automate this process?

LuV-Level. You will need Rhodium-Plated Palladium for machines. Suggested planets and moons to visit: Jupiter's Moon Io, Venus and Mercury. Machine parts will now require an Assembly Line - Check Multiblock Goals for details.

Time for a second EBF!

You can make ingots faster in 3 ways - better coils, higher tier energy hatches, or adding more furnaces. It's probably time to add a second EBF to your base.

Multiblock machines can share casings, mufflers, and input/output hatches/buses, but not maintenance hatches (you can share the auto ones though). You can share energy hatches, but only if you can supply enough power to all machines it's a part of.

Remember, pollution will be very high with two EBFs active at once! Watch out for high pollution effects. Use the best mufflers available and don't place the EBFs in the same chunk as farmland or other high pollution machines like Pyrolyse Ovens and Large Boilers. Maybe it is time to do something more active?

You can use whatever coils you have lying around, but you certainly want to start searching for Mica if you haven't found any yet.

Thanks to our amazing devs, you no longer have to use a command block to reload your questbook between updates. This means you'll get all new quests automatically upon updating to a new version of GTNH! Isn't that convenient?

If, for whatever reason, you want to manually reload your questbook, you can do so by typing /bq_admin default load in the chat window. You will need to be an admin for it to work, though.

Here's another questbook in case you already lost the one you spawned with. Don't forget that it can also be viewed at any time by pressing the Tilde (~) key if you have not changed its keybind.

§3Some command blocks are still used for specific tasks, but they do not concern the average player since they are admin-only and thus are not craftable.

GregTech ore generation is based on veins. Veins have a fixed height and a rectangular base.

There is a vein every 3 chunks in x and z direction. The veins typically extend into the neighboring chunks and have varying forms. The center point however is very regular. It is based on the chunk number. Look at upper left of the screen to find the chunk number. This info is displayed by InGame Info XML mod. For now, you need to see chunk info like "Chunk X: 3 Z: -2".
