The 3,-2 is the chunk's address. The ore centers are located at chunk numbers of the form 3N+1 for both x and z. So, 4,7 is an ore center, as well as 10,16, -23,19, and so on. If you are in the right spot InGame Info will also say that "This is an ore chunk.".

Another useful tool is the NEI ore vein overlay which you activate by pressing F9 three times. It shows the 3x3 areas and marks the center blue.

The generation of Ore Chunks is not related to biomes.

[note]After finding an ore chunk you can view it in your JourneyMap by clicking the ore icon up top. If you are playing multiplayer and on the same team, you both should be able to see the same prospecting information.[/note]
betterquesting:10.name:8: §a§lHow the Heck Do I Find Ores?

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Now that you know what an Ore Chunk is, dig all the way down to bedrock to find if there is a vein located in it.

Check out an ore in NEI to see where you can find a vein that contains it. Search for it and click on it to get this info, among other things.

There are many types of ores, even just for getting one material like Iron, so don't stick to only one ore.

You can also search small ores in NEI, but not all of them are used.

Wait, what? You want more byproducts from your ores? A cheaper way to make paper? Well, the chemical bath is perfect for you!

You'll have to provide liquids like mercury to extract different products like nickel, silver, copper, and platinum (only as PMP) from ores.

For paper you'll only need some water and wood pulp. Maybe you'll find more uses for it!

Better Questing has a number of useful commands for the questbook (QB) if something goes wrong. You need to have cheats enabled to use them.

/bq_admin default load
Use this command to update your QB after you update the modpack. It reloads the quest database from the file. Your save file stores a version of the QB that can be different from the one in the file.

/bq_admin edit
Toggles editing quests. Pressing RMB on the quest will open a context menu to share it or copy its ID.

/bq_admin reset all <Player>
Resets all quests. Use this if you want to start over, or are editing the QB. You should specify the player as well if it is a server, otherwise you can skip that part.

/bq_admin reset <ID> <Player>
Resets a specific quest, defined by the quest ID. Sometimes it may be easier to go into Edit Mode > Designer Tool to specify what to reset.

/bq_admin complete <number> <Player>
Completes a specific quest, similarly to the above. You can still claim the rewards. Use this command if a quest is broken, and then report it on GitHub, but please check if it's already reported.

/bq_admin default save
Saves changes to the QB after editing it.

/bq_copyquests <PlayerWithQuestsCompleted> <NewPlayer>
If you want to sync the quests with someone in your party, then use this. They won't get any rewards for that though.

/bq_admin hardcore
Enables BQ3 Hardcore Mode. You only start with 3 lives, so best of luck. Additional life hearts are available in the Kill all the Things tab.

Aside from the consume-type quests, a quest counts for everyone in the party if one person finished it. However, if someone joined your party later, you need to get them up to speed first either through /bq_copyquests above, or manually. Otherwise, your quest completion won't count for them because the requirements for that quest are not fulfilled for them.

If your singleplayer world does not have cheats enabled, go to the ESC screen, open to LAN, then enable cheats. This makes pausing impossible until you reload afterwards. If you host a server, you can run the commands in the command line, without "/". You can also edit the level.dat file, and set 'allowCommands' to 1, but make sure to backup your world before doing that.

[warn]For quests to save properly, you must be online and logged into your Mojang account when starting the game. Sorry, it's a limitation of Better Questing.[/warn]

The mod ServerUtilities (SU) is included in the pack to backup your world. You can adjust save path, frequency, and the number of backups to keep in its settings at '.minecraft\serverutilities\serverutilities.cfg'.

If you need to restore from a backup, you can find them in the backups folder in the instance directory.

The SU backups include several folders outside of the save folder that store the data from JourneyMap, VisualProspecting, and the Thaumcraft Node Tracker.

If you move to another drive or computer, don't forget to migrate all files, not just the world folder.
Tired of sticking your EnderIO items in the capacitor bank to charge it? Time to make a wireless charger.

...right? So when building multiblocks, make sure you keep in mind that electric machines don't like getting rain or snow on them. They'll start fires, and those fires have a chance of causing an explosion. This explosion will explode other machines, cascading until your whole base is a hole in the ground. This is one of the reasons backups are a thing. Stay safe out there!

If worse comes to worst, there is logs/Explosion.log that tracks what caused an explosion. However, this file appears to reset on world load.

The Ore Finder Wand reduces the tedium of locating needed veins. If you're not sure how to craft Magnetic Iron Rod for it, check its Shapeless Crafting tab in NEI.

Once you put an ore sample into the wand, it will tell you if this ore is nearby. When you get close to the target, you will hear the sound, and the wand will tilt down to the point of being upside-down if there's a lot of target ore nearby.

Use NEI to figure out which ore is the best for your search. If you don't have the needed ore, some basic ones can be purchased in the Vending Machine.

Open the wand's inventory with Shift+RMB when looking at the ground. Put the sample ore into the slot.
The rod has a 60-block range both up and down, so it can miss a vein that is located very low or if you are above the sea level.

The rod appears to work based on the GT's Material system, so anything of the same material will work.
That includes crushed ores, dusts, ingots, gems, rods, you name it. For things that don't belong to a particular Material, the rod appears to search only for that exact block - for instance, you won't detect small ores with the usual ore block.

If the detected ore is a part of a vein, you will see a discovery message in the chat, and the vein will be automatically logged into the visual prospecting tab of your journey map.

The wand also works from inventory and hotbar, so you don't need to be actively holding it, but you get style points if you do.

The ore in the wand is stored with the player, not the wand. In other words, remove the ore if you want to give the wand to your teammate.

The Ore Finder Wand doesn't work in space! The vast cosmic energies of the sun interfere with its inner workings! Or the devs want you to use something more complicated than a stick. You choose.

More like too many items! Here are some tips for using NEI.

When you have your inventory open, you can type the search terms in the text bar at the bottom. Make sure your GUI size is set correctly, or you won't be able to see it. Double-click the bar to highlight any matching items in your inventory or inventories you're looking at. Handy for searching for a specific ore, as they tend to look the same!

Even better, you can use T to search nearby inventories, which will emit some particles.

We have also provided the special Y command to look for a machine in the world, in case you've forgotten where you placed that Advanced Circuit Assembler.

We now have an extra-fancy Bookmark feature! The default key is A, but can be changed in the NEI config window. Bookmarks will be on the left side of the inventory, and you can look up their recipes or uses as normal. To move a bookmark, drag it with Shift+LMB. You can even bookmark entire recipes with Shift+A or recipes with amounts using Ctrl+Shift+A.

Pressing O will hide NEI, useful for fancy screenshots.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §a§lNot Enough Items - Now with Bookmarks and Recent History!

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
NEI has some really nice advanced features too.

Clicking LMB or pressing R on an item shows the recipes to create it. RMB or U show recipes that use the item. Backspace moves you back to the previously browsed recipe.

Hold Shift to stop the oredict cycling through items, and to show the oredict entries for the current item under your cursor.

Search using @ to find all items from that mod; for example, §o@thaumcraft§r will list all Thaumcraft items and blocks.

You can combine multiple search terms with a space. §o@thaumcraft table§r will search for anything with table in the name or description, in the mod Thaumcraft.

It has even more advanced features than mentioned here and many configuration options, you can look in the NEI option menu under Inventory to find a few. Here you can change more things about how the search works (like using regex), toggle collapsible items or the item zoom panel, or configure the history panel to your liking.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §a§lNEI is More Powerful Than You Imagine

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
As your base grows, you're going to have a dozen different long term goals each with many steps. Build a clipboard to keep track of what you need to do.

[note]Hint: You can put the clipboard on a wall using shift-right-click.[/note]

Tired of your stuff falling out of your crafting table every time you walk away? This fancy table from Tinker's Construct has slots to hold the items in your recipe.

You can also use it to upgrade tools with modifiers like Redstone for additional speed and Lapis for fortune/looting!

When it's placed next to a vanilla chest, it will even show the chest's inventory in the crafting window. Single or double vanilla chests only, please.

Cut it again for a sleek, low profile version.

A staff of traveling can get you really moving around your base. Hold shift and right-click to teleport in that direction. If you've got travel anchors, just right-clicking will send you to them. The range is 16 blocks for normal TP, 128 to an anchor.

Tired of searching all over the map for that Bamboo Forest or Tropical Rainforest? Desperate for clay dust and need to find a Canyon or Mesa biome? Nature's compass will lead you to the biome you're looking for, if it's within its range.

The compass menu has the following functionality:
* When Sorted By: Name, you can filter the list by name or its parts. The search is case-insensitive.
* You can search by keys and their combinations. For instance, name: bamboo, climate: warm, bh: -1.8, tag: forest.
All available keys are:
name,
climate [hellish, hot, warm, normal, cold, icy],
baseheight | bh (float, can be negative),
heightvariation | hv (float),
rainfall | rain (float),
temperature | temp (float),
humidity [damp, normal, arid],
tags.

Some things to keep in mind:
* Biomes from other dimensions show up on the list, don't bother searching for those unless you're in that dimension.
* In general, the full list has biomes that are not generated by Realistic World Generator, like Sunflower Plains.
* Radius 10000 means it couldn't find the biome. In this case after the initial search, its menu will show only the biomes in the 10k radius. Use Shift+RMB to see the whole list again.
* You can try again at a different location - the range is 10k from your current position.
* Artificially created biomes count, so remove them if you want to find a natural one.
* There's lots of different 'versions' of biomes under the same category, so if you want a tropical one for tropical bees, there are actually a bunch of places you can get it.
* For those who don't mind the freeze when searching, the radius can be changed in a config. The HUD position can also be changed in the config.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §2§lBiomes Everywhere, But Not the One You Want?

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Stop guessing what the humidity and temperature are for your biome. Use the habitat locator to get a reading on your current climate.

Once you get good effects from your bees, instead of just trashing the excess drones, you can put them in collector's jars to get the effects anywhere in your base.

Healing? XP? Poison?

The collector's jars can even be piped or connected to a conveyor so that drones last a long time.

[note]PS: Using the regen effect of Imperial bees while doing Blood Magic may be useful.[/note]
betterquesting:10.name:8: Put the Drones in a Jar and Shake it Up

betterquesting:10.desc:8: These frames will let you kill your bees faster. It's to breed the next generation sooner, right? Not because you don't like them?
These frames will keep your bees buzzing for longer. If you care, that is.

These frames cause mutations at an increased rate. They're super useful.

About the stats on frames you see when holding shift, you'll note that some have a different number in brackets next to them, this means that this is the maximum they can be stacked. This only applies to the Extra Bees ones.

The stats on the frames are also multiplicative instead of additive, so after 4 frames in an alveary, soul frames will max out. On the other hand, accelerated frames will take 9 to get there, but you can just keep on going.

If you pile up the multipliers, 5x from stimulator, 3x from mutator, and 4x1.8x frames, it'll get you to 157x, getting you those 1% bees in a single generation!
betterquesting:10.name:8: Are the Bees Buzzing, or Screaming?

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
If bee breeding is a dice game, then these are the biggest factors you'd control to win:

1. Fertility: How many dice you can roll each turn.
2. Mutation Rate: How good of a roll you need to make.
3. Lifespan: How often you can play the game.

The Oblivion Frame dramatically helps with #3 by reducing the bee's lifespan to the point that you can play the breeding dice game in one "tick" of 27.5 seconds. A bee with the "Shortest" lifespan trait cycles for 10 ticks (275 seconds), so you'd minimally cut the cycle by a whole order of magnitude!

You can find Oblivion Frames in Stronghold libraries. This is how you can get them in the early game for very aggressive bee breeding. Later, you can make them from Dragon Eggs. These frames are very precious and you don't want their durability to run out. A typical repair method is to use a Thaumic Restorer on them.

§oWait, to find a Stronghold reliably, I need some Eyes of Ender, and that's an HV-tier Chemical Reactor recipe!§r If you happen to have a Large Chemical Reactor, remember that it overclocks perfectly, so you can crank er' up with a bunch of MV-tier Energy Input Hatches.

§nThe Oblivion Bee Meta
§r
The oblivion bee meta can be enough to breed most bees quickly. You could do the whole bee breeding quest line with it, but you can ultimately improve on it with Alvearies and genetic modification. What you need for this meta is:

1. An Apiary
2. An Oblivion Frame
3. Some way to repair the frame (typically: thaumic restorer)
4. A Beealyzer and a lot of honey

This is a hands-on process. You don't automatically send the princess and drones back through because you need to watch the oblivion frame's durability. You inspect all the offspring bees after each cycle and hand-pick which to try next after a pass through the Beealyzer.

You can accelerate the Apiary with a World Accelerator. [warn]Be sure to protect the World Accelerator and supporting equipment from rain![/warn] You can use glass or a breakable clear glass so the Apiary can still see the sky while the World Accelerator is protected. If you need to use batteries, you can use a State Cell to draw out a button pulse to the world accelerator so it runs juuust long enough for an accelerated cycle.
...at last, the final chest, it will keep its inventory even after breaking! Item transportation will become much simpler with this!
betterquesting:10.name:8: §5§lNeed a Place For All Those Ores?

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Tired of applying bone meal or fertilizer by hand? A sprinkler can take water and boost your crop growth rate. Bone meal will make it work even faster.

[note]Note that the sprinkler does not work with crops on cropsticks.[/note]

How about large steel fluid cells instead? Each holds 8000L, and they can stack to 64. Unfortunately, you have to load and unload them using a machine's interface - like ULV tanks for example - but hey, 512 buckets in a single slot is pretty good!

You cannot use these cells directly in the world, like BC tanks, or to dump the fluid on the ground.
512 buckets in a stack not cutting it? Aluminium cells can hold 32 buckets per cell, and stack to 64. 2,048 buckets in a single stack? That's half a supertank!
The sifter runs sooo slow, you should make an HV sifter to get gems faster.

Now that you are in MV and have an EBF, you can make new bolts with vanadiumsteel-tipped magnalium. Your enemies will tremble at your might.

Check "fletching" under NEI for fletching options.

Good hunting!

That meteoric iron you found on the moon, when sent through the EBF, turns into this amazing meteoric steel, able to keep a fine edge. Put some on an Energetic Alloy tool rod to make an awesome bolt. Your next bolt you'll have to figure out yourself.

Use whatever fletching you want.

Energetic alloy has proven to be an amazing material. Its light weight and high stiffness makes it perfect for a crossbow limb. It is slightly slower to draw but still has amazing stopping power with its very high bolt speed. Durability is much improved over a carbon limb.

The material would also make an excellent bolt body. Perhaps you will find a suitable tip to match?

Ever wanted to trap a wither but the only option was non movable bedrock? Now that you've made dark steel you can get reinforced obsidian which is wither-proof. Useful for manual killing and even automation once you get a powered spawner supplying you with wither skeleton skulls.

[note]Hint: Unlike vanilla obsidian, reinforced obsidian CAN be moved by pistons which might come in handy.[/note]
Making rum can be automated, but you need to follow this industrial way for it.
Rum. Yummy!
Stockpiling sugar might be a good idea if you have a sweet tooth. Or not?

Since honey contains a lot of sugar, it might be a good idea to get some honey.

[note]Just having the fluid in cells or buckets in your inventory lets the quest detect and consume it.[/note]

Giant wasps can be found in the Nether. Quick! Sneak into their hive and steal some honey!

[note]Just having the fluid in cells or buckets in your inventory lets the quest detect it.[/note]

Diamond Spikes damages mobs (or you!) that touch any side of it other than the bottom. With 7 attack damage, the Spike does as much damage as a Diamond Sword. Mobs will not walk around the block, but will try to walk over it as if it were a regular solid block. Most explosions won't destroy the Spike because it has a very high blast resistance.

These can also be enchanted with all the enchantments a regular diamond sword would receive. This includes Looting and Sharpness, which function exactly as it does on a sword. Interestingly, mobs killed by the Diamond Spike will return experience as if killed by the player.

There are weaker versions, but who wants that? If you happen to want the last hit, you might want the wooden ones though.

Primal shrooms allow you to refill wands easier before you can move nodes to your base.

Go and find some Vishrooms in a magical forest biome. Try using a Nature's Compass. Or buy some using coins if no biome is close to your location.

1 pumpkin and 4 tiny piles of stone dust are the perfect combo to make these.

Whenever they're fully grown, you can break them to get some vis orbs to drop, just like enemies do. You do need to be holding the wand to collect it though. For these to grow, they will need a certain light level.
If you don't want pure alcohol, but beer, breed some hops!

An HV Bender is 4x faster than your LV Bender, but it also opens up an important recipe - Tin Cans!

With this bender you can turn Tin Casings into Tin Cans. Using the Tin Cans with food in a Canner will make Canned Food. This can stack up to 64, and will fully restore your shanks - no need to rotate food types anymore! You will eat as much as you need with one click. One drawback is you will no longer get the Well Fed buff with its slight health regen bonus, nor will you gain more hearts from eating new food. Also, these cans don't fit in the lunch bag or lunch box so you don't need those anymore.

Charged certus quartz is one of the basic components for a lot of AE recipes. Just mix some certus quartz and redstone dust to get charged certus quartz dust.

Use the autoclave to make crystals. Or if you have lots of sodium, you can use the chemical reactor recipe. You can also make the charger to go directly from crystal to charged crystal, but it's not very fast. The charger can connect directly to a GT cable or a fluix cable from the bottom.

[note]Note that some recipes only have a chance of producing a charged crystal, which is true of many of these.[/note]

Helps with fluctuating power. Energy cells store up to 2,000,000 AE. They do not accept power directly but are used to buffer some power in an already existing ME network. Energy Cells do not use a channel.

The ME Drive is designed to do one thing, store storage cells. This block holds 10 storage cells so you can tightly pack your storage into a very small space. ME drives show their contents and the storage cell status on the front of the drive face.

The ME Chest which you used to craft the Drive is very similar, except it can only store 1 cell (though it comes with an in-built terminal!).

Red - Indicates the storage cell is full.
Orange - Indicates the storage cell cannot hold any more types, but it can store more items.
Green - Indicates the cell can hold more types, or more items.
Black - Indicates there is no channel, or power is offline.

It's important to note, that without an ME Network this block does nothing. It's only useful when combined with a way to input, and output items, and requires 2 AE/t power to function, and additional power for each storage cell stored inside it.

About Priority: Many devices in AE2 have a priority setting, this determines what gets items first. This is useful in some situations, but not so much in others. Higher number = higher priority.

Used to accelerate the process of purifying crystals, which allows you to create pure certus quartz crystal, pure nether quartz crystal and pure fluix crystal. Must be powered by an ME Network via the sides with the +, and consumes a steady 8 ae/t while plugged in. Crystal Seeds must be in an adjacent water block to be affected - the seeds will shimmer more rapidly when in the presence of a powered crystal growth accelerator. These do not use a channel.

The §5§lCrystal Growth Chamber§r is used for fast crystal growth, and it is possible to increase its speed by installing acceleration cards in an upgrade slot. It works more like a normal device, with the crystals growing in its internal inventory. Unlike the more primitive versions, it doesn't use power when not in use. It also doesn't use a channel.

The purified versions of Nether, Certus and Fluix crystals can be grown from seeds made in the assembler from crystal dust and sand.

You may need the Pure Nether Quartz later, but for now let's create some Pure Fluix Crystal and Pure Certus Quartz Crystal.

They can be grown in-world for free by dropping them in water, or at a much faster rate in a GT Autoclave.

[note]Distilled water reduces the recipe time in the Autoclave by half.[/note]

Allows you to configure which users, and what permissions the users have with the ME System. By existing it enforces permissions on the usage of the system.

The security system does not prevent destructive tampering, removing cables / machines or breaking of drives. If you need to protect your system from physical vandalism you will need another form of physical security. This block provides network level security.

The player who places the ME security terminal has full control over the network and cannot exclude themselves any rights. By adding a blank biometric card you define a default behavior for every player who has no biometric card registered.

In addition to security on the software layer, you can link up your wireless terminal with the network and access it wirelessly if you have that setup already.

If you have one on your main network, your subnets may also need one to have access to your main network, but this is not always the case depending on how you set it up.
Giving your network even more stability. Dense energy cells store AE energy up to 16 million units. They do not accept power directly but are used to buffer power in an already existing ME Network.

After you link up the wireless terminal in the ME security terminal, it grants portable access to the ME network. Put it into a charger to recharge it.

Holds 1.6m AE in its battery and drains 1 AE/t for each block you are away from the nearest ME wireless access point.

Charge your Wireless Terminals (and the successors) with an EIO Wireless Charger if you don't want to wait a century for them to charge.

Formation Core - a component which can convert energy back into matter.
Annihilation Core - a component which can convert matter into energy.
Gates all network I/O.

The ME Interface is the only component which can be used as a part, or as a Block. Crafting an ME interface in either form by itself produces the other form. The thin form is useful if you want to provide several different interfaces in a single block of physical space, but each will need its own channel. The block form lets multiple other blocks connect to a single ME interface, using only one channel for the interface. The ME Interface acts as an in between when working with pipes, tubes, networks, or machines from other mods.

[note]If you're using a resource pack and the interface's GUI doesn't show up properly, you'll need to delete the assets\appliedenergistics2\textures\guis\interface.png file in your resourcepack zip file.[/note]

The ME Storage Bus, when attached to another inventory block in the world lets you access that inventory via networked functions. This allows you to use chests, barrels, or other types of item storage in your networks.

The storage via the ME Storage Bus is bidirectional, it can both insert, or extract items from the inventory block it is attached to as long as the ME storage bus has its required channel.

The UI allows you to control which items are selected as storable items, this selection has no effect on what items can be extracted once they are in the storage.

The storage bus will function with nearly any inventory block, including ME Interfaces, EFR barrels, JABBA Barrels, Storage Drawers, etc. They can also be used to route items passively into Buildcraft pipes.

If you place a storage bus on an ME Interface the storage bus will be able to interact with the full contents of the target network, unless that interface is configured to store items inside itself, in which case it will see those stored items.
Storage bus for fluids only.
Placing your fluid crafting patterns in a Dual Interface. That will allow AE2 to push the fluids and items both. Note. Fluids are being sent first, then items.

The ME export bus extracts items from the ME network's networked storage and places them into the inventory it faces. You must configure which items it will insert, leaving the configuration blank will result in nothing. The ME export bus will try to export any of the items on its list skipping over those it cannot fit into the destination. This is the functional opposite of the ME import bus.

Pulls items from the inventory it is pointed at and places them into the ME network's networked storage. You can specify which items it will pull out via the UI, else it tries to pull out any item in the adjacent inventory. The ME import bus will attempt to import any possible options, even if 1 or more of the configured items cannot be stored. This is the functional opposite of the ME export bus.

When your machines are very fast, it's better to have them output directly into an ME interface instead, since that works instantly.
Import Bus for Fluids only.

An empty storage container, you can insert the vanilla AE2 storage cell parts into it to create a usable storage cell.

You can also craft it with the storage components when making them to skip combining them.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Something to Put Your Components in

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
The main processor for 1K and 4K cells.

Storing items directly in AE cells is very performant and usually the best option.

Is a component of the crafting CPU multiblock. This particular block provides the CPU with no additional features, but can be used as a "filler" block and as a crafting ingredient for the crafting storage, monitor and co-processing units.

Lowest tier storage cell, which can contain 1,024 bytes of storage. 1,024 bytes of storage can hold 127 stacks of a single item, or 65 stacks, while holding 63 different items. The 1k storage cell uses 8 bytes of data to store a single type.

When placed inside a drive or chest will consume 0.5 AE/t. It must be in an ME drive or ME chest to be usable.

You can remove the 1k ME storage component by fully emptying the storage cell, and sneak-clicking it in your hand.

You can format it in the cell workbench.

Smallest storage component, used to make 1k ME storage cells, or can be upgraded to make 4k ME storage components. Can be recovered from a crafted 1k ME storage cell by fully emptying the storage cell, and shift-clicking it in your hand.

Component of the crafting CPU which provides 1024 bytes of storage for crafting. The Crafting Storage blocks are the only necessary part. Each crafting CPU multiblock allows for a separate crafting job (this is different from sub-tasks of the same job). The more items in the recipe and sub-recipes, the more crafting storage you'll need. Having one big and a couple small might be a good idea, but remember it will try to use the best one available first when you order a craft. They are also used when a crafting card requests a craft, so you'll need several separate ones if you intend to use those a lot. A crafting CPU multiblock uses only one channel, regardless of its size. It must be square to form.

Second tier storage cell, which can contain 4,096 bytes of storage. 4,096 bytes of storage can hold 508 stacks of a single item, or 260 stacks, while holding 63 different items. The 4k storage cell uses 32 bytes of data to store a single type.

When placed inside a drive or chest will consume 1.0 ae/t.

Second smallest storage component, used to make 4k ME storage cells, or can be upgraded to make 16k ME storage components. Can be recovered from a crafted 4k ME storage cell by fully emptying the storage cell, and shift-clicking it in your hand.
Component of the crafting CPU which provides 4,096 bytes of storage for crafting.
The main processor for 16k and 64k cells.
The MV compressor is twice as fast as the LV one but uses 4x the power.
The MV macerator is twice as fast as the LV one but uses 4x the power.
The MV centrifuge is twice as fast as the LV one but uses 4x the power.

Choose the IC2 or the GregTech way to make Biomass. Water and Bio Chaff is needed.

You can also use the Pyrolyze Oven to make Biomass in a more efficient way if you make it.

Note that Forestry has its own Biomass as well. It can also be turned into Fermented Biomass.

The MV fluid extractor is twice as fast as the LV one but uses 4x the power.

To make bio diesel you need seed oil or fish oil. Seeds give seed oil and fish produce fish oil when placed in a fluid extractor.
Time to get more blood. Mobs are a good source for more blood. Transform your knife of sacrifice in your tier 2 altar into a dagger of sacrifice.

Component of the crafting CPU which provides additional item delivery from the CPU to the ME Interface for crafting.

This can be used to make more machines active in parallel for the job, and thus increase overall crafting speed. 

Every Co-Processor adds one AE2 operation per tick. AE2 uses operations to push items to interfaces, this speeds up the rate at which it can push into your machines. As a side benefit, AE2 will split a task between multiple interfaces with the same pattern (or simulated pattern like with P2P Interface). This means if you have two interfaces with the same pattern for the same item AE2 with no co-processors will only push to one of those interfaces until it is full (so, if the craft is small it may not split it at all) whereas with a co-processor it will round robin between the two by splitting its operations per tick.
Save patterns onto these to do autocrafting. They go into molecular assemblers and ME interfaces.

A specialized version of the ME crafting terminal designed to encode blank patterns into encoded patterns.

Lets you browse the contents of your network like other terminals, but also contains an area for designing patterns. There are two modes for pattern encoding. Crafting patterns, and processing patterns. Processing patterns are designed for use with machines that do not use standard crafting recipes - such as furnaces, or other machines. To select between modes, click the button to the right of the interface: when it shows a standard crafting table, it will create crafting patterns, and when it shows a furnace, it will create processing patterns.

For crafting patterns ("Crafts..."), you specify the input crafting materials on a standard 3x3 crafting grid, and the output materials are determined automatically.

For processing patterns ("Creates..."), you specify the input materials and output materials, including quantity, by placing stacks of items in the interface. If a processing operation is not guaranteed to succeed (such as secondary products from some machines), it will not work correctly as a processing pattern.

When designing crafting patterns you can click the output to extract a crafted item as long as you have the materials required to craft the item.

[warn]Be cautious about accidentally enabling oredict substitution, it's rarely used and you will keep it disabled 99% of the time.[/warn]

[note]Works exactly the same with items, fluids, and essentia.[/note]

Wireless Connectors are a close range Quantum Network Bridge alternative.

Connections are point-to-point - you can't connect more than 2 blocks together. Each block will use 10 + distance * ln(distance^2 + 3) AE/t. Does not work across dimensions. Power needs to be provided on only one side. Up to 32 channels can be transferred through the connection. Can connect directly to dense cables. The Wireless Connector itself does not use any channels.

The Wireless Kit can be used to link the connectors together. There are three modes: Simple, Advanced, and Super. In Simple Mode, you §osimply§r right-click your source and target, and they will link. In Advanced Mode, you can do this in queue/binding groups instead of individually. In Super Mode, you can manage the connections through a menu that opens after you right-click.

[note]Also, these are more TPS friendly than large chains of dense cables![/note]

The ME ore dictionary export card will attempt to push the configured item/fluid [From the same ore dictionary] from the ME network into a machine or other input inventory. To configure an item/liquid, type in the item's name [e.g. if you want to export all ores put "ore*"]. The rate of export is very fast.

[note]PS: Use crushed* & !crushedPurified* & !crushedCentrifuged* to get any crushed ore, but not ore that has been washed, then crushed (to get purified) or run through the thermal centrifuge.[/note]

The card can be used in more devices, and causes less lag, but works in a similar way. Put it inside a bus and set the filter using the T looking button that appears.

A small item that can be used to store, copy, and paste settings. Shift-right-click on a configurable object to save the settings onto the memory card, then right-click on any other block of the same type to paste the settings. Shift-right-click on a non-configurable object (or the air) to clear. They are also used to link the input P2P tunnel to the corresponding output P2P tunnels. They can also link Vis Relays to compatible devices.

If you're doing more advanced operations in a large network of P2Ps, it's recommended you use the advanced memory card. It has a helpful UI that allows you to visualize and set names, inputs, and outputs of P2P tunnels. 

[note]Remember P2Ps can only have 1 input! The only exception being fluid P2Ps whose input can function as an output and whose outputs can function as an input.[/note]

[warn]Make sure there aren't any cards in your network tool when you craft the Advanced Memory Card, they will be deleted![/warn]
The power of the sun x10. This solar panel works like 10 regular ones, but costs only 8. How is this possible? Magic! NOTE: They give out GT EU. NO TRANSFORMER NEEDED!

Aren't you tired of voiding all that useless potentia essentia? Well here's the solution:
A generator that consumes potentia and outputs GT EU NO TRANSFORMER NEEDED!
This Generator is quite tricky. It requires Auram Essentia, that isn't that common, but its output is nice.
Compressed Solar Panels can be infused with Aspects for certain additional features. Check them out and choose one of them.
100EU/t for 64x1EU/t Solars? Sounds like a good deal. Get one of these. They can be Infused as well.
You can infuse double or triple compressed solars as well.

Triple Compressed Solars. Yes, that's right. They are a bit more expensive than their lower counterparts, 512 Solars in total. But they give out 1,000 GT EU per tick and have no need to be cleaned. How so? Magic.
So, you got rid of the Potentia, maybe you don't want Ignis, but Potentia? Get this one to be able to burn Ignis.
When using magical plants to get Praecantatio Essentia, you'll end up with a couple dozen of Arbor Essentia jars. But no worries! This generator runs on Arbor! Awesome!
Sugarcanes to power...? This generator runs on Aer Essentia, it might not be as powerful as its counterparts, but its fuel is cheap.
This highly-warped, high-power Essentia generator is a lifesaver, when you run out of energy. Just toss some gold into your Arcane Furnace and burn the Lucrum you get.
You want to fly. Badly. So go and ductape wings!
Since you have access to better materials than cardboard now, you wanted to make wings. Angel wings.
Infusing your Wings with nano technology seems to be the next step, to further improve them and combine magic and technology.
You've heard rumors of a mighty weapon, dropped in Asgard and fallen to earth. Could this be the mystical Item?
betterquesting:10.name:8: Dropped in Asgard, Fallen to Earth

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Sadly enough, the hammer was broken. But you have the skills and the knowledge to repair it, don't you?
Additional tweaks to your Mjolnir have changed it. Now you can summon some Guardian Snowmen to help you out!
As you wander with your Goggles of Revealing you noticed that they tend to break easy. So craft yourself some electric ones that just need to be charged again!
The #1 product for spies and wanna-be-spies. Nano-Goggles. Don't you want one of these too? But they are sold out? Craft some!
As you continue to progress, you notice that your black goggles don't match your nice white and shiny armor. You decide to get a pair of white ones.
This special pair of goggles recharges itself while you wander in sunlight. How convenient.
YELLOW! What an ugly color! I want PURPLE Nitor! Get me some and you'll receive something nice in exchange.

Are you tired of getting all the Ink for your scribing and you don't want to use your blood either? Get this Hi-Tech Scribing Device which will make your life much easier! Treat it like an HV battery - charge in any HV machine's battery slot, or in an HV battery buffer.
From ore to ingot, from nano to quantum, as you progress, your technology level increases, so should your wings as well.

The Angel Wings aren't very protective on their own. Crafting the Infused Quantum Chestplate allows you to combine with the Angel Wings to have a functional and protective combination!

[note]This is still not nearly as good as the other option, the GraviChestPlate.[/note]
While the Hoe of Growth breaks easily, we have a fix for you! Get this one and simply recharge it when it's empty.
This device allows you to charge your wands using EU, but it costs 10kEU per Vis restored.

The Wand Focus: Shield creates a shield around you which blocks any incoming damage and removes potion effects. Sneak away if you're fighting an enemy too strong for you!

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrade in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
betterquesting:10.name:8: Press and Hold the B Button to Block!

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Shield Blocks - explosion proof - single use. Get a couple of these to shield your reactor!
You found a yellow-ish glowing ball. It might be useful later on.
Find a Mjolnir
Find? or make an LS

With your woven silk you can upgrade your Forestry backpacks. Each Pack has 45 slots.

You need a carpenter, your old backpack and a bit of seed oil.

If the recipe isn't working, put the bag in a crafting grid to reset its NBT data. After removing anything in it of course.

If you're in the Twilight Forest and your portal gets broken, you're kinda stuck. Every 24h you're able to exchange some materials to get a new portal crystal to escape.

§3Also consider making an extra yourself and sticking it in a chest on the TF side, just in case.
Every Thaumcraft Infused Stone vein has a bit of amber ore in it. I'm sure you have a bunch by now.

The arcane lamp creates additional light sources which acts like a Torch in a sphere with a radius of 16 blocks centered on it. This will include caves or other areas behind walls. That might be useful...

When attached to the base of an arcane bore, the arcane lamp gains an additional ability: It will light up the tunnel that the bore digs.

The LOX canister is an alternate solution to refilling your oxygen tanks.

To make liquid oxygen you need to put an oxygen cell into a vacuum freezer to get a cell of liquid oxygen. Transfer this liquid oxygen into a tank, and then into a LOX canister.

To refill your oxygen tanks just put the tank and the LOX canister in the oxygen compressor to transfer oxygen, or use an oxygen collector.

Each LOX canister can fill 4 Heavy Oxygen Tanks, 6 Medium Oxygen Tanks, or 12 Light Oxygen Tanks.

So much Greggy!

Wand Focus: Fire is a basic wand focus that is able to spew a short-range cone of fire that deals damage and sets mobs ablaze.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§5Potency§r: Increases damage dealt every level
§5Alchemist's Fire§r (even levels): Hit mobs burn for longer and lights blocks on fire
§5Fireball§r (level 3): The focus now shoots a large, explosive ball of fire which sets the ground on fire if paired with §5Alchemist's Fire§r
§5Fire Beam§r (level 3): Concentrates the cone of fire into a beam that does more damage and shoots farther
betterquesting:10.name:8: I Don't Want to Set the World on Fire

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
The Wand Focus: Excavation emits a green beam of light that will mine blocks of any hardness (except for unbreakable blocks like Bedrock) from a distance.

This focus is also required to operate the Arcane Bore. Upgrading foci to be used in the Bore with §5Enlarge§r is highly recommended, as it increases the radius by 1 per level.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§5Potency§r: Increases block breaking speed every level
§5Treasure§r: Acts like vanilla Fortune
§5Enlarge§r (even levels): Breaks an extra adjacent block per level
§5Dowsing§r (level 3): May drop Thaumcraft Native Ores from ores, but does not apply to GT ores
§5Silk Touch§r (level 5): Acts like vanilla Silk Touch

The Wand Focus: Shock will shoot a bolt of lightning. It homes in slightly to the nearest mob/player from where it is aimed. It is even fast enough to hit Endermen before they can teleport away!

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§5Potency§r: Increases damage dealt every level
§5Chain Lightning§r (level 3): The lightning bolt now arcs to two nearby creatures. Great for dealing with bats from warp!
§5Earth Shock§r (level 3): The focus now shoots a ball of lightning that leaves the ground electrified
§5Enlarge§r (requires §5Chain Lightning§r): The lightning bolt arcs to two additional targets per level. Show those bats who's boss!

Wand Focus: Equal Trade is able to switch out blocks in the world with blocks in the player's inventory. Shift-right-click on a block to attune the focus to the block. Once attuned to a block, left-click on a single block to replace it with the substitute block. Right-click will transform a contiguous 5x5x5 area of the same block that has air on at least one side. This can go through thin walls or into caves, so be careful. Very useful for upgrading EBF coils or for swapping other blocks that are slow to break like Obsidian! It cannot be used to break or place blocks with Tile Entities like chests.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§5Enlarge§r: Expands the maximum range by 1 block in each direction per level
§5Treasure§r (level 3): Works like vanilla Fortune
§5Architect§r (level 3): Allows the focus's working area to be modified with the Misc Wand Toggle keybind. Sneaking with the keybind changes which axes are modified. This upgrade also changes the working area to a plane, so be sure to test this upgrade out before committing to it and applying further upgrades
§5Silk Touch§r (level 5): Works like vanilla Silk Touch

The Wand Focus: Frost will launch a ball of ice that can bounce off of blocks and mobs.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§5Potency§r: Increases damage dealt every level
§5Alchemist's Frost§r (odd levels): Applies Slowness to hit mobs. Higher levels increase the potency of the effect
§5Scattershot§r (level 3): The focus now shoots a volley of shards that break on impact. The normal damage immunity timer is ignored, so multiple shards can hit the same mob at once and all will deal damage. §5Potency§r increases the number of shards instead of the damage
§5Ice Boulder§r (level 3): The focus now shoots a larger, bouncier, and deadlier ball of ice

The Wand Focus: Warding can be used to make blocks invincible with right-click. Warding may be removed by right-clicking it again. It is not able to ward transparent blocks like Glass or non-full blocks like slabs, but there is a block known as Warded Glass available with the Warded Arcana research if you want a protected transparent block. It is also unable to ward blocks with Tile Entities like chests. Take note that only the player who warded the block can unward it.

Holding a wand with this focus will show an outline on nearby blocks you have warded. They look normal otherwise. Warded Blocks are [note]completely indestructible[/note] and will produce particle effects similar to runic shielding when a player tries to break them. Blocks will lose any special properties when warded: sand or gravel will not fall, grass will not grow, and packed ice will no longer be slippery. Warded blocks cannot be affected by any outside influence such as redstone or pistons. The only way to break the warded block is via the owner right-clicking with a wand with this focus.

[note]Special Note: Warded blocks emit light. They can also cause quite a bit of lag if used at scale.[/note]

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§
§5Architect§r (level 2): Allows the focus's working area to be modified with the Misc Wand Toggle keybind. Sneaking with the keybind changes which axes are modified. This upgrade increases the maximum area to 7x7x7
§5Enlarge§r (Requires §5Architect§r)§r: Expands the maximum range by 1 block in each direction per level

The Wand Focus: Portable Hole will create a temporary 3x3x32 hole centered on the targeted block. Some blocks cannot be passed through, such as Bedrock or blocks warded by the Wand Focus: Warding.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§5Enlarge§r: Extends the hole by 8 blocks per level
§5Extend§r: The hole will stay open 3 seconds longer for every level
betterquesting:10.name:8: Keep it Away from Bags of Holding

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
When transporting oil from long distances, a train is going to need a chunk loader. Craft one, and I'll give you a second one for free.

[note]This quest might not be completable in MP?[/note]

The Wand Focus: Pech's Curse is a rare wand focus which cannot be crafted by players. It can only be obtained from a Pech Mage -- either by bartering valuable items or by killing it for its wand to drop. Pech Mages are rare and the drop chance is quite low, so bartering is recommended. [warn]If attacked, the Pech will use this focus against you![/warn]

This focus fires a small ball of energy with a bright bluish-green trail. This missile is affected by gravity, so the shots need to be "arced" to hit distant targets. When the shot hits a mob, it does one heart of damage and randomly inflicts one of several effects on the target: Poison, Weakness, or Slowness.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§5Potency§r: Increases potency of the applied effect. Being able to apply Weakness III to mobs might be useful for Blood Magic...
§5Extend§r (even levels): Extends the duration of the applied effect
§5Nightshade§r (level 5): Applies all three effects at once

The Wand Focus: Primal will hurl an orb of primal energy with right-click. The orb explodes on impact, and it has a small chance to cause other effects. It sometimes creates taint when it lands, and it very rarely creates a node if it destroys the block it impacts. Its base vis cost constantly fluctuates. [note]Maybe studying it and its projectiles will give you a better understanding of vis.[/note]

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§5Seeker§r (level 3): The orb homes in on the closest target, but loses some of its special effects like creating taint or nodes

The Focal Manipulator requires both XP levels and centi-vis in order to upgrade foci. Each focus can be upgraded a total of five times, with the level cost increasing by 8 and the vis cost doubling for each upgrade.

Most foci accept Frugal (lowers the vis cost to cast by 10% per level) and Potency (increases damage dealt or improves the focus in another way if it doesn't deal damage) at every level. Foci with an area of effect (like Wand Focus: Equal Trade) accept Enlarge, which usually expands the max area by one block in each direction. Some foci have special upgrades that can only be applied at certain levels (often level 3 or 5), some of which have prerequisite upgrades. See the Focus on Wand Foci & EMT tab for more information about focal upgrades and their effects.

If you regret your past decisions, you can remove upgrades in the Focal Manipulator if you have the Focal Disenchanting research. It will even refund some of the XP!

The advanced node stabilizer acts like a normal node stabilizer but with key differences. It will still stop the node it affects from being drained but the node can still drain from other, lesser nodes. It also has a higher chance to improve fading and unstable nodes. The downside is that any nodes it affects will have their recharge rates effectively reduced to nothing. They will recharge at an extremely reduced rate.
Rockets require heavy duty plates for the main hull. Let's craft 13 tier 4 heavy duty plates out of tier 3 plates and compressed ice plates.

Callisto Ice is a material you need for Tier 4 Rockets. Look for it at Y 40-60. You can also find platinum series and radioactive ores here.

[note]You can also find Mytryl and Ledox here as small ores.[/note]

Ledox is a material you need for Tier 4 Rockets which can be found on Europa. Look for it at Y 55-65. You can also find Chrome, Molybdenum, Manganese, Tungstate and Rubracium, among others.

[note]You can also get Ledox from small ores on Callisto.[/note]

After weeks of hard work and a thousand stacks of iTNT your fourth rocket is finally ready.

You need to use Dense Hydrazine Rocket Fuel.

Wand Focus: Efreet's Flame shoots a beam similar to the Wand Focus: Excavation that smelts blocks like a Furnace.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrade in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level

Wand Focus: Dislocation is a very useful focus that allows its user to take and place nearly any block, even Tile Entities and one that usually can't be moved, like Mob Spawners, planted crops, and more.

[warn]Please use responsibly, and don't move things you shouldn't, like door halves, or some multiblock parts, unless you like the idea of world corruption destroying your world. That said, if you're in SP and make a backup, do whatever you want, just know the risks.[/warn]

It uses:
5 Ordo + 5 Perditio + 1 Terra to take any mundane block.
25 Ordo + 25 Perditio + 5 Terra to take any block with a tile entity (such as a Chest).
100 Ordo + 100 Perditio + 20 Terra to take a Mob Spawner.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrade in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level

The Wand Focus: Mending is a wand focus that will slowly mend the caster's wounds by expending Vis. It heals half a heart at a time. It's an invaluable tool in a Blood Mage's arsenal.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§5Potency§r: Increases healing by half a heart per level.

The Wand Focus: Uprising propels its caster forward. It works well to gain height to glide for long distances or to scale tall obstacles. Fall damage is only reset when cast, so be careful when using it!

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrade in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level

The Wand Focus: Distortion protects the caster from "ordinary" projectiles such as arrows, snowballs, and potions while right-click is held.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§5Enlarge§r (even levels): Expands the projectile deflection range by 1 block in each direction per level

The Wand Focus: Ender Rift opens your vanilla Personal Ender Chest when used. It can also be attuned to an Ender Chest from Ender Storage with shift-right-click. Shift-right-click a block of obsidian to set it back to your Personal Ender Chest.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrade in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level

The Wand Focus: Telekinesis is a wand focus that can move nearby dropped items. It either moves them where you are pointing with the wand or toward you while sneaking.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrade in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level

The Wand Focus: Experience Drain will drain the player's experience every tick, using 15 XP to restore 5 vis to the lowest aspect in the wand.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers experience cost per tick by 1 per level
§5Potency§r: Creates 20% more vis per level

The Wand Focus: Shadowbeam shoots a beam of dark energy that is reflected by any block and damages everything it passes through. The beam travels about 40 blocks and does about 100 damage.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§5Potency§r: Increases damage dealt every level

The Wand Focus: Tainted Storm will emit a stream of tainted bubbles which damage anything in a short distance and inflict Poison for 5 seconds. The focus may also debuff the caster with Flux Flu III for 50 seconds.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§5Potency§r: Increases damage dealt and increases the number of bubbles every level
§5Tainturgy§r (level 3): The caster will no longer get Flux Flu. This adds 0.6 Ordo to the casting cost
§5Enlarge§r (level 4): The tainted bubbles fan out across a wider area. This adds 0.6 Aer and Aqua to the casting cost
§5Corrosive§r (level 5): The tainted bubbles inflict the Wither effect instead of Poison. This adds 0.6 Perditio and Ignis to the casting cost

The Wand Focus: Tainted Shockwave will release a powerful shockwave around the caster which travels 10 blocks away, damaging all mobs in the radius and launching them into the air. After using this focus, the caster will be unable to use any other foci for 6 seconds.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§5Potency§r: Increases damage dealt every level
§5Enlarge§r: Increases the radius by 2 blocks per level. This also adds 2.5 Perditio, Terra, and Aqua to the casting cost per level

The Wand Focus: Vis Shard can be used to cast a homing projectile which deals 35 damage. This projectile can bounce off of solid blocks. If the target is not hit in 10 seconds, the projectile disappears.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§5Potency§r: Increases damage dealt every level
§5Persistent§r (level 5): The shard will seek another target if its current one dies or gets out of range

The Wand Focus: Dark Matter allows its wielder to shoot the same projectiles as Eldritch Guardians. There is a chance for the caster to gain sticky warp for each projectile cast.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§5Potency§r: Increases damage dealt every level
§5Corrosive§r (level 3): The orbs now inflict the Wither effect upon their targets
§5Sanity§r (level 5): The caster will not gain warp from using this focus
betterquesting:10.name:8: A Taste of Their Own Medicine

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
The Wand Focus: Time can be used to move time forward by 12 hours. Using this focus at noon will set the time to midnight, while using it at dusk will make it dawn. This focus will also make the player unable to use any other foci for 30 seconds.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrade in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
betterquesting:10.name:8: So Take Me Back in Time...

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
The Wand Focus: Meteorology can be used to start or stop rain at will. The perfect thing for Water Infused Solar Panels!

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrade in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level

The Wand Focus: Mage's Mace can be equipped by any wand and will boost its attack damage to 30 hearts. Equipping it to a staff will deal double damage.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrades in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
§5Potency§r: Increases damage dealt every level
§5Bloodlust§r (level 5): Slain mobs may drop Crystal Blood like when killed with a Crystal Dagger

The Wand Focus: Blink is a very powerful focus that allows its user to teleport anywhere in sight, as long as the destination is less than 50 blocks away. There is no teleport cooldown, so it can be used to travel very quickly in the right conditions.

[note]This focus accepts the following upgrade in the Focal Manipulator:[/note]
§5Frugal§r: Lowers vis cost to cast by 10% per level
Try to add Potency to your Shock Focus. At Level 3 you can add Chain Lightning or Shock Wave.
Enderium screws are nice, but they seem to break if too much vis channels through them. Get some Oriharukon screws.

Using Steam as your single power source in HV is pretty difficult. Your fuel automation will have to be very fast, your pipes will have to be very big and the final efficiency of HV Steam Turbines is 66%, much lower than the other generators' 85%.

This is best used with an efficient furnace, like the GT++ Advanced Furnaces, to power something specific like a farm. Powering your entire automation in your path to an EV, using only these, is a nightmare. If you want more efficiency out of your Steam, consider building a Large Steam Turbine.

How about lossless 128 EU Wires? Pentacadmiummagnesiumhexaoxide is a superconductor wire and will transfer your energy without any loss. Every Voltage going forward has a superconductor wire with zero loss.

Mix Cadmium, Magnesium and Oxygen in an MV mixer. Next, the base dust needs an EBF with Kanthal Coils to be smelted. Make some MV Superconductor Base Wires and use an Assembler to combine these wires with Helium, Stainless Steel pipes and MV pumps to get your 128 EU/t superconductor wires.

[note]Whether these are worth it to save a little power or not is up to you of course. Also note that although they're wires, you aren't hurt by coming into contact with them.[/note]

How about lossless 512 EU Wires? Titaniumonabariumdecacoppereikosaoxide is a superconductor wire and will transfer your energy without any loss.

You'll need Nichrome Coils and an HV Assembler.

[note]Whether these are worth it to save a little power or not is up to you of course.[/note]
An EV assembler is required to make lapotron crystals, coils, and other stuff.
An EV precision laser is required to make quantum crystals.

How about lossless 2048 EU Wires? Uraniumtriplatinide is a superconductor wire and will transfer your energy without any loss.

You'll need TPV Coils.

[note]Whether these are worth it to save a little power or not is up to you of course.[/note]

How about lossless 8192 EU Wires? Vanadiumtriindinide is a superconductor wire and will transfer your energy without any loss.

From now on, SCs are not optional, you need to make them to craft stuff.

An IV mixer is required for example to mix HSS-S dust or to make IV superconductors.

You can also check out the Mass Processing tab and make a multiblock mixer out of this one.

Platinum, Palladium, Iridium and Osmium can be extracted with a chemical reaction from Chalcopyrite and Pentlandite using sulfuric acid. You don't have the technology to process them properly right now but later on you need large amounts of them.

Note that this is not the proper method to get rare metals. This means none of them are pure, and cannot be utilized without the platline method, aside from EBF-ing platinum. Proper Platinum processing is EV, but you'll have to wait until IV to use the rest. Collecting a lot of it now (especially using this method) might not be a great idea depending on how long that will be.

[note]A Chemical Bath also extracts Platinum from Nickel Ore if you use Mercury. Time to head back to the Twilight Forest![/note]

The Assembly Line (or 'Assline') is an important machine for high tier components in LuV tier and above for making Motors, Pistons, Robot Arms, Pumps and many more.

The multiblock can be 5-16 blocks long. The minimum length required depends on the number of components and fluids required by the recipe it's crafting. A length of 11 blocks will fit 80 percent of all recipes in GTNH.

The bottom layer must have on one outer side all the Input Hatches for fluids (4), in the bottom middle layer Input Buses for items (10), and on the end 1 Output Bus. Also on the bottom outer layer must be one Maintenance Hatch. The rest is Solid Steel Machine Casings.

The second layer on the outer sides left and right are Reinforced Glass and in the middle center Assembly Line Casing.

The third layer has on the left and right Grate Machine Casings and in the middle Assembler Machine Casings (Note the name change!). The Assembly Line control block and Data Access Hatch are on the opposite edge from the Input Hatches - not at the end with the Output Bus.

The fourth layer is a single line of Solid Steel Machine Casings in the middle (11), with two Energy Hatches for power. Once you have it built, you can replace the two IV energy hatches with 1 LuV energy hatch.

Automating the assline is a difficult challenge! You can use advanced tools like SFM or OpenComputers, but maybe you can figure out how to do it with EnderIO or just AE2.

For more details on using the Assembly Line, check out the wiki page [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Assembly_Line[/url]

[note]BTW the input buses are ULV to help with your automating, if you don't want to automate it, you can use higher tier ones, unlike the CAL.[/note]

[note]You can have up to 16 input buses. If you use the full 16 you should put the output bus to the side.[/note]

[note]When using buses of a higher tier than ULV it will look for items starting at the top left slot, down to the bottom right slot.[/note]
Pumps, pistons, conveyor modules and robot arms are the most needed machine parts in IV. Go and craft one of each.
Some machines need Emitters and Sensors, like the Scanner or the Circuit Assembler.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §9§lYou're Gonna Hate This 5 and 6 in IV

betterquesting:10.desc:8: If you want pure uranium ores for your nuke, you'll need to visit Deimos or Phobos to fetch them. They're at Y 20-30.

Or is it Alloy Blast Smelter? Well, that makes more sense. This multiblock creates the higher tier alloys needed for more advanced multiblocks and your soldering needs. It directly smelts ingredients into liquids. You can even melt down metals like Tungsten faster too! Until you get better coils for your EBF at least.

[note]Most of the multiblocks you can now make are optional, but quite powerful upgrades to your current singleblock setups. Not only do they provide more speed, they also have a bit of advanced functionality: you can also electrolyze materials without using cells or use a single multiblock for many different extruder shapes. They also act as cleanrooms where needed.[/note]

Birds falling out of the sky, fish dead and floating belly up in the rivers, acid rain melting the ground...Time to start picking up the trash and cleaning up the air. Small black steel turbines should be fine for now. You'll need two amps of steady power to keep the scrubber working.

The detector's setting can be changed by clicking on the +/- texture with a screwdriver. Also, in general, better (and larger) turbines work better at cleaning up pollution. The code is too complex to fully explain here, but that's basically it. More EU turbine = more pollution cleaning turbine.

[warn]This quest covers one method of combating pollution - there are others, including not making as much to begin with.[/warn]
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lCough Cough - Something Needs to Be Done About the Smell

betterquesting:10.desc:8: ...in my dreams. What if instead of having battery packs on every generator, we could centralize all the generation in one location? Put it away from the well traveled parts of the base? Out in the country somewhere? Let the animals deal with the pollution. Anyways, let's start working on a Power Sub-Station to store EU and deliver it to our base.

...when it means you don't have to strip naked to recharge your nanosuit?
The Wireless Charger will keep your armor and tools charged up without having to put them into a battery buffer.

It will charge armor and tools at the tier and below.

You didn't want kids anyways...
betterquesting:10.name:8: Who Cares About a Little Cancer...

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
...out of the purified ores. Anyway, a §5§lLarge Sifter§r grants §6§l4§r parallels per voltage tier and will increase your sifting speed by §2§l5x§r. It will also give you a §3§l25%§r discount on all recipes.

What will you do with all these gems?

Mass destruction! Or at least, lots and lots of crushed ores. Build an §5§lIndustrial Maceration Stack§r to keep up with all the ores you are getting.

This processes items at §2§l1.6x§r the speed and with up to §6§l2§r parallels per voltage tier.

[note]In IV you can upgrade the multi with an upgrade chip and better casings.[/note]

...go round and round, all the live long day. A large ore washing plant gets your rocks nice and clean. 

The §5§lOre Washing Plant§r gives a §2§l5x§r speed boost and §6§l4§r parallels per voltage tier compared to its singleblock counterpart.

Spinning around, getting hot - sounds like a dance. Or a thermal centrifuge. Build a §5§lLarge Thermal Refinery§r to get the most out of your ores.

Unlike with the singleblock, you get a base §2§l2.5x§r speed bonus and a §3§l20%§r EU discount on all recipes. You unlock an extra §n§l5%§r increase to both speed and EU discount per coil tier.

As a bonus, the LTR provides §6§l8§r parallels per voltage tier, and §6§l2§r additional parallels per tier of solenoid on top of that.

[note]Glass tier is irrelevant; use what works best for you![/note]
You actually get more Ilmenite from the Bauxite Vein. But maybe you are here for the Chromite?

To reach tier two planets like Mars or its moons, Phobos and Deimos you need a better rocket. Your next goal is Tier two rocket plates which need Meteoric Iron.

You will find small meteoric iron ore under the surface. Use an HV miner or multiblock miner to get extra fortune on small ores. Small meteoric iron is only from Y 50-70, so try to find tall hills.

You can also just mine the fallen meteors on the surface. Use your ears to listen to their impacts.

Rockets require heavy duty plates for the main hull. Let's craft 11 tier 2 heavy duty plates out of tier 1 plates and meteoric iron plates.

You'll need to make a couple of tungstensteel ingots to make these plates. You can process end stone or end stone dust, or macerate moon blocks to get some.
Each rocket needs a Control Computer, appropriate to the tier of the rocket.
After hours of hard work and tons of stacks of iTNT your second rocket is finally ready. But before you can go to Mars you need to craft a few more things.

Why not recycle your old Tier 1 rocket to get components for your new tier 2 rocket? Put your old rocket in an arc furnace to get back lots of materials.

Make sure you don't need it anymore first!
betterquesting:10.name:8: Recycle Your Rocket and Save the Environment

betterquesting:10.desc:8: The distance between Mars and Earth is much larger than to the Moon, so the rocket needs boosters to reach it.

The Mars lander is required for a soft landing. Put the Moon lander on a Parachute and surround it with airbags - that will do the trick. You hope.

Hint: Sometimes you can't loot or break the lander. Try to retrieve the contents with a hopper underneath. To prevent this, make sure to wait until you come to a full and complete stop, like when at a stop sign. Everyone does that, right?

While looking around for meteoric iron you might find a moon dungeon. The entrance looks like a deep hole. Go and kill the Boss Monster. It will drop the key for the chest in the next room with the schematics for tier 2 rockets.

Kill the Boss Monster again in a different dungeon if you want an extra tier 2 schematic to exchange for a moon buggy schematic.

Place the schematic in the NASA Workbench and unlock it on the last tab. This will unlock it for your character, so you can move the workbench if you want.

[note]All dungeons work the same, just with a different boss. Also, sometimes the boss room or chest room doesn't generate, you'll need to find another dungeon.[/note]
Moving faster on the Moon or other planets surface will be fun. I'm sure it will be totally safe.

The moon buggy needs a schematic. Place it in the NASA workbench and unlock it on the last tab.

[note]If you've made the chip in an older version, you can turn it back into a schematic in a PLE.[/note]
The moon buggy needs fuel to work. Build a 3x3 fueling pad, connect it with a fuel loader, and place the buggy on top.
The Medium oxygen tank is an oxygen storage tank that can hold up to 2000 units of air.

You decided to have a longer stay on the moon and look for a permanent oxygen setup to refill your outdoor gear and building a small Base.

Don't forget to bring repair stuff for your tools and armor! Dream 2018!

The Oxygen Bubble Distributor takes oxygen from the Oxygen Collector, and makes an oxygen bubble providing an area to safely breathe in without needing Oxygen Gear. The bubble is a sphere surrounding the distributor and will go through walls (or any block). Alternatively, you can use an Oxygen Sealer (which needs compressed Desh Plates) to contain oxygen inside a room.

Normal torches won't work in space, only in the area within the oxygen bubble.

One solution is glowstone torches. You can also use other mods' lights and lamps. You'll probably want 3-5 stacks for mining veins, unless you just use a singleblock or multiblock miner.

Another option is to use nightvision and a magnum torch or GregTech monster repellator to keep mobs away. These do not work on the official servers, instead claim and unclaim chunks.
The compressed steel armor has more durability than the steel armor.
The compressed desh armor has more durability than the compressed steel armor.
The compressed titanium armor has more durability than the compressed steel armor.

The Moon's day-night cycle is 2h 40min long, equaling 8 Overworld days and it is linked to the Moon phases seen on the Overworld. The daytime on the moon lasts from a full moon to the next new moon (4 Overworld days, equaling 1h 20min) and, logically, the nighttime lasts from the new moon to the next full moon.

Since the 1st Overworld night is full moon, you can safely land within the 1st 4 Overworld days, and then the next 4 Overworld days are more dangerous since hostile mobs will be able to spawn in the dark, and so on. If you miscount, the moon phases can tell you when it is daytime or nighttime on the moon. Full moon is the start of the moon day, new (or dark) moon is the start of the moon night.

During the nighttime, the environment light levels get very low, allowing hostile mobs to spawn on the surface.

The Mars dungeon works the same as last time, so go find it!

If you need the schematics for the astro miner or the cargo rocket, kill another Boss Monster and exchange the schematics.
Before you journey home make sure you fulfill the quest requirements in the EV tab.
The astro miner needs a schematic.
Each rocket needs a Control Computer, appropriate to the tier of the rocket.

The Cargo Rocket has the capability to transport solid items between dimensions, and is a perfect way to transport items between dimensions without relying on ender chests.

This rocket can be loaded with 2000L of Rocket Fuel. The safe fuel level is 80 percent.

You can fill up the right slots with chests to increase the storage space to 36 and 54 slots.

The Astro Miner is an automatic mining vehicle which moves around, makes tunnels, mines up everything it finds, and brings it all back to a base station where it docks. It is not player-rideable, so don't try and climb inside it!

It's not very fast or efficient, and it seems to discard half or more of the ore it attempts to collect. Only consider using it if you want the huge amount of planet blocks it picks up.[/note]

To construct the dock, place 8 Astro Miner Base blocks in a cube, 2 blocks high, 2 blocks wide and 2 blocks deep. When the last of the base blocks is placed, it should automatically convert into an Astro Miner Base.

The Launch Controller has been modified in GTNH to provide additional functionality. If you launch from a Launch Pad with the Launch Controller set up, the countdown will be greatly reduced, and you will teleport directly to the receiving Launch Pad. It will use half the rocket's fuel up though. This is very useful on laggy servers and can act as an early teleport option if you don't like the magical solutions. You will need to set up a Rocket Launch Pad with Launch Controller and possibly a Fuel Loader on either side.

If you don't to use it for yourself, you can also try to use it for the Cargo Rocket. To use those at full capacity it is necessary to equip a Rocket Launch Pad, to send items, with:

Fuel Loader
Launch Controller
Cargo Loader
And the receiving side with:

Fuel Loader
Launch Controller
Cargo Unloader

It is also possible to use Buildcraft pipes to transfer items into the Cargo loaders. Next step is to set up the Frequencies in both Launch Controllers (i.e. Set: A to target B, B to target A). Have a look at Launch Controller to set up the automated launch. The first time you have to right-click the Cargo rocket and press launch at the top right corner.
Rockets require heavy duty plates for the main hull. Let's craft 38 tier 3 heavy duty plates out of tier 2 plates and desh plates.

After days of hard work and a hundred tons of stacks of iTNT your third rocket is finally ready.

You need to use Dense Hydrazine Rocket Fuel or better to fuel it.
The Tier 3, or Deep Space lander is required for a soft landing.
Every rocket needs a nose cone. Tier 3 rocket needs a heavy nose cone.
Every rocket needs a rocket engine. A heavy one is needed in the tier 3 and 4 rockets.
Every rocket needs a few rocket fins. Tier 3 rockets need heavy ones.
Every rocket needs fuel storage canisters. For the tier 3 rocket you need to craft two small and two medium canisters.

Don't want to guess at what has what aspect? Just want to get to work? Then scan this stuff. The first set should be scanned in order. If any of them don't work, try scanning something else first (especially the third set).

Watering Can
Torch
Coal

Cognito + Ordo

betterquesting:10.name:8: Just Tell Me What to Scan Already!

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Thermal Padding is a set of garments made out of an advanced insulating material. The garments are able to keep a player from freezing to death in the cold environments of Outer Space. They are also able to keep the player from suffering heat exhaustion in an overly hot environment.

The temperature indicator on the Life Support HUD will show if the player is becoming too hot or too cold - as the temperature approaches dangerous levels, an "Invalid Thermal Protection" warning will be shown. On Mars and the Asteroids, simply wearing a full set of Thermal Padding should be enough to fix this.

[note]You'll also need some Silicone Rubber.[/note]

The Cryogenic Chamber is used to sleep on other planets and skip long nighttimes. It can be used at any time, even during the daytime, and in any dimension, including the Overworld.
