Using the chamber during the daytime will skip the time to the next sunrise, except on the Asteroids dimension where the Sun is always locked on West.

Once the player has used the Cryogenic Chamber, there is a 300 second cooldown before they can use it again. Breaking and replacing the chamber, or trying to use a different chamber, will not reset the cooldown unless the player dies.

The chamber does not require energy to work.

The Arc Lamp is a very bright lamp. It is directional - meaning the light it casts is brighter in the direction it is facing. Its facing can be rotated using a standard Wrench.

Including the Arc Lamp the brightness of blocks which are close to light sources is:

Redstone Torch: 3-6
Torch: 9-12
Block of Glowstone: 10-13
Arc Lamp: 13-14

The Arc Lamp can light up a fairly large area - for example a whole room - at light level 14: it is almost as bright as full sunlight.

The Arc Lamp also has the interesting property of actively repelling mobs. Not only does its light prevent mobs from spawning nearby, but it is so bright that if a mob comes close to the Arc Lamp the mob will turn around and walk away again. This mob-repellant effect is confirmed to work on: Zombies, Skeletons, Creepers, Evolved Zombies, Evolved Skeletons, Evolved Creepers. It may also work on other types of mobs (confirmation required). But it has no effect on Spiders (they are not afraid of sunlight either) or boss mobs.

An airlock is an airtight door used to provide a passage between enclosed rooms and between an enclosed room and outer space. It is made from Air Lock Frames and one Air Lock Controller.

The airlock will keep air inside the room while it is closed. But when the airlock is open, the room is no longer sealed and oxygen gear must be worn until the airlock is closed. In environments with extreme temperatures, Thermal Padding must also be worn.

The Ambient Thermal Controller is an item for use in the Oxygen Sealer to provide thermal protection in sealed spaces.

An Ambient Thermal Controller is useful in the dimensions too cold or too hot for players to survive without Thermal Padding.

It can be placed in the 3rd slot next to the energy and oxygen slots in a working Oxygen Sealer. Once the Ambient Thermal Controller is in the sealer, it will heat or cool the output oxygen according to the local environment, and then the player can safely take the thermal padding off in the sealed room. Though there's absolutely no reason to do so.

The Oxygen Sealer is a machine that fills a room with oxygen (although the oxygen is generally not visible) up to around 800-1000 blocks (the amount stacks with multiple sealers within close proximity) allowing the user to breathe without Oxygen Gear. Unlike the Oxygen Bubble Distributor, the Oxygen Sealer confines the oxygen to the room it is in. The sealer must be supplied with power and sufficient oxygen. See Oxygen Collector for supplying oxygen.

The sealer will only work in a room that is completely sealed off from outer space. This can be achieved with either a completely closed off room, or with an Air Lock. The sealer must have nothing above it to block its vents. It is designed to check for a proper seal about every 5 seconds, so be sure to give it time to seal.

Each sealer requires at least 320 air points per second to work continuously or it will fail.
The Heavy oxygen tank is an oxygen storage tank that can hold up to 4000 units of air.

Bacterial Sludge is a fluid block that generates naturally on Mars.

It generates in the giant underground caves in Mars in small amounts.

Collect it to produce mutagen for bees mutation in gendustry.

Cavernous Vine is a poisonous plant that grows naturally in the Mars underground. It grows from the ceiling down to the floor in the huge caves flooded with Bacterial Sludge, emits light and can trap mobs in it.

Any mob that touches this plant will be poisoned, dragged up and lose health down to 1 health point (half a heart) while trapped in this plant. Mobs that are immune to poison, like Zombies and Skeletons, will not lose health.

They grow from the bottom face of a solid block down to 1 block away from the floor.

Cavernous vines can be broken by hand without taking damage or being poisoned but they will drop nothing. They can be obtained as an item using shears. Even picks with Silk Touch enchant will not obtain anything.

Once obtained, they can be replanted elsewhere and regrow, like cactus.

[note]That said, they're still useless.[/note]

The Slimeling is a utility mob that spawns from Slimeling Eggs found on the surface of Mars. It shares some features from vanilla wolves and mules: it can be tamed and attacks mobs that threaten its owners, and can be equipped with a special chest to transport items.

As an allied mob, Slimelings will actively help and follow the player-owner and will attempt to protect them. They can also have a neutral behavior, that is, they can attack if provoked or hurt by non-owners.

Items that you can feed Slimelings with:

Boat
Cooked fish
Gunpowder
Gold ingot
Redstone repeater
Wooden door

Slimelings can be equipped by their owners with a Slimeling Inventory Bag to transport items.

To complete this quest get any one of the eggs - note you may need a Heavy Duty Pickaxe.

The Grapple is a grappling hook and rope which can be thrown by a player, and then used to swing the player in the direction it was thrown. Useful for reaching places that are otherwise too high to jump to, or traveling around the Asteroids. [note](Or just, you know, fly.)[/note]

Right-click to aim the Grapple at a block you want to reach, similar to aiming a Bow. Release the right-click - similar to firing an arrow from a bow - to grapple yourself in that direction.

For best results, aim the Grapple at a point 1 or 2 blocks higher than the point you want to reach.

If there is no safe platform to land at that point, you can fall back down and you will take fall damage, so it takes some skill to use the Grapple safely.

Take care using the Grapple near a Nether Portal, End Portal or at a low height (less than Y30) on a Space Station. There can be strange consequences if it crosses into another dimension.

These thermal clothes will keep you nice and warm even in the coldest depths of outer space. Tier 3+ planets pretty much all require these.

[note]You'll also need some PBI.[/note]

Or at least play with drums? If you have extra Meteoric Iron after building your rocket and making your thermal padding, turn it into Meteoric Steel and use it to make some drums. These drums can hold 256 buckets even after breaking.

And did you know you can use them as cells? Try loading or unloading a supertank!

What the...? You noticed that sometimes when you kill something, even a cow or chicken, it explodes! What madness!

To stop it, use a proper GregTech Knife or Butchery Knife to kill them. Craft a flint GregTech knife with a stick and a piece of flint.

To see its recipe, see how a generic knife is made - NEI should show you many pages. The recipe you need should be on the last page. You can scroll pages with your mouse wheel.

[note]Alternatively you can use the search bar to search for a specific tool material, in this case flint![/note]

As a reward, here's an iron knife to use once the flint one wears out.

This knife is not going to work for slaughtering the hundreds of animals you will need for food and materials. Make yourself a GregTech Butchery Knife. It stops the explosions, and kills the cows much faster, not to mention has Looting on it. Later when you get Stainless Steel, you can make a new one that will kill cows in one hit.

Note that the GT Tool damage is based on tinkers mining level.
The sixth item you'll need a lot of, namely for the Scanner and the Seismic Prospector.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lYou're Gonna Hate This in MV Too #6

betterquesting:10.desc:8: The fifth item you'll need a lot of. For the microwave, the scanner, the precision laser engraver, etc.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lYou're Gonna Hate This in MV Too #5

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Radon is needed for EV Emitters and Sensors.

You can get Radium-226 from sifting Thorium, Pitchblende, Uraninite, or Uranium 238. It needs 4500 seconds, or 75 mins, to decay, and it will debuff you unless you have complete hazmat protection. It's a good idea to make a Lead-Lined Box and let the Radium decay there.

Thorium can be obtained from the Nether, whereas the other 3 ores are locked after the Tier 2 Rocket. However, Thorium gives a much smaller chance of getting Radium, so you'll need a good amount of it to continue.

After it decays, you can electrolyze Radon out of it and progress into the next circuit line. However, you will not be able to do the Radon loop here, that can only be done with Plutonium 239.

[note]You only need to fulfill one of the listed material requirements.[/note]

The Extreme Combustion Engine is an upgrade to the Large Combustion Engine, the IV version that needs Tungstensteel instead of Titanium. The structure is essentially the same, and it's almost a 1:1 ratio between the two materials, so this is a good generator when you've accumulated several stacks of Tungstensteel.

The caveat is that it only accepts High Octane Gasoline. This is the last and most powerful type of combustion fluid made from Oil, and it has the longest processing line of them all. As a reward, it has an excellent §a2.5M EU per bucket§r, and you can burn it here alongside some Liquid Oxygen for almost §a4 IV amps per tick.

§cThe Liquid Oxygen is very important, because it greatly boosts the speed of the multi and the fuel efficiency as well.§r It needs 40 L/s, so you will need more than one Vacuum Freezer to supply it continuously: for an ECE that is always running, you will need a double Vacuum Freezer, 1 EV and 1 HV. You can run fewer freezers if you overclock them, if the ECE isn't working all the time or if you upgrade to a Cryogenic Freezer,
betterquesting:10.name:8: §9§lWhat Was That? I Can't Hear You Over the Engine!

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Now that you have some tech, you've discovered a way to prospect for ores.

Unfortunately, the tech to make it repairable or rechargeable doesn't work, so you'll have to make a new one each time it breaks. It does work better at higher tiers and lasts longer with better materials.

It doesn't make a convenient book like the Seismic Prospector, but you can look at the results of scanning on the map, thanks to Visual Prospecting.

It can be hard to choose a good material for the Basic Prospector. Here are some good choices for you in their respective tiers, the size searched, and the average amount of veins they can scan:

LV Vanadiumsteel 3x3 - 50
MV Vanadiumsteel 3x3 - 213
HV Vibrant Alloy 5x5 - 299
EV Shadow Metal 7x7 - 1080
IV Oriharukon 7x7 - 2649

As you can see, the prospectors become better and better with each tier, but it might also be worth looking around for better materials.

Good luck.

You've heard about Dezil's Marshmallow, a really OP food which can be found from time to time in chests. What about I show you a way to cook this stuff yourself?

After you've mastered the flowing spirit in the dream dimension (witchery), put a bit of flour, sugar, salis mundus and draconium dust in your IV Mixer.
The recipe starts when you give flowing spirit to it and gives you malformed slush, a very stinky and disgusting piece of...something.

Be careful, you'll get blindness II when holding it in your hand.

Next step is to form this slush into the right shape. Use a Marshmallow Mold and press it with your IV forming press. Remember to sterilize it after using it.

Be careful, you'll get blindness and hunger II holding it.

A Carbon crossbow limb is 1/3 the durability of the magnalium limb, but hits a lot harder and shoots a little faster. But you'll want to carry around a tinker table and extra ingots to repair it constantly, and watch that you don't break it in the middle of combat!

Next step is heating up your Marshmallow in an Electric Blast Furnace at 4500K with some noble gas and making it glow.

Now you'll get a Paralysis II effect in addition to the others.

In the next step you cool your Glowing Marshmallow in an EV Vacuum Freezer to make it more stable.

You still get Weakness II and Nausea II.

Your wings can be equipped with a few modifications such as feather falling and double jump. Place the wings in the center of a Crafting Station.

Feather Fall allows you to glide down slowly in air.
Double Jump means you jump while in the air to jump again.

Hint:
Autorepair can be added to the wings as well.
Every Armor part has 3 Slots for modification.

Putting redstone on my weapon makes it faster. So why don't I put it on my hands directly!
This will increase your mining speed.

Hint:
Every Armor part has 3 Slots for modification, aside from gloves, which have 5.

Your shoes can be equipped with a few modifications like water walk, double jump, lead boots or slimy shoes. Place the shoes in the middle of a Crafting Station.

Water Walk allows you to walk over water.
Double Jump allows you to jump while in the air to jump again.
Lead Boots allows you to walk under water, prevents you from swimming, and may cause excessive Blub. Bring along potions of water breathing.
Slimy Shoes reduces fall damage.

Hint:
Autorepair can be added to the shoes as well.
Every Armor part has 3 Slots for modification.

So, if you want to do more than one recipe in your Assline, you want a Data Access Hatch. There are 3+1 versions.

Data Access Hatch: It holds 4 data sticks, so 4 recipes.

Advanced Data Access Hatch: It holds 16 data sticks. Ironically, you can make this right away.

Automatable Data Access Hatch: It's UV, but it allows I/O of the sticks. Skip it.

The Data Bank Multi: Can be connected to multiple Asslines, and can contain more than 1 DAH. This is the best way, when you can do it. Look in ZPM for the quest.

[note]You only need to make one.[/note]
More advanced recipes need an MV chemical reactor. It also speeds up your existing recipes.

Hello there, my name is Teirdalin and today we shall embark on one of the most exciting and fun mods; OpenComputers! First things first though, you will need some patience to get through this mod, but it will certainly pay off in the end!
Microchips will be used in most things you make, so if possible; I suggest bulk crafting quite a few of these.

Place the power converter you got earlier near a cable (you could also power it with RF if you wanted) and connect it with your wire cutters. Now place your computer case by the converter and by the magic of technology it shall fuel the computer case! Now take your hard drive, memory and graphics cards and place them inside, place the disk drive next to the computer and insert the operating system disk. Insert the BIOS we made into the case and turn it on.

Arithmetic Logic Circuits are used in numerous parts, typically in groups of 8-16, and occasionally up to 64.

So be sure to make plenty.

Card bases are just as you might think they are; they're the base part that each card you make will use to connect onto the motherboard.

I suggest making a handful of these for future cards.
betterquesting:10.name:8: All Your Card Are Belong To Us

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Gotta get more RAM.

Memory, or RAM, is essentially a temporary storage of data on your computer that can be rapidly accessed via your programs.

Hence the name Rapid Access Memory.

See the digital world.

Your graphics card allows the computer to draw text and other things to the screen.

The better graphics card you use the higher resolution, and better features can be drawn.

You also need a higher tier monitor to display colors or to get touchscreen compatibility, but that's something to worry about for another day.
Control Units are used for a variety of crafts, but most namely CPUs and GPUs. You will be needing quite a few of these, let's just make 16 for now.

Cache me outside.

Your CPU will essentially be how fast your computer processes data.
A stronger CPU = A faster computer.
betterquesting:10.name:8: What Did the Data Say to the CPU?

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
100 Percent Waterproof.

The Computer Case is the HUB of all your computer parts essentially. It takes two memory sticks, a BIOs rom, a CPU, and a hard drive at the very least to run your computer.

The power converter allows you to power it from your GregTech power grid, and the floppy drive will allow you to install your operating system onto the hard drive.
A screwdriver and wrench in one. Not really a necessary tool, but has some purposes; I suggest referring to your computer manual.

Your hard drive is where all your programs and data is stored.

You're playing minecraft, you should already know this though. Unless you use an SSD I guess.
We'll need these for our hard drives.

The ROM disks are necessary to get your computer to start, they're also what you use to run a drone off from.

Your BIOS go onto these little disks, get a blank one and write the basic BIOS onto it.

You can do this later when you make more computers by flashing your existing BIOS onto new cards or combining a blank with the manual.

Congratulations, we have the parts to start making a computer!

Let's start with the basics here.
This block allows our computer to interact with GT machines and everything else. A must have!
betterquesting:10.name:8: Intelligence is the Ability to Adapt to Change

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
First things first, let's install OpenOS to the computer so you don't always need disk in the drive. Type in 'install' and then type 'Y' when asked if you wish to install OpenOS.

When finished, remove the disk and toss it on your wall and reboot the computer.

Type 'df' to display all present file systems and mount points, you'll notice one named OpenOS; this is your hard drive's default name after installing the OS.

Let's change it with 'label -a OpenOS HDD', '-a' checks for names starting with what you type after it with that command. [note]<-- part of this is apparently wrong? Thanks for the non-ticket explaining what part, guys.[/note]

Now for fun, let's make your first program! How about something functional, make a with 'edit startup' this will bring you to an edit page for a new program called startup. Let's just have it do something simple, 'print("Hello World!")' Like that'll never get old.

Now press Ctrl+S to save, and Ctrl+W to get out of that screen. Back in your home root let's now type startup and you'll see it display "Hello World!" neat huh?

Let's now make startup actually work on startup. Type 'edit .shrc' .shrc is a mystic file that runs shell commands when booting your PC. So in .shrc type 'startup' save and reboot the computer. Now it should say "Hello World!" upon starting. Double neat right?

It's so refreshing.

Place a keyboard facing a screen, or stuck to the back of a screen to make it able to interact with a computer.

Absolutely necessary to doing anything on your computer, but can safely be removed once you have an endlessly running program.
betterquesting:10.name:8: I Love Pressing the F5 Key.

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Alright, you have your computer, it says "Hello World!" When you start it, and you feel awesome and capable of world domination.

Now let's set up your HDD. Open .shrc again in the editor, and press ENTER to go down a line after the print, and type in 'cd ../' this will move your viewed directory that's being viewed to the absolute base directory.

Now go down another line and type in 'mount HDD C:' because why not, it's Classic; this mounts the file drive into the folder you're in. Go down another line and type cd 'C:/' save and reboot the computer.

You'll now start in C:/ nifty! Try typing 'mkdir programs' and now you have a dedicated directory to put your programs in for the sake of organization.
'cd programs' will then take you to programs, and 'cd ../' will take you back a directory; you can also do things like, let's say you have a folder called apples in C as well but you're in apples, type 'cd ../apples' and it'll take you to apples. '..' essentially just means previous directory and this can be stacked; works with copying files and moving them as well, very useful to know.

But right now we're going to do something functional, come over to the next quest and bring your adapter and cables.

For this part we will learn how to use our adapter, place it next to, let's say your EBFs battery buffer and connect it to the computer with cables.
Now let's type in lua while on the computer to open the LUA environment where we can test things without worrying about saving and trying our program.

Type in 'component.list()' this will display a table of all of .list from component. What we're looking for is gt_batterybuffer.
If you have too many nearby things it may not display and the way to search the entire list of components is too advanced for starters.

So now assign a variable to it; for example 'a = component.gt_batterybuffer'; now we can call 'a' to see what methods the batteryBuffer has.
What we'll be using in this example is the 'getBatteryCharge' method. So type  'a.getBatteryCharge(1)' this will call the method getBatteryCharge from the first inventory slot on the gt_batterybuffer in component.

So if we're using a 2x2 battery buffer; we can type something like, 'for i=1, 4 do print(a.getBatteryCharge(i)) end'
Poof you now see what all the batteries EU values. Now what can we do with this?

Try making a variable called 'batteryCharge = 0', now do 'for i=1, 4 do batteryCharge = batteryCharge + a.getBatteryCharge(i) end'

Now print(batteryCharge) will display the total charge. Here's a program example of this being used.

Place in your tape drive and type 'install', and follow the prompts to install it into C. Then edit it, test it, figure how it works.

I suppose that's enough for now; congrats! Experiment and learn, and don't forget to check google as much as possible!
This questline will be updated again in the future; but I figure this is a good ending point for now.
Hey, a use for bitcoins!
I'll sell you a Network Card for six Bitcoins.
I'll sell you a Tier 1 Wireless Network Card for 12 Bitcoins.
I'll sell you a pair of Tier 1 Memory Chips for four Bitcoins.
I'll sell you a Tier 1 Graphics Card for four Bitcoins.
I'll sell you 16 cables for two bitcoins.
I'll sell you a Tier 1 Screen for three Bitcoins.
I'll sell you a Tier 1 Hard Drive for eight Bitcoins.
I'll sell you a Floppy Disk for a Bitcoin.
I'll sell you a Keyboard for two Bitcoins.
I'll sell you a Tier 1 Microchip for two Bitcoins.
Sell 32 of those Dogecoins for a Bitcoin.

Thaumcraft offers considerable power from its devices and tools. But power comes with a price.... That price is represented by Warp: A corruption of the character's mind and soul, inflicting progressively more dire effects upon them.

While the effects of warp can range from annoying to deadly, accumulating enough of it can also grant you access to greater power... at the cost of increasing madness, and attention from dark powers. At least, others may call it madness... but is it truly insanity, when the voices in your head grant useful knowledge?

Warp Theory adds a bunch of new Warp Effects to the Player. Be very careful because you don't want to spawn a Wither in your base.

[note]If you're still early on in your thaumcraft journey, Warp shouldn't be something that scares you away from progressing further. You'll only stumble upon dangerous warp effects once you've done a lot of research. If you still wanna play it safe, make sure to avoid research that's labeled with "§5Forbidden Knowledge§r" [/note]

5 warp: Message
10 warp: Fake Explosion
15 warp: Coin, Pumpkin
20 warp: Lay Eggs, Spawn Phantoms
25 warp: Fake Creeper, Fake Rain
30 warp: GregTech Fake Sounds, Spawn Bats
35 warp: Blood, Fake Enderman
40 warp: Spawn Friendly Creeper
45 warp: Jump Boost, Nausea
50 warp: Insomnia, Vis Drain, Strange Noise
55 warp: Thunderstorm
60 warp: Spawn Fire Bats
65 warp: Blindness, Poison
70 warp: Livestock Rain
75 warp: Spawn Doppelganger
80 warp: Spawn Endermen, Wither Potion
85 warp: Wind
90 warp: Ender Pearl
95 warp: Blaze Fireball
100 warp: Litmus Paper, Junk, Call from the Deep
110 warp: Obsidian
120 warp: Lightning
125 warp: Inventory Swap
130 warp: Random Teleport
140 warp: Acceleration
150 warp: Fake Wither, Inventory Scramble
160 warp: Countdown Bomb
170 warp: Mushrooms
175 warp: Snow
180 warp: Decay
190 warp: Swamp
200 warp: Spawn Wither

The Piston Boots are a bouncy pair of shoes for adventurers.

It functions as a piece of armor for the foot slot that gives a fun jump boost! They let the wearer jump up to THREE blocks in height and increase run speed. They also grant a Step-Up enchantment to allow the wearer to step up a single block without jumping while sprinting. You can repair them with leather using an anvil.

Basically, make them ASAP.

The goggles, wings, shoes, vest, belt and boots itself are not really special.

You can zoom with the goggles, have an extra inventory hotbar with the belt, step-up assist with the shoes, jump boost with the wings and faster swimming ability with the vest.

You get protection like with normal armor too.

Later on you can upgrade your items to become more powerful ones.

Nightvision is very useful. If you combine your Goggles with a night vision potion (3:00, make sure to make 3 at a time), a golden carrot, and a flint and steel inside the Tinkers Crafting Station you get Night Vision Goggles. Place the Goggles in the Center of the Crafting Station.

Hint: Autorepair can be added to the goggles as well.

Every Armor has 3 slots for modification.

Your vest can be equipped with a few modifications like perfect dodge and stealth.
Perfect dodge means you're harder to hit and can be stacked up to 3 times.
Stealth turns you invisible while sneaking. Place the vest in the center of a Tinker's Crafting Station.

Hint:
Autorepair can be added to the vest as well.
Every Armor part has 3 Slots for modification.

I've found a use for the Ectoplasm you can collect from spirits of the dead. It makes a very useful glass that you can walk on, but mobs cannot. However, they think they can!

So you can use this to create a moat around your base that drops mobs to their death in various ways, or just to shuttle them off somewhere else. Separate babies from mothers? Use it in a mob farm? Capture pigmen walking into the Overworld from your Nether portal? So many possibilities!

Tired of having to replace tools all the time because they constantly break? Now that you can make batteries, it's time to make some electric versions of the Screwdriver and Wrench! Charge them up like Batteries, and they'll last much longer than the non-electric versions of these tools.

You can use Lithium Batteries, or if you're on a budget, Cadmium or Sodium Batteries instead. This does reduce their energy capacity though. Later on, Vibrant Alloy will make excellent tools with great durability. There are, however, a multitude of other great materials that you may have access to, so take a look around in NEI and decide for yourself.

There are also MV and HV versions, though they require that you can process Aluminium or Stainless Steel, respectively.

You can find the same ores as Callisto minus callisto ice here, but the real goal is the dungeon and the small ores: Naquadah and Quantium.

Naquadah is used for efficient Silicon Wafer, as well as highly advanced components you'll need tons of at ZPM.

Quantium is used for T5 Rocket and item pipe that has the best throughput in GT.

[note]Make sure to bring your MBM to maximize ore yield.[/note]
Both the IV emitter and sensor need a Quantum Star to craft them. Hope you automated Radon production.

Magnesite, the source of Magnesium can be found in the Twilight Forest at Y 10-25. Fullers Earth can be found on the Overworld at Y 50-70. Marble dust is a great source of Magnesium too.
Other options in LV are Pyrope, Olivine, or Ashes.

§3You only need one of the three to complete the quest.

The Crop Manager is a single-block machine that will monitor crops in an area around itself and automatically apply fertilizer (fluid or item), Weed-EX, and water as needed. The water, fertilizer, and Weed-Ex can be pumped in directly, or use IC2 Universal water cells, normal cells aren't returned when they're used.

Just like any other single block machine, Crop Managers are NOT rainproof, but you can cover them with a water source block just fine!

Tilled dirt still requires a nearby water block to be hydrated as the Manager will only water the crop, not the soil. Try putting a lily pad on top so it isn't annoying to walk on.

Weed-EX is used to prevent the growth and spread of weeds on empty crop sticks.

You can either spray it manually using a spray can, or supply it to a Crop Manager to automatically apply it to all crops in range.

Got Fish?

[note]There are rumors of a weird crop in the shape of a fish...

Otherwise, look under the Feeding Yourself tab for fish catching options.[/note]

Auto Miners are nice but you're going to reach a point where you will want MOOOOOOOOOOOOORE ores. This multiblock will help with that. It will also pre-macerate your ores and give you a little bonus crushed ores as well.

Higher tiers of power will drill faster. You need to upgrade the energy hatch corresponding to the power tier. You will also need an energy hatch, an input hatch, and an output bus - at least MV but you can choose.

Later you can upgrade the ore drilling plant so it extracts from more than a 48 block radius. If you don't want to mine that far away, adjust the range with a screwdriver. Each tier of the controller also gives 1 bonus fortune for small ores starting at 4. At tier 3 you'll want to spread the wealth to multiple compressed chests!

The multiblock miners have been upgraded so that they will chunkload the area they dig in. They will NOT chunkload themselves however. They will dig §odown§r in the chunk they're in like normal, and then dig §oup§r one chunk at a time in other chunks within its range.

You need mining pipes in the controller and drilling fluid in the fluid hatch. You can also feed mining pipes into an input bus.

You'll need to make lots of Drilling Fluid. 64 is a tiny amount to get started with! Plan to make thousands of buckets - perhaps onsite, or pumped in via Long Distance Fluid Pipes.

These are GT machines, so remember to protect them (and their power sources!) from rain (and meteors!) on any side. And set a waypoint with JourneyMap so you don't forget where you placed it!

Did you look for days to find Diamonds, Redstone, Tantalite, Certus Quartz, or Mica?

Well for a few mixes you can use different ores like Coal for Diamond Vein or Quartzite Ore for Certus Quartz Vein. Mica ore mix can be found if you have Cassiterite Ore, but not the Cassiterite Sand.

Tetrahedrite in the nether can be found with copper ore.
With the MV forming press you can make aluminum iron plates for solar panels, turbine blades for turbines and some items for Logistics Pipes.
The second route is probably even better! With just 2 singleblock chemical reactors you can make Silicon Solar Grade. In the first step, make some Trichlorosilane.

The standard wood cutter can only chop down (and replant) vanilla trees. If you want to use saplings from other mods however this add-on will come in handy. Who knows - maybe you're tired of clicking rubber trees with a treetap.

If you want to load and unload a lot of different items from your cargo manager the pipes can get quite messy. The external distributor is a block you can place next to your cargo manager and it will help you to access different slots which you can specify in its GUI. Quite handy for pumping items in and out!

Now that you have a cargo manager you need a specific rail so that your cart can interact with it. Just place it next to the cargo manager, depending on the color of the side it is on you will have to adjust settings in the cargo manager GUI.

Exhale of the Horned One is an ingredient used in many recipes. It is acquired with a random chance when burning Oak saplings in an oven.

You'll also get Wood Ash when burning saplings. It's useful, don't toss it.

Mutandis is a mutagen that is used by witches and warlocks to mutate plants into other species. Simply use Mutandis on small plants, grass, flowers, saplings, etc. and it will be randomly converted to another plant. Mutandis cannot mutate multi-stage plants like wheat and cactus.

Mutating plants is the only way to acquire Rowan, Hawthorn and Alder saplings.

Mutandis has another interesting property when crafted with raw meat. It seems to mutate it into another type of raw meat. It even seems to have an effect on Rotten Flesh.

Some recipes require Mutandis as an ingredient.

Mutandis can be upgraded to Mutandis Extremis to have an effect on a wider variety of plants.

Mutandis is made in a Witches' Cauldron using Mandrake Root, Exhale of the Horned One and an Egg.
The Breath of the Goddess is an ingredient used in many recipes. It is acquired with a random chance when burning Birch saplings in an oven.

These saplings can initially be acquired only by using Mutandis on a valid block, such as a sapling, grass, etc.

You can cook them in the oven for unique fume types:
Rowan: Whiff of Magic
Hawthorn: Odour of Purity
Alder: Reek of Misfortune

Rowan trees drop Rowan Berries, and you'll need to get some Alder Wood for your altar.
A Whiff of Magic is an ingredient used in many recipes. It is acquired with a random chance when burning Rowan saplings in an oven.
Odour of Purity is an ingredient used in many recipes. It is acquired with a random chance when burning Hawthorn saplings in an oven.

To get Witchery seeds, use a hoe on grass blocks away from water. To open the rest of the questline, you will need to do Thaumcraft quests and research the Witchery tab in the Thaumonomicon.

According to legend, when the root of the Mandrake plant is dug up it screams and kills all who hear it. This is only partially true. A fully grown Mandrake may scream causing immense discomfort to those around. This is why it is best to harvest the Mandrake root at night when the plant is more likely to be dormant. The fully grown Mandrake can be harvested to obtain more Mandrake seeds and a Mandrake.

Breaking a fully grown Mandrake plant will either yield Mandrake Root or the Mandrake may awaken and cause all sorts of mischief (and pain to the ears!).

Belladonna seeds can be planted and eventually grow into the multistage belladonna plant. The fully grown belladonna plant can be harvested to obtain more Belladonna seeds and a Belladonna flower.

Snowbell seeds can be planted and eventually grow into the multistage snowbell plant. The fully grown snowbell plant can be harvested to obtain more Snowbell seeds, snowballs and occasionally an Icy Needle.

Water Artichoke seeds can be planted and eventually grow into the multistage Water Artichoke plant. The fully grown Water Artichoke plant can be harvested to obtain more Water Artichoke seeds and a Water Artichoke Globe.

Water Artichoke seeds can only be planted on water source blocks.

Garlic is a plantable crop that can be used to make tasty food, and to deal with vampires. It may be planted on tilled farm land, and will grow in five stages. When full grown the plant may be harvested for up to three dropped garlic bulbs. Which may either be replanted, or used in a crafting recipe.

Garlic bulbs can be used to make meaty stew, a particularly nourishing meal. It is also the main ingredient in making a Garlic Garland, a useful tool in warding off vampires. Finally, garlic can be used by witches in a Witches' Cauldron to make a vampire Weakening brew, and by Witch Hunters, to make vampire resistant armor.

Wolfsbane seeds can be planted and eventually grow into the multistage Wolfsbane plant. The fully grown Wolfsbane plant can be harvested to obtain more Wolfsbane seeds and the Wolfsbane flower.

Purified Milk is an antidote in a similar way to normal milk, although it only has a chance of working and will only remove a single status effect. It is advantageous because it can stack to 64 items.

Purified Milk is an ingredient in the Brew of Sleeping.

The Brew of Love is a throwable potion that causes farm animals and villagers to get their luvin' on. When used on animals the effect is the same as if all hit animals were fed and their breeding cooldown is reset.

In the case of villagers, two (or more) must be hit by the same brew.

The Brew of Love may be thrown at a group of two or more enthralled zombies (created with a Brew of Raising or enthralled with the Infernal Infusion power), which will cause pairs of them to produce a baby zombie. It will also cause them to become zombie villagers. Zombie villagers can be turned back to villagers either using the normal method, or by casting a Rite of Fertility.

The Brew of Love is created in a kettle using the recipe found in the book Witchcraft: Brews & Infusions. Into the pot, throw a Rose, a Golden Carrot, Whiff of Magic, a Lily Pad, a Water Artichoke Globe and Cocoa Beans.

Wear a Witches Hat (and/or robes) while brewing to get more brews than just three.

The Brew of Sleeping is the normal way for a Witch to enter the Spirit World.

Needless to say an unprepared witch will almost always experience a nightmare when they head to the spirit world this way.

The witch must drink the brew and then will fall into a deep sleep, leaving their body and items behind and entering the world of spirits.

The spirit world is an alternate reality that mirrors the Overworld in topography. When people dream they often end up in the spirit world without realizing it (often appearing as one of its many denizens). Powerful witches can create Brews of Sleeping that allow them to pass their still awake consciousness into the Spirit World, leaving their bodies and gear behind.

The Spirit World is the only source of Wispy Cotton, Disturbed Cotton, and Mellifluous Hunger - the materials needed to make Dream Weavers. Also Brews of Flowing Spirit can only be made in the Spirit World.

Very few things can pass into, or return from the Spirit World - keep this in mind when heading there (Icy Needle always stays in the inventory). Wispy Cotton, Disturbed Cotton, Mellifluous Hunger and Brews of Flowing Spirit can pass from the Spirit World to the Real World but not the other way.

Two important things to note: Circle magic does not function in the Spirit World; and Endermen cannot enter the Spirit World.

[note]If you got the Dream version instead of nightmare, collect at least 16 Wispy Cotton for later.[/note]

Hardcore darkness is a pain, but now the night will be bright. Or at least, your perception will be that it is, mobs can still spawn! Be careful, the mobs aren't any weaker.

If you want, you can make a longer-lasting potion out of the Potion of Night Vision. Also, you should probably make them in batches of 3 so you don't waste materials.

You woke up very early because of the nightmares following you in the dream world.

You weren't prepared for it, so let's get some stuff together first and enter a second time to get some wispy/disturbed cotton.

If you haven't unlocked your Brewing stand yet, you have to do it first. Look in the Novice Thaumaturge tab for the quest.

Your second visit hopefully went a little better. With night vision and the flight potion you should have found a few disturbed cotton.

Disturbed Cotton can be spun into Tormented Twine. It cannot be replanted.

An attuned stone is a Mana Diamond that has been further infused with natural magic in a fiery medium. Attuned stones can be used to link non-magical devices to the magical currents present in the world, and are one of the main ingredients in crafting distilleries, kettles, altar foci and poppet shelves.

The other main use of attuned stones is to act as a portable power source for circle magic rites, when a nearby altar is not available. To act in such a way, the attuned stone must first be charged with a Rite of Charging.

[note]If you haven't yet obtained a Mana Diamond, checkout the Flower Power tab for more information![/note]
Reek of Misfortune is an ingredient used in many recipes. It is acquired with a random chance when burning Alder saplings in an oven.

Tormented Twine is spun from Disturbed Cotton using a Spinning Wheel. It is an ingredient used to make Dream Catchers.

It is made in a Spinning Wheel using Disturbed Cotton, Blood Burned String and Reek of Misfortune.

[warn]You need a T2 BM Blood Altar to make the string, so go over to the BM tab if you want to continue and haven't done that yet.[/warn]

An Altar must be nearby to power the spinning wheel.

A distillery used by a witch is a construct used for distilling magical ingredients. It is unlike a normal distillery, because it heats itself using energy obtained from a nearby altar. The distillery must be within about 14 - 16 blocks of an altar to draw power from it - a small icon is shown in the interface if no power is available.

One or two ingredients are distilled together and will result in up to four resulting materials. A supply of clay jars is also needed to capture some or all of the distillates.

The Dream Weaver of Nightmares has two effects, firstly it will add a short weakness effect to a player when they wake up from a good night's sleep. Secondly, it will corrupt all other nearby dream weavers so that they have the opposite effect. If the dream weaver is itself corrupted by another nearby Dream Weaver of Nightmares, it will add a short blindness effect instead of nausea.

The Dream Weaver of Nightmares can also be used to fend off nightmares when a Brew of Sleeping is drunk. Having the Dream Weaver nearby will reduce the chance of a nightmare to 50 percent (this can be decreased further by other means!).
Oil of Vitriol is an ingredient produced in a distillery by using Foul Fume and Quicklime.
Diamond vapor is an ingredient made by distilling diamond in a distillery according to the recipe in the book, Witchcraft: Distilling, using a Diamond and Oil of Vitriol.

A foul fume (commonly known as sulfur dioxide) is an ingredient used in many recipes. It is acquired with a random chance when cooking vanilla food items (such as bread or raw meats) or jungle saplings in an oven.

[warn]Food and Wood burning in the oven is currently broken, use saplings instead.[/warn]
Placing your Dream Weaver of Nightmares close to where you sleep and entering the Dream World again, you have a 50% chance now that it will be Daylight. Try a few times if necessary.

In the daytime you can find a few wispy cotton, which are needed for further progression. There are no mobs in the Dream version, so hang out if you like.

It can be collected and replanted, but will only spread if planted in the Spirit World, on Dirt or Grass that is next to a pool of Flowing Spirit.

Planting Wispy Cotton nearby when using a Brew of Sleeping near to a Dream Weaver of Nightmares will further reduce the chance of a nightmare by 10 percent for each cotton plant (up to 2).

Wispy Cotton will remain in a players inventory when they return from the Spirit World.

Fanciful Thread is spun from Wispy Cotton using a Spinning Wheel. It is an ingredient used to make Dream Catchers.

It is made in a Spinning Wheel using Wispy Cotton, String and Odour of Purity.

The Charm of Fanciful Thinking is the only way to protect oneself from some of the worst effects a nightmare can throw at you. It just needs to be in a player's inventory for it to function.

A Charm of Fanciful Thinking is crafted using Sticks and Fanciful Thread.

The Dream Weaver of Iron Arm will add a mining speed boost to a player when they wake up from a good night's sleep. If the dream weaver is corrupted by a nearby Dream Weaver of Nightmares, the weaver will instead add a mining speed slowdown effect to the player.

The Dream Weaver of Fleet Foot will add a speed boost to a player when they wake up from a good night's sleep.

If the dream weaver is corrupted by a nearby Dream Weaver of Nightmares, the weaver will instead add a slowdown effect to the player.

The Dream Weaver of Fasting will add a boost to the saturation of a player when they wake up from a good night's sleep, essentially meaning they will not get hungry for the duration of the effect. If the dream weaver is corrupted by a nearby Dream Weaver of Nightmares, the weaver will instead add a hunger effect to the player.
Mellifluous Hunger is an ingredient used in other recipes. It is dropped when a Nightmare is killed.

The Brew of Flowing Spirit captures the essence of the Spirit World in liquid form. It can only be brewed in the Spirit World!

The Brew can be thrown at the ground and the liquid will burst out (the source block can later be picked up in a bucket). Standing in the liquid will have a minor healing effect for most creatures. Demonic or undead creatures will be weakened. Nightmares standing in the liquid will lose their invulnerability effect!

Having a pool of flowing spirit near a Dream Weaver of Nightmares will decrease the chance of a nightmare by 10 percent for each source block (up to 3).

First of all you can't visit any other dim to get materials. Not the Twilight Forest, not the Nether or the End. Let's start with crafting a new oven and a stack of jars to start with some basic ingredients.
You probably want a Distillery too.
After we have enough coins we can craft the cauldron and transfer it.
Need more coins? Kill demons for coins. The world is better off without them.
Need more coins? Selling wispy cotton for coins.

Go and find some chicken and eggs, brew some Exhale of the Horned One in your oven and plant some mandrake. Make a stack of mutandis to get some witchery tree saplings. Gravel hoes are good enough for planting stuff.
For later use do a few Exhale of the Horned One.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Exhale of the Dreaming Horned One

betterquesting:10.desc:8: For all your offerings you'll need an altar too. The spinning wheel needs it also.
A kettle is needed in the spirit world too.
You need the spinning wheel for the fanciful thread to finally make the Potion of Flowing Spirit.
Fanciful Thread is spun from Wispy Cotton using a Spinning Wheel. It is an ingredient used to make the Potion of Flowing Spirit. This can be brewed only in the spirit world.
For later use do a few Odour of Purity.

The Dream Weaver of Intensity has two effects, firstly it will add a very short night vision effect (or blindness if corrupted by a nightmare) to a player when they wake up from a good night's sleep. Secondly, it will intensify all other nearby dream weavers so that they have either a stronger (but shorter lasting) effect or their duration is increased.
Time to make the MV version of the assembler.

Nodes can take many upgrades. For now, try building a World Interaction Upgrade. With it, you can set up simple autocrafting.

Put a WIU in a transfer node attached to a crafting table. On the other side of the table, the 3x3 area is now treated as a crafting grid. Place items in inventories on the other side and if they make a valid recipe, the WIU will craft it. To speed it up, you will need to wait until HV for stainless steel.

Also, if you place a node on a block of cobble that has lava and water next to it, and a WIU in it, it will produce cobble for you automatically. Use upgrades to get more at a time and faster.

[warn]The WIU can NOT be used for infinite water in GTNH.[/warn]

While Sugarcane alone is quite useful, its close relative Sticky Cane is even moreso! Thanks to its production of sticky resin, it is a near universally used crop for the production of rubber in all sorts of electronics.
You should grow some essence berries to level up!
betterquesting:10.name:8: Feeling a Little Like a Noob?

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
... with the Bio Diesel you produce from Canola!


While some still see Canola as nothing but a younger brother to the Goldfish, maybe you will find something greater hiding behind its oily guise.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Put the Petal to the Metal...

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
I haven't been feeling well lately. Would you grow me some Gaia Wart? They're better than milk, since they only remove negative effects, and stack to 64. Really nice when fighting that Alchemist infernal! Or moving super tanks.

They also have some quite rare essentia on them, very useful for the budding thaumaturge.

[note]In order to get your hands on some Gaia Warts, you'll need to right-click some snow onto some Netherwart until it transforms[/note]

Sugarcane not keeping up with your sugary needs? Sugar beets give 8 sugar per beet.

Hmm, now I want some candy. Give me some sugar from your beets. I'll share some with you.

[note]Electrolyze the sugar into O2 for an easy source.[/note]

EV motors need Neodymium. Rare Earth is an §oOK§r source, but on the Moon you can find a vein with pure Neodymium ore. Bastnasite is a great source of fluorine. And Monazite can be taken apart for more Rare Earth.

Your Electric Blast Furnace needs Nickel. Now that you've reached the Twilight Forest, it's time to get some. The Nickel Vein that contains it is located at Y 10-40. In MV, you'll need tons of Nickel for Cupronickel, so stock up.

You can get some Cobalt out of Cobaltite through the side processes such as washing or thermal centrifuging. To electrolyze it, you'll need an MV electrolyzer though. Or you can EBF it after your EBF is done. Remember that the Sulfur Dioxide you get is based on your muffler tier. This is probably easier than searching in the Nether for Cobalt.

§3You can also find small quantities of Pentlandite ore in the Overworld if you care.

Dehydrate your grapes to raisins. Or make some Styrene, Benzene or Ethylene at MV. Either way, this device is a nice to have.

It also does the Drying Rack recipes as well.

Want to make the synthetic rubber styrene-butadiene?

I'll show you a way you can get it. You'll need an Oil Cracker and a Distillation Tower. There are different ways to do it and this quest is only an example of how you can make it.

The first step is to crack your Naphtha with steam.

§6Already automated Styrene-Butadiene rubber or Polystyrene? Hold 128 sheets of each to skip their respective questline.
For the next steps you need a few fluids/gases like Benzene, Ethylene and Butadiene. Run your distillation tower a few cycles to get them.

Putting Benzene and Ethylene in the Chemical Reactor gives you Styrene.

[note]And also hydrogen, just pack that away with the rest.[/note]

Hate magic (and fluid P2P), but still want to TP fluids? TT has your back with the Ender Fluid Link Cover!

Place one on a tank and open the GUI.
Channel: Covers with the same text will connect.

Public: Links to any of the same color not set to private. Use an internet program to find out what the numbers mean, and get colors you like.
Private: Does not link to public version of that color. Meaningless in SP.

Export: Fluid moves from Attached Block -> Cover Network
Import: Fluid moves from Cover Network -> Attached Block

You can use multiple as inputs and/or outputs. It runs at 8000L/t.

You can send §ofrom§r an output hatch or §oto§r an input hatch for multis. Probably won't work well for anything with multiple I/O, like a singleblock Chemical Reactor.
The second last step is Raw Styrene-Butadiene Rubber. Mix Butadiene, Styrene and Oxygen to make the dust.

First we're gonna need some pipes to connect everything. Do not use these pipes in junctions or the items will choose which path to go at random and you don't want that.

[note]Keep in mind PR automation is laggy, so don't use it more than the minimum you can get away with on servers, wait until AE2 for that. In SP, do what you want, but keep in mind that AE2 is way more powerful.[/note]
So how do we deal with junctions then? We use these pipes. They are smart and they will send everything where it needs to go, so if you make a junction make sure you put this pipe there.

That's all nice and all, but none of these pipes connect to chests and machines. What am I supposed to do with them?

I'm glad you asked. You are going to need a special pipe for that. This is a pipe you need to use to connect to machines and chests. You'll have to set it up with chips that we'll make soon.

Now you need to make some chips to use in those interface pipes. These are useless on their own but essential for crafting the others.

Now would be a good time to look into crops or magic to get all the dyes you will need for your advanced chips.

[note]If NEI's bookmarks are blocking you on the left, you can turn it off (O) until that gets fixed.[/note]

This chip also stores items in connected inventory. It designates a storage for items that are set in the filter of this chip. They do not actively request for items, they only serve as a destination for items to go. You can open up the menu by right-clicking the chip. There you can set which items should it accept and the priority. Items will go to item responders with higher priority first.

This chip stores the items in a connected inventory. It designates a storage for items that have no other place to go. It is strongly recommended to have a default storage for items in every pipe system, otherwise bad stuff can happen. Best used with a large chest (diamond for example).

It seems to have some bugs though, so don't craft more than one without testing it first.

You might have to just use a normal item responder and add the items you want routed back to your overflow spot.

The dynamic item responder chip behaves exactly like an item responder chip, but instead of you setting up which items it should accept, it looks in the chest what items are there and those items it will accept.

This chip will extract items from the connecting inventory. The extracted items then look for pipes with item responder chips where there's a free space they could go. If they don't find any they will go to the overflow default storage chest.

If you want it to extract everything leave the filter empty and set it to blacklist.

The item broadcaster is a chip that tells everything in the pipe system what items it has in the connecting inventory and if another chip needs anything it will send it to them. Right-click it to set the items it will transmit. If you leave it empty and set to blacklist it will transmit everything.

Definitely use one in combination with an item overflow chip on your default storage chest. That way overflow will end up in the chest, but will be usable by the rest of your system.

The item stock keeper looks at the connecting inventory and keeps item stocked in there. If the item is missing it will keep bothering item broadcasters every few seconds if they have the item and if they can send it. It's basically like an annoying child.

It is really useful though. Want a chest that will always have 64 cobble and dirt in it and if you take them they will get replaced? This guy is perfect for that job. It's great for keeping machines stocked. When stocking GT machines, the top left slot of the 3x3 is equal to the left slot of the machine. Want a chemical reactor that keeps 3 hydrogen cells ready to go to make ammonia, just add nitrogen? This is the chip for you.

The crafting chip does exactly what it says. It's not just for default crafting. You can use it with GT machines. Just put in the matrix that it should insert and the output is what it should extract. A great use for them is in combination with fluid canners or super tanks for filling cells.

[note]While these chips are really powerful for your PRT system they become a lag hazard relatively quickly, so be careful.[/note]
This pipe lets you request stuff from the system. It shows all items that are available thanks to broadcast chips and even stuff that can be crafted thanks to crafting chips.

[warn]Using the drawer controller with large amounts of I/O will tank TPS! If you're on a server, do not use drawer cubes, or expect the possibility of it being deleted or you getting banned.[/warn]

Time to build a simple system to store your stuff. Place down the drawer controller and place the drawers around it. Connect the interface pipe to the drawer controller and put the dynamic item responder and broadcaster chips inside. Don't forget to set the broadcaster to transmit everything by leaving the filter empty and setting it to blacklist. Now you can request stuff from your storage and if you have a chest with a pipe and extractor chip everything you put inside will be sorted into the storage.
This quest line will show you how to automate desulfurizing of oil products. Return here once you have unlocked the LV distillery quest and have some polyethylene plates.

First we should make a place to store all the fluids we'll use.

If you're interested what they'll be used for:
1 for oxygen
1 for hydrogen
1 for sulfuric acid

Now let's automate electrolyzing water into oxygen and hydrogen. You'll need hydrogen for tons of stuff including desulfurization, obtaining tungsten, and nitric acid production. Oxygen is also useful as I'm sure you noticed when making steel.

How to set it up:

Place the electrolyzer down and connect it to water and electricity. Place the 2 super tanks nearby. Set the electrolyzer to produce hydrogen gas and oxygen cells. Use normal GT fluid pipes to output the hydrogen gas into one super tank. That is now your hydrogen storage. Now connect interface pipes to all 3 machines.

For the electrolyzer put in item stock keeper set to keep 2 empty cells stored. Also put in extractor set to extract oxygen cells.

Now for the oxygen storage put in item responder chip set to accept oxygen cells and extractor set to extract empty cells.

Now put some empty cells inside your default storage chest and don't forget to have a broadcaster there.

Now it's time to start the actual desulfurization. Use a chemical reactor of your choice, fill it with sulfuric light fuel and hook it to power. Now connect an interface pipe to it. Put an item stock keeper inside set to store 4 hydrogen cells. Then put in item extractor set to extract hydrogen sulfide and empty cells.

Go to your hydrogen storage super tank and put in a crafting chip set to make one hydrogen cell from one empty cell.

And that's all.
Whichever path you followed, you now have the Solar Grade Silicon Dust. You want to smelt it into ingots to make plates for Transistors, but you will also need some to make Silicon Boules.

For your new Factory you need iron doors. Unfortunately, the recipe is really hard, needing steel.

You can choose two more iron doors as reward if you like.

For your new House you need some wooden doors. Well, the recipe is really hard and needs iron/copper and a lot of wood.

You can choose two more doors as a reward if you like.

Oilsand is another way to get heavy oil. Maybe you got lucky and found some in a mountainous biome. With your centrifuge you're able to get heavy oil and sand out of the ore. The veins can be found between Y 50-80.

Sadly, you can't use heavy oil until MV, so just stick them in a barrel or something until then.

[note]Until MV it can only be used for lubricant and burning in a semifluid generator.[/note]
betterquesting:10.name:8: §2§lOilsand, or How You Get Heavy Oil

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Now let's convert all that H2S into sulfuric acid. Hook up a chemical reactor to electricity, water and interface pipe. Put inside an item responder chip set to accept H2S cells and extract empty cells. Distill that diluted sulfuric acid in distillery and store it in super tank.

Congratulations. You now have a completely automatic desulfurization of oil, automatic production of hydrogen and oxygen and you also store all that sulfuric acid.
Here's a small reward for making all those chips.

The greatest reward is having your stuff automated if you've done everything correctly, but here's a reward for making it this far.

Some other setups to look at automating are making polyethylene and nitric acid.

With stock keeper chips you can always keep a set amount on-hand and when you pull out the cells to use elsewhere, your setup will automatically make more.

...so make them lose their heads.

Make yourself a Cleaver with your tool forge and collect some wither skeleton skulls.

[warn]If you have problems finding wither skeletons, once you get to HV you can put a powered skeleton spawner in the Nether.[/warn]
...that I know creepers have hearts. Extract a few with your Arthana. You might want to add a few levels of Looting to get more drops.

Spinning hay into gold sounds like a fairy tale, but with your new magical spinning wheel you too can try tricking a queen into giving you their firstborn child.

You will need three for your witchwear, and can turn extra into gold nuggets in a furnace.
To make appropriate witchwear, you'll need to make some impregnated leather with your diamond vapor.

...and you're going to be in trouble.

Dress for success in your new Witches Hat and Robes. A girl has to look her best, so I'll give you a nice bag as reward.

Check NEI uses for impregnated leather for other accessories to your outfit.
...And sexy male librarians. And also smart witches who want to learn their way around. Craft the first group of Witchery books, or find them in a village.
...to fit all this knowledge. Get some more books!
betterquesting:10.name:8: Going to Need a Big Hat...

betterquesting:10.desc:8: ...but a path laden with power beyond imagination. Behold mortal, and be terrified!
betterquesting:10.name:8: A Dark Path to Travel Down...

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Combine Sodium and Sulfur to get Sodium Sulfide.

Tired of talking one by one with every villager to determine their trades? A trading post will show you all available trades from villagers in the area.

You'll need an Assembler to finish it up.

Once you have a GT boiler or Large Combustion Engine with a long startup time, you may wish to automate turning it on/off to save fuel, since extra power or Steam will just be voided. Additionally, the bigger your Steam/EU buffer is, the less time your generators will spend heating up, which makes them more efficient.

Use a Machine Controller Cover on the controller for that. You can put it on top, bottom, or sides next to a casing - casings will transmit the redstone signal. You can use a Soldering Iron and Fine Soldering Alloy Wire to set the Redstone Output of a controller block to strong. When set to Strong it can go through a casing, but not hatches, buses, or other blocks. Use it with an activity detector if you want to receive a signal from the controller rather than turning it on/off with one.

With a Machine Controller Cover, you can use redstone to turn the machine on and off. This is handy if you don't want to use a Soft Hammer to disable a machine yourself constantly.

The best way to do that is with an RS latch. One input will turn the machine on, and one input will turn the machine off. Use a comparator attached to a valve to measure the steam level in your multiblock Iron or Steel Tank. Invert the signal to turn on your boiler when the steam level is low. When the steam level signal is high, turn your boiler off. Use a trail of redstone to lower the signal strength. Because of boiler/turbine warmup, try to set the ON strength to 30 percent of capacity and OFF strength to about 90 percent.

Red alloy wire will hold a redstone signal for a longer distance than normal redstone, while redstone conduits will go indefinitely. You can also use amplified redcrystal to improve the strength of the signal for a long distance, repeating as necessary.

You can use an Energy Detector Cover in Normal Electrical Storage (including batteries) mode to monitor the power in a battery buffer and use it to enable/disable generators in a similar way. Change mode using a screwdriver. If you use a dense redcrystal, it will only allow signal through at a certain level, perfect for automating this kind of thing.

For a video version, check out this video: [url]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jPfnifJEO64[/url]

Dragon eggs are very rare and only drop after a dragon's death. How about I show you a way to recreate this powerful item out of a monster spawn egg?

Let's start with step one. Using a mob spawn egg (any work, you can purchase one from the Vending Machine if you do not have one), growth medium, and bacteria to create a bigger egg. This process needs one hour.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §8§lOne Dragon Egg is Not Enough Mr Bond

betterquesting:10.desc:8: After you've gotten some mutagen try soaking your Big Egg in it along with some U-238.
Next, we need to start infusing it with the essence of The End. Start with endium dust and molten ender to get an ender egg.
The next step is to add draconium and ender goo to the ender egg to get a draconium egg.
The last step to create a dragon egg is to add enderium using a dragon heart as a catalyst. It's not used up.
Add sulfur to the raw dust to get molten styrene-butadiene rubber, then solidify it to get sheets.

Want to make the synthetic rubber Silicone? As the first step you need Chloromethane.

You can use 2 Chlorine and 1 Methane per Chloromethane in your chemical reactor. Alternatively you can use Methanol and Hydrochloric Acid.

There are different ways to do it and this quest is only an example of how you can make it.

§6Already automated Silicone Rubber? Hold 128 sheets to skip this questline.
For the next step you need Chloromethane and Silicon Dust. This gets you Dimethyldichlorosilane.
Put Dimethyldichlorosilane and Water into the chemical reactor to get Polydimethylsiloxane.
Lastly we add a bit of sulfur to the polydimethylsiloxane dust and get molten silicone rubber.
Now that you have HSS-G, it's time to make HSS-S. This new alloy is an important part of a lot of LuV recipes.

To process some of the new ingots you will find, you might want some argon. Your first source will come from air, in small amounts. Unlike centrifuging Compressed Air Cells, you'll need to turn the Air into Liquid Air first in a Vacuum Freezer so you can centrifuge it more efficiently.

You can also make the Air Intake Hatch - it's much better than spamming compressors!

Don't bother with the DT recipe unless you need the other fluids from it, it's not nearly as good as centrifuging. You also need the Liquid Air Fluid Hatch (only works with Liquid Air!) and Giant Output Hatch when you want to do that.

You may have noticed that you can't get naquadah dust from the naquadah ore, it will only give you the Naquadah Oxide Mixture (NOM) dust, annoying.

The full naquadah processing line is too complex and does not fit in IV. I believe you won't want to set up another line after finishing Platinum, PBI and Lanthanide lines.

Lucky, you can directly smelt the NOM dust into naquadah nuggets in EBF, but it is inefficient and you will lose the byproducts in it.

[note]PS: The Naquadah Oxide Mixture was once called "Naquadah Metal Oxide Mixture" and someone called it Nq-MOM for short.[/note]
The IV circuit assembler will let you make easier MV circuits, as well as single step EV circuits.

To make more advanced wafers, you need to make Naquadah Doped Monocrystalline Silicon first. The process takes 750 seconds and requires Silicon Solar Grade blocks, a Naquadah Ingot, and a Gallium Arsenide Crystal in the Electric Blast Furnace. You can make 64 wafers out of every boule.
To create some naquadah doped silicon wafers, place the monocrystalline naquadah doped silicon boule in a cutting machine. An HV cutting machine is needed for future advanced wafers and chips.
The next solar panel you can make is the EV one. It generates 2048 EU/t.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §9§lPower of the Sun at EV Level

betterquesting:10.desc:8: To make cheaper LV and MV circuits you need SoCs. System on a chip.
With the IV circuit assembler and SoCs you can now make integrated processors for a reduced price.

Glass Fiber is used in Fiber Reinforced Boards for circuits. [note]For next tier. Go left for this tier's circuits.[/note]

Borax can be extracted out of Salt ores. Electrolyze it to get Boron and mix it with Glass dust to get Borosilicate Glass Dust.

The ingots can be turned into glass fiber in the wiremill or extruder.

You can also use borosilicate to make higher tier glass for higher tier SB recipes, or for the blocks for the multis that need it.
Fiber Reinforced Epoxid Sheets are needed for More Advanced Circuit Boards. Mix glass fiber or carbon fiber with epoxid to get your sheets.

Fiber Reinforced circuit boards require fiber-reinforced epoxid resin sheets, aluminium foil, and sulfuric acid to make an empty board. By adding energetic alloy foil and Iron(III) Chloride or Sodium Persulfate you can craft a More Advanced Circuit Board.

[note]With these new boards you can make Lapotronic Energy Orbs. You could use them to upgrade your LSC. The boards are also used in IV for the next circuit line.[/note]
Quantum Processors are your first chance to make EV circuits in a single craft.
The Qbit Wafer is made out of a Nano CPU Wafer and either Quantum Eyes and Gallium Arsenide, or IGP and Radon. Cut it for Qbit processor chips.
Field generators are a big part of lategame crafts. And yes, they always suck to make.
While the ender quarry on its own with speed upgrade is good, why not speed it up a little bit more?
If Speed upgrade II is too slow craft a speed upgrade III.

You may have noticed that the circuits you're thinking of crafting cost way more, 6x more. This is intended for circuits needing LuV+ voltage. You now need to craft your circuits in the Circuit Assembly Line or CAL if you don't want to pay out the ears in materials. You'll still need to craft your first ones using the normal Circuit Assembler though.

Once you've done that, you can make an imprint for use in the CAL to set it to make that (and only that) type of circuit.
You can make Nano Processors cheaper than before. You'll need to make an imprint first though.

ASoCs. Advanced system on a chip, will be used for a new multiblock, the Precise Assembler.

And just like SoCs, ASoCs will be used to make cheaper HV and EV circuits.

However you'll need to wait until ZPM to make the cheaper EV circuits.

Now that you're this far into LuV, you can make easier IV circuits, as well as your first UV circuit.

After crafting each circuit, make an imprint of it to reduce the cost of following ones.

To make these chips you need Europium, as well as an HV Autoclave in the Asteroids dimension (or on your space station) to achieve "low gravity".

[note]Alternatively you can use an Industrial Autoclave.[/note]
A new circuit line, a new board. Also required for the Hi-Computation Station MK-I.

The LuV laser engraver is an important part of lategame circuit production. You need to make crystal CPU's for both the crystal processor series of circuits, and later on for the wetware series.

[note]If you've made the Hyper-Intensity Laser Engraver, you can just upgrade that instead.[/note]

Polybenzimidazole or PBI is a synthetic fiber needed in ZPM Hulls and in high tier solar panels, and can also be used to make some other items more efficiently. It has many steps to produce it. Let's start with chlorobenzene, but keep in mind you'll need to complete the other non-platline IV-tier chemical quests too.

§3Already automated PBI? Hold 128 sheets to skip this questline.
We also need nitration mixture. We can do it out of nitric acid and sulfuric acid.
Next step is to mix the nitration mixture with your chlorobenzene in the HV chemical reactor to get 2-nitrochlorobenzene.
Mixing 2-nitrochlorobenzene with copper dust gives you 3,3 Dichlorobenzidine in an EV Chemical Reactor.
Mixing 3,3 Dichlorobenzidine with Ammonia and Zinc in an IV Chemical Reactor gives you 3,3 Diaminobenzidine.

High tier chemical recipes need a high tier IV chemical reactor.

Alternatively you can use your Large Chemical Reactor with either two EV energy hatches or one IV energy hatch.

[note]...Which you can make after you finish the platline. Have fun![/note]

§6If you missed it or forgot, hold a stack of the platline dust to skip the quests in between.

You can also skip the PBI chem quests, but you need to hold 128 sheets in your hand.
3,3 Diaminobenzidine and Diphenyl Isophtalate will finally give you molten Polybenzimidazole. Use a plate mold to get plates.
Mix Sulfuric Acid, Phthalic acid and Phenol to get Diphenyl Isophtalate. An IV Chemical Reactor is needed.
You can get Phenol in different ways, but if you don't have any, you can make some using chlorobenzene and some water.
To get Phthalic Acid you need mix Dimethylbenzene, Potassium Dichromate and Oxygen in an EV Chemical Reactor.
Dimethylbenzene can be distilled from Wood Tar or using Benzene and Methane gas in a Chemical Reactor.
Potassium Dichromate is made out of Potassium Nitrate and Chromium Trioxide in an HV Chemical Reactor.

Potassium Nitrate is made from Potassium and Nitric Acid.
If you have some saltpeter you can use that instead.

Potassium nitrate can only be crafted while saltpeter has many different sources.
Pick the one you prefer, only one is needed to complete the quest.
Chromium Trioxide is made out of chrome and oxygen in two steps. First you make Chromium Dioxide and then Chromium Trioxide.
Quantum Assembly is an IV Circuit.
The Quantum Supercomputer is an LuV Circuit.
The Quantum Mainframe is the first ZPM circuit you can make.
The Crystal Assembly is a LuV Circuit.
The Crystal Supercomputer is a ZPM circuit.
The Crystal Mainframe is the first UV circuit you can make.
How about lossless 32768 EU Wires? Tetraindiumditindibariumtitaniumheptacoppertetrakaidekaoxide is a superconductor wire and will transfer your energy without any loss.

With the EV circuit assembler and SoCs you can now make microprocessors for a reduced price.

Remember that these can't be made into MV circuits.
SoCs (Systems on a Chip) are used to simplify circuit crafting. In this case, you can use Simple SoCs to make ULV circuits more easily.

The NAND chip is an industrial replacement for the vacuum tubes that is much cheaper. You can't use it to make circuits though, only to make other things as a ULV circuit. Make sure to check out all the possible recipes!

[note]You will need a cleanroom to cut up the NAND chip![/note]
Tier 4 Planets are Jupiter's Moon Io where you will find the next dungeon, Venus (needs a SpaceSuit) and Mercury.
The only interesting ore on this planet is the deep iron from small ores. Grab a ton of it so you can get trinium out of it.

Venus has 3 different veins, with quantium and titanium the most important to grab. And Naquadah if you still don't have enough.

[note]You can also get firestone from small ore if you still need it.[/note]

§5Warning! Venus requires a full set of armor with the Spacesuit capability in it or it will kill the player on entering it!!

Check the space race chapter for more information.
Yttrium Barium Cuprate becomes more important in LuV Tier. It needs an EV Mixer to mix and an Electric Blast Furnace with TPV heating coils.
Put those 2048 EU panels on a block to make them placeable in the world.
The next solar panel you can make is the IV one. It generates 8192 EU/t. This is probably the last tier it's worth it to make solars, unless you just really like them.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §d§lPower of the Sun at IV Level

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Put those 8192 EU panels on a block to make them placeable in the world.
The LuV assembler is needed for IV Solar Panels and other high tier stuff. Let's build one.

Go get the schematics for tier 5 rockets. Watch out for lava!

This will open the Moons from Saturn and Uranus.
Rockets require heavy duty plates for the main hull. Let's craft 61 tier 5 heavy duty plates out of tier 4 plates and compressed quantium plates.
Each rocket needs a Control Computer, appropriate to the tier of the rocket.

After a month of hard work and ten thousand stacks of iTNT your fifth rocket is finally ready.

You need to use CN3H7O3 (Purple) Rocket Fuel or better to fuel it.
Every rocket needs a nose cone. Tier 5 rocket needs a heavy nose cone tier 3.
Every rocket needs a rocket engine. A heavy one tier 3 is needed in the tier 5 and 6 rockets.
Every rocket needs a few rocket fins. Tier 5 rockets need heavy ones Tier 3.
Every rocket needs fuel storage canisters. For the tier 5 rocket you need to craft two medium and two large canisters.
The distance between Planets and Moons is much larger now so the rocket needs bigger boosters to reach it.
Who wants to trudge around on the surface when you can fly? Upgrade your chestplate with a jetpack and fly around Venus.

Venus is hot, so hot it can melt lead. On top of that the atmosphere is so thick, 90x the Overworld, that it will crush you. Not to mention the Sulfuric Acid! You will need to construct a special suit to survive on Venus without dying instantly.

[note]Some armors can now also survive this atmosphere. It will say so in their tooltip.[/note]
betterquesting:10.name:8: Journey to the Bottom of a Molten Ocean

betterquesting:10.desc:8: These boots will help you fall faster in low gravity environments. Or not. Maybe. Give them a try.

Or at least factories full of item pipes. You can take items out of one machine using a hopper pointing directly into your pipes, and from there deliver them to a second machine.

Later on you can make better item pipes. Search for "item pipe" in NEI for options.

[warn]You'll need a Steel Wrench to remove them. Don't place them down unless you're sure of the location until you have one.[/warn]

Now that you're in MV, you'll want to start automating Polyethylene, Oxygen, Nitrogen, Hydrogen, Rubber, Charcoal, etc. Faster item pipes will help with transporting items quicker around your base. For now, use your spiffy new extruder to craft some brass item pipes.

The reward - restrictive item pipes - allow you to prioritize destinations. Locations on the other side of a restrictive pipe are treated as much further away than locations on the same side of a pipe. Very handy when you want overflow (or non-matching) items to go somewhere else!

For higher tiers, look up "item pipe" in NEI or use the wiki: [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Fluid_%26_Item_Pipes[/url]

[note]If you require higher speeds than the Brass pipes offer, you can try out the Electrum pipes, but beware the gold cost![/note]

Simple, easy, redstone-girl.

[note]Redstone torches are great to get the light level just right.[/note]

...the whole world looks like a nail. 

When looking for good tool materials, see "GregTech Material Tools" tab in NEI. Remember that NEI bookmarks are your friends.

The GT tools each have special uses.

§lScrewdriver§r - Used on covers to change their behavior or on machines to change their input mode.

§lWrench§r - Used to change the output direction on a GT machine, or to break it. Can also disconnect/connect pipes or enable their built in shutter.

§lCrowbar§r - Remove covers from machines or pipes.

§lWire cutters§r - Connecting/disconnecting/breaking wires/cables.

§lSoft mallet§r - Turning machines on/off.

§lHammer§r - Prospecting for ores in a limited way in front of you, smashing ore blocks into crushed ores, and muffling machine sounds.

§lPlunger§r - Drain fluids from a machine or tank

[note]On a side note, Tin Pipes need a Steel Wrench to dismantle, so don't place them randomly, and pay attention to material levels![/note]
betterquesting:10.name:8: §a§lWhen All You Have is a Hammer...

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
