Tired of the Multifarm's requirements? The EnderIO Farming Station is here to ease your suffering. It only requires EU and tools and can be easily upgraded with capacitors. Most standard crops and trees work with it, but unfortunately, CropsNH crops do not.

[note]If you want to use it for farming crops from Pam's HarvestCraft, you'll need to provide the crop itself, not the seed, for it to work properly.[/note]

Your old and trusty combustion engines don't quite cut it anymore, not to mention they're polluting the place. If you want to keep burning liquids, you need to build a better engine. This multiblock can produce 1A of EV voltage by default and 3A if you supply it with oxygen. However, this power doesn't come for free - you need to supply the machine with small amounts of lubricant constantly (and oxygen if you want to boost both its efficiency and output).

You will also require 3 Input Hatches, a Muffler, and a Dynamo Hatch. Their tiers are up to you.

Cetane Boosted Diesel and High Octane Gasoline (HOG) are excellent fuel sources for this engine.

You will need to keep the area in front of the engine clear so it can pull enough air - not even torches.

There are a few very useful Nether trees out there which give resources like Redstone, Gunpowder, Bone meal or Fertilizer.

Go and get a few trees like Bloodwood, Fusewood, Darkwood or Ghostwood out of the Nether.

These trees can be planted like normal trees, except for Bloodwood. That has to be planted on a ceiling and will grow down instead of up.

The Moon is rich in Helium 3 because the Sun has been embedding it in the upper layer of moon by the solar wind over billions of years.

Salt water is also available in smaller quantities. You can get chlorine out of it. You will want plenty of chlorine for processing Rutile to get Titanium.

There are more planets and moons with gas and fluids underneath the surface. Bring along a multiblock fluid drill to recover these fluids.
Mars is rich in Salt Water and Chlorobenzene. If you run low on chlorine you can electrolyze the fluids.
These boules are the most efficient when making wafers out of them.

Just listening to this tank gulp water makes me thirsty. If placed next to a water source block, it is a decent water source. It also supports several upgrades to speed and capacity. Try out this glyph near your cows, and get a tank full of milk for all your cheese and butter needs.

Now that you have an MV Electrolyzer, you can extract Boron from Borax. This element is used later on for Borosilicate Glass and fiber, but for now you can use it to make some volumetric flasks to hold precise amounts. This is handy for recipes that may only need a tiny amount of a substance, like 1L.

Camouflage blocks allow the faces of cable blocks to be made to imitate any other block. This works in the full workflow and thus can be updated on the fly.

Please note that this block is placed the same as all SFM cables. It does not act as an inventory cable and thus will need to be in an advanced cable cluster in many situations.
The inventory relay can access the inventory of non-stationary entities, such as minecarts.
Double sided cable camouflage blocks allows setting the inside face of the cable block, allowing you to imitate glass.
Transforming Cable Camouflage allows you to change the collision box of the cable, so you can turn it into a door or whatever.
An Advanced Inventory Relay can add/remove items from a player's inventory.

Only dangerous cliffs to fly off. TecTech can be the source of adventures, scary and satisfying.

Thanks to Piky/Scripted for giving you some guardrails to stay on the road. Scripted/Piky shed blood over these quests for you. Now it's your turn!

For additional details on TecTech, check out the wiki at [url]https://github.com/Technus/TecTech/wiki[/url]

You'll probably receive better help in Discord, though.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §b§lLearning Curve? Where We're Going There Are No Curves

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Welcome to TecTech! The pinnacle of absolute high-tier machinery for all your end-tier needs. However, learning TecTech is incredibly confusing, so listen very carefully.

First, you'll need to gather various casings for your machines that you'll need. We've provided some examples of the blocks you'll need, but you should expect to have to craft more. Lots more.

You use the optical cables to connect machines together. Just make sure that they're painted, as well as what you want to connect them to.

The Quantum Computer (QC) is an incredibly complicated machine used to generate computation for the Research Station and a few other multiblocks. There are a few things you need to understand before using one.

§lCONSTRUCTION§r. Much like an assembly line, the QC is built as a series of slices. The first and last slice are the only valid locations for hatches. The slices in between are primarily for computer racks. The Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector shows the minimum length QC, but holding multiple in a single stack will show/build longer versions up to the maximum length of 16. There is also a mandatory air block in front of the computer heat vents.

§lOUTPUT§r. Computation is nothing more than an integer input for certain recipes--much like EU. There may exist a minimum throughput requirement, a threshold to reach, or both (NEI will tell you everything). Computation is generated every second by the QC, transmitted by an Optical Transmission Connector, received by an Optical Reception Connector, and "consumed" by the machine or process that needs it. There is no storing computation and there can only be ONE transmission or reception hatch connected to the same Optical Fiber Cables at a time. If absolutely necessary, the Network Switch with QoS can split/join connections but know that it takes both power and maintenance to run.

Additional QC can be chained together using another set of Optical Transmission and Optical Reception Connectors between machines, but they cannot wallshare the same Optical Transmission Connector.

§lUNCERTAINTY§r. The QC has a unique maintenance requirement that can only be corrected by balancing the Schrödinger Matrix inside an Uncertainty Resolver- an additional hatch that must go on either the first or last slice of the machine. Start with the Uncertainty Resolver X, but know that there is another tier unlocked later on (Uncertainty Resolution) that will solve the puzzle on its own.

The interface of the Uncertainty Resolver X has the Schrödinger Matrix in the middle and two sets of 8 buttons on the left and right. Clicking on one button and then another will switch the states of the two corresponding cells in the matrix. This means switching their shade/color. The goal of the puzzle is to balance the states of the matrix around the glowing LED lights, turning all of them green.

§lPARAMETERS§r. In the GUI of the controller, there are two configurable parameters, overclock and overvolt, that change how computation and heat are generated. Higher overclock values contribute the most to computation and higher overvolt values contribute the most to heat. Alone, this would encourage the player to make overclock as high as possible and overvolt as low as possible, but there is a penalty to computation for large differences between these two parameters. Furthermore, overvolt values <1 will cause the QC to randomly drop computation proportional to its distance from 1. It is highly encouraged to play around with these parameters, as all the best setups do.

See the adjacent quest for more information on computer racks and generating computation.

Now that you've started building up your precious Quantum Computer, how about the Research Station? Once again, using the Multiblock Structure Hologram Projector will tell you how to build this Multiblock. There should be 3 empty blocks beneath it so you can see the whole blueprint. Once it is nearly assembled, place down an Energy Hatch, an Optical Reception Connector, and a Maintenance Hatch all on the back side and an output hatch on the front side.

Once fully assembled, you can begin operating recipes at any time, so long as the Quantum Computer is also active and connected. The Research Station requires you to put the item to research within the Object Holder, then a data stick in the Multiblock interface. Once the Computation is fully completed, the data stick that houses all the data of the completed item will be inside the Multiblock Interface.

Still confused? Good, that's the spirit of learning! Always make sure to test these things in creative single player if you wish to find exact measurements and such. Don't forget to ALWAYS COLOR THE OPTICAL HATCHES AND FIBERS!

[note]Note that some researches require a significant amount of power, so keep that in mind.[/note]
The Sign Updater allows your MIM to update an external display of information.
The Item Valve allows your factory manager to suck in dropped items from around them in a 3x3x3 cube. Or you can use them to push items out into the world in the direction they are pointing.
Rapid Item Valves can pick up items in the world without any delays.

The cable cluster allows you to combine as many of the other cables together into one block. You could have a redstone receiver and emitter and an inventory relay all in one block.

This cable is a "terminal" cable. It does not extend the MIM beyond it.
The Advanced Cable Cluster will also act as an Inventory cable, extending the range of your MIM.

Sometimes you don't want a 3x3 area chunkloaded, but a long straight line instead. This can be handy for rail lines or power lines going across long distances. An anchor sentinel can perform this function. Right-click on a chunk loader with a crowbar, and it will activate. Go in any straight line from the chunkloader and place the anchor and hit it with the crowbar. Those chunks, up to 25x1, will now remain loaded.

This will draw an amount of chunkloader time relative to the 9 chunk area normally loaded. If for some reason you wanted only a 1 chunk area loaded, this will extend the time. Stock up on those pearls or server coins!
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lAll Those Chunks, All in a Row

betterquesting:10.desc:8: The Redstone Receiver reads redstone signals on each of its 6 faces.
The Block Gate can break, pickup, or place blocks.
The Block Detector allows your MIM to detect when a Block update occurs.
Now that you've reached EV you're going to need a more advanced cutting machine. Better get one built.

Variables - Declaration vs Standard
Declaration is simply creating a variable with eligible blocks in it. This allows easy updating of workflows. For instance you could have a variable that contains 2 chests. You use it in a nifty for each loop and later add another chest. Simply update the variable and the for each loop will start using it.

Standard variables are able to be inserted into the middle of a workflow (it has input/output) and thus can be modified on the run.

Please note that for each loop it will require an empty variable to work with. This is listed as "Element" in the loop.

Global vs Local
Global will keep changes to a variable that are done in the workflow, whereas local keeps anything done local to that part of the workflow.

This magical box is amazing. No matter how many are created, they all seem to connect to the same dimension. I can store items in one location, and pull them out somewhere else!

I can use dyes on the top of the box to assign its location, and any box with the same colors will share the same space. Using a diamond on the box locks it to me, and me alone.

Shift-right-clicking will remove the diamond and the chest will rejoin the public network.

This tank always seems to connect to the same dimensional space. I can push fluids into the tank in one dimension, and retrieve them in a totally different dimension!

I have discovered a way to assign a location to each tank using dyes applied to the top. Using a diamond makes the tank private, attuned to the user's mind, and will not share fluids with any other player's tanks.

Shift-right-clicking recovers the diamond and makes the tank part of the public tank network again.

The dial on the front controls the input/output of the tank. When blue is up, the tank accepts fluids. When orange is up, the tank will eject fluids.

§3If you get FPS problems from large numbers of them, try the setting in the config to turn off the fancy render at the bottom.

Instead of a chest you have to keep placing and breaking, how about a nice convenient pouch you can use? You'll have to synchronize it with the chest you want to link with. To set it to a new chest, sneak-click with the pouch on a new chest.
betterquesting:10.name:8: That Chest is Too Big to Carry Around

betterquesting:10.desc:8: EBF and LCR recipes are going to need even more power. You'll need to craft EV energy hatches to supply them and keep them running.

When the pack updates and changes an assembly line recipe, your old data sticks also need to change their recipe. In old versions, you needed to update the sticks by scanning new items, but now they will update automatically if placed in the assembly line, so you don't need to change things manually. If there is some kind of bug with data stick recipes after updating, do let the developers know, either on the Discord server or on GitHub.

NEI has a built in search feature for finding an item stored in an inventory nearby. A Stockroom Catalog can give you a list of everything stored in your inventories.

Sneak-right-click a block with an inventory (a chest, bookcase, barrel, anything with an inventory) to add that inventory to the list of inventories for the catalog to keep track of.

Sneak-right-click the same block again to remove that block from the list.

A small particle effect will render on any block that has been selected with the catalog when holding the Stockroom Catalog to let you know that block is being tracked.

Right-click to open the GUI and see the list. You can sort the list in ascending or descending order by quantity (Count) or alphabetical order.

You can also see a list of all the inventories that have a particular item and easily add the location of one of those inventories to a stockroom catalog so you can easily find your stuff.

The Stockroom Catalog can also be copied with the typesetting table and printing press.

Click on the title to change it to anything so you can custom label your stockroom catalog.

Click on the small chest icons on the right hand side of each listing to open the inventory list view.

If you want, you can craft a waypoint compass and use that to point you towards the chest. Since we have JourneyMaps and NEI, it's not really necessary.

[warn]The Catalog seems to be a bit broken though and doesn't work well with GT items.[/warn]

If you want energy from Lava and the byproducts, the Thermal Boiler is the perfect solution. It processes Lava super fast for Steam, and with a Lava Filter will provide some centrifuged lava byproducts as well. A great source of Copper, Silver, Gold, Tin, Tantalum, and Tungstate, better outputs than regular lava processing in a Centrifuge.

You can get even better efficiency pairing it with a Large Heat Exchanger. The LHE will turn normal vanilla Lava into Pahoehoe Lava, which will provide Steam and byproducts in the Thermal Boiler. Win/Win/Win!

The §5§lIndustrial Centrifuge§r is the best solution for handling the thousands of ores being produced by the multiblock ore drill. You will eventually want to have an array of these running, though one or two is fine to start.

This multiblock gives you §6§l4-8§r parallels per voltage tier, operates at §2§l2-3x§r the speed, and grants a §3§l10%§r EU discount. This makes it a far better alternative to both singleblock Centrifuges and the Steam Separator.

The parallel and speed modifiers start at their minimums and increase to their maximums as the Centrifuge gains momentum.

The Centrifuge will gain 1% momentum every 10 ticks while running §3
(50s to go from 0% -> 100%)§r

On the other hand, it will lose 2% momentum every 5 ticks while idle
§3(12.5s to go from 100% -> 0%)§r
betterquesting:10.name:8: §8§lI Think I'm Going to be Sick

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
§r[warn]This multiblock always runs recipes at the same tier as the energy hatches in the structure. If the machine does not have enough power supplied, it won't turn on.[/warn]

Although this multiblock is available in IV, we recommend building one §nafter finishing the Naqline§r.


This multiblock has 3 different modes: §3Normal§r, §4EBF§r, and §6Ore§r.


In §3Normal§r mode, this multiblock §3processes normal arc furnace recipes§r.

In §4EBF§r mode, this multiblock can process §4every EBF recipe regardless of coil tier requirement§r. This feature comes at the cost of §lbase recipe voltage being increased by 2 tiers§r. The available recipes are limited to the energy hatch tier.

In §6Ore§r mode, this machine can only process ores and raw ores that can be smelted in a normal furnace, giving molten metal directly.


In addition to the modes, this machine has 3 different processing phases.

§lStartup:§r The machine ignites its arc for 6 seconds before it can process recipes. Startup power depends on the installed electrode's stats: §6maximum parallels§r * §2EU Modifier§r * (1 + §4Startup Penalty§r). The required amperage is shown as §lStartup Amperage§r in the electrode tooltip.

§lProcessing:§r During this phase, the machine processes recipes using the Speed, Parallels, OC, and EU Modifier statistics of the installed electrode. If the machine fails to find a recipe that it can use, it goes into the shutdown phase.

§lShutdown:§r The machine enters a 6-second phase during which it does not process any recipes and does not use any power. After the shutdown phase, it needs to go through startup again before processing recipes.


Electrodes also have durability and may provide unique special effects. Some electrodes can modify the normal Startup, Processing, or Shutdown behavior, so always check the electrode's tooltip.

Below §c25% remaining durability§r, every processing attempt has a §c5% chance§r to cause a random arc surge, forcing the machine to go through Startup again.

Abuela, will you teach us the chocolate song?
Con mucho gusto
Will you sing the chocolate song with us?
Great, sing along with Abuela!

Bate bate chocolate
Bate bate chocolate
Bate bate chocolate
Bate bate chocolate

Mix your chocolate, chocolate
Mix your chocolate, chocolate
Bate bate chocolate
Bate bate chocolate

Aside from mixing chocolate, the Industrial Mixing Machine offers §6§l8§r parallels per voltage tier and an additional §2§l100%§r speed boost per tier of Item Pipe Casing.

[note]Eventually, when you unlock §9UIV§r tiered glass, this can be given multi-amp hatches![/note]

I never wanna grow up, I wanna play with my §5§lIndustrial Extrusion Machine§r. This machine offers a §2§l3.5x§r speed boost and §6§l6§r parallels per voltage tier.

You can use multiple input buses with a different extruder shape in each and then throw the items to extrude into the bus with the appropriate shape.

Alternatively, you can also use an Extrusion Bus. These are more expensive but come pre-loaded with all of the extruder shapes so you can manually set them without needing to create one.

When all you have is a machine full of knives, everything starts looking like bread.

In order for the §5§lIndustrial Cutting Factory§r to function, it will need to have a sawblade put into it. The performance of the machine is directly correlated with the quality of the sawblade put in.

The first type of sawblade available to craft is the §lTungsten Titanium Carbide Sawblade§r. It gives you §6§l2§r parallels per voltage tier, a §2§l2.5x§r speed boost, and a §3§l10%§r EU discount.

Need lots of oxygen or hydrogen? Maybe you just want to rip apart materials for tons of aluminium? Both are perfect tasks for this multiblock.

The §5§lIndustrial Electrolyzer§r is much more effective than its singleblock variant. It offers §6§l4§r parallels per voltage tier, a §2§l2.8x§r speed increase, and a §3§l10%§r EU discount on all recipes. Sounds like a good deal to me!

The Cryogenic Freezer is a direct upgrade to the §5§lVacuum Freezer§r. It allows for §6§l16§r parallels, operates at §2§l3x§r the speed, and offers a §3§l10%§r EU discount.

Similar to the Volcanus, it has a running cost. It will consume §c§l10L§r of cryotheum per second while in operation. It must be supplied with Cryotheum via a Cryotheum Cooling Hatch

The Volcanus Advanced EBF will process items faster than you can believe. You'll need a constant supply of Pyrotheum to use it. And coils.

[note]This multi is IV, but uses 2 ZPM circuits.[/note]

Need enough wire to go around the world? Here you go.

The §5§lIndustrial Wire Factory§r is the only Wiremill multiblock, delivering §6§l4§r parallels per voltage tier, a §3§l25%§r EU discount, and a scalable speed bonus of §2§l+50%§r per Item Pipe Casing tier, ranging from §2§l1.5x§r speed while using Tin to an impressive §2§l5x§r speed while using Black Plutonium.

[note]Glass tier is irrelevant; use what works best for you![/note]
When you need plates by the thousands you use the §5§lIndustrial Bending Machine§r. It grants §2§l6x§r the speed and §6§l6§r parallels per voltage tier compared to the singleblock.

The §5§lAmazon Warehousing Depot§r is the ultimate multiblock for all your packing needs. Got tiny and small dusts coming out of your ears? This is the machine for you.

The AWD offers a very generous §6§l16§r parallels per voltage tier, as well as a §2§l2-8x§r speed bonus (depending on item pipe casing tier) and a §3§l25%§r EU discount on all recipes.

[note]Glass tier is irrelevant; use what works best for you![/note]

When you use the seismic prospector, you'll need a scanner and a printer to create the books full of tasty ores and delicious fluids.

Use ink sacs in a fluid extractor to get squid ink. Then move it using pipes or cells.

The portable scanner is a direct upgrade to the plant lens.

Just like the lens, the scanner can tell you all the information about a crop growing inside of a crop stick, but unlike the plant lens it also displays the exact Nutrient Score provided by the crop stick.

[note]The portable scanner isn't just for crops, it can tell you a lot of information about basically everything! Look for the Portable Scanner quest after the EBF quest in Multiblock Goals tab for more information![/note]
betterquesting:10.name:8: Tools Of The Trade 5 - Electronic Scanning

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
There are a couple of ways to increase your Gallium.

1. Find TiCo zinc gravel ore and process it to get gallium.

2. Breed Zinc Bees and react the Gallium Combs with Hydrochloric Acid. The bee is not too deep in the breeding progression and the processing only requires LV.

3. Use crops under the Green Revolution tab to get Galvania leaves, to 4x your zinc and sphalerite crushed ores to purified ores.

4. Use the HV macerator on the centrifuged ores to get a 10 percent chance of a whole Gallium dust.

5. Use plentiful Bauxite ores from the Moon.

6. Kill Redcaps/Redcap Sappers in Twilight Forest. Also Kobolds drop Arsenic.

7. Duplicate nugget with Thaumcraft. This requires §lTaboo§r researches, so you might not want to do this.

For Arsenic, Cobaltite ore in the Twilight Forest is a great source for more information go to the quest "Cobalt and Arsenic from Cobaltite".

Cobaltite can also be multiplied 4x by the crop Nickelback.

Tired of killing spiders for string? Grow some flax for an easy non-biting source of string, add in some cotton and weave them together and you're almost to tanned leather! Just need some Corium now...

Need an alternate source of Chlorine? Breed some Tearstalks to get Ghast Tears for making salt water.

;-;
Then grow some Blazereed to save yourself the trouble.
Need to impress a lady or gent? How about growing diamonds on reeds...
Because it can lay eggs!
betterquesting:10.name:8: Why Does My Plant Bawk Like a Chicken?

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Like little mini black holes.

Don't try to eat them, you'll never feel full again.

There are a number of different ways to produce that wonderous material known as glowstone dust, pick your poison. 

No matter which crop you end up picking, the mass centrifuging of glowstone dust can produce a number of useful materials passively.
This crop can produce its own fertilizer! Alongside other byproducts, making it one of the best crops to get statted up early. Once you have infinite fertilizer, breeding for stats gets a lot easier.

Oil from crops? Makes as much sense as oil from bees!

If you're looking for passive oil before the §5MV§r Crop Breeder, there is another crop that can help but it is §omuch§r slower.

[warn]You can't use an §5MV§r Crop Breeder or Seed Generator in order to breed 31/31/31 seeds since their fluid capacity is too low.[/warn]

You'll need to follow these steps in order to get your hands on oil-berry seeds if your parents have maxed stats:

1. Down-stat one of the parents via manual breeding.
2. Use a spade to get some spare seeds.
3. Use the lower stat seeds to create an oil berry seed using the §5MV§r Crop Breeder.
4. Max out the stats of the oil berry seed like you originally did when you got your first maxed crop.
5. Use a spade to farm enough seeds to fill your fields.

Alternatively, if you don't want to bother with this process you can just wait until you can get your hands on the §5HV§r Breeder and Seed Generator.

[note]If you want to go with the §5MV§r route, using random breeding is the easiest way to get your hands on a mid-stat version of the parents. For oil berry, the simplest solution simply involves breeding withereed with a 1/1/1 sugar cane until you breed a new mid-stat withereed.[/note]

High speed transition and booster tracks get your carts moving at really ridiculous speeds. Do not use normal track without several transition tracks or else your cart will explode. Do not try turning at high speed or, you guessed it, your cart will explode.
4000 buckets not enough storage? Stockpiling diesel for a lifetime? Try a Super Tank 2.

To make PTFE, aka Teflon, you only need a few steps.

The first one is hydrofluoric acid. If you haven't reached the moon yet, the best sources for fluorine might be cryolite. Other options are treating Sand or Sandstone in a Chemical Plant for some Fluorite Ore, and centrifuging stone dust or black granite dust for biotite. You can also get small amounts from Lepidolite in salt veins and Mica. Mix it with some hydrogen to get hydrofluoric acid.

If you have reached the moon, you can also process Bastnasite ore.

§6Already automated PTFE? Hold 128 sheets to skip this questline.

The next step is to mix methane and chlorine to make chloroform. Make sure you have your circuit set correctly.

Now is probably a good time to look at stockpiling chlorine. Look for salt ores, or lapis veins. You can also make salt water with ghast tears. Better get started with crops, you'll need a lot of chlorine later!

[note]Lucky for you though, in this line we can recover all of our Chlorine.[/note]
Molten plastics smell great, don't they? Mix your Hydrofluoric Acid and Chloroform to make Tetrafluoroethylene. React the TFE with oxygen to make molten PTFE.
There's no limit to how much fluid you might want to store. Make yourself some super tank III's for all your bulk storage needs.
To process more advanced materials like Cosmic Neutronium, Tritanium and Awakened Draconium you need more than 9000K. Upgrade your EBF to 9900K.

Get yourself some Silicon Dioxide! Smelting it in your EBF with some carbon is the best way to obtain raw silicon ingots. It is used in a few places but most importantly you can macerate it back down to raw silicon dust. You can also turn the silicon dioxide into raw silicon dust via chemical processes using aluminium or magnesium.

You can get silicon dioxide easily by centrifuging glass dust or electrolyzing sand.

If you have raw silicon dust but want silicon dioxide for some reason, you can use an arc furnace or an autoclave.

The L.E.S.U. is one of the oldest machines still available in GregTech. Its origins are in Minecraft 1.3.X but has been redone to fit into this modpack. You can add a nearly infinite number of LESU casings to it and you'll have a huge Energy Storage. You might also live inside your Battery.

[note]PS: It sucks, don't make it. Maybe somebody will rework or buff it some day.[/note]
Sometimes you just need a Diode, either to prevent burning up cables when splitting off a main line, or on a Thermos Server's chunk borders. Make one 4A Diode and get a 2A one for free!

Annoyed by building chains of transformers? Don't want an Explosion Risk at your base? Want to use these fancy 64A Hatches and Dynamos from TecTech to convert your power? Make a Manual Dynamo and convert it all!

Hatches placed must be touching a Transformer-Winding block, with dynamo hatches being on the top and energy hatches being on the bottom. The height of the Transformer-Winding blocks can be optionally extended up to 8 blocks.

[note]Also needs a muffler, energy hatch, and dynamo. Not guaranteed to work, wishing you all the best though.[/note]
The Rock Cutter is an unbreakable and Silk-touched Mining Device. It will enable you to mine blocks without damaging them, like glass or stone, while it is charged. Uh, Woo?
Adding this many Cells anywhere to your LESU will upgrade it from ULV to LV.
Adding an additional amount of Cells will not only cause your storage capacity to rise, but also will enable MV Voltage.
The HV Tier upgrade first needs over a Stack of Casings. More Casings, more Energy, more Capacity.
Close to 8 Stacks of LESU Casings, this upgrade enables EV Voltage on your LESU. It's easy until now.

24 Stacks of LESU Casings. These do fit in your Inventory, but crafting them is another problem.

[note]If you don't want to clear out your inventory, just check the box when you have enough.[/note]

To reach the highest Voltage Tier the LESU can offer, you need to add an additional amount of LESU Casings. 8193 Casings in total (all upgrades below and these additional) enable the LuV Input Voltage.

[note]I mean you could do that, but maybe just check the box once your autocrafting is done.[/note]

To build a Windmill you will need a Dispenser, but that item is locked behind the next Tier. Go and find one in a Witchery Circle. They look like small versions of Stonehenge.

Look for the main quest in Multiblock Goals.

The Windmill is a grinder that uses the force of wind to macerate Items and Blocks. You will only get one crushed Ore from it sometimes. However it does give a bonus when you try to macerate other things. That bonus depends on the item inserted, for example Netherrack has a chance to give two instead of one dust and Wheat will always give one and a quarter flour.

The dispensers replace a clay block in the walls. Put anything you like in the interior - a bed, stairs, torches, etc.

Normal multiblock rules apply - do not cross chunk boundaries with this multiblock.

If this is your first GregTech multiblock, as with all the rest you will need to whack the controller with a soft mallet to activate it.

If you have troubles forming the multiblock, try breaking and replacing the controller block.

The controller can be fed items via hoppers etc. to allow for larger batches. Just don't allow the dispenser to fill up or it will void outputs.

The rotor blades will run if the controller is disabled or has no recipe. Remove the blades when not in use or else they'll be used up.

Speed and output will be affected by wind speed, recipe, and rotor.

Macerates 16 items at a time.

High wind speeds will decrease output.

The durability will decrease according to the wind speed.

To process the most advanced materials like Infinity Catalyst or Infinity you need more than 9900K. Upgrade your EBF to 10800K.

[note]With the heat adjustment included, you can get up to 11601K if you OC with UHV hatches. Not that you need it or anything.[/note]

The GTNH pack is made for the Realistic World Generator (RWG).

If your setup uses the vanilla biomes worldgen, you will get huge Mushroom biomes over the map. If you have this problem, please generate a new world with the RWG.

If you met this problem on a server, put "level-type=rwg" into the server.properties file and generate a new world.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §9§lMushroom Biomes? Why Are There So Many?

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Tantalum is used in many important GT recipes, and is also a source for niobium. You can find Tantalite at Y 20-30 on the Overworld and at Y 20-30 in the Nether.

[note]Tip: The Manganese you get from these ores can be used for EnderIO capacitors.[/note]

§4Keep in mind you need an HV + Kanthal EBF and an MV Chemical Bath to get Tantalum Ingots.

GregTech tools like the knives get used up when crafting foods. Pam's Tool like the Cutting Board, Juicer or the Bakeware can last forever.

After you reach stainless steel in HV you can make these tools that last forever.

Ironwood is a much harder and durable material than you imagined at first. Making Tools and Armor gives them unique features. With a pickaxe, you can mine ores up to Cobalt level, meaning you can harvest Ardite and Cobalt without an EBF.

If you stay in the Twilight Forest for more than a few minutes you'll find Canopy Trees. This big tree generates a lot of logs for your Coke Ovens and some roots when planted which give sticks. Be careful that no building or chest right beside or above the tree otherwise the tree replaces it. You might find a use for this, to sinfully get above a ceiling you really shouldn't.
Ironwood Armor is a magic armor with some special enchants. The Helm gives aqua affinity, the shoes feather falling, the plate and the legs extra protection.
You'll never §oever§r need to fix maintenance problems on any multi that has this, nor will it cost parts. Well, except to make it.

If you haven't noticed, this world is a true hellscape full of Special Mobs and Infernals around every corner. Unlike in vanilla, a player has to actually stay aware and pay attention to what they are fighting. Here are some tips.

If an infernal has Vengeance, don't shoot it with your 56-damage crossbow!

A high health infernal with regeneration is hard to kill. Even worse if it is a witch that can also heal herself. In those cases, run like hell, or bring a soul vial to capture it and throw it into Mount Doom.

Watch out for zombies with fishing poles - they can pull you to them. And zombies with a bow and arrow - they can shoot you back!

Creepers can make you have a baaaad time.

Drowning Creeper - when it explodes, it surrounds you in a ball of cobble filled with water. Not only do you have to escape, but the cobble is infested with silverfish! And those silverfish are all infernal! The best way to deal with it is to first escape up or down. If you have to clear the cobble ball, first clear the water. Surrounding the cobble with a dirt moat will keep the silverfish inside and unable to hide. Put down punjis, quicksand, or lava, and/or spectral glass. Make a wall with a 1x1 window and use that to break the cobbles - fishing silverfish is especially dangerous.

Concussion Creeper - Randomly teleports you a short distance - possibly deep underground.

Some spiders have nasty modifiers:

Witch spiders reflect missile damage back at you. If you see a red X on their back, draw your melee weapon and prepare for close combat...

Mother spiders will spawn a lot of baby spiders on death, some of which may be infernal.

A flying spider can grab the oblivious flier.

Ghost spiders are partially invisible and can pass through thin walls.
The only zombie pigman to watch out for is the Vampire Pigman. He hardly takes any damage unless you use a wooden sword as a stake, or have a magical sword.

Blazes are all infernals, and all nasty. Avoid like a plague. Get awesome weapons, awesome armor, and prepare for a fight.

The alternative is to figure out a way to destroy them with technology.

The alternative to the alternative is to figure out a different way to get blaze powder and blaze rods.

Need to make a lake? Look no further than the Flood Gate. It will fill the world with any fluid you provide it, up to the level below the gate. This can get kinda laggy in a large area, so keep that in mind.

With further research, I've discovered a key made of spectral iron can open a portal into a pocket dimension. It's only one chunk wide, but perfect for storing stuff I might need while exploring faraway planets, or as a quiet refuge after a difficult battle. Using it as a teleportation hub might also be an idea...

I've found another use for Ectoplasm - making Spectral Iron. An armor made from it is better than diamond and highly enchantable.

It also will drop healing orbs that will heal the nearest player when picked up.

Unfortunately, a side effect is that you'll become partially transparent. Side effect, I mean bonus feature!

Jumping all the time is exhausting and makes you really hungry.
To reduce your food depletion, you might want to use stairs instead.
Looking for an alternative to flowing water for your mobfarm? Use a fan to blow mobs or items where you want. Apply a redstone signal to activate.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lAll We Are is Dust in the Wind

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
But you really do care. Trying to find a good place to locate a windmill? You could just build one and see, or try this fancy windsock.

Paper rotors are great in low winds.
Wool rotors are cheap.
Leather rotors are durable.

Don't leave the rotors in the windmill when you aren't using it, it will use up durability.
...But she'll never stop because you'll always have something to grind. You can use a hopper to keep the windmill full of items to process. Just remember to retrieve them from the dispensers.

Welcome to the latest Moron's Manual, Effective EBFing! This manual covers common problems encountered when using the GregTech 1000 Electric Blast Furnace.

Setup
When setting up your EBF, make sure to place it a few chunks away from things pollution affects, like farmland. Pollution is nobody's friend!

During setup, make sure the center of the EBF is hollow. Sometimes things can sneak in there without you noticing, like a Thaumcraft light orb!

Make sure your muffler hatch is placed on a middle block. The EBF can't work if it is not spreading those delightful odors!

When placing your power hatches, make sure to minimize the distance between any generators and the EBF. Especially at LV, those few blocks make a big difference! Every amp of energy traveling over a cable loses a little bit - and you'll need as much as you can get! Your best setup is to put two generators right next to each hatch, with a 2A cable. If you're poor, you could use 2 battery buffers with 2 batteries each directly attached to each hatch. Make sure to top off the buffers' generators. If you make 9 slot battery buffers, you can fill them up over time to get longer running time until you get stable power.

Output hatches and buses will automatically push into tanks and inventories placed next to them such as chests or BC tanks.

When building multiple EBFs, the GregTech 1000 Electric Blast Furnace can share walls. This can save you on input, output, and maintenance hatches too. Not recommended for energy hatches!

Jelly sandwiches are a great food source with decent saturation and are easy to make. Almost any fruit can be converted to jelly with sugar and a saucepan. There are a few different nut butters available. Peanuts can be found in Ground Gardens in forest, mountain, or taiga style biomes. Cashews are trees located in jungles or swamps. Chestnuts can be found in warmer forests. Pistachios can be found in jungles. Many of these saplings are also available for trade from villagers. You'll need a mallet or a juicer to turn those nuts into a buttery paste!

To keep all your recipes together, you can use either a Kitchen multiblock if you want to see all recipes available to you, or a Forestry Worktable if you're fine with the limit of nine recipes.

Some sandwiches have better saturation than others, so be sure to check before buying that sapling!
betterquesting:10.name:8: Just Like Mom Used to Make

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Now that you have dough, there are several options for large sandwiches. They offer great saturation restoration and are easy to make.

The veggie and cheese options aren't quite as good and need more work to produce.

There are also normal-sized varieties of these sandwiches if you need more diet choices.
If you happen to be near a snowy biome, you can harvest the snow to make delicious smoothies. They are more satiating than eating the berries by themselves.

Do you like pies? I sure do! There are many varieties of pies available for you. The chicken pot pie is one of the easiest to make. Just a chicken, potato, carrot, and some dough. The fruit pies are a little simpler, so they don't quite restore as much saturation, but are great for filling tummies while you wait for the best foods to wear off.

If you haven't received one in a lootbag already, you can craft a nice magnet with a vibrant crystal. It doesn't work great on servers if you're moving around too fast, but it makes harvesting crops a lot easier.

Already have barrels full of cobblestone? The voiding drop filter can be set up to automatically void any item on pickup. Cobble, dirt, arrows, saplings, etc. It's handy for when you don't have much room for junk.

To use, right-click the item filter you get as a reward. Put the things you want voided in the item filter list by clicking in there with them. Esc, then right-click the voiding drop filter, and put the item filter inside.

In this pack you have to first gain expertise in Thaumcraft to craft the Tinker's Construct Ball of Moss. Go and become a dangerous wizard, and you'll gain the power needed to craft the Ball of Moss and make your tools heal themselves. Of course, you need to get to the Twilight Forest and get some aluminium ingots before you can begin. The Ball of Moss is in the GTNH tab of the Thaumonomicon, and requires infusion. There are many other great things in the Thaumonomicon, but be wary of warp.

Have a beer to prepare for your long journey.

Need enderpearls? Getting them by killing endermen can be dangerous. Instead of doing that, put an enderman into a smeltery with hot fluids and use a gem cast to get guaranteed pearls.

The higher the hit points, the longer they'll last, so the more pearls you get. If you can find a regenerating enderman, or an enderman spawner, you'll have all the pearls you would ever want. Later on with EnderIO you can even create your own powered spawner to make endermen on-demand. Or just place it in the End and move the mobs inside.

Use a nametag on a regenerating enderman to make sure he doesn't despawn. You'll want to keep him from seeing the sky or else he'll teleport away.

If you haven't found a regen enderman yet, you can buy enderman spawn eggs to put into your smeltery with coins. Maybe you'll get lucky and get a regenerating one. As a slightly more volatile alternative, an ender creeper works too.

The primary way of getting Zinc early on is via small chunks for Zinc Gravel Ore that can be found on the surface

If you're having trouble finding Zinc Gravel due to an unlucky world seed or playing on an old server, there are alternative ways made available for you to obtain it:

1. Search for Small Zinc Ore in the overworld
2. Use the recipe with XP buckets in a crafting table
3. Buy the Zinc Gravel Ore in the Vending Machine (Unlocked later in this tab!)

[note]Once you reach LV, you can get Zinc from processing various ores like Antimony, Sphalerite, Tetrahedrite and Tin. You will also be able to macerate the gravel ore for twice the product so save what you can until then![/note]
Most machines in MV need a motor as well. If you haven't built a polarizer already, go craft one. MV motors need magnetic steel rods and aluminium rods, 2x cupronickel wires and copper cables.
MV Energy hatches need ultra low power ICs. Go and craft some.

The MV Gas Turbine pairs excellently with Benzene, now that you can actually make it. Look at the "Bio for the Masses" tab for more details on how to go about it, or just check NEI. Benzene is renewable from trees, and it's a powerful source of EU that can keep you going for several tiers as long as you upgrade it with the new multiblocks you unlock over time.

It's a good idea to switch off Steam, since you need big pipes to carry that around and the fuel efficiency on Steam Turbines is lower. Instead, make a Pyrolyse Oven or an Advanced Coke Oven to make Charcoal faster, extract Benzene from it and run it through a few of these Gas Turbines.

The MV Combustion Generator burns Light Fuel faster than the LV version, but you can also automate Diesel and burn that instead, since it's even more powerful. It is arguably the easiest and most efficient way to generate lots of power for automation at this stage, and it'll last you a couple more tiers if you upgrade it as you go.

Additionally, Diesel can be used as fuel for the Copterpack, a good jetpack that makes it much easier to move around, inside and outside of your base. It's heavily recommended that you make one, if you have Diesel.

[note]This will also unlock new quests in the Armors and Jetpacks tab.[/note]
Field Generators are powerful devices. They're generally used in super tanks, super chests, in UU-Matter production and use, or in teleporters. Also, anything someone wanted to make harder to make.
Vinyl Chloride is the base product for making PVC for advanced pipes. These Pipes are needed in LuV machines or the Hermetic Casing IIs for Super Tank IIs.

Polyvinyl Chloride is PVC which can be used for the PVC Pipes. You need Vinyl Chloride and Oxygen to make it. You'll also want it for SMD capacitors later.

Do the recipe twice if you want to clean out your reactor, or three times if used the eight second recipe.
PVC Sheets make SMDs (make foils), plastic circuit boards, and really good item pipes.

The Soul Brazier from Thaumic Exploration will store your permanent warp.

As long as it has Ignis centi-vis and Mortuus essentia fed from underneath it will stay active, even while you are in other dimensions. Turning it off or running out of power will dump all that warp back into your body, so watch out.

Containing warp does have a bit of a downside - taint. You'll need to figure out a way to stop that.
To get UU-Amplifier out of your scrap you need an Amplifabricator. Both types of scrap are equivalent.

Now you can actually make the UUM with a Mass Fabricator. Well, technically you could make it without UUA, but that's way more expensive. To make sure it only runs with UUA, put a programmed circuit (any value) in the machine's slot. UUMatter can be used for some very specific things, such as replicating §osome§r materials (check NEI, mostly/all periodic table), used with crops to create an ore, some specific high-level recipes need it, and...you can also sit in it to get regen.

The energy usage and overclocking of the Mass Fabricator is different from the usual GT way. To have fixed EU to UUM ratios for all tiers, the machine does 2/2 OC. It also starts with a very high amperage in LV. The following chart should make it more clear:

Tier  Amps       EU/t         Time
LV     8A         256          160
MV     4A         512           80
HV     2A        1024           40
EV     1A        2048           20
IV     0.5A      4096           10
etc.

Put in power (and hopefully UUA), and out comes UUM.

For now, just stockpile the UU matter. You need data orbs to use the replicator, and that's explained next tier.

[note]You only need to fulfill one of the listed Mass Fabricator requirements.[/note]

Data Orbs are high tier data sticks to replicate materials or used as data storages. 

Additionally, similar to how a Data Stick can copy the configuration of a singular multiblock hatch, the Data Orb can copy the configuration of multiple hatches on a multiblock and paste to another that is laid out in a similar fashion by clicking it on the controller.

Using the scanner, you can scan certain items (check the replicator's NEI recipes) to store the information of the item to a data orb so you can make copies of them with the replicator. This process uses a varying amount of UUM and time, depending on the item. Scanning also takes forever.

Some items you might want to replicate include:
Indium
Platline metals like Iridium and Osmium
Neon, Krypton, Xenon from liquid air distilling
Oganesson

For some things (Oganesson), this might be considered the only reasonable way of getting a decent amount.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §8§lCreate New Materials Out of Pure Energy

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Field Generators are powerful but expensive devices.

It's, like, faster than a normal one I guess? But uses power.

If you would prefer to use steam instead, then the multiblock is also a good option.

Be careful when wearing your hazmat suit all the time. The durability is not very high. Even just falling a few blocks will damage the boots quickly.

You can repair your suit long before you can craft a new one in late LV Age, using some rubber sheets and a glue bucket.
An IV assembler is required to make new coils, or enriched Sunnarium for HV Solar Panels.

For more tungsten and tungstensteel, you'll want scheelite and tungstate. But the most important is desh, found only as small ore elsewhere, and used for the next rocket. Check Y 5-40.

[note]Since there's a good chance you have the MBM by now, you can do the crushed ore task instead of the ore one. This holds for other, similar quests.[/note]

Turbines require precise amounts of fluids or else they will [warn]explode[/warn]. Use the fluid regulator on the pipe attached to the input bus to control the rate of fluids into the turbine. To raise the fluid limit, look at the right side of the regulator and:

1L - Right-click with an empty hand
16L - Right-click with a screwdriver
256L - Right-click with a screwdriver while sneaking

To lower the fluid limit, do the same while looking at the left side. [note]If you shift-right-click on it you can use the interface which is more precise.[/note]

Use the GTNH Power Planner linked below to find what to set it to, after deciding on a fuel. At GTNH, we do the math for you! For this at least.

[url]https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1FTFdfmY_UWbTbFOyNzARKeI90pbHvPBH6M3JHJmaC-E/edit?usp=dsharing[/url]

A Large Gas Turbine is more fuel-efficient than singleblock turbines, and can have lower pollution output with upgraded mufflers.

You will also need a Muffler and Dynamo Hatch to complete the multiblock. Don't forget to use a Fluid Regulator, to control the flow rate into the multi! It can usually be an LV Fluid Regulator, since the optimal flow is much lower here than in Steam Turbines.

Each turbine material has a specific fuel efficiency (the higher, the more EU you get from the same amount of fuel), and the multi only reaches this efficiency if the fuel flow into it matches the optimal flow.

If you go beyond the optimal flow, you will get a higher EU/t value, but less fuel efficiency, and the maximum EU/t value depends on the turbine type and its Overflow Efficiency tier. For this type of turbine, tier 1 reaches the max at 150% of optimal flow to produce 112% of the EU/t, tier 2 reaches the max at 300% of optimal flow to produce 180% of the EU/t and tier 3 reaches the max at 450% of optimal flow to produce 252% of the EU/t. The closer you get to this maximum, the more fuel efficiency you're throwing away.

For the best turbine materials, see the spreadsheet and Large Turbine Calculator.

For someone who needs to blast a truly §lridiculous§r amount of stuff, the §5§lExothermic Hearth§r is the machine for you. This monster machine can handle up to §6§l256§r parallel recipes at a time.

If allowed to heat up fully, the machine will run with §6§l2x§r as many parallels (though that takes around 30 minutes). You can optionally provide it §c§l250L/s§r of Pyrotheum to speed up this process by §2§l6x§r.

The glass tier limits the energy hatch tier that you can use. You can even use multiamp hatches from TecTech! If you want to use laser hatches, however, you need at least §2§nUV§r glass.

The §5§lEndothermic Fridge§r can process up to §6§l256§r parallels! You can also optionally provide §9§l250L/s§r of Cryotheum to the machine to give it a §2§l5x§r speed boost.

[note]Eventually, you will be able to upgrade this to its T2 variant.[/note]
Now that you have lead you can convert your bronze pipes to potin pipes with higher capacities.

Some machines have a very, very large number of recipes. To avoid conflicts, many recipes have programmed circuits to ensure that the correct recipe is used. These programmed circuits are not consumed.

In this modpack, all singleblock GT machines now come with an icon in the GUI on the bottom-right that represents a ghost circuit. Click it or scroll to choose the number you need. If you do that, you don't have to insert a physical circuit. This is going to be your main option for all single block machines. This option is now also available for input buses of multiblocks, which you will use much later.

There are a few places throughout the modpack where you still need the physical circuits. You can turn an LV circuit into a programmed circuit in the crafting grid and then program it in various ways:

1) Find a correct crafting recipe with a screwdriver in NEI and use that.

2) Right-click while holding the programmed circuit to open an easy menu. You still need to at least have the screwdriver in your inventory though or it won't work. Eventually you can also make an electric screwdriver.

3) Use the BartWorks Circuit Programmer. It's only available in MV, but it does not use any durability and runs on EU.

4) Use the GT++ Circuit Programmer block. It isn't portable and only available in MV, but it allows for automation.

The tasks in this quest are just the showcase of what programming circuits there are. You can just click the checkmark once you understand how the programmed circuits work.

These are...not worth it. Go do something else with your enriched naquadah, like putting it in a naq gen if you want power. They work §oexactly§r the same as uranium other than materials cost/output.

[note]PS: You can get Nq+ from both centrifuging Nq dust or processing the ore.[/note]

[note]And why are they Naquadah rods when they're made of Enriched Naquadah?[/note]

They're so not worth it I'm just going to give you back the materials. Like naquadah, they're the same as MOX other than materials.

[note]PS: You can get Nq* from both centrifuging Nq or Nq+ dust, processing the ores, or thermal centrifuging the depleted Nq+ rods.[/note]
The MV GT++ Steam Boiler is the next machine you can make to produce steam efficiently. It regulates its fuel more efficiently if it ends up being full.

Need even more power? Why not combine rods? Produces more power (NOT double, it varies per rod type) and more heat (again NOT double) but only uses up one slot. You need more complex designs to handle them, but you were ready for that, right?

So how about doubling your doubling to double your double (4x)? Quad rods put out even more power and heat, expect all the other rods to work similarly (for the most part).

After your rods have finished their cycle they turn into depleted rods. You can then thermal centrifuge them to get some materials back. Depending on the rod, you can get different stuff, see NEI or the wiki for details.
The HV GT++ Steam Boiler is the next machine you can make to produce steam efficiently. It regulates its fuel more efficiently if it ends up being full.

With a nuke, you can cause some real catastrophic damage to your base. You can either place it 20 chunks away, or surround it with blast proof materials.

Fused Quartz is no good now, forget about it OK? Instead, use the GTNH approved Plated Reinforced Stone series! Or one of the other options I guess, like Warded Glass. You may need multiple layers depending on your reactor, try it out in creative. Remember you must close in the corners - blasts can slip through the cracks. To get power out, do right angle turns on the wires as blasts go in a straight line.

[note]There are 6 of them, use NEI.[/note]

[note]Okay, okay, you don't have to forget Fused Quartz, I'll give you some. Maybe you can stop rain with it.[/note]
The HV energy hatch is crucial to a faster EBF that can do higher tier recipes. You will probably want to make at least two.

Higher tier superconducting wires and energy hatches will require helium. Compressing air and liquefying it requires 1802 compressed air cells to get 1 He cell. It's probably better to get it from end stone dust or monazite from the Moon. Another option is to have a look at your oil processing and see how you can get Helium from there.

[note]PS: If you've progressed far enough in the TF, you can also chip off parts of the snow queen's lair. She won't mind, right?[/note]

The Large Heat Exchanger is a powergen multi that accepts a non-direct fuel, and doesn't output EU. What is it for, then? §7To heat up water with hot liquids, that's what!§r

Effectively, it's a Steam Boiler that uses fluids instead of solids, but it's more complicated. The three sources of energy are Lava, Hot Coolant, and Hot Solar Salt. The salt is the most powerful, but hardest to get. Lava can be automated from Everburn Urns or a myriad of other options, Hot Coolant usually comes from Fluid Nukes, and Hot Solar Salt is produced in the Solar Tower.

For Lava, the LHE outputs §d160 L of Steam for every 1 L of Lava, up to 1000 L/s of Lava input§r (§a4000 EU/t§r at 100% turbine efficiency). For Hot Coolant, the LHE outputs §d400 L of Steam for every 1 L of Hot Coolant, up to 800 L/s of input§r (§a8000 EU/t§r at 100% turbine efficiency). For Hot Solar Salt, the LHE outputs §d2000 L of Steam for every 1 L of Hot Solar Salt, up to 160 L/s of input§r (§a8000 EU/t§r at 100% turbine efficiency).

§cIf you go above these input rates, the output becomes Superheated Steam, which needs to pass through a Large HP Steam Turbine before the regular Large Steam Turbine.§r The maximum input rate here is twice of what was before and the conversion rates are now §d1:80 for Lava§r, §d1:200 for Hot Coolant§r, and §d1:1000 for Hot Solar Salt§r. The energy output at 100% turbine efficiency is §a12000 EU/t§r for Lava, §a24000 EU/t§r for Hot Coolant, and §a24000 EU/t§r for Hot Solar Salt.

§6§lVery powerful, but complicated, and needs turbines!§r

For more information, visit [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Large_Heat_Exchanger[/url] or [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Fluid_Reactor[/url].

If you have too much wood, saplings, netherrack or other garbage, you can recycle it and get scrap [note](this does not have a 100% chance)[/note]. Scrap can be used to make UU-Amplifier to make UU-Matter in 1/4 the time, saving you a significant amount of energy.

Certain items such as cobblestone, stone, and tiny/small dusts are too easy to make and don't give any scrap. But otherwise any items can be recycled to get scrap.

Or 4? Need to store ludicrous amounts of cobble? Stone dust? Saplings? Super chests are the thing to use. A Super Chest I can store 4 million items, worry free. You will need to take items out manually 64 at a time, or use conveyors etc. to extract them.

With an alloy smelter and some netherrack dust you can make Nether furnaces, which are extremely efficient cooking machines. Very handy for someone needing a lot of stuff furnaced in a jiffy.

In comparison to the Blast Furnace, they operate at half the speed and half the fuel usage. So they have the same fuel consumption ratio but are slower. Another downside to crafting Nether Furnaces is that they cannot be used as a component for the Electric Blast Furnace (EBF) craft later on. Blast Furnaces can.

Then again, Nether dust is practically free, and unlike Blast Furnaces these can process every type of furnace recipe, so what's the loss? You can always use them to bake stacks of bread!
A super chest III is just ridiculous. Who would possibly need to store 16 million items? You, that's who.
Now that you have an MV extruder you can make the next level of Tinker Tools - Vanadiumsteel head parts with Damascus Steel rods.
Now that you have an EBF you can make vanadiumsteel GT tools. With 192k durability they'll last you a long time.

When doing infusions, it's always good to know how close you are in stability. The Arcane Abacus will tell you at a quick glance how stable your infusion altar is, and any asymmetries present. 

For now, you can have one in exchange for a few types of common infusion stabilization blocks- but if you need to replace it, it will cost you some circuits!

When used together, the Typesetting Table and Printing Press allow you to duplicate enchanted books. You'll need a lot of XP, so either build a mob grinder or get farming. A Fortune III book, for example, requires 40 levels to convert into an enchanted plate.

To use the §lTypesetting Table§r, place a print press chase in the top slot and an enchanted book in the bottom left slot. Sneak right-click the enchanted book to convert it into an enchanted plate if you have enough XP.

To use the §lPrinting Press§r, place an enchanted plate in the center of the machine, ink sacs on the top metal plate, and books on the bottom left side of the counter. It immediately starts processing without any power or redstone signal.

Wearing Reading Glasses, Tinted Glasses, or a Monocle will display more information about these blocks when looking at them.

Each enchanted plate can make three enchanted books before breaking, but the trick is to make two books and then repair it in a Thaumic Restorer for unlimited uses.

[note]You'll need some Thaumium ingots. You can get into Thaumcraft, find some in a chest, or try breeding the Thaumium oreberry crop.[/note]
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lGut-Enough For You? Bet You Thought Newspapers Were Dead!

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Well not anymore! With some emeralds and a blank book, I'll give you a Fortune I book you can use in your printing press. Once you've duplicated it, you can combine the 2 Fortune I books in an anvil to get a Fortune II. Duplicate the Fortune II books to get a Fortune III!

With a Fortune III book and a tier-specific item you can remove the trash item rewards from your loot bags. More good stuff!

Soulbound is another good enchantment, it will keep an enchanted item in your inventory in case of death.

You may have found plenty of mud piles around the wetlands and thought of them as mere annoyances when jumping in the water or for that armor. Waste not! With your new extractor, you can pull out the clay hidden in the mud!
betterquesting:10.name:8: §c§lMud, Can Also be Used For Facials

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
A Needs Maintenance cover will send out a redstone signal when the controller it's attached to requires maintenance. This is handy for the cleanroom you'll need to build in HV, since maintenance issues reduces cleanliness level and will cause voided materials.

For the cleanroom you can place this on the top or bottom. For other machines you might want to place it on the side so you can have access to the front face. In that case, you can use a soldering iron and fine solder to have it emit a strong redstone signal that will penetrate through a block next to the cover.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lWhere's That Handyman When You Need Him?

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Knowing that your cleanroom needs maintenance is pretty important. Instead of just turning on a light, why not use a howler alarm? It'll notify you up to 128 blocks away.

[warn]Warning: May cause uncontrollable urine leakage when activated.[/warn]
Impossible! If you really think you have so much fluid that you want to just get rid of it, make a fluid trashcan. You can route as much excess creosote or whatever into it that you want.

Impossible! But if you really want to get rid of excess items, make yourself a trashcan. If you want to be really fancy, you can use a hopper with a lever next to it to make sure you only throw away items you really want. I mean, §lI've§r never thrown away a tool accidentally, nope, never me.

When breeding new crops, you will come upon hundreds of different species! While every species has a unique texture which a dedicated farmhand will be able to discern between, this tool will clear things up much quicker for you. 

After using it you can tell the following:
- Species
- Stats
- Crop tier
- Whether it can grow (many crops have special requirements)
- Whether you can harvest it
- Growth progress
betterquesting:10.name:8: Tools of the Trade 2 - Mendelian Identification

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Many centrifuging recipes are slow. You better upgrade your machines.

There are many interesting things you can centrifuge outside your normal ore processing or Methane production. Glowstone, Redstone, Soul Sand, Lava, Ashes, Planet Dusts, Compressed Air, etc. Make sure to look around a bit.

When you get to HV you'll want to start thinking about centralizing power generation and delivering power over longer distances. An HV to EV transformer will let you send power across your base without too much penalty.
How about 4x more? A Hi-Amp transformer will transform 4A to 16A. Great for setting up a large power grid and locating polluting power generators further from your base.
For the truly insane, there is a 16 to 64 A power amp transformer. Just ludicrous!

Wondering how to make your Radium decay? With a §5Lead-Lined Box§r you can safely leave your Radium in it and it'll decay while you do real work.

[note]Pipes work with it, but you can not use a WA.[/note]

Additionally, you can also choose to use the §5Decay Warehouse§r for this task; it's more efficient but comes at a much higher cost. (More info in Multiblock Goals tab)

Are you ready for a longer trip? With your new lunch box, saddle, lead and of course a horse, we can start a small journey. Be sure to make paths over water, horses don't like going through deep water. If you get unseated in deep water, you can try getting on repeatedly and moving a small distance each time, this may be faster for small rivers. You can also try jumping over the deep parts if it isn't that big.

If you are playing single player or a local server, horses make a great way to get around. On non-local servers they can cause problems and desync if you have poor internet, or if the server doesn't have good TPS. Like all the official servers.

You can tie the lead to your horse and the fence to get it to stick around while you investigate something.
Withereed is a rare species which produces coal but, rarely, can also produce fully formed wither skulls!
The God of Thunder crop lets you increase your Thorium ore from the Nether to 4x. It also will give you Uranium you can use for Reactoria crops.

A great source of uranium and Pitchblende.

Reactoria crops will drop Reactoria leaves which will 4x your Pitchblende ore.
If you want to save your cows and horses for milk and... glue... you can use Corium to produce your leather instead.
Creeperweed can supply your gunpowder without needing to deal with bothersome explosions.

Oat Milk? Nay.
Soy Milk? Nay.

Wart Milk. Say goodbye to your cattle.

Chisel is one of the main building mods in this pack. It adds hundreds of new blocks which will help make your base beautiful!

The mod also adds different variants of many vanilla blocks. Make a chisel to check them out!
Tinker's Construct has their own chisel tool variant, for converting Tinker blocks into different types. Not a lot of uses, but if you check NEI you can see what you can do.

Tinker's Construct offers a couple of useful blocks from the smeltery. Rough Brownstone takes Tin and Gravel and makes a block that lets you move a little faster. Cobblestone can be turned into Seared Stone, usable in the smeltery walls to make it larger without having to use clay.

The TiCon chisel doesn't have a lot of uses, but here are a couple of interesting ones. Use NEI to see other options for more decorations. You can also slab these blocks if you want something monsters cannot spawn on.

You can also use the chisel in-world on Tinkers' blocks to change them into different variants - just be aware that sometimes you can't change them back!

[note]Brownstone roads are slightly faster than rough brownstone.[/note]

[note]Using the chisel on seared stone allows you to turn it into seared bricks.[/note]
If, for some reason, you need to chisel a large number of items, the autochisel is what you want.
The autochisel speed is pretty slow. Craft some upgrades to make it faster.

The one place Chisel is weak is in stairs. It would be nice to have more variety, but later I'll show you how to make any block into a custom stair.

You can also search NEI for "stairs" to find stairs from other mods.
Chisel offers a wide variety of blocks. Searching NEI for "chisel" gives pages and pages. Here's a small sample.
There's also some really funky blocks available.
Chisel can also transform Concrete and GT stones into new interesting blocks. Some of the GT stone blocks will even prevent mobs from spawning on top. Concrete will let you run faster.

The only thing going for the stone builder's wand is that it's cheap. It doesn't offer much in special modes, and doesn't last long either. But you can make a lot!

To use, right-click on a block while holding more of that block in your inventory. An outline will show you what it will do.

[note]Tip: /wandoops will undo any block placements you make with the wand, just in case you misclick.[/note]
The Iron wand will last longer than the stone wand, and has a few modes.
The next tier up wand is the Diamond wand. Has all kinds of fun modes. Just be careful using it, would hate to place a bunch of blocks accidentally!

Troll plant! What does it do? Troll you! 


And give you cancer. Sorry!
betterquesting:10.name:8: Better Put On That Rubber Suit

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Want some emeralds for trading or other uses? These are the source.

The Botany mod offers more colors for blocks and glass, and simple tile patterns or more complex patterns using a Tileworker. For now, we'll make an iron trowel.

This mod will make lots of butterflies, so make sure to do your gardening underground or under glass. The butterflies will spread and infect leaves around your area, making more butterflies, causing lag.

To start, you'll need to find some flowers. Then take your trowel and use it on some dirt blocks to turn it into soil. Next place your flowers on the soil to turn them into Botany flowers. If you've reached MV tier, check out the How to Be(e) tab for info on Genetics.

Botany uses various powders to enhance soil properties.

Raise Ph - Ash Powder, Pulp Powder
Lower Ph - Mulch Powder, Sulphur Powder
Increase Nutrients - Fertilizer Powder, Compost Powder

Nobody likes weeds. Weedkiller will keep the weeds off your soil.

Bone meal can be applied to germling flowers to make them mature faster.
The soil meter will tell you the soil stats - how dry, how many nutrients, etc. You can amend the soil with the various powders so that it matches the requirements for your flower.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lLike Having a County Extension Office in Your Hand

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
When you plant a vanilla flower, it is already mature. Cut it with shears to get a germling you can replant to make more. Break the flower to get a mature flower. Turn the flower into pigment using a crafting table.

To get crosses, plant flowers next to empty soil blocks. Keep an eye out for weeds. Eventually a small germling will start growing.

Remember, do this underground or in an enclosure or your TPS will regret it.
The pigments color an amazing variety of glass. Just one warning - unlike normal glass, this glass isn't fireproof.
With some clay and pigments, you can make pigmented clay. Put the pigmented clay in a furnace to get basic ceramic blocks. These blocks are great if you want an area of nice even colors.

To make ceramic tile patterns, you need to convert your blocks into tiles. First make mortar, and then use the mortar with your blocks in a 3 block + 1 mortar pattern in the crafting table to get ceramic tiles.

Now that you have tiles, you can make simple tile patterns. A 2x2 of red/yellow and yellow/red makes a simple checkerboard. Using the checkerboard again in a 2x2 makes a checkerboard with smaller tiles. Use Binnie's Botany wiki page to find more patterns you can make with just tiles.

The tileworker can take the single-color ceramic blocks and turn them into pretty patterned blocks.

And contrary to the name, you use ceramic blocks here, not tiles.
Want some custom glass shapes and configurations? A glassworker can provide some unique patterns to put in your windows. You'll need to make some glass fittings to hold the glass together.

Yes indeed, time for another type of hammer. The master carpentry hammer will allow you to rotate the blocks from the various workers.

Sneak to rotate the blocks vertically.

Why is the lower tier hammer the master hammer? Who knows??
The panelworker will create wood flooring pieces for you to use.
With the woodworker, you can create fancy looking types of wood blocks. You can use wood planks from Vanilla, Forestry, and Extra Trees.

Tired of a base using nothing but torches? This set of quests will go through the various options available to light up your beautiful base.

First up, Railcraft lanterns. These come in stone and metallic varieties. The stone varieties don't need much to craft. One plus/minus for these lanterns is that they are solid blocks - while you cannot walk through them, they also do not fall if the surrounding blocks are removed. Search "lantern" in NEI for more varieties. They are a bit annoying to craft now, but if you check NEI you can make them pretty easily with assemblers later.
Forge Microblocks can be really handy to make custom pieces. There are many saw tiers available. If you make me an iron one, I'll give you a diamond one.
Bibliocraft offers fancy looking lanterns. Make the candles from candleberries or beeswax.

Now that you've been to the nether and gathered Glowstone, you can use that for light as well. You can color it to make the block color change (unfortunately 1.7.10 does not support colored lights) or you can use the Forge Microblocks saw to cut it up into tiny nooks to light up areas without taking up much space.

There are also various glowing plants you can find or breed, such as glowflowers.
The basic ProjectRed Illumination lamps only need an LV mixer to make. The normal version needs a redstone signal to turn on. The inverted version is on unless a redstone signal is applied.
The fancier ProjectRed Illumination lamps, lanterns, and fixtures require the Forming Press and Assembler to create.
ProjectRed offers a couple of special lights that can be used as buttons. The normal buttons are always lit up. The Feedback buttons are lit up when powered by any redstone signal.
These simple lamps from Ztones are a nice, subdued looking lamp style. I like using them on ceilings for the "office" look.

When traveling off-world, you want the best in torches. Torches that will work in no-oxygen environments like the Moon. For that, you need glowstone torches. You can chisel these torches into a variety of torch types, also proven to work in deep space.

If you have a relatively large area you need to light up without using electricity, you can use these floodlights. They can take normal furnace fuels, including blocks and compressed blocks. They do require some electronic components to make, but can send out a beam a long ways, or various cone shapes a shorter distance. Use the wrench to change modes, and shift-right-click to invert.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lLighting Up a Large Area, Without Electricity

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Now that you have a vacuum freezer, you can liquefy compressed air cells and centrifuge them for rare gases. You'll need those to make the incandescent bulb for these lights. As long as they have EU, these lights can shoot a beam or do narrow or wide cones. Use the wrench to change modes, and shift-right-click to invert.

It's better to provide power to an Ender IO capacitor and then power these machines with RF, instead of powering directly with GT EU, because they don't work well with GT's EU amp system, and will draw a whole EU packet for a single RF.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §5§lLighting Up a Large Area, With Electricity

betterquesting:10.desc:8: EnderIO also has its own lights. These lights have a radius of 8 blocks vs the normal 7.
The Powered and Wireless Powered lights from EnderIO provide light up to 10 blocks away vs the normal 7 for a torch. They will require centrifuging liquid air to get the bulbs.

The Malisis Door Factory lets you go crazy with all kinds of ideas for custom doors.

A Player Sensor is a nice way of opening a door. Better than pushing a button or stepping on a plate!

Maybe you can find a use for this block mixer, it's kinda weird and doesn't work right.

There are some craftable Malisis items as well, check them out in NEI.
You can build it! The Building Guide helps show you an outline of simple geometric shapes. Provide it with a redstone signal to activate.

The Enhanced Building Guide offers more features than the standard model. Most importantly, you can right-click on any white part of the block with the item you want placed and the block will place in the world. It needs a redstone signal to activate.

Elevators are great for fast transportation vertically in your base. Leaving a tinted elevator will stop at the same color elevator. Use some Malisis doors for a nice "real" elevator effect.
The rotating elevator will turn the player as they go up or down to face a specific direction. Handy if your elevator shaft is on one side at a floor and a different side at another floor.

The sawbench can turn most full cube blocks into amazing shapes of various kinds.

Right-click with the hammer to rotate 90 degrees. Shift-right-click with the hammer to change the orientation of the "bottom" face.

The Chisel is used to alter the structure of blocks in various ways. Some blocks automatically form connections with adjacent blocks. These connections can be disabled and re-enabled by right-clicking with a chisel near the side that you want to change.

Some blocks can have a secondary material applied to them. The secondary material can be removed by right-clicking on the center of the block with a chisel.

You can also right-click on a vanilla Glass, Glass Pane, Glowstone or Ice block with a chisel to harvest the block without breaking it.
Drawer upgrades are different from barrel upgrades. First you need to make the upgrade template.

There are many tiers of upgrades for storage drawers. Make some iron and gold tier upgrades and I'll give you some of the special purpose upgrades to experiment with in your base. Check NEI for more options such as Obsidian, Emerald, and Diamond upgrades.

[warn]To remove upgrades, shift-right-click with an empty hand to access the drawer interface.[/warn]
betterquesting:10.name:8: §c§lYour Mom Says to Upgrade Your Drawers

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
