The core block of Stacy's...er Steve's Factory Manager. SFM is a high tier automation system. While AE2 can handle a lot of different crafting tasks, SFM can handle even more complex crafting. It's not actually needed for the Assembly Line. But still, this is one place where you can go that route.

Inventory Cables connect the MIM to inventories or tanks.

Right now until some Moron figures it out, your best bet is to experiment, ask for help on Discord, and search Google. The interface resembles most GUI based automation systems like LabView.

There have been TPS problems caused by poorly designed SFM setups. Make sure your outputs are properly emptied, and don't get filled.

Inventory cables are the "basic" cable of SFM. They allow the MIM to interact with an inventory, and act as a connector cable to other cables.

mehdi2344 thinks my jokes suck, but he's an idiot, so there.

Thanks to Nori Silverrage for writing up these quests!

[note]BTW, there's a Creative Supplier for creative testing. The Energistics Connector is disabled because it doesn't work correctly.[/note]

Ever finished a wonderful program and then realized your Manager needs to move and you have to rewrite the whole thing? Ever need to copy and paste a section of code a bunch of times and been frustrated that you can't? Well we've got you covered with the Manager Duplicator!

The Factory Labeler allows you to assign unique names to anything that can be connected to a Manager - making it easy to identify when you are setting up commands.

Type in the text box to set a label or to searched stored labels - click any stored entry to select it, double-click to edit it. Closing the GUI will set the Labeler to whatever was in the text box at that time.

Left-click to set labels, right-click to open the gui. Setting a blank label will remove any existing labels.

[note]May or may not be buggy. Will lose the label in MP when relogging, but works fine in SP. It'll still work until you need to change it though. Have fun![/note]
Thaumic Machina offers Wand Augmentations. These useful modifications to your wand can boost their capacity, lower their vis usage, or do other interesting effects.
A Charge Buffer augmentation to your wand allows it to hold 25 percent more vis.
This wand augment will lower the vis cost when using your wand by 10 percent. I'm not sure it works, but give it a try and report back, OK?
Enchanted Fabric is the key material to fancy robes and wizard's clothing.

Every point of vis is critical, so make yourself some magical robes to help conserve how much you use. Later you can make even better robes. They don't offer much in protection, so remember to change before going to hunt!

And swimming. These boots of the traveller will make you a blur as you go around the world. You'll need to research infusion before you can make these.

§3There are also Electric versions with greater discounts in the Getting Around... tab.

With your new wand, you can make Goggles of Revealing. You can now see nodes clearly, more so than with the thaumometer, but all the time! Additionally, the goggles give you a 5 percent vis discount.

Simple lens upgrades will grant you various seeing abilities as well.

Later you can make more advanced goggles and even integrate the goggles into advanced armors.

With TC Node Tracker, it makes remembering nodes trivial. The default key is I. You can select from the list of nodes you have scanned, and an in-world arrow will show you the way. You can also sort the list.
The Redstone Emitter sends redstone signals on each of its 6 faces. The redstone signal strength can be set to any value, add, subtract, and more.

Platinum Chloride? You were promised Pure Platinum Metal at a much higher efficiency than just smelting it! No worries, just react the Platinum Chloride with Calcium and you're done. The Calcium and Chlorine can be recycled as well!

Hooray! All my Platinum Metal is now a fluid.... Time to add the second chemical to recrystallize the dust.

You do different things with each of the results:

Reprecipitated Platinum: Go to step 4, the last step.
Platinum Salt: Go to the recycling step.
Palladium Enriched Ammonia: Keep it like the Platinum Residue until IV. Or process it now if you like, but you don't §oneed§r it until later.
Others: Can be reused.

What, recycling? That's lame. I just wanna void this stuff! - is what you might think right now, but be aware that Platinum Salt still holds a high concentration of Platinum. We can recycle it to get even more Platinum out of it!

You need to sift it to get Refined Platinum Salt. You only have a 95% chance to get a dust.

Now, start with dissolving all the PMP into the Aqua Regia. You will also gain some Platinum Residue Dust. This highly concentrated dust contains a lot of even Rarer Metals, like Rhodium, Ruthenium, Osmium, and Iridium. You will need this at IV and higher, so stockpile it!
Brazil Nuts don't give you much in the way of important attributes. Breed them from Common Beech and Jungle.

Coconut is King for seed oil production - 300L per nut. Breed them from Brazil Nut and Balsa.

§eCoconut and Seed Oil Get!
Aromatic Lumps are twice as effective as Royal Jelly in an Alveary Swarmer. You'll need Enchanting Drops from Arcane bees and Pollen Clusters from Industrious bees.

Tired of the constant chirping from the thousands of bats drawn to your world-bending activities? Use this handy device to attract them to a central location where they can be...disposed. The Corporeal Attractor can be configured to attract or repel mobs, and the redstone strength applied divided by two determines the range.

You can use Soul Molds to filter the mobs the Attractor draws in or pushes away. This gives you some idea for automating...

Electric Boots of the Traveller grant you a 2% Vis Discount along with all the benefits of the regular Boots of the Traveller.

In addition, they come with a wide variety of new features thanks to our amazing magic devs:

- Configurable Jump Boost: You can choose between 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, or a 100% jump boost.

- Configurable Speed Boost: Similar to the jump boost, you can adjust the speed boost percentage to your preference.

- Flight Inertia: When toggled on, this feature cancels inertia while flying, allowing for precise movement even when traveling at high speeds.

- Omnidirectional Movement: This toggle lets you decide whether your speed boost applies in all directions or only while running straight ahead.

[note]None of these keybinds are set by default. The easiest way to configure them is to go into Options -> Controls, turn on the "Category" button, and type "Thaumic Boots." Then, assign keys for the features as needed.[/note]

[note]If you want to advance in the dark arts you can also make them voidwalker boots.[/note]
betterquesting:10.name:8: Better Boots with a little pizzazz

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Nanosuit Boots of the Traveller provide all the benefits of the Nanosuit, plus a massive speed boost, higher jump, and improved Vis Discount. These are the perfect boots for the master magical engineer.

[note]If you want to advance in the dark arts you can also make them voidwalker boots.[/note]

Quantum Boots of the Traveller, for when you really need to run as fast as the wind. Might cause you some problems standing still!

[note]If you want to advance in the dark arts you can also make them voidwalker boots.[/note]

If you're tired of constantly replacing branch cutters, this Industrial Grafter is rechargeable.

[note]Or you could just make better ones.[/note]

You'll need a block of Sapphire beneath these beauties to get them to maturity. They can be a good source of aluminium and oxygen in late LV once you've gotten your first EBF but there are better options...

Garnets are actually more valuable than Sapphires. They're an early source of Chrome and Manganese, which you'll need for HV machines. You can also centrifuge Pyrope, Almandine, and Spessartine Dust with Nitric Acid to obtain a variety of additional passive resources. To reach maturity, you will need a block of Garnet (either type) beneath this crop. You can get Garnets from the HV macerator and Spessartine Ore, or you can use an Implosion Compressor to turn Garnet Sands into crystals to make blocks.

To process all products of Garnydiania, you may find those steam multiblock machines quite useful! Though, to be honest, it will likely be much longer until you can make the most of this crop with the chemicals required.

Lonely? The Traveling Trunk is a simple companion, giving you some extra space. With upgrades (one per trunk) it can offer you some nice advantages. Like other golems, you can pick it up with the Golemancer's Bell. Its brain is pretty small though, so it can easily get stuck. You can order it to stay in one spot via the GUI. It will attempt to teleport to you, as long as the chunk is still loaded. It can also follow you into different dimensions.

They will heal slowly on their own, or faster if you right-click on them with any food, including rotten meat. Keep away from lava.

Golem upgrade effects:
Aer: Moves faster
Earth: 1 more row of item slots
Fire: Attacks hostile mobs, setting them on fire
Water: Nearly invulnerable. In SMP, can only be opened or picked up by player who placed it.
Entropy: Sucks in loose items nearby if it has room
Order: Can be picked up with its contents, and nested in other inventories. Don't be stupid about this.

Luggage is better than a dumb old traveling trunk. It automatically picks up dropped items, saving you time while mining. It's near-invulnerable, including in lava. It will follow you like an eager puppy, to the ends of the earth - but you probably should pick her up before changing dimensions. A lightning strike can provide more room. Shift-right-clicking will turn it back into an item without losing its contents. Look for her in the GTNH tab of the Thaumonomicon.
Magenta bees are also Fastest production, but come with +- 3 Climate. Breed them from Pink and Blue.
Pink princesses provide pink dye. They also have Fastest production and +-3 Humidity. Breed them from Red and White.
White bees provide white dye. Breed them from Wintry and Diligent.

Dye bees obviously provide dyes, but some of them are also useful for their traits. There are many dye bees, these are just a sample. They can be useful for the hard to find dye colors from flowers. Breed Red from Common and Diligent.
Blue princesses will provide a handy source of blue dye. Breed them from Forest and Diligent.
Batty bees will spawn firebats. So prepare for battle. Their specialty is Gunpowder. Breed them from Skulking and Windy.

Ghastly bees will spawn Ghasts, so beeee careful. Their specialty is Ghast Tears. They only have 1 fertility so you want to make sure you breed the drones with your master template princess. Breed them from Batty and Ethereal.

Smouldering drones will spawn blazes, and make Blaze Rods as their specialty. Breed the drones with your template princesses so you can prevent the harmful effects from destroying your base. Also, their Hellish temperature and Normal humidity requirements are interesting - use an Acclimatiser from Genetics to make the bee tolerant or other methods to adjust the biome. Must be bred in the Nether. Breed them from Ghastly and Hateful.

To get their Blaze Rod drop, however, you'll need to place them in a biome that matches their default requirements. Sorry.

Ah, here it is. This bee has been known to power whole civilizations. Placed in a top tier bee housing like an Alveary or Industrial Apiary, with appropriate frames, it can produce oil faster than some wells. In addition, you will get small amounts of Diesel fuel as well! Breed them from Oily and Distilled.
What's this? A step back you say! Yes, the Distilled bee doesn't make anything of use, but the potential is there. Breed them from Oily and Industrious.

Finally, the Oily bee! Its combs produce the most oil, but its output isn't that thrilling...yet. Breed them from Primeval and Ocean. As an alternative, you can breed them from Primeval and Frugal if you can't find an Ocean biome or used up all your Beekeeper coins.
Primeval. The next step. Breed them from Ancient and Secluded.
Ancient bees are the first step to the best oil bees in the game. Breed them from Diligent and Noble.

The Ocean bee is bred from Diligent and Water in an ocean-type biome. Note that this doesn't mean literally an ocean. It is any biome that has the OCEAN tag. The stock terrain generator does not generate oceans in The Overworld, but there are a few biomes that carry the tag.

Skipping The Overworld, you might have luck trying in a Twilight Forest lake - you'll know you are in the right biome if you see Water Creepers!

You can dump the biome data in NEI by clicking on the NEI options button (the wrench), then the Tools button, then the Data Dumps button, and finally the Dump button in the biomes category. This creates a "dumps" directory in the root folder of the modpack with a biome.csv file inside of it. Try anything that has OCEAN tagged to it. You can feed these biomes into a Nature's Compass and see if there are any nearby.

Some examples: Shield, Tropics, Twilight Lake, and Lush Swamp.

If you have trouble locating an appropriate spot, you can also purchase Ocean bees from the Vending Machine. Breed them from Diligent and Water.

[note]You get more than one princess per purchase, so it's a useful way to get a few extra pristine princesses.[/note]
Well at least you can get a couple of Sticky Resin from this otherwise boring bee. Breed them from Miry and Primeval.

Miry bees aren't too useful yet. They'll open up the Boggy branch for you. You'll need to find a biome with Warm/Damp to cause their mutation. Use your Nature's Compass and Habitat Locator to find them. An easy one to find is Rainforest. Breed them from Marshy and Noble.
Finally! A useful bee from the Boggy branch. The Elastic bee will actually produce rubber bars for you! No more smelly Sulfur! Breed them from Distilled and Resinous.
The master beekeeper needs a master registry. Make sure you don't get any tears in your apiaries as you collect all the requirements!

Agrarian bees are supposed to help crops nearby grow. The effect isn't really that noticeable, is it? You'll have to be in a Plains-like biome for these to appear. Breed them from Farmerly and Industrious.

Like most farmers, these bees seem to spend all their time complaining about the neighbors or the weather instead of actually doing much. They'll need a Plains-like biome. Breed them from Unweary and Rural.
sudo make me a sandwich. Or a bee that makes sandwich parts anyways. Breed them from Batty and Agrarian.
The Fertilizer bee will make your crop empire purr — or grow, anyways. They are a good source of Fastest production and Faster pollination as well. Breed them from Apatite and Ash.
The Apatite bee requires an Apatite Block beneath it to breed. Its Seedy comb will make seed oil as well. Breed them from Ash and Coal.
A bee to make ashes? What insanity is this? At least you can get Large territory from them. You'll need to pay the Nether a visit. Breed them from Clay and Coal.
Another ingredient for the final rocket fuel is Nitrogen Tetroxide. Combine some Copper Dust and Nitric Acid along with an Orange Metal Catalyst in the Chemical Plant.

The Rocket Engine is a very dirty device which generates power out of rocket fuels at 80% efficiency, and produces 250 to 2000 pollution/s.

[note]There are 4 Rocket Fuels. Follow the Space Race tab quests to see how to make the rest. Expect to need more than one (probably several) Chemical Plants if you want to automate production.[/note]

Efficient Platinum processing is quite complicated. But for now, we can just smelt it directly into nuggets. This might not be the most efficient route to take, but it is enough for what we want to do next.

At this tier, your best source of Platinum is Nickel ores from the Twilight Forest, or maybe Endstone Dust if you've managed to survive the End already.

Here are a few crops to spice up your solarpunk base, or help you climb up a treehouse.

No thousand block treck to the nearest Temperate Rainforest required here!

Your research into energy has led you to energy buffers - a single block that can store enormous amounts, and is also portable. Better than a battery, these devices can be configured to output 1-16A. Using a high-amp transformer, that means you can up tier 2 tiers with these devices. This HV energy buffer can power an HV machine for several hours, or an EV machine for almost an hour. Perfect for mining operations in far off dimensions.
The Greedy Chest from Automagy looks to have some interesting uses. It also gates a pretty important device for a magician...
Using a fermenter with excess saplings or other garbage will give you Forestry biomass. Higher Sappiness trait on your trees will get you better results.

Taking the biomass from the Fermenter and using it in a still will give you Ethanol. Not really worth it for power, but useful if you want to turn it into ethylene. You could set it up on an old steam setup with nothing better to do to get a more useful power source out of it, or use the Ethanol to power the setup and the forestry farm.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Why No, This is Not Fit For Human Consumption

betterquesting:10.desc:8: If you stuck with fish for bio diesel this long, you can now make the §5§lZhuhai Fishing Port§r to get cartloads of fish and other byproducts.

The large scale auto-assembler will put things together for you, in volume. This multi is available in ZPM.

[note]While it unlocks much later, has much fewer parallels, and has no TT energy hatch support in contrast to the Precise Assembler, it has one upside: If you use two energy hatches you can craft items of the next tier.[/note]
betterquesting:10.name:8: §b§lPutting All Those Workers Out of Jobs

betterquesting:10.desc:8: With a Squeezer you can boost the output from your fermenter, saving on Fertilizer or Mulch and getting more per sapling. There's a variety of crops you can use to make fruit juice, so have fun breeding.

Now that you have a Scuba Helmet you can safely explore underwater for long periods of time. You just need some compressed air cells. I'll trade you some Tin ingots for a few compressed air cells.

As your air drops, the helmet will take a compressed air cell and give back an empty cell. Throw these cells into your compressor and you can easily gather clay from beneath rivers. You'll be able to make more cells later once you get an extruder or a plate bender.
Steeleaf armor is the next level in Twilight Forest armor. It can be handy as a defense in the Nether.
Knightmetal is the top tier Twilight Forest armor. It doesn't come with any free enchants but it has high durability and high armor rating.
Knightmetal ingots are loot taken from Goblin Knight Strongholds. They can be made into Diamond-tier armor. You can take Armor Shards dropped by helmet crabs and turn them into Knightmetal ingots.
The Thaumostatic Harness grants you flight, using up Potentia from a jar. The speed isn't great though, so perhaps further research will yield some results.
Ahh, that's better. With this girdle you can really fly around like a true wizard. It does take a little extra potentia to use though, so keep an eye on your flying time.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Flying With the Greatest of Ease

betterquesting:10.desc:8: With these devices you can now fly and work at the same time without penalty. They can be found in the Witching Gadgets tab of the book. You'll need a Swiftness potion for this device.

No mage wants to be restricted to short flying times. With this spire from the Automagy discipline you can transmit magical energy directly to your flying harness. To get the correct Thaumium block, compress 9 ingots to get the GT Thaumium block and then chisel that block to get the correct type.

This multiblock requires centi-vis to operate. You can use 2-6 Thaumostatic Pylons, with additional pylons extending the range. Provide the construct Aer centi-vis to operate, and it will accept Potentia essentia to transfer to flyers. The construct will also accept Aer and Volatus essentia to increase the range and rate of transfer, respectively. Right-click the sides of the controller to control which type of essentia each side will accept.

Many of the nodes of the wild have damage, and unjarring a captured node can also cause damage. The Node Manipulator can help you recover the nodes to full strength, and increase their recharge speed.
The Witching Gadgets Spinning Wheel will unlock a few materials and items. Hopefully without that creep Rumpelstiltskin! Make sure you get the WG Spinning Wheel and not the Witchery version.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Clothes Make the Magical Man or Woman

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
This cloak is a nice substitute for the Glider. There are plenty of other magical items worth a look in the Witching Gadgets tab.
If you want to toggle gliding with a key - configure binding for "Hotkey for activating some worn items" in control settings.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Flying Like a Eag - I Mean Raven

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Now that you have Goggles of Revealing, Thaumic Horizons offers various lenses with handy uses. This one will grant night vision. Try out some of the others.

If you found an item or book with a good enchantment - but also a bunch of garbage, you can strip the enchantments into separate books using a Disenchanter. Surround it with bookcases to reduce damage done to the item.

Once you build your vacuum freezer, you're going to have to carry around hot ingots all the time (assuming you don't automate it). Your old gloves are falling apart, and take up both hands. I think there's a way to glue them together so you can carry hot items with just one hand. Give me some parts and I'll do it for you.

Now that you've reached LuV you can make the god-tier prospector - The Electric Prospector. This handheld machine can provide detailed information on ores in the area, and return maps of how much UG fluid and what type is in each chunk.

Note that the range is determined by the tier and material (the durability seems to not matter). You can select an ore from the list to show only that ore, or double-click to switch dark/light mode.

...Did you expect a raid boss of some kind? If you count the number of bats you'll encounter and kill, then probably yes.

This kind of wolf does not take kindly to you marching close to them or offering them bones! Neutral at first, but extremely hostile upon approaching close to them and dangerous. They'll rip the bones right off ya! Found within snowy forest biomes.
Aggressive and can apply fire, although not a fast enemy either. Recommendation, avoid melee combat and offerings of bones.
Now a Hell version of your slime! Always appears with Infernal status.
Sticky and bouncy! Now in many variations. Say hello to my little friend, Lemon Slice!

Be wary, they like to disguise and clone themselves in stone-related blocks! (Applies to Vanilla blocks only) Can be found within dungeons and hills. Can also be found in Drowning Creeper spawned cobblestone blocks.
Aieee, no it's not, it's a nether wasp, kill it kill it kill it!
betterquesting:10.name:8: Hey is That a Friendly Bumblebee?

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Binnie's Genetics mod will allow you to pick and chose traits for bees, trees and Botany flowers. But not for free! Doing this comes at a price.

[note]Note: We'll be focusing just on the bees in this section.[/note]

You will need a few streams of resources you can automate into passive generation. These are used across the process in different machines for different purposes, but Growth Medium is a super-resource you can substitute for some of the steps if you're able to produce that in abundance.

The research process can be easily automated. Gene modification and drone generation can be automated, but are slow and infrequent enough that you will probably just attend to them when you need them.

The general idea is to sequence a pile of leftover drones until you get all the traits you want from it. You'll then have those traits forever and can inject your own combinations of everything you've found into drone Larvae to make new drones that carry those traits. Larvae hatch only into drones. You don't get to directly hatch princesses and queens, so you have to worry about these new traits sticking across generations.

These genetic edits don't let you create new traits out of thin air. They just let you pick and choose what you have already researched, and that has to come out of bees you already have. You may use this to set up all your production bees through the rest of the game, but traits like 4x fertility also help with breeding.

You'll want to prepare a lab workspace for this. The actual machines won't take too much space. In fact, you'll probably wind up smacking a bunch of them against world accelerators, which will require direct contact due to using Tile Entity mode. What will end up taking up more space is any passive resource generation you prepare to make the process more hands-free.

You will need an alveary with a hatchery to produce Larvae of the base bee you want to modify.

These machines require RF power. It's recommended to provide power to an Ender IO capacitor and power these machines with RF instead of powering directly with GT EU. You can connect GT EU power up to these, but you run into strange consumption from amperage conversion glitches, or machines not getting power despite looking like they have proper cabling.

Ultimately, you'll need at least 7 of these casings and could end up making 14+ casings for all the machines you may opt to produce. You will also need HV-tier circuit production. There is §oone§o§r EV circuit involved in the complete process too.

[note]We give special credit to Three for a video explaining all these machines and their interplay:

§oAn Early Game Guide to Genetically Modify your Bees in Gregtech: New Horizons§r
[url]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EmhDlga2SCA[/url]

Note that he will rant about the quest book. That was--ahem--an older version of the quest book.[/note]

The Acclimatiser can widen the temperature tolerance of a bee. This is technically a little side quest with Binnie's Genetics machines, but these alterations are permanent and carry into their genome.

Note that the bee's species determines its favored temperature for jubilance. You can't use this to make a bee produce secondary products in a different climate.

Drones, princesses, queens, and even larvae can go in these machines. This means you can boost one queen and be set for life for that bee.

(You can also use it for pollen, butterflies, caterpillars, plants...)

When a specimen's tolerance has been pushed as far as it can go, that bee will go in the output slot. The typical thing to do here is pipe the bee automatically into another Acclimatiser like a little trauma conga line. At the end, the bee should be able to tolerate being anywhere.

Here's what you can use for what at what factors:
* Temperature down
  * ice: 0.75
  * snowball: 0.15
* Temperature up
  * lava (canned!): 0.75
  * blaze powder: 0.5
  * blaze rod: 0.75
* Humidity up:
  * water (canned!): 0.75
* Humidity down:
  * sand: 0.15

Fluid containers are consumed. If only you had a waxy substance in overabundance you could use for throwaway fluids!

[note]The Ole' "Both Trick": If your specimen already has at least Up/Down 1 for temperature or humidity, acclimatising it in the opposite direction will make it Both 1. The trick is that it'll now grow both ways for the price of expanding only in one.

So, if handling canned water and lava is annoying, and you can start with Up 1 for temperature and humidity, then you can just bombard it with temperature and humidity lowering steps. It'll switch to Both 1 and then eventually Both 5 without ever raising temperature or humidity again.

This lets you skip out on canning liquids, you sly dog.
[/note]

Now that you have entered MV you can begin breeding Forestry trees the smart way. Start by getting a Treealyzer, and scan the vanilla trees. They will transform into the forestry versions. You will need to gather honey or honeydew drops from bee combs to power the Treealyzer.

If you want to bulk scan saplings, you can feed them through a GT scanner filled with honey.

You can also try the Genetics mod to modify them. It's on the first bee tab.

If you got lucky and found some bees in a village, put them in their houses next to some trees. Over time the bees will slowly pollinate the leaves of the trees. Using a grafter you can break the leaf blocks to retrieve a sapling 100%, useful for getting the forestry saplings. This doesn't seem to work with magical trees though. You can trade with villagers to get proven grafters that have a longer lifetime. Also investigate magic, you have heard rumors of long lasting grafters available to magicians.

GregTech also offers a really nice tool, the Branch Cutter.
It can be difficult to see which leafy blocks are pollinated. Craft a pair of spectacles to get a better view.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Seeing the Fruits of Your Labor

betterquesting:10.desc:8: While the SAG mill will work with no grinding heads, flint heads only save a little power. If you want to exploit the true capability of the SAG mill, you want to use Diamond or Tungsten grinding heads. Craft me a Diamond head and I'll give you a Tungsten one as a reward.

Barrels by default allow locking the barrel to a specific item, even when empty. For drawers, however, you will need to make the Drawer Key to lock its content types.

Different keys can also be used to show/hide the item icons and labels, and protect your barrels from the thieving hands of others.

The Incubator is a general production machine that serves two purposes:

1. Hatching (modified) Larvae into drones at the end of the whole process.
2. Heating items and liquids to produce different resources you will need in different parts of the entire research and modification process.

There are up to five different resources you can create from Incubators:

1. Liquid Growth Medium: Water + Growth Medium
2. Bacteria: Liquid Growth Medium + Wheat OR more Bacteria + Growth Medium
3. Enzyme: Bacteria + Sugar
4. Bacteria Vector: Bacteria + Blaze Powder OR more Bacteria Vector + Growth Medium
5. Polymerizing Bacteria: Bacteria + Bonemeal OR more Polymerizing Bacteria + Growth Medium

Three of the recipes can optionally be extended by injecting them with more Growth Medium instead of using a different ingredient. If you're able to produce a bunch of Growth Medium, consider "priming" incubators for these outputs and then switching them to use Growth Medium indefinitely in a feedback loop.

Enzyme is usually produced in a pipeline from Bacteria, which is in turn produced from Liquid Growth Medium.

Bacteria Vector is only used by the Inoculator to modify Larvae, and you don't need it if you use a Splicer instead.

PS: You'll also need a source for Ethanol for the Genepool and the Isolator. This technology line has a drinking problem.

PPS: Blaze Powder also comes up with at least Fluorescent Dye later.

If you need endgame high speed production, industrial apiaries are the way to go. Industrial Apiaries take upgrade frames that never break. Production frames can be stacked up to 8 high. It also has many options for emulation, more pollen retrieval, and others.

The Industrial Apiary is now a GT machine. It takes up to UV voltage and up to 4 amps but the base usage is just 37 EU/t. You can no longer use a World Accelerator and there is only the one machine, so no GT overclocking. Instead, there are new §oacceleration upgrades§r that act similar to a World Accelerator but are directly integrated into the machine. You will want to use them, they increase the speed and energy usage by a lot. The final tier also increases productivity.

But I shouldn't drone on too long. Go make one and find out yourself.

A GT++ Mutagenic frame will get your bees to their final destination faster than you can blink. Just remember to wear your rubber suit while making it!

[note]These will break in the alveary before they take effect since their durability is under 6. So you can only get to 125x, but I think that's enough, don't you?[/note]

These basic upgrades to the Alveary make it more powerful.

Frame Housing - Automation-enabled frame slot for the Alveary. Uses §55 durability§r every bee tick (27s). If it runs out on that tick, it has no effect.
Alveary Stabilizer - Prevents the bees from mutating into another species. Ideal for breeding traits into a line.
Alveary Transmission - Power input for upgrades that use power.
Alveary Sieve - Instead of the pollen from a bee fertilizing a nearby tree, it is stored here and can be manually applied. Requires manually placing woven silk in the inventory.
Swarmer - Creates additional Ignoble queens in hives around the Alveary. These are genetic copies of the original. This uses Royal Jelly or Aromatic Lumps. The latter are more effective.

[note]Note that all upgrade blocks must be in the bottom 2 layers. The center block also cannot be an upgrade block, though the bottom center can.[/note]

[warn]When using power, the transmission block will suck down entire amps to fill a tiny amount. Use the EnderIO capacitors or something similar to prevent this.[/warn]

These upgrades can significantly increase your production rate by keeping your bees from stopping production due to the environment.

Rain Shield - Can work through the rain
Lighting - Can work day and night
Alveary Heater - Increases temperature a flat 30% each (needs power)
Alveary Fan - Decreases temperature a flat 20% each (needs power)
Alveary Hygroregulator[sic] - Has two modes, water and lava
Lava - Temp+10%, Humidity-20%
Water - Temp-10%, Humidity+20%

Unfortunately, there's no way to make them like caves with a block.

Supporting circuit boards that can hold 4 electron tubes, the Electrical Stimulator provides a variety of functions. Use a Forestry Soldering Iron on an Intricate Circuit Board to set four slots worth of electron tubes. The tubes' capabilities are listed here as percentages:

Iron ET -> +0.5 Production
Diamantine ET -> +1.5 Production
Apatine ET -> 1.5x Pollination (Max 5x)
Obsidian ET -> 0.8x Lifespan
Lapis ET -> 1.5x Lifespan (Max 5x)
Blazing ET -> Simulates Hellish temperature
Golden ET -> 1.5x Mutation Rate (Max 5x)
Tin ET -> 0.4x Territory (Min 0.1) & -0.1 Production
Bronze ET -> 1.5x Territory (Max 5x)

Genetic Decay is also increased by 50% for all of them. This affects how long until ignoble bees die off, so don't worry about it if your bees are pristine.

Remember that lifespan is represented by ticks, not time. You need a world accelerator if you want a lifespan that is really less than 1 tick.

[note]Breeder's Notes:
12x Golden ETs and 20x Obsidian ETs across eight of these will make a super breeding party alveary; it will spike your mutation chances while dramatically decreasing lifespan. If you have been using the oblivion frame in an apiary to shorten lifespan for breeding, then this *does not* replace that because you cannot use world accelerators in alvearies. So the shortest you can reduce a bee's life cycle to is 1 tick = 27 seconds. On the other hand, dramatically increasing the mutation rate in the alveary may be faster for crossbreeding.

Production Apiarist's Notes:
Alternately, you can slam down three of these with:
* 10x Diamantine
* 2x Iron
That'll take you right up to the production limit. Any higher and you risk your pristine princesses turning ignoble from overwork.[/note]
betterquesting:10.name:8: A Stim a Day Keeps the Doctor Awake

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
The Mutator can vastly accelerate genetic mutations, even allowing those ultra rare bees to be bred. Items inserted into the Mutator control how much mutation it causes.

Soul Sand - 50 percent increase
Ender Pearl - 100 percent increase
Eye of Ender - 300 percent increase
betterquesting:10.name:8: X-Men, or Should I Say X-Bee?

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
You will need to feed Raw DNA into a Polymerizer to prime your gene samples for injection into Larvae. The Genepool eats Enzyme and guzzles Ethanol in order to produce more Raw DNA than you could ever find even in a public gas station's restroom.

It is basically a chipper shredder for your leftover drones. You were hoarding them because you might need them some day, right? Today's that day! Whatever you put in here is going to go bye-bye. Make sure you keep some of your different drones around just in case.

It will also take saplings, flowers, and any excess Larvae you should be pumping out by now for modification and hatching.

The Isolator will take Ethanol and Enzyme to extract a single gene from a candidate bee. Sometimes it gets hungry and eats the bee too. Don't feed it any bees you won't mind getting destroyed!

You must provide a Blank Sequence to store the output gene. This will be stored with a "faint" level of strength that can be sequenced slowly, or made stronger to be sequenced faster by passing the sequence through a Polymerizer.

The exact gene you get from the bee is going to be a random choice from that bee's genome. You won't know what it is until you run it through the Sequencer. It will then be accessible forever in the Gene Database.

You can wind up isolating the same gene from the same bee multiple times. It's just bad luck. They won't be isolated in any particular order.

The Sequencer will drain the container back into a Blank Sequence, so you can feed them back into the Isolator. You only ever need to make a few Blank Sequences because you can just loop like this indefinitely. If, however, you have a sequenced gene and want to make it blank again immediately, then just run it through your smelting/furnace device of choice.

After obtaining a DNA Sequence with the gene that you wish, it must be placed in the Sequencer. This uses Fluorescent Dye to determine the correct sequence, and when completed, logs the discovery. The important thing here is that §nthe discovery goes to the person who placed the machine.

§rThis process takes §l16 minutes§r! If the gene has been passed through a Polymeriser beforehand, it'll speed it up to only 4 minutes. You could also hug the machine with World Accelerators in Tile Entity mode to speed it up further.

The Polymeriser is necessary to turn Serum into something you can actually inject into a Larvae. It has a bonus use of strengthening an isolated gene so it can be sequenced faster by a factor of 4x.

The Polymeriser requires Raw DNA and Polymerising Bacteria. Raw DNA is obtained from the Genepool, and Polymerising Bacteria is made from incubating bacteria with bone meal. Gold nuggets can be used as a catalyst to speed up the process. You can also make more Polymerising Bacteria by feeding it back into an Incubator with Growth Medium.

When using the Polymeriser to prepare some Serum for a Larvae, the result will have a number of "charges." In other words, you get multiple uses out of it. This is nice because you are going to need to make a bunch of drones if you are trying to get all those traits to stick. Remember that you cannot use this process to modify a princess or queen directly! If you are satisfied before you use up all the Serum, you can recycle it by passing it through a smelter/furnace of your choice.

It takes two minutes to polymerise stuff. If you already use a World Accelerator for sequencing, then the Polymeriser would also benefit from cuddling up with that accelerator on another side.

Discovered genes are logged into the Gene Database. This handheld device lists all genes by the type of organism they apply to.

§oThis device requires an EV circuit! Of all the things in the Binnie's Genetics line, it has the most technologically sophisticated requirement!
§r
Use an Empty Serum Vial or Empty Serum Array on the different discovered traits to prepare a cocktail you want to inject into a Larvae. If you misclick, you can just click on the one you wanted without consequence.

The Lab Stand is a block on which an Apiarist Database, Arborist Database, Botanist Database or Gene Database can be placed by right-clicking on the placed stand with the database, attaching it and allowing the database to be accessed by right-clicking on the stand.

This is not a required structure, but people like to put their Gene Database on one as a kind of trophy case.

The Orchard Apple tree has a couple of nice traits. The Faster maturity trait means it will turn from sapling to tree quickly. The Higher yield is the best yield from any Forestry tree. Breed the Orchard Apple from an Apple Oak and Hill Cherry.

If you want Fastest maturity for quick tree farms, you can breed Golden Raspberry. Try and figure out the breeding chain yourself.

Higher Yield Get!
The Registry combines the existing four databases into a new sleek browser to allow the properties, mutations and genes of all discovered bees, trees, butterflies and flowers.

§n§rFinally! You can hack bees*! You have two choices, and you will only ever need one. Either way you go, you will hatch the modified drone using an Incubator that's been loaded with Bacteria Vector afterwards.

Both scale their requirements by the number of genes you intend to apply to a single Larvae.

§nThe Inoculator§r

Run Time: 10 minutes per gene
RF Cost: 600,000 RF per gene
RF/t: 50
Bacteria Vector: 15 mB per gene.

This one has a lower power and recipe cost at the expense of needing Bacteria Vector, created by incubating Bacteria and Blaze Powder, to transfer the gene into organisms. The consumption for Bacteria Vector is quite low.

It is also §oslooooow§... 
§r
§nThe Splicer§r

Run Time: 1 minute per gene
RF Cost: 12,000,000 RF per gene
RF/t: §l1,000
§r
The Splicer is much like the Inoculator in function, however it has the benefit of not requiring any liquid. Its power consumption is terrifying compared to the Inoculator, but overall it only consumes twice the RF despite gobbling it much faster.

*or trees and flowers via their pollen, or butterflies via their caterpillars.
This handy device will keep track of the flowers you have discovered so far, and their properties.
Butterflies don't do much, but this analyzer will give you details on their abilities.
This device will keep track of all the trees you have discovered.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Keeping Track of All Those Trees

betterquesting:10.desc:8: This database keeps track of everything bee.

This database tracks all your knowledge of butterflies.

BTW, see the BBB tab for the Botany stuff.

Many mods don't have methods of speeding up their slow machines. For this, you'll need a GregTech World Accelerator. It guzzles amps though, so your power infrastructure better be ready for it. The tooltip will list the performance boost provided. For block-based acceleration, the WA will do an area around it. For TileEntities like most machines, it will only accelerate the blocks directly touching the WA, and will need to be reconfigured with a screwdriver. This uses twice the power though.

[warn]This does not work with GregTech machines![/warn] For those, build more or higher tier ones.

If you want, you can change the level of acceleration by using a wrench on it. It will go back to the minimum, then increase one tier from there for every usage. It will use that tier's amount of power (and acceleration), increasing as per GT standard of 2x speed (acceleration) and 4x EU per tier.
If you get lucky, you might find a King Slime in your travels. Kill it and I'll give you a really nice replacement head for one of your tools.

Now that you are MV, you can make an Adventure Backpack. This very useful backpack can do many things. It can store 2 tools for quick access, has internal tanks for containing liquids - use the Hose to access them, a built-in crafting table, and storage.

When placed on your back, it can be accessed using the quick-access key; the default is B. Check your controls for details.

When placed on the ground, it can be accessed with a right-click. While on the ground, the bedroll can be deployed and used.

They can also be upgraded to add special abilities. For a full list, visit [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Adventure_Backpacks[/url].

[note]It uses up the same slot as the Coal Jetpack and the Copterpack, so you'll either need to choose one, or swap them around.[/note]
betterquesting:10.name:8: Sometimes Life is Scary and Dark - Bring a Backpack

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Night vision is a great backpack ability.
If you need to go deep or explore in the water, this is the backpack for you.
The Pigman backpack will make the Nether ezpz with fire resistance. You'll have to figure out a way to get struck by lightning while wearing a Pig backpack to get it...

An ocelot backpack will get those creepers running away from you. Nice protection against those drowning creepers! Don't get too close to them or else their repulsion will be overridden and they'll blow up!
A Cow backpack will generate milk from wheat placed in its inventory. Great for a lazy farmer!

The Dragon backpack gives you Fire Resistance, Strength, Night Vision and Regeneration.

[note]It may be really good, but also uses up a dragon egg, so be sure you want it, or can craft another.[/note]
Smart cables are better than glass or covered cables because you can visually see many channels are in use.
Dense cables are going to be your network backbones. They can transfer 32 channels and display the number of channels in use. Buses and flat interfaces cannot be placed directly on them.
The GT Branch Cutter is much better than the forestry grafters. It can have much higher durability based upon which material you use to create it.

You'll need to find a bunch of vanilla trees to start your breeding program. To convert them directly to Forestry trees, you can use a Treealyzer - but you'll need a carpenter and aluminium from MV for that. Alternatively, you can just grow a bunch of vanilla trees and surround them by good pollination bees in bee housing. Spectacles will help you see the fertilized leaves to harvest with your Grafter or Branch Cutter.

Completing the quests will require scanned trees, but you can progress on breeding while waiting for your GT Scanner or Treealyzer to be made.

Silver Lime, a basic tree breed. Breed it by mating Silver Birch with Apple Oak.

Note: For all tree breeding quests, the required tree must be a pure species, not a hybrid, and must be scanned.

Teak is the first step to Giant Sequoia, a true giant. Breed it by mating Dark Oak and Jungle.

Note: For all tree breeding quests, the required tree must be a pure species, not a hybrid, and must be scanned.

Balsa has some pretty wood. Breed it by mating Teak and Acacia.

§eHigh Fertility Get!

Common Beech gives you access to the Faster maturity attribute. Breed them from Silver Birch and Apple Oak.

Note: For all tree breeding quests, the required tree must be a pure species, not a hybrid, and must be scanned.
Hill Cherry is a key tree for breeding purposes. Breed it by mating Silver Lime with Apple Oak or Silver Birch.

You can breed a Mundane Larch by combining Red Spruce and Silver Birch or Apple Oak. You also need to do these to get Sequoias.

Note: For all tree breeding quests, the required tree must be a pure species, not a hybrid, and must be scanned.
You can breed a Bull Pine by combining Red Spruce and Mundane Larch.
Lemon trees are great for maximum fruit juice production. Breed it by mating Hill Cherry with Silver Lime.

The Plum is a great multipurpose tree. It has High yield and its fruit produces mulch with the highest chance. It also has decent sappiness for biomass production. Breed it by mating Hill Cherry with Lemon.

§dPlum and Mulch Get!
Desert Acacia. Another step on the road. Breed it by mating Teak with Balsa.
The Cocobolo is a nice tall tree, perfect for mating into your other trees to maximize their yield. Breed it by mating Desert Acacia with Dark Oak.

The Blue Mahoe has the most sappiness of any tree. It will vastly increase the efficiency of your biomass production with Fermenters. Breed it by mating Balsa with Desert Acacia.

§6High Sappiness Get!

The Energy Acceptor is an alternative place to inject energy into your AE2 network. You can form a "dumb" network with just an EA, but for real capability, you'll want a Controller.

[note]If you're making a subnet, just transfer power over with a Quartz Fiber.[/note]

The heart of your ME network. You can inject energy into here as well to power your network, but you probably want to save all available spaces for networking. Without this, you're limited to 8 channels.

This is a multiblock, and can be expanded up to 7x7x7, and can have 2 adjacent blocks in at most 1 axis, or it will be disabled. Whatever that means, just try it out, OK? You can only have one per network.

About channels:
Generally, every device uses a channel unless specified otherwise. If you don't have enough, that device will not function. If you can't determine what's causing your network problems, try looking at the lines on the smart and dense cables, or use a network visualizer.

Nobody likes an untidy base. Why don't you use some color to organize things a little!
The paint brush, painter, and spray cans can be used to color machines, wires, cables, pipes, wool, stained glass, and more!

Colored pipes, wires, and cables can only connect to uncolored cables/pipes/wires, or those of the same color.

Input buses and hatches can also be colored, and multiblock machines will enforce input separation based on their colors. Inputs of the same color can only see each other, and un-colored inputs work with any color. While outbut buses and hatches can be colored as well, doing so will have no effect on where the machine sends outputs.

Any painted block can be painted over with another color, but to remove the color entirely you need to break the block while sneaking or use a can of solvent.

The paint brush is the cheapest to make paint for, only requiring one piece of colored dye.
The painter requires distilled water and a chemical bath to create paint for.
The spray can uses chemical dye, which requires an MV chemical reactor to make.
The color applicator uses paint balls and can store all 16 colors at once.

[note]Sneaking while using a spray can or paint brush will color an entire line of blocks![/note]

[note]The priority of colored hatches is the same as the order of vanilla dyes in NEI, from highest (black) to lowest (white).[/note]
While the Pig backpack is useless on its own, it can be turned into a pretty powerful tool with the right... motivation.

Only the craziest fool would use diamonds to make a tool! Or is it crazy like a fox?

§3PS: You can also §oburn them for fuel§r§3 for that extra bit of craziness.

If you made it to MV using steam, you're probably wondering how to survive going further. One option is to switch to Light Fuel, discussed in LV. Another option is to use Benzene. Benzene is made from Wood Tar. There are a couple of pathways for that. Both start with logs from trees.

One path is to use Coke Ovens or Advanced Coke Ovens to make Charcoal, and fluid-extract Wood Tar from it. Then distill the Wood Tar to make Benzene. This method produces less pollution, but will also provide less Benzene.

The second path is to use the Pyrolyze Oven multiblock and Nitrogen gas to extract Wood Tar and Charcoal. Fluid-extract the Charcoal for additional Wood Tar. Then proceed as above. This method will create pollution from the Pyrolyze Oven, but will provide more Benzene per log.

Excess wood tar can also be turned into Toluene, a key ingredient for explosives that you'll need later on to make rockets.

If you use the Charcoal Byproducts recipe, you can get a plethora of useful byproducts as well, but you'll need 4 DTs.

[note]Later on, you will get an even better option: the Industrial Coke Oven.[/note]

The Auto Workbench is a simple automated crafting system. You place ghost items in the grid to create the recipe, and place components in the inventory. They will slowly be converted into the crafted item. While not fast and can only do 1 recipe each, it does support automation - only items acceptable to the recipe are allowed in the inventory. It does not use power.

Need a map on fuel choices? Well, we don't have that, but we have suggestions. You can use Steam up to IV, but beyond MV it gets pretty painful.

In LV you can start refining oil for either Light Fuel for a Combustion Generator or Refinery Gas for a Gas Turbine. Or you can use Creosote in a Semi-Fluid Generator.

Once you hit MV, you can switch from Steam to renewable Benzene (Gas) from your logs. Other renewable alternatives are Fish Oil or Seed Oil based bio diesel (combustion). Seed Oil can be sourced from Pam's peanuts, Canola or Forestry tree nuts.

At MV you can also upgrade your Light Fuel with Heavy Fuel to get Diesel. When you reach HV turn diesel or bio diesel into Cetane Boosted Diesel. In EV, you can make High Octane Gasoline (HOG), but it's complex, and you'll need to rejigger your whole oil distillation setup, since it uses different fluids than Cetane does.

EV introduces the Large Gas Turbine, Large Steam Turbine, Large HP Steam Turbine, and Large Combustion Engine, which are more efficient versions of the earlier ones. The first 3 require turbines.

You can also make Nukes, or Wind and Water Kinetics.

For low-power operations, or dedicated players willing to set up autocrafting, you can begin using Solar Panels at MV.

If you want to pass multiple amps through your cleanroom walls, use a one-way Diode. It's also handy when branching off a main power line to limit amps in thinner branches and prevent them from overloading and catching fire.

An MV Diode will suffice for now, but you can also consider making an HV Diode since you will need to run HV machines in the near future, and you won't have to wait for 100% cleanroom efficiency again when upgrading to HV.

[note]P.S.: Don't forget to use an HV->MV transformer if you choose the HV Diode.[/note]
betterquesting:10.name:8: §6§lDon't Put a Finger in That Socket

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
ERROR: Too many keys to fit a 104 key keyboard.

There are many keybinds in this modpack. To avoid conflicts, most of them are unbound by default. Only the ones available from the start are bound. Note that NEI keybinds are found in the NEI menu and not with the rest of the keybinds.

Here is the list of what some of them do :

BetterQuesting
GRAVE - Open Questbook

Draconic Evolution
V - Place the item you are holding on the block you are looking at

Journeymap
B - Create a Waypoint
Ctrl+B - Open the Waypoint Manager
J - Open Fullscreen Map
= - Zoom In (works on minimap too)
- - Zoom out

Share Where I am
INSERT - Places a temporary beam where you are looking at that will be seen by you and other players
SHIFT + INSERT - Places a temporary beam where §oyou§r are that will be seen by you and other players
CTRL + INSERT - Shares the position you are looking at with other players
CTRL + SHIFT + INSERT - Shares your position with other players

Waila - Shows information about what you are looking at
NUMPAD1 - show/hide the Waila HUD
NUMPAD3 - shows how to craft what you are looking at
NUMPAD4 - shows the crafting usages of the thing you are looking at

[note]If you have a non-standard keyboard layout, using the Java 17-25 version of GTNH §omight§r help you in being able to use certain keys for keybinds.[/note]

Automagy is a little subtle about what the "smort" mage needs to do next. Make some crystalline brains and scan them to unlock the next stage. You'll want to use the zombie brains you've been collecting from dangerous Furious zombies spawned by Eerie nodes.

The Avarice Pearl is the next object Automagy requires you to interact with in order to unlock the next section. Make an Avarice Pearl, throw some stuff on the ground, and throw Avarice Pearls at them by right-clicking quickly over and over to get a Shattered (ha ha) Pearl to unlock a few more research items.
IV tier batteries require a large investment. First, you will need to laser engrave 8 Lapotrons.
The Lapotronic Energy Orb is the IV tier battery item. It can store 100M EU.

If you want a stationary battery, you can make an AFSU capable of storing up to 1 billion EU and charging items. You can pick it up with a wrench, but you'll lose a percentage of the stored EU. Make sure you right-click, not left-click. Left-clicking will cause it to lose all stored EU.

As an alternative, if you can afford them, try the GT++ Energy Buffers. They are more expensive and cannot charge items, but store more, don't lose any EU, and can be configured from 1-16A.

[note]These can apparently draw infinite amps, so maybe use a diode or something if you like having the power on.[/note]

Aqua Regia, the water of the Kings, is a chemical that will dissolve Platinum. The perfect solvent for Platinum processing. Get a few Cells of it.

§6Don't wanna do all these cell quests because you already automated it? Hold a stack of any platline dust to skip to the end of that chain.
Ammonium Chloride is used to precipitate the dissolved Platinum into a purer form, you'll need some of this.

The Refined Platinum Salt can be heated to evaporate the last remaining impurities. Now you are left with PMP again, which you can use back in the first step again.

[note]Add an output hatch to the bottom layer of your EBF to capture the Chlorine for reuse.[/note]

Palladium is a rather useful Platinum Group Metal, necessary to make all machines in LuV.

This questline will help you figure out how to process it properly.

First, process some of your Palladium Enriched Ammonia to Palladium Salt Dust.
Fruity bees will make your Forestry trees ripen their fruit faster. Breed them using a Sweetened and Thriving.
Sweetened bees can make you sugar. Breed them from Valiant and Diligent.
Thriving bees don't have an effect, but are a necessary step for Fruity. Breed them from Growing and Unweary.
Diligent bees are a core breeding stock bee. Breed them from Common and Cultivated.
Unweary bees are key to a couple of breeding lines. Breed them with Diligent and Cultivated.
Growing bees are the start of the Fruity specific breeding tree. Breed them from Forest and Diligent.

Get the princess bee and reward bag in NEI first.
Copy this quest.
Press Icon and set the icon to the bee.
Change the name, description, and rewards.

Press Task, and select the stone, and replace it with the princess.
Before closing, select the ... next to the bee name and press Raw NBT
Go into Tag, Genome, Chromosomes. The first one is the name and must stay.
Go inside there and delete the first entry, keep both of the species so players
must have purebreeds.
Delete the rest of the chromosomes.
Delete the rest of the entries for Genome.

Press Requirements. Remove the Infinity unlock requirement and select the required bee quests. Use the common bees quest if nothing applies.

Change Show:Hidden to Show:Normal.

To reduce waste in the questbook file ideally you should also go into the advanced options, then press ... for the icon, and remove unnecessary NBT there as well. Just leave the species as above.

§3You can change the visibility of requirements by pressing the eye symbol in the requirements menu.

Yet another custom block system! Carpenter's blocks are crafted blank and placed in-world, and then plain block textures applied to them. The blocks must not be Tile Entities, so Botany blocks don't work correctly with them, but GT Stones like Red Granite, and any colored clay or vanilla glass block will work. Some Chisel glass types will work, and Ztones blocks and Tinted Glass also work.

The Garage Door requires a block at the top to hang "down" from, but can pretty much be any length. A redstone signal on any block next to the Garage Door blocks will open or close the door. The open/close will propagate across multiple vertical doors, so you can set up non-square doors. Sneaking and right-clicking with an empty hand will change the door's polarity.

The pressure plates are player-only activation, making them great for doors into your base.

The hatches must be clicked on the side of a block to place. They can be handy for protecting you from crucible...byproducts.

There is a lot more block shapes possible, check NEI for "Carpenter's" to see the options.

The Chisel allows you to chisel blocks while attached to a Carpenter's block.

The Hammer allows various functions.

Hammer on door - changes door shape type
Sneak Hammer on door - Changes from iron to wooden behavior
Sneak Hammer on lever - Changes polarity (which direction is on/off)

For those new to GregTech, here are some tips and warnings about electricity.

Machines don't like being out in the rain, and will start fires nearby. Fires next to a machine have a random chance of an explosion. Also, sending a higher voltage than a machine's tier causes an explosion. Or several, if you pack things together, like many people. Sending more amps than a machine can use doesn't harm anything though.

Sending too high a voltage or too many amps down a cable will cause the cable to burn up and start fires, which may then cause machine explosions. Make sure the number of amps provided by generators and buffers to a cable does not exceed the amps it is capable of carrying.

A generator that supplies 1A can possibly feed multiple machines, if their recipes require less than the full voltage. For example, macerators processing ore only need 2 EU/t, so you could run several from a single 1A generator, as long as the wires aren't too long. Why does that matter? Because there's loss for every amp for every block, listed on the wire/cable. Note that cables are better than wires. But be careful! Sometimes a recipe needs a lot more EU than you expect, like a macerator sand -> quartz dust recipe.

Most machines only use 1A, however there are exceptions, such as the thermal centrifuge, world accelerators, and the UUM machines. Note that machines can accept more amps than they use (usually 2) in order to top up their energy supply, especially if they didn't receive most of the amp because of loss (mostly a problem in LV). The formula is (EU/t of Recipe * 2) / Voltage Tier + 1. Keep this in mind when deciding on cables.

Some machines are specifically there to help you deal with multiple amps, such as battery buffers, transformers, and diodes. Check out the quest tab Storing and Transforming EU for more on those.

If you want to send more amps, use a larger cable or a superconductor (MV+, but ULV and LV have their own lossless cables). You can use laser hatches much later to send even more. There even are wireless options, but not right now.

A single block machine starved of EU will restart progress but not lose the recipe items. A multiblock machine will lose the items.

Note that any block that emits EU has loss when doing so: 2 ^ (tier-1) per amp. So 1 EU at LV, 2 EU at MV, and so on. Using large numbers of battery buffers in a row is thus very wasteful of your power. You have to be careful with losses when making your first EBF later in LV, maybe rather power them directly? Of course, if you want to keep your amps topped up over longer distances, you'll need to place BBs occasionally to 'top up' the amps, though this is less the case the further ingame you get, as the loss becomes less of something to worry about.

If this info isn't enough for you, head on over to [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Electricity[/url] to read more.

If you prefer to learn via video there are also great YouTube resources such as HamCorp's Electricity Guide: [url]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lpDPY8J-4QY[/url]

The Copper bee is the first of the metal lines. There are too many metal breeding lines to cover here, but by now you should be able to use NEI to figure out how to breed more bee types. Copper bees require a copper block beneath the bee housing. Breed them from Majestic and Clay.

The Copper Combs have a strong chance of centrifuging into copper dust, but you'll also see a Chemical Reactor recipe to use hydrochloric acid to get a 1:1 exchange. You have some bee options for getting chlorine so you should think about a sustained hydrochloric acid production line soon. You'll eventually §lhave to §ruse hydrochloric acid and won't have the Centrifuge option for later combs.

To breed a Clay bee, you must put a Clay block beneath the housing. Clay bees are the bedrock of many important bee lines. Breed them from Industrious and Diligent.

[note]Breeder's Notes:

This bee is an ancestor for a diverse group of species. A lot of them have incompatible biome requirements--especially the humidity. While breeding, you'll find that you have to alter the biome from cycle to cycle. You probably want to just earmark a spot that is NORMAL/DAMP right now if your only option for handling this is to run around with your breeding setup.

You're probably on your way to more interesting production bees, but don't forget that clay dust can be electrolyzed into some useful stuff![/note]

Industrious bees produce pollen clusters, a key ingredient to the Alveary. They're also used for breeding many other bees. Their pollination speed is Fast, better than most bees. Breed them from Diligent and Unweary.

Slimeballs aren't super useful, but you can easily breed this bee to make them. It's a necessary step on the way to Oil though. You will need a Congealed Slime Block beneath the bee housing. Breed them from Clay and Marshy.
Never having to use a treetap again? Sign me up! You'll need to put a Rubber Wood log beneath the bee housing. Breed them from Slimeball and Peat.

Finally, Black Gold. The Oil bee, with proper... encouragement... can take care of all your power and chemical needs for quite some time. An alternate bee, Oily, requires less processing to get oil but has a longer breeding chain. It is below the Magical bees. Breed them from Coal and Sticky Resin.

Ah yes, Coal is King indeed, but Coal Bees are matriarchal. A great bee, giving you Coal to use to power your industry. This will require a Coal Block under your bee housing. This bee will also have the first really dangerous effect - it will apply a creeper explosion to you if you are not wearing your Apiarist suit. Breed them from Peat and Industrious.

[note]Breeder's Notes:

This is a major prerequisite ancestor species to a lot of other bee species in this chapter, and they're advanced ones too. The problem is the Coal species is long-lived, so it takes a long time for the queen to drop down to a princess and two drones (assuming the Coal species default of 2x fertility). Consider using some lifetime-reducing frames to accelerate that so you can get a Coal drone stock more quickly and start on those other species.[/note]

Peat from these bees can be used in furnaces and boilers. Free fuel is free, right? Breed them from Rural and Clay.

[note]Breeder's Notes:

You probably are only doing this because it's a prerequisite for other breeds (especially Coal), but this is a really productive bee! Its peat should be able to pull off a little side hustle somewhere.

Now, its §omulch§o§r is useful for growth medium with the Genetics tool line. If you're going that way, you might as well put this bee to work for it because you're already invested in bees.[/note]

Rural bees like to live out in the country - you'll have to relocate to a Plains-type biome for these. Breed them from Diligent and Meadows.

They produce Wheaten Combs, which make . . . wheat. Hey, it ain't nothing! Still, this bee is more of a speed bump on the way to bigger projects.

[note]They will take any biome with the PLAINS tag. You can dump the biome data in NEI by clicking on the NEI options button (the wrench), then the Tools button, then the Data Dumps button, and finally the Dump button in the biomes category. This creates a "dumps" directory in the root folder of the modpack with a biome.csv inside of it. Any listed biome that has the PLAINS tag is fair game. You can feed these biomes into a Nature's Compass and see if there are any nearby.[/note]
A Blooming bee will bonemeal nearby saplings. This can definitely help your log and sapling production rate. They also provide the fastest pollination. Breed them from Industrious and Thriving.
Ah finally, a girl... I mean Queen's best friend. Will require a block of Diamond. Breed from Certus and Coal.
The Certus Quartz bee. Hmm, does it have any breeding requirements? I can't seem to remember. Maybe try a block of Certus Quartz? Breed it from Lapis and Hermitic.
Finally, a bee with some real promise. The Lapis bee will require a block of lapis to breed. Breed them from Demonic and Imperial.
Hermitic bees have the same no-entities requirement as Secluded, but they solve that problem themselves. They are so repugnant they repel mobs near them. Breed them from Secluded and Monastic.
Better be careful with this one! It will set you on fire. In addition to combs, this bee can produce Glowstone Dust. It will require Nether to breed. Breed them from Sinister and Fiendish.

Sinister bees will hurt nearby mobs and players. Make sure to wear your suit. They will require breeding in the Nether. Breed them from Modest and Cultivated.

Their Simmering Combs are no joke! You can centrifuge them down to get Phosphor, which you can then squeeze to get lava. Lava!
Just like Sinister, Fiendish requires the Nether and a protective bee suit. Breed them from Sinister and Cultivated.
Secluded bees are real loners. There must not be any entities within their territory for them to produce their combs. The Mellow combs can produce Nether quartz. Breed them from Monastic and Austere.

Another bee that requires an attentive beekeeper. Without an Apiarist suit, this bee will inflict creeper explosions on you. Watch out! It will require a hot or hellish biome with Arid humidity. Breed them from Modest and Frugal.

[note]Breeder's Notes:

Austere may want a hellish biome, but that doesn't mean this species wants to be in The Nether. By default, they need to see the sky. You will either have to use an alveary with climate modifications to appease them, or alter an Overworld biome to their tastes. Something like the Potion of Shifting Seasons can put a little bit of a nether biome like Boneyard in the Overworld. You could get lucky and find an Overworld biome scorching hot enough to make them happy, but that's some serious luck.

The creeper explosions are usually just a bit annoying, but we once had an apiarist in steel armor and full, §agreen§r hearts get turned into a gravestone in §oone hit.§o §rThey were prepping to gear up into their apiarist suit, but they happened to be in its territory. Don't mess around with this species![/note]
The Frugal bee doesn't have much direct use, but is part of many breeding lines. It will require a hot or hellish biome and arid humidity. Breed them from Modest and Sinister.
Obviously, a block of Redstone Alloy is required, right? Breed them from Red Alloy and Redstone.
The Red Alloy princess will require a block of Red Alloy. Breed them from Redstone and Copper.

The Redstone princess will require a block of Redstone. Breed them from Industrious and Demonic.

[note]Breeder's Notes:

The stock versions of Industrious and Demonic have incompatible climates:

Demonic:
  * HELLISH down 2 (to WARM)
  * ARID zero tolerance
Industrious:
  * NORMAL temperature, zero tolerance
  * NORMAL humidity, zero tolerance

You will probably have to do something to make it work, which can include just running around a lot between apiaries in different places depending on the queen you get on any cycle.

When the Redstone species starts to appear, it'll probably also want NORMAL/NORMAL with zero tolerance, but will need nether pollination.[/note]

Monastic bees aren't found in hives or bred. Instead, you will need to find a Beekeeper villager and trade with them for it. There are various ways to make more villagers, so do some research.

[note]Trader's Notes:

Beekeeper villagers spawn in houses that have a fenced back yard with apiaries. If the apiaries are missing, the villager didn't spawn. Or, well, a player already came along and looted the apiaries. They might have abducted the beekeeper too. The beekeeper should be wearing an apiarist outfit. Their initial trades probably don't have this bee. You will have to work up to this by trading what is available. If they require a princess for a trade, an ignoble one is fine. Honorable mention goes to the trade of some logs for an apiary. That's so much easier than having to make them yourself! If trades lock up, one trade of the "rightmost" trade should unlock preceding ones so you can keep trying to get this trade to pop up.

You can make a golden lasso at LV tier and run off with the villager. If you do, prepare a heavily-fortified spot. Even single-block-wide walls won't keep all zombies away. Consider just keeping the beekeeper in the lasso when you're not using them.

Beekeeper's Notes:

The base fertility for a Monastic bee is 1x. That's really annoying. When each cycle ends, you get a princess and a drone. That's it. You don't get surplus stock for carrying on breeding. If you can't just straight up alter the genome, then you can try to convert an arctic princess (or something else with a high fertility) with monastic drones in a way that gives you a higher fertility.

On the flip side, their long life is useful to try to get into production bees so you don't quickly clog up your bee product inventories with drones.

The "monastic line" of bees have other quirks. They'll take stuff like wheat and bookshelves as pollination sources. They can have some nasty aggression habits. They are long-lived, so you want something that cuts their life cycle for breeding--like an oblivion frame. You will start out here with a bee that likes average temperatures and humidity, but that'll drift to outright hellish and arid (but not The Nether!) for descendant species.[/note]
Finally. It was a long, hazardous road, but you can now get Vibrant Alloy directly from a bee. Great job. You'll need a Block of Vibrant Alloy. Breed them from Energetic Alloy and Phantasmal.
Energetic Alloy will require a block of Energetic Alloy, of course. Breed them from Redstone Alloy and Demonic.

Phantasmal bees are similar to Spectral, except they cause the other drops to reanimate, like ghasts, spiders, creepers, endermen, or even Ender Dragons if their drops are lying around. Breed them from Spectral and Ender.

Spectral bees will require Ender bees to breed. This will test the ability of even the toughest beekeeper - don't forget your apiarist suit. To work in a bee housing, there must be a Dragon Egg nearby. Don't drop any bones, blaze rods or rotten meat! This bee will cause those to come back to life! Perhaps you can find a use for this ability. Breed them from Ender and Hermitic.
If you go deep into AE2, you'll want cheap sources of Fluix from these bees. Breeding will require a block of Fluix. Breed them from Lapis and Redstone.
For early Chrome, a Ruby bee is a great source. It will require a block of Ruby. Breed them from Redstone and Diamond.

Tin is a great early bee to get, it can save time you'd otherwise spend looking for Cassiterite Sand. You'll need a Tin block. Breed them from Clay and Diligent.

The Tin Combs have a strong chance of centrifuging into tin dust, but you'll also see a Chemical Reactor recipe to use hydrochloric acid to get a 1:1 exchange. You have some bee options for getting chlorine so you should think about a sustained hydrochloric acid production line soon. You'll eventually §lhave to §ruse hydrochloric acid and won't have Centrifuge recipes for later combs.
Iron bees as a resource isn't that big a deal, so much stuff makes iron anyways, but they are a key breeding species. They will need an Iron block. Breed them from Copper and Tin.

Nickel bees provide a pretty useful resource. You'll need a block of Nickel. Breed them from Iron and Copper.

Nickel Combs cannot be centrifuged. You now need to use a Chemical Reactor with some hydrochloric acid.

Zinc makes great early game item pipes when mixed into brass. Also, these bees have a small chance of producing Gallium combs, which is very useful for players needing to make circuits or SMD devices. These bees will require a Zinc block. Breed them from Tin and Iron.

Zinc Combs cannot be centrifuged. You now need to use a Chemical Reactor with some hydrochloric acid.

[note]Breeder's Notes:

You probably only bred this as a stepping stone into the other metals. Nonetheless, that gallium is no joke! The queen will need to be jubilant for you to get those, so you need to match up its temperature and humidity band exactly. Your HUD will have a note when you are pointed at the apiary about if it's not jubilant. The default band is just NORMAL/NORMAL so any old plain/prairie kind of place will probably do.[/note]
Lead will be necessary in large quantities once you start making nuclear reactors. You'll need a block of Lead for these. Breed them from Copper and Coal.
Silver is a key metal at HV and up with the amount of Electrum you will need. Requires a block of Silver. Breed them from Lead and Tin.
Aluminium isn't necessary until MV, but when you want it, you'll want lots. Requires block of Aluminium. Breed them from Nickel and Zinc.
An otherwise mostly useless bee, Olivine is required for breeding better bees. I guess if you need Magnesium? Breed them from Ender and Certus.
Ah yes, a very useful bee. Emeralds are used for many upgrades, and trading with villagers. Will require a block of Emerald. Breed them from Olivine and Diamond.
Titanium from bees will make getting those LCRs and distillation towers a breeze. Hey, I rhymed! You'll need a block of Titanium for this bee. Breed them from Aluminium and Redstone.

Chrome, a necessary ingredient for Stainless Steel. Better to get it directly instead of having to deal with Rubies or Garnets. This bee will require a block of Chrome to breed. Breed them from Titanium and Ruby.
The Platinum bee! Useful as a decent aid to your platline as well as a slow source of pure platinum. Requires a block of Platinum. Breed them from Diamond and Chrome.

All that hatred had a purpose - to create this bee, capable of producing enormous power. As before, keep away from everything. This bee will require a block of Uranium. Breed them from Avenging and Platinum.

To actually get the combs you need to either find a biome with cold temperature and normal humidity or emulate these conditions.

[note]With these combs and the iridium ones you can now make climate control units for modules in your industrial apiary![/note]

A metal that represents the epitome of technology. Never existing in the universe before man. Destroying everything around it. This bee will require a block of Plutonium. Breed them from Uranium and Emerald.

[note]Plutonium Combs are also used in a few crafting recipes![/note]
Hatred distilled into its most violent form. Keep away from everything. Breed them from Vengeful and Vindictive.
Hatred. Of all things, living and solid. Keep bee housing away from anything valuable, or even not valuable. Breed them from Monastic and Vindictive.
Beware. These bees not only hate everything, they even hate blocks. Put their bee housing far away from everything. Breed them from Demonic and Monastic.
