First off, don't be scared by the massive amounts of bees you see here once you unlock the breeding trees. There's even more that aren't included and you'll need NEI to find!

Ha ha, just kidding - don't panic! The breeding lines unlock bit by bit showing you what you can go for next, mostly from the top to the bottom. The large icons represent particularly powerful bees. Many of the basic bees have multiple breeding options, only one is shown on the Bee Breeding Tree.

Bees have two sets of traits, active and inactive. The active one affects the behavior of the bee while the inactive one is only relevant for breeding.

Every trait further either [warn]Dominant[/warn] or §9Recessive§r, normally respectively colored red and blue. When getting newly bred princesses and drones, check both sets in case you got the desired traits. You can breed the ones with inactive traits to try and make them active in later crosses. A Field Kit or GT scanner cannot see passive traits, you need a Beealyzer for that.

When breeding bees, a good idea is to settle upon a master template bee - a bee that has little to no crossbreeding potential but has all the traits you want - short life, nocturnal, cave dwelling, rain tolerant, humidity tolerance, temperature tolerance, 4x fertility, and so on. Once you have that bee, breed a bunch of pure princesses with those traits as both active and inactive. These will be your breeding stock.

When you are trying to get new species, what you want is a drone - this way you can use your "breeding stock" princess with the drone to get new species without the annoying effects or limitations. Poorly-crossed princesses can be returned to normal by crossing with breeding stock drones, or just thrown into storage if they now have annoying restrictions. Make sure you keep the trait and species you want, and slowly merge the good traits from your breeding stock. You don't have to do this part in an Apiary, you can use a Bee House to swap around traits. Remember that no species mutations occur in a Bee House. Ignoble bees are good to swap traits because they're mostly disposable - they have a chance to die after 100 breeding cycles, increasing slightly more each generation after that, though genetic stability frames can let them live longer.

Once you solidify your species, create a pool of drones. You can use those to convert pristine princesses to the new species. Pristine princesses will not die, but they can become Ignoble under certain circumstances like using tons of production frames. Rocky bees are a great source - all their princesses are always pristine, they have decent traits, and there's a bunch of them underground. If you have an ender quarry, you can collect them with that.

Turning two different species traits into a third species trait is a §omutation§r. Merely turning one species into another is not. The chance of this happening is shown in the bee breeding tab, as well as the conditions. Bees can require things like blocks underneath their structure, certain moon phases, or other things nearby in order for the mutation to happen at all. Mutations happen across Active-Inactive and Inactive-Active pairs. So if you have an A:B princess that you want to turn into a C:C princess, you want to use an A:B drone. This crosses the princess' active A with the drone's inactive B, and the princess' inactive B with the drone's active A. This gives a shot at mutation for both the active and inactive traits for the resulting princess and drones.

A new bee mutant is considered "pure" or "purebred" when both the active and inactive traits are the new species. This is what you need to complete the breeding quests, but also to retain that species indefinitely. If the mutated trait only appears in one trait, the chance of it carrying is basic cross-breeding and not whatever was required to cause the trait to mutate in the first place. New bee species also have a set of default traits, and the new species will try to manifest these traits. You could start with two species that have compatible climate conditions and wind up with one needing completely different temperature and humidity. You want to encourage traits as you finish breeding the pure bee to get the other traits you want out of it. 

Ultimately, the species trait determines what the bee produces and everything else is fair game. All traits can be bred into any bee species, aside from the species itself. Species also determines the initial preferred temperature and humidity. Species require their preferred temperature and humidity to be in the 'jubilant' state and produce their special drops. You can also mimic this with the alveary or industrial apiary, but increasing tolerances will NOT work.

Advanced frames can provide useful boosts to mutation chances or lifespan reduction for faster breeding cycles. However, the excessive multipliers will increase genetic decay, giving a chance for a pristine princess to become ignoble.

A recommended early-game meta for bee breeding is to find an Oblivion Frame in a Stronghold library, and then a means to keep it repaired like with a Thaumic Restorer. This rapidly speeds up the turnaround time to turn a queen into offspring. You monitor the process manually at an apiary, and use any additional frames you can to improve the mutation rate. You can push this well past the point you can make alvearies, but there are alveary components that can further improve on this.

It looks complex, because it is! But it's also a lot of dangerous and useful fun!
betterquesting:10.name:8: Moron's Guide to Breeding Better Bees

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Nuclear materials cause two types of radiation effects. One is a large number of standard debuffs. These can be removed the normal ways, with milk or Gaia Wart or other methods that imitate them.

The other effect is a special Radiation unique debuff. This gets applied the longer you hold onto the radioactive item. Severely radioactive items can apply minutes of this deadly debuff. Regeneration might delay the inevitable death, but most regeneration sources aren't fast enough or long enough to keep you alive. You can try using an Amulet of Remedium to get rid of the effects. You should have one from your Moon trip, if not you'll have to dive into Thaumcraft to make one.

There are a couple of basic bees that have good stats you want to breed into your breeding stock.

Cave Dwelling - Rocky - This lets you put the bee housing underneath or inside. Handy for putting a chest on top for products.

Nocturnal - Rocky - This keeps your bees working all night long, and in the dark.

Rain Tolerant - Water - Keep producing even when it is raining.

High Fertility - Wintry - For breeding purposes, you want the maximum number of drones produced.

Keep in mind that specialty products from bees require the Jubilant state.
To be in this state, a bee needs to have its naturally preferred humidity and temperature. Just being able to work due to tolerance traits is not enough.

For example, a Salt bee needs Warm/Normal climate. Even if it has +- humidity and temp, it will not produce its Salt comb unless it is in a Warm/Normal climate. Use Alveary upgrades to make sure it is in its preferred temp/humidity.

Enchanting drops from Arcane bees are used to create Aromatic Lumps for use in the Swarmer. It has a higher chance of success than normal Royal Jelly. These bees are the other bedrock of the Magic Bees branch. Breed them from Esoteric and Mysterious.

[note]Thaumaturge's Notes:

If you are playing with disabled Thaumcraft research, and instead pay for research with aspects, then review descendants of this line. You can cross with Monastic bees, working your way to Pupil, and then on to Savant. Savant queens will produce lore fragments that you can combine into knowledge shards. That will help you stock up on aspects that you can put towards all the Praecantatio the alternate research mode requires.

It doesn't get its own quest progression because that's a pretty niche use. On the other hand, those ... academic bees also produce Paper Combs that can be centrifuged into paper.[/note]
Eldritch are the start of the magic bee family. Breed them from Mystical and Cultivated.

What have those two brothers gotten into now? The Supernatural bee is a keystone of the Magical branch of bees. Check NEI for details on the best lunar phase for breeding. Breed it from Charmed and Enchanted.
Enchanted is the next step in the progression. Breed them from Charmed and Eldritch.
The power of three! Charmed bees are your next step up the magic bee tree. Breed them from Eldritch and Cultivated.
Just your mysterious stranger... Breed them from Eldritch and Esoteric.
Another basic Magic branch bee. Breed them from Eldritch and Cultivated.
Ethereal bees are critical for all the magical aspect bees. Breed them from Arcane and Supernatural.

Aqua requires a Water Crystal Cluster. It will produce Water infused dust. Staying nearby will clear potion effects, like drinking a bucket of milk. Might be useful for the clever industrial engineer! Breed them from two Watery.
Firey bees must be bred on top of Lava. Breed them from Ethereal and Supernatural.
Earthen bees must be bred on top of Bricks. Breed them from Supernatural and Ethereal.
Windy bees must be bred on top of Oak leaves. Breed them using Ethereal and Supernatural.
For Aer bees to appear, you must put an Air Crystal Cluster beneath the bee housing. They will produce Aer infused dust for you. Being nearby will grant a Swiftness buff. Breed them from two Windy.
Solum bees require Earth Crystal Clusters. They can produce Earth infused dust. It will also give you a mining speed boost. Breed them from two Earthen.
Ignis bees require Fire Crystal Clusters beneath the bee housing. They will produce Fire infused dust. Watch out! They will set nearby entities on fire! Breed them from two Firey.
Watery bees must be bred over water. Breed them from Ethereal and Supernatural.
Not much to say about this bee. Breed them from Ethereal and Attuned.
The Spirit bee is the first bee to give you Soul Combs, necessary for Soulful Wax, used in many magical frames. Breed them from Aware and either Ethereal or Attuned.
The Soul bee has the highest chance of making Soul Combs, 20 percent. Well, except for Dreaming bees. Anyway, breed them from Aware and Spirit.
Chaotic bees require an Entropy Crystal Cluster. They will produce Entropy Infused Dust. Breed them from Ethereal and Supernatural.
Ordered bees require Ordered Crystal Clusters. They can produce Order Infused Dust. Breed them from Arcane and Ethereal.

Vis bees lead to some of the most powerful bees in the whole pack. They require a node within 75m of the bee housing. Make sure the lunar phase matches the requirements. Breed them from Ethereal and Infernal.

[note]Astronomer's Notes: The waxing and waning phases happen on alternating days. The moon starts its next phase at sunrise and will keep to the same phase all day and all night. You want to prepare the day before, get to bed to start the next day, and immediately get to work. Also, congratulations if you just learned that the moon in Minecraft has phases!

Breeder's Notes: Just because this bee only mutates around specific lunar phases doesn't mean you can't work on them in other phases. To get the mutations to show up at all, yes, you need correct lunar phases. However, you will need a spare Infernal or Ethereal princess to get started, and you can prep that any day. Also, once the Vis species trait shows up in some drones and/or a princess, it's just regular cross-breeding to get a pure princess and pure drone. That can be done any day too.

Despite the focus on moon phases, you do not need to breed at night to trigger the mutation.

The Ethereal and Infernal bees are a rough combination. Since you'll need a new princess for this bee, consider using a pristine princess that isn't aggressive and is closer to your Ethereal bees' climate. If you get lucky, you may breed out the aggression and produce hybrid Infernals that don't need to live in an oven to function. You will probably need your apiarist suit if the bred queen gets a dominant Infernal trait for a few cycles.[/note]
Rejuvenating bees must be bred within 25m of a node. They will slowly charge the nearest node. Breed them from Vis and Attuned.

The Empowering bee will randomly add aspects to nearby nodes, allowing enormous power to build up. The best chance to breed them is during a full moon. Breed them from Rejuvenating and Vis.

[note]The maximum node size was capped for a few versions, but that cap is now removed! Maybe go on the GTNH discord and praise Runakai for that. :)[/note]
The Edenic bee has the remarkable effect of giving experience points to players nearby. Breed it from Exotic and Tropical.
Watch out, just like its parent the Exotic bee will poison you. But it is also a source of silk wisps. Breed them from Austere and Tropical.
Thaumium is pretty easy to make, but with this bee you can automate and get enormous quantities. It requires a block of Thaumium. Breed them from Edenic and Ignis.
Skulking bees are the core of the various mob bees. Check out the rest of the recipes in NEI, there are too many to show here. Breed them using Eldritch and Modest.

Watch out, the effect from this bee will attract spiders. But it has one nice trait - a large working area. Perfect for breeding into your fast pollinators or for providing useful effects. Breed it from Skulking and Tropical.
The Thaumic Shards bee has a chance of giving you any shard propolis. It will require a Magical Forest biome. Breed them from Thaumium Dust and Aqua.

Tired of all the effort it takes to make Salis Mundus? After hours of breeding you can now do magic trouble free with this bee making all the Salis Mundus you need. It requires a Magical Forest Biome. Breed them from Thaumic Shards and Thaumium Dust.

This one takes a little luck. You'll have to find Steadfast drones in chests classified as dungeon chests. Note that doesn't mean the chests have to be in a dungeon! You could find one in the middle of some Thaumcraft obsidian pillars right on the surface of The Overworld. 

Heroic bees have the pleasant effect of causing damage to hostile mobs. Breed them from Steadfast and Valiant.

[note]Breeder's Notes:

Specifically, you'll only ever find Steadfast drones in the chests. §nNo princesses.§r You'll have to convert a princess if you want to make a stock of them. Heroic is the only thing you can use them for, but you'll have a better time of it if you have more than a handful of drones. So if you play your cards well and use a high-fertility starter princess, you could take one or two Steadfast drones and multiply them into something safer before trying this mutation.[/note]

Nameless bees are required to get Draconic bees. They are also where you can get Amnesiac Wax. Breed them from Oblivion and Ethereal. Oblivion bees can be purchased with coins, or found in The End.

[note]Breeder's Notes:

The Oblivion bees are going to be the main problem here if you haven't reached The End yet. You can try to cross-breed without that access, but you're stuck when the mating pair creates an Oblivion Queen that needs End pollinators.[/note]
Abandoned are the next step up. Breed them from Oblivion and Nameless.
The Draconic bee is required in order to get the dusts needed to recreate the Dragon Egg using magic. It must be bred in the End. Breed them from Imperial and Abandoned.
The Wither bee will let you generate Wither skulls and small amounts of Nether star dust. It requires a block of Nether Star, and must be bred in the End. Breed them from Withering and Draconic.

Inflicts Withering all those who come near. Must be bred in the Nether. Chances are going to be low, so now would be the time to look for frames that increase mutation rates. Breed them from Demonic and Spiteful.

The sheer disdain this bee shows you is awe inspiring. Must be bred in the Nether. Don't walk around it without proper protection, it seems to laugh when you think about that. Breed them from Hateful and Infernal.

You can feel the waves of hate radiating out of her eyes. Don't even think about getting close without an Apiarist Suit. Must be bred in the Nether. Breed them from Eldritch and Infernal.

[note]Breeder's Notes: Infernal bees are used to make both this species and Spiteful, which is next in line from Hateful. That means you'll probably start winding up with Spitefuls while trying to make this species. Since this is a progression to more interesting species, you could say it doesn't matter, but:

1. Skipping straight to Spiteful means not getting this quest done and then losing your progression.
2. Maybe you want to do a Smoldering bee, which needs this one.

What we recommend is tucking away any Spitefuls you get and just act like that didn't happen until you finish this bee. If the princess starts turning Spiteful and you don't want to just start a new one, you'd want to pump it with Infernal or Eldritch (pick one!) until you've cleaned out the Spiteful trait.[/note]

You might be thinking to yourself, huh this sure is an easy bee to give redstone....well, it also gives destructive lightning strikes. You might want to place them far from you. Or set them up in a Creeper spawner to make charged creepers for...experiments. Breed them from Valiant and Cultivated.

This fun bee doesn't have any useful products, but it does produce a fun effect - constant fireworks! You can breed the effect into other lines, and the color of the fireworks will match the bee. Make the bees require sky and you can disable the effects by covering them up with a piston. Great for a celebration! Breed them from Austere and Excited.

After a couple of hours...days...weeks...of processing redstone for chrome you'll have a massive stockpile of Mercury and not know what to do with it. You can store it all in supertanks, but really, how much hypochlorous acid does one need? Instead you can build an Acid Generator and at least get a little power out of it.
This deadly little princess will get you Arsenic, perfect for use in your circuits. Requires a Block of Arsenic. Breed them from Silver and Zinc.
This frame will let your bees last longer, and also increase the territory to help with tree breeding.
Oh you fell out of the world, I'm sorry. Try again.
Haunted miners are the flying fire devils. They shoot you into the abyss with their bazookas.
Bugs everywhere! These damned bastards! Better run away quickly.

So you're probably wondering what all the underground fluids are. You can actually check so in NEI now!

Just look for the tab called §oUnderground Fluid Stats§r. You can click §oSee All§r for a general overview, search by fluid, or search by planet.
The Diffusion and Coalescence cores are basic components needed to make the Thaumic Energistics devices. They're made out of the Formation and Annihilation ones.
Does exactly what it says. But you probably won't need it much, if at all.
Attach to either Alembics or the output of the Advanced Alchemical Furnace. If that doesn't work, have them pipe to a jar and import from there. You can finally get rid of your shifty-eyed golems.

You can use this device to either transfer the contents (CV) of a Vis Relay to another vis relay, an Arcane Assembler, or an Arcane Crafting Terminal. Either way, place the relay on the device (and send some CV to it), and use the memory card to link to the second device. If you send it to another Vis Relay Interface, you'll obviously need another Vis Relay on the other side.

So apparently you can attach this to a void/oblivion jar and have it void overflow if you set the priority low. Neat, huh?

What? Store essentia in jars? Seriously? I guess you could, if you really wanted to, or if there were new, larger jars...
betterquesting:10.name:8: Storing Essentia in Jars? Why, again?

betterquesting:10.desc:8: The Arcane Crafting Terminal is the terminal version on the Arcane Workbench. It can hold a set of vis discount gear in its inventory in addition to a wand. You can also link a vis relay through the network to it to recharge the wand.
All terminals are made from these. You'll probably want several.

Unlike regular Pattern Terminals, the Processing Pattern Terminal doesn't have a crafting mode. Instead, you have a lot more slots for input and output, and the ability to swap them. Great for your Assembly Line patterns.

[note]If you need to rename an item for use in a specific pattern, you can use Ctrl + Middle-Click to set the name of the item straight from the terminal. Very handy for some Forming Press & Assembly Line recipes![/note]

The ME Storage Monitor allows you to visualize how much of an item or fluid you have. For example you can tell if you're running low on circuits and should make more, or how a long crafting process is proceeding. There are a couple of ways to use them.

Right-click with item or control-right-click with fluid container: Will display the current level of that item or fluid if not locked.
Right-click with empty hand: Will reset the display if not locked.
Right-click with AE2 wrench or network tool: Will toggle the lock.

The ME Conversion Monitor is the upgraded version of the ME Storage Monitor. It adds the ability to directly withdraw from or store items and fluids in the ME Network. It has the normal interactions, plus more.

Shift-right-clicking with item or fluid container: Attempts to insert the item stack into the network. This works even if it's not the displayed item!
Shift-double-right-clicking: Attempts to insert all item and fluid stacks of the type displayed into the network.
Right-clicking (while locked): Attempts to pull out a stack of the item displayed or fill held cell.

This device will turn on (or off) a redstone signal based on how much of an item, fluid, or energy you specify you have in your network. The 'Level Type' will toggle between Item / Fluid mode and Energy mode.

To add an item, left-click your desired item into the blank space between the 1000 numbers to add, click again while holding nothing to remove. 

To add a fluid, left-control-click a cell containing your desired fluid into the blank space, removable in the same fashion.
This block provides unlimited AE for your network.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §4§l§nI'll Send Wireless Signals Where I Want, Thank You

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
If you want to teleport stuff around using these, you'll need a drive in the SIOP, and at least 6 pylons hooked up. The pylons need to indicate the X, Y and Z dimensions, with you needing 1 more than you would think. If the efficiency goes below 100%, the AE cost will balloon enormously, so add more pylons to counteract that. After using a redstone signal to activate the SIOP, the blocks will be moved to the spatial IO dim, and the drive will move to the output, so you can send it somewhere else. This is very important to do properly if you want to use it as a teleporter. Otherwise, you can get stuck there. Your network will need to be able to hold all the power needed to teleport at once, so you'll need at least one energy cell. You can only have one Pylon setup per controller, so consider putting them on a subnetwork.

Using 2 in the X and Z dimensions and 3 in the Y will give you a 1x2x1 teleporter to teleport yourself. You'll want a SIOP port on each side for sending and for receiving. But you'll still need to design a redstone contraption to activate them properly!

Read this if you want to know more about spatial IO in general, and larger setups: [url]https://old.reddit.com/r/feedthebeast/comments/3c2b2r/a_treatise_on_nocheat_smp_ae2_spatial_io/[/url]
Also see this if you want to see a fancy teleporter: [url]https://old.reddit.com/r/feedthebeast/comments/2mhrf8/ae2_spatial_transporters/[/url]

[warn]Spatial cells, once used, will only work in the XYZ dimensions first used, with no way to format or recraft. Test in creative first![/warn]

[warn]Expect your world to lag for a second after using, blame AE.[/warn]

So, when you first started AE, maybe you dumped a bunch of your items into 1k drives, but now you want to clean them up, or empty them to reuse them in making higher tier ones. The ME IO Port will allow you to fill or empty your drives by connecting to the rest of the network.

You can use the Cell Workbench to format your drives, so they'll only contain the stuff you want. Remember, more item types mean less space overall. You can set them to lapis for example, then put them in the ME IO Port with the transfer direction to the drive to fill it with only that item. Don't put in an unformatted drive while using storage drawers to store tons of stuff! If you want to move your stuff around, put in new drives, then empty old ones, or disconnect your storage drawers temporarily.

You can use the Workbench to format fluid and essentia drives too.

Cell Workbenches do not connect to the network, so they don't need a channel.

The ME Annihilation Plane destroys blocks as if you had mined them, and places them into the network. The Identity version acts as if silk touch was used.

The ME Formation Plane does the opposite, it places blocks into the world. You'll need to tell it what to place/drop though. This can work in both block and item mode.

You may have noticed that the ME Interface's GUI is different than before. That is because with this card you can have more patterns, adding 9 more per card up to a total of 36. HOWEVER, it also uses 4 times the energy for every item when crafting, and this is multiplicative for each new card. If doing large crafts, make sure you have some dense energy cells ready.

So basically: (sum of amounts of items in the pattern) * config multiplier (which is 10 for GTNH). With cards, it's also multiplied by 4^(number of upgrades)

E.g: (wood log -> planks) in the interface w/o upgrades would draw: 1*10 AE units, which is 5 EU (remember 1 EU = 2 AE)
(9 charcoal -> charcoal block) compressor recipe in the interface with 3 upgrades will draw 9*10*4^3*0.5 = 2070 EU, but only 45EU without any cards

They're kind of expensive, so consider holding off if you can't afford the material or EU costs. If you remove it, all the extra patterns will pop out, so be careful of that when moving your stuff.

Quest names are hard sometimes, ok? To make a Singularity (for the Quantum Network Bridge), you'll need to dump 512,000 items into the Matter Condenser set to Singularity Mode, while using a 64k component or higher.

These singularities have a few purposes. Primarily they are used in creating quantum entangled singularities for the quantum ring, but they can also be used to create void cells and a couple other useful items.

A Quantum Network Bridge allows you to connect faraway places to your main AE network, even in other dimensions. So you can shove that pollution producing Mega EBF in the Void where it belongs, but still use it from the safety of your main base. To create this, you'll need a Quantum Link Chamber surrounded by Quantum Rings. Then put a Quantum Entangled Singularity in the link chamber, and connect to one of the 4 Quantum Rings around it with a fluix cable. They cost around 1000EU/t for each ring.

You can power the other side from the first, but you need to jumpstart it first, so bring an energy cell when setting it up. Remember that it's part of the same network, so you can only have one controller, and you're still limited by the channels of the cable you connected with, so you may wish to use the P2P Tunnel to bring more across.

If you use several, you may wish to rename the QESs.

The Network Tool is AE2's main utility tool.

Right-click on a network to see the power usage, and what makes up the network.
Right-click on air to interact with its inventory to store cards or turn facades transparent.
Shift-right-click to remove fixtures (import bus, interface, etc.) that don't take up a full block without removing the cable, or remove any AE block immediately the same way.

The Network Visualizer does exactly what it says, it allows you to visualize the channels of your network. First, right-click a network to select it. At first you'll see everything, but you can change the modes by holding sneak and right-clicking to see different things. Remember that if you have a subnetwork, like one that P2P tunnels go through for example, those nodes won't show up since it's a different network, but the P2P tunnels entrances and exits will. This goes through solid objects, so you can look at your whole base.

They're exactly what they sound like.

The first is for items and acts like a terminal. It can hold 4,032 of a single item.

The second is for liquids, and also acts like a terminal. It can hold 128 buckets of a single liquid.

It costs AE to put things in, take them out, or have the interface open. Use the Wireless Charger from EIO if you don't want it to take forever.

These cards add additional functionality to certain devices or fixtures. They specify what devices they work on in the tooltip.

§6Redstone Card: §r

The Redstone Card adds redstone interactivity to the devices it can be used on, with the following options: 

§cAlways active
Active with redstone signal
Active without redstone signal
Activate once per pulse§r

§6Capacity Card: §r

The Capacity Card adds more slots for items that use them. 

If you add this to an Export Bus, an icon is added to select item priority.

§6Crafting Card: §r

The Crafting Card allows you to automatically request autocrafting of items.

§9In an ME Interface: §r

If you put in items to be stocked, if there aren't enough, it'll craft them until it reaches the selected amount. 

These crafts are being stocked for recipes that the ME Interface has.

[note]If you want them to be seen by the network, you'll need to put a storage bus on the ME Interface.[/note]

§9In an ME Level Emitter: §r

§aFirst Mode: §rIt'll emit a redstone signal while the specific item is being crafted.

§aSecond Mode: §rIt will emit a redstone signal once a crafting job for the item has been requested, [warn]but it won't send the items to be crafted.[/warn] 

This is useful if you're using a dummy pattern, and are using the level emitter to tell something else to happen. 

You still need to get the item(s) requested back into the system so it doesn't tie up a crafting CPU though.

§9In an ME Export Bus: §r

It'll attempt to send whatever item(s) are selected in the export bus' GUI.

§aFirst Mode: §rIt'll send available items first, then create crafting jobs for the rest. 

§aSecond Mode: §rIt will only send crafted items.

§6Acceleration Card: §r

The Acceleration Card makes the device/fixture work faster. 

[note]You'll probably want a lot of these.[/note]

§6Inverter Card: §r

The Inverter Card allows you to invert the item filter of certain fixtures.

§6Fuzzy Card: §r

The Fuzzy Card allows you to apply fuzzy logic to filtering to allow items with different NBT or damage data to be counted as the same. This is different from metadata. 

If you just want it to be fuzzy for NBT, set to §9Match Any.§r 

If it is set to §c99%§r, it will work on anything that is damaged. You can use the Inverter Card to reverse this.

When used in an ME Interface, each fuzzy card (up to 3) will control 3 slots of the interface, from right to left.

The ME Fluid Auto Filler will add crafting recipes for any fluid in your network that has a bucket version. When crafting a water bucket for example, it will send a bucket to it, and the filled water bucket back.

This is the good wireless terminal. It allows you to combine 4 different types of terminals into one ultimate terminal for usage on the go; Crafting, Patterning, Interface, & Level.

If you make this combined version, it even allows you to program large processing patterns without needing LuV parts to make the Processing Pattern Terminal first.

[note]Recommended to set a keybind for this so you can keep it in your Baubles rather than in your hotbar.[/note]
This upgrade allows unlimited range. You don't even need a Wireless Access Point!

The ME Toggle Bus allows you to cut off access through a cable if it doesn't receive a redstone signal. The inverted version is, well, inverted. It must be placed between the cables, like a Quartz Fiber.

The Essentia and Infusion Providers both do basically the same thing, send essentia to a device that requests it for crafting.

The Essentia Provider needs to be next to the device, it's mostly for the Thaumatorium. Since it's effectively a magic ME Interface, you can also use it instead of an Essentia Import Bus next to your Alembics or the Advanced Alchemical Furnace.

The Infusion Provider is for devices that draw essentia through the air, like the Runic Matrix (infusion) or Overchanting Table. It doesn't need to be next to the device.

They both obviously need the essentia they request to be accessible by the network to work.

The Distillation Pattern Encoder allows you to automatically melt down items in your alchemical furnace to provide essentia.
First, place something that is already scanned in the device, along with a blank pattern. You can create the pattern by clicking the button, or click the different aspects to select one that is not the highest. This will create a pattern of item -> essentia. Then use an ME Interface pointing at a furnace with the pattern in it. You can now craft that type of essentia the same way you would a normal craft.

[warn]There isn't a way to have the system craft essentia on demand for a craft, unfortunately.[/warn]

The Arcane Assembler works like a combination of the Molecular Assembler and the Arcane Workbench, allowing you to autocraft anything crafted in the latter. You need to link a vis relay through the network to supply vis to it, and a Knowledge Core with recipes on it for it to work. Additionally, you can add vis discount gear into the interface to take advantage of the discount. The base discount starts at 20%. Each Acceleration Card reduces the time taken by 20% and increases power usage by 50%. For every point of warp on the discount gear, the power costs increase by 15%.

The Knowledge Core holds up to 21 patterns for use in the Arcane Assembler, but you need a new assembler for every Knowledge Core if you want to autocraft more than that.

To encode the patterns, you need a Knowledge Inscriber. It works exactly as you would expect. It doesn't connect to the network, so it doesn't need a channel. If you want to erase a pattern, select it and the save icon should become erase instead.

There are several AE items that aren't particularly useful, but probably deserve mention, so here they are:

§lCertus Tanks§r: They hold 32B and are portable and easy to make.

§lView Cell§r: Format in a Cell Workbench to filter what you see in a terminal (when they're installed in it)

§lCertus/Nether Quartz Cutting Knive§rs: Right-click to open interface and choose a name. The press can be used in the Inscriber to name stuff without using an anvil. You can also rename p2p tunnels and interfaces in world with the knife.

§lME Block Container§r: Holds only one type of item, but the amount of a 64k drive. Can place the item in world, or replace in a 1x1 or 3x3 area. Blocks replaced will be dumped in world. This will be horizontal or vertical depending on which side of a block you select. Shift-right-click air to change mode, right-click a block to activate mode.

§lCharged Quartz Fixture§r: Emits light at the same level as a torch, but fancier.

§lLight Detecting Fixture§r: Emits redstone signal based on light. Since it only starts at 7, it's not as useful as the Light Sensor.

§lME Upgrade (Tier 1/2/3)§r: If you're an OC person, there are 3 upgrades you can make to add access to your network from robots and drones.
T1: 0.5 access point range
T2: Normal access point range
T3: Unlimited range, any dim

§lEntropy Manipulator§r: Changes grass/dirt/dried dirt into each other, or starts fires. Or melts ice. Useless.

§lMatter Cannon§r: Shoots Matter Balls made in the Matter Condenser. Put it in an ME Chest or Drive and put items in a Terminal to fill. Decent I guess? But it destroys blocks every time you use it, so... Well, I guess you could use it with Paint Balls?

§lColor Applicator§r: Use dye items or Paint Balls (more efficient) to dye stuff. You can dye cables, or anything Forge-compatible, like wool or glass. Place items inside like the Matter Cannon. You can cycle through the colors by holding shift and right-clicking, or scrolling the mouse wheel. If you use snow balls, you can remove paint instead. You can also use it in a dispenser.

§6§lWalrus§r: It's a walrus, what were you expecting?
You can use the Wireless Golem Backpack to connect your golem to the network if it's close enough to an access point. See the Thaumonomicon for details.
They live on a fiery island in the end and spit at you with fireballs. Better run for your life.

If you've been processing Platinum, you should have a lot of Platinum Residue Dust lying around.

Now you can finally process it and gain all the rest of the delicious rare metals from it. But to do so, we'll need some to make Potassium Disulfate, and then fluid extract it to get the molten version beforehand.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §9§lPlatinum Group Processing - All the Other Metals

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
The Platinum Group processing line (AKA Platline) is a multi-step complicated process. Because of its complexity, and how much you need, you should have a processing line running all the time. You should be able to comprehend it better after doing these quests. Or maybe you set it up already, and you're siphoning off some of the results? Either way.

As a first step in getting Rhodium, Ruthenium, Iridium, and Osmium, we will split apart the Rhodium from the other metals in an EBF with the Potassium Disulfate you made previously.

The amounts for this step are pretty annoying, blame Bart for that.

For the next step in the process, we will split up the Ruthenium from the Leach Residue. Remember that you can get it from both Platinum Residue and a little bit more from making Rhodium Sulfate Solution.

You'll need Saltpeter and Saltwater for this. You can pump saltwater or make it, and mine saltpeter or make it too. Given how much KNO3 you need, you should probably automate making it.

For the steam, you can just void it.
Hmm, the sifting did well, you lost a lot of impurities, but also, new ones from the sifting grates are there... Time to filter them out with water.
Now that you have Palladium Salt, you need to sift it to get Palladium Metallic Powder. You only have a 95% chance to get a dust.

Formic Acid, also known as methanoic acid, is an organic acid. We'll need it for the final Palladium step, so don't be shy, make tons of it! The Sodium Sulfate can be recycled.

Make Sodium Formate, then the Formic Acid.

Reprecipitated! It means you have separated a solid from a solution/suspension, then dissolved it again, and then separated it again.

Combine the original Palladium Enriched Ammonia with Palladium Metallic Powder. This will get you Palladium Salt again, but also Reprecipitated Palladium.

From now on you should skip the first step, it's not necessary anymore as this gives the same thing, but more. You do need to find a way to combine the dusts automatically though.

When/if you run out of Palladium Enriched Ammonia, you can make more by adding Ammonia to Palladium Metallic Powder.

Ross128b is a lovely and habitable planet, that does not contain any hostile lifeforms. It offers several new ore veins and, rumors say, there are ruins of ancient civilizations that left quite a few machines there. You can find this planet to the galactic south.
You will need heat and Hydrochloric Acid to separate Iridium and Osmium from the Rarest Metal Residue, but we're getting to the end.
Separating Iridium from the Sludge is quite easy. Just heat it in the Blast Furnace and you're done with this step. The Sludge can be centrifuged into Gold and SiO2.
Add Chlorine to Sodium Ruthenate to get Ruthenium Tetroxide Solution.
Your Acidic Osmium solution is way too weak to precipitate out Osmium. Go and distill it in a DT to get a more concentrated variant of it.
Adding Hydrochloric Acid to Iridium Dioxide yields Acidic Iridium Solution.
Since you have concentrated your solution, it's now time to gather the solid Osmium from it. Go ahead and mix it with Hydrochloric Acid.
The final step to get Ruthenium is to react it with Hydrochloric Acid and you're done. You also get some Chlorine and Water.
By combining your Acidic Iridium Solution with Ammonia Chloride you'll get some Iridium Chloride, which is rather easy to process into Iridium. You're almost done.

Well, what might happen if you combine 64 Distillation Towers in one...? You know... you get a 54-block-tall Multiblock.

This can handle up to §6§l256§r Recipes at once and provides a different set of bonuses depending on which distillation mode is active.

Add Calcium to Iridium Chloride to finally get pure Iridium.

You can run the Metallic Sludge through a centrifuge to get nickel and copper, while the Calcium Chloride needs to be electrolyzed for calcium and chlorine.

BTW, this step is only EV, the only part that is, so you could do it earlier if you really wanted to.

Combine the Rhodium Sulfate you got with Water, and you'll get Rhodium Sulfate Solution, as well as some more Leech Residue, and Molten Potassium.

You get just over 13 ingots' worth of Potassium back, you'll want to use the fluid solidifier and then macerate it to use it again.

Gathering Zinc might not have been a pleasant task in the past, but here, it's just used as a catalyst, so you will regain all of it.

When you electrolyze the Zinc Sulfate, you get a Sulfur and 4000L Oxygen back too.
Hey, why're you looking at me that way? You ain't finished yet. Get more Chlorine and Salt, to process your Rhodium.
Combine Rhodium Salt Solution with Sodium Nitrate to get Rhodium Nitrate.
Sift Rhodium Nitrate to get Rhodium Filter Cake. You only have a 95% chance to get a dust.
Place your solution in your Chemical Reactor to heat it while it spins. That way you get a dust out of your Solution, 100% lump free!
This is the last step for Rhodium. You also get some Chlorine and Ammonia back.

Rhodium Plated Palladium is the LuV Tier Hull Material. Now that you know how to make it, you should automate it and make a bunch, you're gonna need it.

Why is it called plated if it's clearly an alloy you ask? I don't know either!

Combining Ruthenium with Iridium yields a very special metal, that is needed for LuV components.

You're gonna need a bunch of it.
Osmiridium is a quite expensive alloy. You'll need it to make Pure Tears to get rid of your Warp if you've been doing Thaumcraft. It's also used in the ZPM emitter and sensor.

Your iron doors make your Machine Hall or House more safe. They cannot be opened by hand.

Now let's craft some Pressure Plates and Buttons to open these heavy iron doors.

Wooden doors make your House safer. Let's craft some wooden Pressure plates and Buttons to open these Doors.

Doors will open when they receive a redstone signal, and close again after it stops. If you place the plates on either side of a door, it will open when you step on it. Or a monster does. Double doors will open together.

You'll need to use Oak for this quest. Purchase some saplings from the Vending Machine if you don't have any nearby.

Pressure plates will send a redstone signal when an entity is on top of them. There are different types, like items or not, or mobs/player/any entity/etc.

Buttons will emit one for about 2 seconds before resetting.

Levers will emit a signal until switched back off.

A Demonic Contract is written on parchment made from the resurrected flesh of the dead. The contract is signed in the blood of the individual to whom it pertains.

A plain demonic contract is used to make a deal with Flame Imps. The basic contract is crafted with a Taglock Kit containing the blood of the witch (or warlock).

When performing Imp Magic, a plain contract is first crafted with reagents pertaining to the spell effect, and then signed in the blood of the target by crafting it with a Taglock Kit containing the targets blood.

Taglock Kits are used to collect taglocks from other players or creatures. Taglocks, such as locks of hair, fingernail clippings or blood, are used in various recipes to create a link between the creature and the magic.

Use a taglock kit on a creature, or the used bed of a player, to collect some taglocks from that being. Repeated use on the same bed will cycle taglocks for each player who has used that bed. The kit can also be used on a Leech Chest to collect taglocks from users who have opened the chest or on a Blood Rose to collect the taglock of the player that walked over it.

Shift-clicking on any bed will fill the kit with the current players taglocks.

Collecting taglocks by using the kit on a player has a chance of failing and informing the other player what you were trying to do. To increase the chance of collecting a taglock from a player, sneak, and prefer approaching from behind.

Taglocks can only be collected from players who are logged into the same world.

Taglock kits are made by crafting a Glass Bottle with a Bone Needle.

Mutandis Extremis is an upgraded version of Mutandis that is used by witches and warlocks to mutate plants into other species. Mutandis Extremis has all the same properties as basic Mutandis but it can even be used on multi-stage plants like wheat, cactus, etc. and can also mutate cooked meat.

If Mutandis Extremis is used on a Grass block there is a chance it will mutate it into Mycelium and vice versa.

If Mutandis Extremis is used on an underwater dirt block there is a chance it will mutate it (and nearby dirt) into clay blocks.

Mutating plants is the only way to acquire Rowan, Hawthorn and Alder saplings.

Some recipes require Mutandis Extremis as an ingredient.

Mutandis Extremis is crafted using Mutandis and Nether Wart.

[note]Some cauldron recipes require altar power. This is one of them. Make sure you read the Witches' Brews book for information on Altar requirements.[/note]

Where would a Herbologist be without a trusty pair of Earmuffs? As soon as it comes time to harvest a crop of Mandrake, the farmer has two choices, either do it at night (and risk the typical nightly terrors), or don a pair of Earmuffs, and harvest away without fear of the Mandrake's screams. Indeed, Earmuffs are so effective at what they do, the wearer is unlikely to hear pretty much anything. This property may have benefits when dealing with Banshees too.

Earmuffs count as leather armor in terms of protection and durability.

An Ent Twig is dropped when an Ent is killed, which can be used to craft Mutating Sprigs and Mystic Branches.

Ents will appear occasionally when trees such as Rowan, Hawthorn and Alder are felled in large quantities.

They are rather hard to kill by normal means, but they do have a healthy hatred of certain tools for some reason or another.

They can also drop a Twilight Forest Moss Patch or Biomes O' Plenty Moss.

Redstone soup is a witches brew that forms the base for all infusions, although it does have other uses.

Filling a chalice with redstone soup will increase its magical affinity and upgrade it to a filled chalice, doubling its effectiveness.

Drinking redstone soup will boost the health of the drinker for a few minutes.

Redstone Soup is made in a kettle. Into the pot, throw Redstone, Drop of Luck, Wool of Bat, Tongue of Dog, Belladonna and Mandrake Root.

The chalice is an upgrade for an altar that improves the maximum amount of power an altar can hold. The chalice will increase the maximum power by 1x the base power rate.

The chalice upgrades to the Filled Chalice. Only one chalice upgrade will have an effect on an altar.

An Arthana is a ritualistic knife used by witches and warlocks to both collect special ingredients and to perform some rites. It has the same general properties as a golden sword (damage, enchantability, etc.), although it has the durability of an iron sword. It is repaired with a Gold Ingot.

The main purpose of the dagger is to collect specialist ingredients used in witchcraft, and to this end it will dramatically improve the chance of a mob dropping such ingredients (e.g. Wool of Bat, Tongue of Dog, etc.). It also gives a small chance of undead dropping Spectral Dust.

When only using vanilla Minecraft with Witchery (and no other mods), an Arthana dagger is the only way to get a skull to drop when a skeleton is killed, the drop chance is about 5% (the skull is a key upgrade for an altar). The dagger even gives a very small probability for other head drops (from mobs and players). All drop chances are increased with the Looting enchantment.

An Arthana does not change the drop chance for Wither Skeleton Skulls, that will require the Looting enchantment as usual.

Some Circle Magic rites use an Arthana as a focus, the Arthana is not consumed in the process.

Happenstance Oil is an ingredient used in the production of a Crystal Ball and the Seer Stone.

It's created in a kettle using Redstone Soup, Potion of Night Vision (8:00), Eye of Ender, Golden Carrot, Spider Eye and Mandrake Root.
A Quartz Sphere is a component used in the production of a Crystal Ball and the Seer Stone for summoning coven witches.

A Seer Stone is a variation of a Crystal Ball, that allows witches to communicate with one another over great distances. It is mostly used by one witch to summon other members of their coven either to help out in a fight, or to help perform a ritual. The seer stone may also be used on another player to reveal if they are afflicted by a curse.

To summon a coven witch for aid, use the Seer Stone while held. Holding for longer summons more coven members.

If near a Witches' Cauldron, the summoned witches will circle it ready for a ritual.

To call the entire coven to perform a rite, start the rite normally while holding the Seer Stone.

To determine if another player is cursed, to find out if they have a coven or familiar, and how much time they can manifest for, use the Seer Stone on them when they are within 3 blocks distance. Sneak-using the stone will show the same information for the bearer of the Stone.

A Seer Stone is created by infusing a Quartz Sphere with Obsidian and Happenstance Oil using a Rite of Infusion.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Seer Stone or Summon the Witches

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Once you have the required materials, you will need to find an ocelot to tame.

Ocelots can be found in Jungle Biomes.

If you are having trouble finding an ocelot, you can always summon an ocelot using a spawn egg.

You can tame an ocelot by giving it a raw fish. So add the raw fish to your inventory and select the raw fish in your hotbar.

Just like vanilla Minecraft, a tamed ocelot turns into a cat. The cat will repel creepers.

§3TIP: Make sure you are in a large space when trying to tame the ocelot so that the ocelot has lots of room to move. If you are in a space that is too small, you will not be able to tame the ocelot.

Next, while holding the raw fish, do not move. If you move, you will scare away the ocelot. If you are very still, the ocelot will eventually notice the fish in your hand and begin to walk over to you.
betterquesting:10.name:8: §c§lTame an Ocelot to Get a Friend

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Flame Imps are demons strongly associated with fiery magic.

Not as physically strong as their dimmer cousins, Flame Imps are mischievous creatures who are very easily swayed with the promise of personal gain. They may even be bound into the service of a witch (or warlock) if the offer is good enough.

Flame Imps are summoned using a Rite of Summoning, and they are most likely to attack the first person they see. It is advisable to make a deal with them quickly.

Making a deal

To bind a Flame Imp into service, a witch must write the agreement into a Demonic Contract and sign it with their own blood (craft with a Taglock Kit).
This contract must then be given to the Flame Imp, who will require a down-payment of Experience Levels (typically 25).

Once a deal is struck, the imp will be bound to the location of the deal, not able to wander too far away. The Imp will attack anyone hostile to its master.

Imps like receiving valuable gifts, once suitably impressed an imp may be prepared to perform various flame related spells at the request of their master.

Spells take the form of contracts describing what must be done and to whom.
Simply craft a Demonic Contract with the necessary components and then the resulting contract with a taglock.
Then give the contract to the Imp. So long as the creature is in the same dimension, the magic will take hold.

A Flame imp may also occasionally give a gift in return for being given valuable things. These have been known to include the souls of demons that can be consumed to allow a witch to cast demonic spells.

A very well treated Flame Imp may even yield knowledge to summon a Lord of Torment.

A Lord of Torment is a mighty demonic being that is able to create prisons to Torment its victims.

Those foolish enough to summon one of these creatures must prepare for an arduous fight.

A Lord of Torment may only be summoned using the Ritual outlined in a Torment Scroll.
These scrolls are hard to come by, but it is rumored that well treated Flame Imps have occasionally given them up.

Consuming the Soul of a Torment Demon grants the ability to Torment others.

If you are very unlucky and the Lord of Torment disappears when entering the Torment dimension, use the Egg and spawn another one.

Once you've explored a bit, you'll find large towering buildings that increase in difficulty as you go upwards, culminating in a dangerous boss fight.

Be wary and bring strong protective armor!

If you are incredibly lucky, these towers can also offer rare items or blocks.

Welcome to the End! And more importantly, Hardcore Ender Expansion.

If you've already fought the Ender Dragon, you'll have noticed that the fight itself was challenging, far more than usual. Though much of the island may be destroyed, have no worry, there are plenty of End blobs out there for you to gather ore or endstone from.

First, you will want to gather some End Powder, a key catalyst for most of HEE. Any means of flight is also highly recommended.

Hint: Press the P key (unless you rebound it) for a key list of information about HEE related stuff. Once you've looked through it you'll realize you need knowledge in order to unlock pages. Looking at blocks or items or certain things will also grant you knowledge. Consuming Knowledge Notes will also grant you knowledge points. Here are some for you to get started on. Good luck!

You can also search for the Adventurer's Diary for some lore if you want.

[note]PS: Hold shift and whack the egg with a vanilla sword to get it to drop.[/note]

[warn]The End has invisible rain, cover up your miners, and then complain on Discord.[/warn]

To create a Dragon Essence Altar, a player has to use Dragon Essence on the Basic Essence Altar (right-click the altar with the Essence).

After that, the Altar will request 8 random items to be fed into it, one at a time.

The Dragon Essence Altar may request the following items: Obsidian, Stone Bricks, Map, Book, Bookshelf, Iron Bars, End Stone, Ender Pearl, Eye of Ender, Enderman Head.

After this, the Altar will transform into a Dragon Essence Altar, and now you can store more Essence inside the Altar.

This little enchanting table like-block doesn't do much on its own, but has two other separate paths that can be taken (the third has no uses currently) to accomplish different tasks.

It is up to you where and how you want your personal Essence Altar to be upgraded. Firstly and more importantly, make the Basic Essence Altar.

[note]One of the upgrades uses Dragon Essence, but if you play on a public server and someone else killed the Dragon, that stuff can be difficult to come by without external help. Here's some to get you started.[/note]

End Powder Ore:
Generated in the End in between End Stone at every height level. When the ore is mined with any type of pickaxe, it will drop one or two pieces of End Powder.

Endium Ore:
Rare ore that starts to appear near Dungeon Towers, and gets more common the further you travel.

Igneous Rock Ore:
Generated in the End in the Burning Mountains and sometimes in the Endstone Blobs. This block emits lava particles but does no damage to the player. When the ore is mined with an Iron Pickaxe or better, it will drop one Igneous Rock.

[note]Note: the Fortune enchantment does not affect Igneous Rock Ore. However, the Silk Touch enchantment does work with this block. You can get better output with a Macerator.[/note]

Instability Ore:
Generated in the End in the Biome Islands, especially common in the Fiery Mines. When the ore is mined with an Advanced Pickaxe, it has a 40% chance to drop one Instability Orb, otherwise it breaks without providing any items.

[note]Note: the Fortune enchantment increases the chance of getting an Instability Orb by 4% per level, and the Silk Touch enchantment also works with this block. You can get better output with a Forge Hammer.[/note]

Stardust Ore:
Generated in the End in the Biome Islands. When the ore is mined with an Advanced Pickaxe, it has a chance to drop 0-4 pieces of Stardust. Even though this ore comes in clusters, two ore blocks from the same cluster can be generated away from each other, making Stardust Ore a rare resource which requires thorough exploration and mining.

[note]Note: the Stardust Ore block has different textures on its sides.[/note]

Sphalerite: Often found floating in the open space around Endstone Blobs. You can macerate it for crushed normal Sphalerite.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Find all the Ores in the End

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
After the Altar creation is complete, a player has to place up to 8 matching solid blocks (of any kind) near the altar. These blocks require 1 block of air above them and no solid blocks touching them on the sides and diagonally. These blocks are the pedestals. The Dragon Essence Altar will project purple particles to all the pedestals connected to it.

Dropping an item onto the pedestal will place it there. After the item has been placed on top of the pedestal, the altar will start "infusing" the item using Dragon Essence stored in the altar itself. Adding more essence to the altar is done by right-clicking.

Infusing makes items repair themselves (this does not work for items that require Energy), increases the level of existing enchantments (up to 4 enchantments per item) and can even add new enchantments.

There are two items in this mod that can be obtained only by Dragon Essence infusion:

Enhanced Brewing Stand - by infusing a vanilla Brewing Stand, requires 20 pieces of Dragon Essence.

Temple Caller - by infusing a vanilla Eye of Ender, requires 50 pieces of Dragon Essence. [warn]It's disabled though, so don't bother.[/warn]

The Biome Compass is a special type of compass, which points to the nearest Biome Islands as long as one exists and the player is in the End. Right-clicking will scroll through all existing biomes.

Holding the compass shows all biomes of the selected type as markers on the screen. The markers are small rectangles with the color of the selected biome. The rectangles also get bigger the closer you are to the island (they also disappear if you reach the island, and reappear when you leave it).

[note]The Fiery Island is orange, the Enchanted Island (both variants) is purple, and the Infested Island is dark red.[/note]

The Laboratory is a large structure used by Endermages to experiment with magical items from the End, and is also in the Enchanted biome found via the HEE Compass.

There are also regular chests with loot. Those can contain Obsidian Fragments and Auricion, amongst several other items.

Energy Clusters, the little glowing orbs you may have seen floating around, have different health levels, which affect the regeneration (or leaking) speed.

Clusters can be moved using an Energy Wand. Moving them too far or across dimensions can have negative effects on their health.

Blocks that use Energy will take it from Clusters up to 16 blocks away, and from the environment if placed in the End.

Items that use Energy automatically refill in the End, or can be used on a Cluster to start and stop draining the Energy.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Energy Clusters and the Energy Wand

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
A very flat biome with small amount of caves.

The Homeland variant has lakes of Ender Goo, piles of Falling Obsidian and a strange Obsidian road-like structure.

You can often find a Homeland Cache, a floating transparent cube that can be broken for some goodies, most importantly Arcane Shards. Endermen, Baby Endermen, and Ender Guardians spawn here.

The Infested Islands are mostly a flat biome with occasional hills, long caves and a decent amount of ores. There are 2 variations of the biome - Deep and Ravaged. Both of these variations contain Silverfish, Infested Bats and occasionally Endermen.

The Deep variation is massively populated with Spooky Trees that can have faces on them, which are how you get Ectoplasm. The ground has all types of infested plants, including Thorny Bushes.

The Ravaged variation has patches of infested plants and occasional Spooky Trees, but the most important feature is the Ravaged Dungeon which is an open gate to getting your Charms.

About Infestation:
Simply by standing on the Infested End Stone, the infestation level will rise. After leaving the area for several minutes, if the infestation level is low, it will reset and won't do any harm to the player.

However, if the infestation level gets high enough, it will trigger one or more potion effects, which include weakness, slowness and mining fatigue, and if the player's level is severe, blindness, confusion and/or poison may take place as well. These effects cannot be cured using milk; however you can drink Infestation Remedy to shorten them.

A Fire-oriented biome with huge mountains and a large amount of caves and ores. Apart from default ores, this biome also has common Igneous Rock ore. There are 2 variations of the biome - Scorching and Mine.

The Scorching variation has large blobs of cinder, streams and pools of Lava and Lilyfires. This is the only place where Fire Golems and Scorching Lenses spawn. Each island can contain a Dungeon Puzzle.

The Mine variation spawns Haunted Miners, which protect Resource Pits (holes with ores from the End and Lava) and long patches of Overworld ores. Not all Overworld ores are present on a single island, usually one or two random ores are missing.

The Ghost Amulet (Impure) is an item that can only be obtained by throwing one Emerald, one String and one End Powder into Ender Goo.

Once you have that, you can purify it with a TC infusion, but that's expensive, so maybe the Ender Compendium has a more traditional way to infuse it.

As long as it stays anywhere in the inventory, it protects players from Forest Ghosts, and thus provides a way of acquiring Ectoplasm.
The Blank Gem doesn't do anything on its own, but is used to create higher level Gems.

The Spatial Dash Gem is used for enderpearl-like teleportation.

The Spatial Dash Gem uses Energy and can be charged in an Energy Extraction Table. Right-clicking with the gem in hand sends a purple beam straight to where the player is aiming. When the beam hits a block, the player will be teleported to it. Maximum travel distance is 75 blocks horizontally. The teleportation doesn't hurt the player, unlike Ender Pearls.

The Spatial Dash Gem always tries to place the player on top of the block, even if the beam hits the side or bottom of it.

The Spatial Dash Gem can teleport the player through 7 solid blocks in a row, making the gem a good way of teleporting through cave walls and ceilings. If the wall is thicker than 7 blocks, the gem then tries to find 2 air blocks inside the wall. If the air blocks are not found, the player will be teleported into a wall, leading to suffocation.

[note]A Spatial Dash Gem is also dropped by the Ender Eye mini-boss upon death.[/note]

The Transference Gem is used to teleport to a marked location.

The Transference Gem uses Energy and can be charged in an Energy Extraction Table. Shift-right-clicking on a block with a Transference Gem in hand will link the gem to that block. The state of the gem itself will then switch to "Linked", as seen in its tooltip.

After linking, the player can right-click with a Transference Gem in hand to teleport to the linked block, using some of the Energy stored in the gem.

Using F3+H to enable detailed item tooltips makes the Transference Gem show the exact coordinates and the dimension of the linked location.

Once the charge of the Transference Gem becomes lower than 44%, negative effects will appear:

Deflection - the player will be teleported to a random location instead of the linked block.

Various negative potion effects, the lower the charge is - the longer they will last:

Slowness II
Nausea I
Weakness II
Hunger I

Endermen - Angry Endermen will spawn and attack the player.

Item drop - a random amount of items in player's inventory will drop to the ground.

Storm - will cause a 2-3 minute storm. This is the rarest effect.

Spatial Dash Gems and Transference Gems can be enhanced in a similar manner, using End Powder and the enhancement item.

Right-click the End Powder, choose an enchantment, and fill four End Powder and four Instability Orbs for instant teleport, four Lapis Lazuli for a longer teleport range, and four Endium Ingots to increase the capacity of the gem.

Transference Gem and Spatial Dash Gems can be enhanced in a similar manner, using End Powder and the enhancement item.

Right-click the End Powder, choose an enchantment, and fill with four End Powder and four Ectoplasm to teleport a monster, four Leather to teleport a whole group of players, and four Endium Ingots to increase the capacity of the gem.

There are 6 types of Runes found in the Ravaged Dungeons on the Infested Islands:

Power
Vigor
Magic
Defense
Agility
Void

The Void rune is less common than other types.

Runes are used to create Charms, which are crafted in a Charm Pouch.

Basic Runes increase attributes, such as strength, speed or health. Void Rune (gray) gives the Louse one of several special and extremely dangerous abilities.

Charms are player enchantments, used and crafted in the Charm Pouch.
If you are lucky you may find a pouch in the Dungeons.

This magical pouch allows creating, holding and activating Charms.

Sneaking and using the pouch activates or deactivates the Charms.

Only one pouch can be active at a time.

Some of the islands have a Dungeon Puzzle inside them, usually near the surface and with a small cave leading to it. The dungeon consists of special blocks which the player can interact with by throwing Igneous Rock, causing a chain reaction during which the lit blocks will become unlit, unlit blocks will become lit and the walls will propagate the reaction into adjacent blocks.

Once all of the blocks are lit, a Fire Fiend is spawned below. It will make its way to the surface, breaking the dungeon in the process.

[warn]Kill it with... well, probably not fire![/warn]

The Scorching Pickaxe is a special type of pickaxe that smelts blocks and applies fortune effect to ores.

It only works on smeltable blocks and ores. Blocks that smelt into items are affected by fortune, including for example Iron Ore and Cactus.

Compatible blocks are also mined much faster.

GT Ores are not affected. You can find Vanilla Ores in the Twilight Forest inside Hollow Hills.

[note]So basically, it's useless.[/note]

The purple flowers found on top of Endstone Blobs are known as Death Flowers. They can be planted on End Stone, Dirt, Grass or inside Flower Pots.

Outside the End, the flower will slowly decay, even if in a Flower Pot.

After some time spent decaying, it starts to occasionally attract Angry Endermen.

When the flower decays completely, it turns dark, propagates a massive amount of decay to nearby blocks and spawns an Energy Cluster.

Partial decay can be healed a little using End Powder.
Living Matter is a combination of microorganisms used to craft curses.

The Infested Island and its dungeons are swarming with Silverfish, and they have a 1 in 56 chance of leaving a drop of their blood behind after you kill them. Golden swords increase the chance to 1 in 14.

This rare material is used to brew Infestation Remedy, as well as in the crafting of some curses.

Infestation Remedy is a drinkable (or throwable) item used to shorten effects of the Infestation.

Obtaining:
The Infestation Remedy is brewed in an Enhanced Brewing Stand, using Silverfish Blood as the brewing ingredient and an Awkward Potion.

Usage:
When drunk, the remedy will shorten each of the Infestation effects by 150 to 180 seconds.

You can make splash potions with gunpowder and 3 more End Powder as well.

The Potion of Instability is a special type of potion, which can be brewed by putting an Instability Orb into an Enhanced Brewing Stand with an Awkward Potion. The brewing process requires End Powder in the stand's special slot.

Usage:
As any other potion, the Potion of Instability can be drunk (or thrown, if it's a splash potion). Unlike regular potions, this potion gives a random potion effect of random tier and duration to each player it affects. It can also apply potion effects which aren't available in vanilla potions, such as Jump or Hunger.

Trivia:
The item tooltip contains ???, as opposed to a potion effect and duration.

You can make splash potions with gunpowder and 3 more End Powder as well.

A Curse is a magical powder that attaches itself to an area of blocks, a mob, or a player, crafted using living matter, End Powder and specific ingredients.

It can be either placed right on a block or an entity, or thrown. If it gets thrown into a group of entities, it will have a chance to hit more than one at the same time.

Curses eventually disappear, but they can be made eternal by crafting them with stardust and an arcane shard. Eternal Curses will stay forever on blocks and mobs, and longer than normal Curses on players.

Curses placed on blocks are only visible to the player who cast it, and for a short duration to players affected by it.

Getting very close to a Curse makes it visible without having it affect you, but it requires extreme carefulness.

It is possible to remove Curses by using a Potion of Purity.

The Potion of Purity is a drinkable (or throwable) potion that removes Curses.

Obtaining:
This potion is brewed in an Enhanced Brewing Stand, using Ectoplasm as the brewing ingredient and an Awkward Potion.

You can make splash potions with gunpowder and 3 more End Powder as well.

The Curse Amulet reveals all nearby Curses placed on blocks and depletes Curses quicker when held.

It is created by throwing End Powder, Gold Ingot, Ectoplasm and String into Ender Goo.

A Brewing Stand with one or more special effects (enhancements).

You can upgrade your Enhanced Brewing Stand with End Powder to modify it like other HEE items.

You can continue adding as many effects to one Brewing Stand as you want.

Enhancements:
Tier (Ectoplasm)
Your potion can have a higher tier and a longer potion duration than vanilla ones. (Tier IV is up to 12 mins)

Speed (Igneous Rock)
Increases the speed of the Brewing Stand.

Cost (Emerald)
Reduces the cost of End Powder used in a brewing cycle.

Enhanced TNT is a special version of vanilla TNT with one or more special effects (enhancements).

The way to make enhanced TNT is to right-click with End Powder in your hand to modify your TNT. You can continue adding as many effects to one TNT as you want.

Enhancements:
No block damage (Feather)
TNT explodes with no block damage.

No Entity damage (Slime)
TNT explodes with no entity damage.

Extra Damage (Gunpowder)
TNT explodes with extra damage.

Trap (Redstone)
TNT explodes when a hostile mob touches or walks over the TNT block.

No Clip (Enderpearls)
TNT falls through solid blocks and explodes after a few seconds.

Fire (Igneous Rock)
TNT explodes with a big fire spread.

No Fuse (Redstone Torch)
TNT explodes immediately.

Enhanced Ender Pearls are a special version of vanilla Ender Pearls with one or more special effects (enhancements).

The way to make enhanced pearls is to right-click with End Powder in your hand to modify your ender pearl. You can continue adding as many effects to one pearl as you want.

These effects are useful when throwing the pearl, for pearl teleportation effects.

Natural occurrence:
It is possible to find pearls with random effects in a Dungeon Tower's loot chests.

Enhancements:
No fall damage (Wool)
Upon the pearl's landing, the player will not receive any fall damage.

No gravity (Feather)
The pearl will not follow the rules of gravity, which makes it possible to throw it straight up. After 10 seconds of flight, the pearl is automatically destroyed without any teleportation or fall damage.

Increased range (String)
Unlike the no gravity effect, the pearl will fall down due to gravity, but will do so 25% slower. If the pearl has the no gravity effect too, it will override this effect.

Double speed (Gold Nugget)
Increases the pearl's speed by a factor of 2, but won't change the flight trajectory. This can be helpful if you are in a bad situation (fell in lava, swarm of mobs around...) and need to be saved very quickly. In combination with the riding effect, you may notice slight stuttering on a server.

Explosive (Gunpowder)
Upon landing, the pearl will explode with radius of 2.7 (TNT has radius of 4). This will not harm the thrower as long as they are far enough from the landing spot.

Freeze (Snowball)
The pearl will freeze mobs and players within 5 blocks of the landing spot for at least 4 seconds. Just as with the explosive effect, this will not affect the thrower unless they throw the pearl close to them, or have the riding effect applied. This effect is also followed by ice cracking sound and snow particles.

Riding (Lead)
The thrower will "ride" the pearl to its destination. During the ride, if another pearl with this effect is thrown, the previous pearl will destroy itself and deal fall damage (unless No fall damage effect is applied).

Trivia:
The Enhanced Ender Pearls can still be used for crafting an Eye of Ender.

You can upgrade your Altar with one or more special effects (enhancements).

The way to make an enhanced Altar is to right-click your Altar with End Powder in your hand, then supplying End Powder and the enhancement material in the UI. You can continue adding as many effects to one Altar as you want.

Enhancements:
Range (Block of Lapis)
Increase the range at which an item can be infused by the Altar.

Speed (Block of Redstone)
Increase the working speed of the Altar.

Efficiency (Block of Emerald)
Reduce the cost of Dragon Essence used by Altar recipes.

Curse of Teleportation
Teleport Entities around randomly.

Curse of Confusion
Confuses mobs. Creepers just explode and have no fuse time or mobs fight each other.

Curse of Tranquillity
Prevent mobs from attacking you. Doesn't work on Boss mobs.

Curse of Slowness
Inflicts slow on mobs.

Curse of Weakness
Inflicts weakness on mobs.

Curse of Blindness
Inflicts blindness on mobs.

Curse of Death
Does 1.5 magical damage to mobs. Mobs bleed for a while and lose health.

Curse of Decay
Items and armor get damaged over time.

Curse of Vampire
Mobs become sensitive to sunlight and take more damage.

Curse of Rebound
Adds reflection damage to a mob.

Curse of Loss
Items will be removed out of your inventory and get destroyed or fall on the ground.
You think you're charming? Craft all these Charms to be the true Master of Charms.

After conquering most of the content inside the End, it is time for a Master Quest.

Bring forth and slay the following and you shall receive some moderately great loot.

The Mutating Sprig brings a degree of order to the chaotic nature of Mutandis, allowing more limited, but also more predictable effects. It is a key tool in the creation of plant-based devices such as the Leech Chest.

The Mutating Sprig is crafted in the Witch's Cauldron using an Ent Twig, Nether Wart and Mutandis Extremis.

Grass - Mutates to Mycelium
Mycelium - Mutates to Grass
Dirt (under water) - Mutates to Clay

Wheat in a proper configuration should mutate to wormwood, but because of other mods it doesn't work. You can buy wormwood from the Coins tab instead.

Once you have some Steam machines, you can make Advanced Solar Boilers. They have more Steam output per second. Otherwise they are the same as Simple Solar Boilers.

Fill it with Water on the bottom side to produce Steam. Unlike the other Boilers, this only outputs Steam on the output port side.

Hint: The Advanced Solar Boiler calcifies and becomes less efficient over time - but it will only drop to 120L/s, not 40L/s, like the Simple Solar Boiler. Later on you can consider using Distilled Water to avoid calcification.

[note]You'll need Silver from the Twilight Forest (LV+) or from small ores for this.[/note]

OK, now you can:

1) Turn the Tungsten Trioxide into Hot Tungsten Ingots in the EBF with some Carbon
2) Keep going for TS

We want TS, so put some Hydrogen along with the Tungsten Trioxide in your EBF to get rid of the Oxygen.

Combine your pure Tungsten with Steel in a mixer to get Tungstensteel. Then EBF and then freeze it to get the Tungstensteel ingot.

Some of Tungstensteel Dust you don't need to smelt as you will want to use it for HSS-G!

[note]Note that Tungsten Trioxide to Tungsten Ingot has reduced smelt time. This does not apply to the pure version. You're gonna need a bunch of it in IV as well as the TS, so keep this in mind.[/note]

Now that you have drums, you want them larger? Already??

Well, in that case, you better start collecting or making cobblestone, by the tens of thousands. And making explosives too.

Compress the cobblestone in an assembler first using circuit 9, then run them through the Implosion Compressor until you get Quadruple Compressed Cobblestone. Do that four times, and then another pass through the assembler with a diamond block, and there you have it - one bedrockium ingot.

Now do that 5 more times, and you can make yourself a bedrockium drum.

64k buckets of portable fluid. Perfect for your new Ore drill!

[note]There's also a Bedrockium ore much later on if you're lazy. By then you probably won't want the drums though.[/note]

With a Chemical Reactor, you can make Fertilized Earth. It ticks faster than normal farmland, so crops will mature much faster. As a bonus, it can be tilled away from water and doesn't get damaged when you fall on it.

It does allow CropsNH crops to be placed on them, but will not accelerate the crops.
Hydrazine is made from Ammonia and Hydrogen Peroxide.
Time for the last tier of Rocket Fuel. First, make some Formaldehyde. It will require a catalyst. You can make it by mixing Iron and Vanadium, and placing the mix into a carrier.

To make Hydrogen Peroxide you combine Oxygen (or Air), 2-Ethylanthrahydroquinone, and Anthracene in a Chemical Plant.

[note]You can fully recycle the 2-Ethylanthraquinone, so don't make a bunch of it.[/note]

This facility will process certain chemical recipes you'll need later on, like Rocket Fuels. Keep in mind that recipes can only be made after meeting the required Chemical Plant tier.
