Remember that you can input plasma beyond the optimal flow, and get more out of each turbine at the cost of fuel efficiency.

Celestial Tungsten - from Advanced Nitinol + Tartarite. A GT++ material that can be made as plasma, at the very end of the plasma line. It provides a lot of power, but the material itself is useful for DTPF recipes, machine components and other things. Check the questline in How to Generate Power, starting at [quest]Welcome to the Plasma Chain[/quest], for more information.

Indium - from Lithium + Silver. This is a nice optional fusion recipe, given how annoying Indium can be to get. Your options are to either replicate it, make it with fusion, obtain it from the naquadria line, or obtain it from processing sphalerite ore.

(You can make Indium in other ways, of course, but this is a relatively popular, non-forced fusion recipe)

Oganesson - from Calcium + Californium. This is the best noble gas of them all, and a very power-hungry recipe compared to most. However, Oganesson will save you power on EBF recipes, reducing recipe time more than any other fluid, and it also boosts Void Miners to their maximum speed. Replicating it might be better, if you have the right setup with GT++ multis.

Americium - from Hydrogen + Plutonium 241. This is the cheaper Americium recipe that was promised to you in t2, and it no longer needs Lutetium. You should be able to get both of the inputs very easily, so enjoy your cheaper Americium!

Neutronium - from Naquadria + Americium. Neutronium fusion? It's quite fast, you might want to give it a try!

It's not smaller, it's compact!

Compact Fusion. If you've been looking for a big multiblock to put together, you have arrived at a very neat thing. There's hardly anything that could beat its size, except for a max height Mega Distillation Tower, but this is instead a wide multi instead of a tall one. It is so wide, in fact, that it cannot fit in one chunk, and instead covers a 3x3 chunk space! Make sure you follow the instructions and the hologram properly, and jump in joy when you have one of these built.

You can choose one of four tiers for this reactor, in the same way as the normal Fusion Reactors. The Compact controller will need 48 of the regular controllers in the same tier, plus some other materials, and more than 2 thousand blocks in the structure, which are conveniently detailed in the tooltip. It is much bigger than the previous reactors, but it also has a huge number of parallels, starting at 64x with MK1 and ending at a maximum of 320x with t5!

This is the go-to when you have found yourself deep into MK3 fusion, perhaps even MK4, and you find yourself running short on power. Instead of making a tower of reactors, why not make one of these? The only power issue that you'll have after getting it done is the amount of turbines you will need to eat up all the plasma. You probably know about the XL Plasma Turbine, but you should also know that they force huge penalties on most plasmas, including Helium and Tin, if you use good turbine materials like Infinity. Do you remember those fusion chains mentioned in previous quests? This is the time for them. Check the "How to Generate Power" tab for more details.

[note]Compacts follow different overclocking rules, needing double the startup power and double the voltage instead of just the voltage.[/note]

Whether you've mathed it out from NEI, looked at the spreadsheet or done something else, you might have figured something out: Fuel 3 is better in every way. More power, more byproducts, more everything. However, both recipes for it use Thorium Tetrafluoride (TF4), and the source of this is salt sparging, done in the Sparge Tower. Not only that, but Fuel 3 can only be consumed by having 4 LuV Buffered Dynamo Hatches in the LFTR, which means that it's a fair bit away from the previous steps in this chain.

Once you've made it there, though, you can start working on getting this fuel. To make it, you will need at least one Sparge Tower dedicated to using Fluorine, with T Salt or TB Salt (TB Salt is better, get it from Fuel 2). There is a recipe that uses Helium, but it's not required for Fuel 3 and is meant for byproducts, so the quest for it is in the breeding half of this branch. Using a single tower for both recipes is a bad idea, so don't do it!

Preferably, you should input Fluorine and TB Salt and let it run for a while. Speeding up the recipe by overclocking and making more towers is a good idea, since the TF4 is your bottleneck now. Alongside it, you get several fluorides: Lithium, Neptunium, Technetium and Selenium. These might prove useful in the future, but your goal is the Thorium one.

What is the most powerful nuclear fission generator there is? The answer to that question isn't even a nuclear fission generator, for the most part. The answer is the Large Naquadah Generator. It follows the same principle as the LFTR, use a new processing chain to turn Thorium, Uranium and Plutonium into liquid fuels, very dense with energy, which are then slowly burned to generate large amounts of power over a very long period of time. This reactor, for example, burns its fuels 1 mB at a time, over several seconds, when running without additives, a very slow burner by default.

Let's look at the NEI recipes. Excited Thorium outputs 2,200 EU/t, Excited Uranium outputs 12,960 EU/t and Excited Plutonium outputs 32,400 EU/t. These are small numbers, clearly, so this can't possibly be the most powerful nuclear fission reactor. However, this multi is more complicated than that! In total, there are 4 inputs you can provide for it: one of them is the required fuel and another is the also required Liquid Air to generate EU from that fuel, but the other 2 are additives that are optional, yet increase both the efficiency and the consumption speed of the fuel. The controller's tooltip lists all the possible additives and their bonuses.

Fuel efficiency here means that the fuel is burned at the same rate, but energy output is increased by the percentage. Let's consider the two best options, Cryotheum and Atomic Separation Catalyst. They multiply with each other, so the energy output is 2.75 x 16 = 44 times the displayed EU/t on NEI! Excited Plutonium, the most energetic of the three fuels, will award you with 1,425,600 EU/t, almost 3 UV amps.

[note]The more popular use for this multi is naquadal fuel, though.[/note]

An LuV LFTR running on Fuel 3 outputs 4 ZPM amps per tick, or 524,288 EU/t. Each bucket is worth 1,048,576,000,000 EU, more than a trillion EU! Certainly, this is the most power-dense fuel you've ever held, and now that you've made it here, you can make it to fusion and beyond much more easily. But wait, there's more!

You might have noticed that the limiting factor in using the best recipe for Fuel 1 and Fuel 2 was the U Salt, which ultimately makes the LFTR Fuel Base. You just can't get enough of it to drop that inefficient 4-input recipe. However, the increased output of U Salt from Fuel 3, alongside the doubling that you can get from processing Helium Sparged U Salt instead of the regular one, means that you can use the 2-input recipe to make all your fuel from now on! If you haven't set up Helium Sparge Towers yet, do so now.

When you do this, you can grab the two Fuel Refineries you should have and set them both to the 2-input recipe. Each bucket of Fuel 3 takes 9000 seconds to make, but is consumed in 4000 seconds, so it's good to have more than one Refinery per LFTR. With this, you will make fuel much faster, and generate much more EU than before. If you continue expanding, it's very possible to match the first tiers of fusion power from something like this.

The Naquadah Reactor has the potential to be an endgame power generator, but only if the right additives are used. These additives boost the EU/t output of the multi, but in different ways, and it's important to upgrade them as quickly as possible. However, going beyond the max output of the Dynamo Hatch is not a good idea!

There are two types of additives: the coolants and the fuel boosters. The coolants boost fuel efficiency, which means fuel consumption is the same, whereas the boosters increase the speed the multi burns the fuel, increasing the output at the same time. There are endgame alternatives for both of these, but they will be ignored here.

There are three coolants, but the 275% efficiency boost by using Cryotheum should not be ignored. To automate it, you will need an automated source of Blaze Rods and Snowballs (Snow is made from Water). To this, you add Redstone and Saltpeter, and you're done.

The boosters are more difficult to choose from. Caesium should be ignored, Uranium 235 can be automated from Uranium 238 with magic at an almost 1:1 ratio, but Naquadah is what you probably have ready to use for this, which quadruples the speed of this reactor. However, if this is too slow, you can instead automate Atomic Separation Catalyst to get a 16x speed boost! There are many recipes for this, so choose your favorite.

If you've looked at the wiki setups, you might have seen some that seem harder to automate than others. Particularly, that one with two kinds of Uranium Rods. More than filling empty slots with Reactor Platings to force all the inputs to move to the specific slots where the rods must go, this one needs each rod to go in a specific slot!

The solution for this is a GT cover. The Robot Arm does the same action of moving items around as the Conveyor, but it moves to specific slots. With this, you can move the Dual Rod to where it needs to be, and the Quad Rods can fill the remaining slots as intended. If you're using other setups, you can use a similar logic to do your automation.

Your sourcing of Uranium is gonna be very small in EV, unless you use crops. Similarly, your ability to put together the multiblocks needed for the fluid nuke will be better in IV, since you can mine Small Titanium Ore directly, and use GT++ multis.

All in all, the Tier 2 Rocket makes things a lot easier by letting you mine ores on Mars and Phobos to get Uranium and Tungstate/Scheelite. However, building it requires considerable progression in EV, due to TPV Coils, which need Titanium and Platinum, and the Field Generators that the rocket needs. In EV and IV, vacuum nukes are one of the best choices for power, but the setup is complicated and needs Uranium and/or Plutonium.

Either way, it's recommended to have a Multiblock Miner in either the Nether, for Thorium or Phobos/Deimos, for Uranium.

Thorium and Uranium have a lot of differences, but also a lot of similarities.

In general, Uranium is a better fuel, but fluid nukes do not follow that general rule. Because they do not output any EU/t, and simply convert heat to Hot Coolant, the difference between the two fuels becomes minimal and Thorium stands out as being much easier to get and turn into fuel rods. The maximum amount of heat you can safely move around in a reactor limits the amount of Uranium Fuel Rods you can use, which means that your HU value will not be as high as you would have wanted.

For regular and vacuum IC2 nukes, however, Uranium has a big advantage. Especially in vacuum nukes, which are the most powerful, the efficient cooling through the cells makes it so a lot of Uranium can be processed at once, which returns incredible amounts of EU/t. The different conversion from fuel to energy between fluid and vacuum means that Thorium is very good for fluid nukes, whereas Uranium is very good for vacuum nukes.

Were you courageous enough to build a vac nuke? If so, are you courageous enough to do it in a MOX setup, with high heat?

Yes, this is possible, and extremely powerful. However, all the risks you signed up for are exponentially increased, since MOX nukes keep getting better and better the closer the nuke's temperature is to the critical point. This sort of automation is more complicated than almost any other, and there are very few tutorials for exploiting the maximum potential of these setups. Here are some links you might find useful:

[url]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BmwZZ7Z_n-g[/url]

Tutorial video for automation of dangerous vacuum nukes. 43,600 EU/t for Uranium, 108,895 EU/t for MOX at 99% heat, 4,979,200 EU/t for The Core.

[url]https://discord.com/channels/181078474394566657/1341554447981219880[/url]

#tips-and-tricks post about the setup in the video above, with more details and discussion.

[url]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=N4iO1HlFvVQ[/url]

Another video about vacuum nuke setups.

In the previous quest, Duranium was introduced as a material used to make Tritanium. While it becomes required for this reason, there is more to it than that. Another recipe that uses it is a Beam Crafter recipe, which has a chance to produce a Quantum Anomaly.

First off, what is the Beam Crafter? That is a multiblock that works a bit like fusion, but only for the purpose of making new materials. It collides single particles with one another, or against fluids, to generate new items while consuming power. You can see more detailed information in the "Crafting, but with Beams!" quest found in Multiblock Goals. Duranium can be used in this machine to create Quantum Anomalies. This is a chance craft, but the Anomaly has a special property: when used to convert some blocks to others, it will not be consumed. Therefore, for that purpose, you only need to get one.

Is this required? Well, yes. When you arrive at a certain stage of the game, you might find yourself needing a new kind of soldering alloy, called Mutated Living Solder. To craft this, you need a Chemical Plant made with Botmium, which is an alloy that required Advanced Nitinol. This, in turn, is one of the blocks that need a Quantum Anomaly for its conversion. Given that Duranium is the only fluid choice to make the Anomaly, then it becomes required for this as well, but only a couple tiers from ZPM.

Additionally, there are other recipes, like the Elemental Duplicator. This is a very powerful replicator that will give you a great boost in automation due to its speed and the replication recipes it can do, but the Quantum Anomaly used in this recipe will be consumed, so watch out: if you only have one, don't use it for this. Later on, however, you will encounter other recipes that consume the anomaly, namely the casings for the Quantum Force Transformer, so it will be important to automate their production by then.

Your first t1 Fusion Reactor is one of the biggest walls to overcome throughout this pack's progression. It's very unlikely you can afford to just build another one right after, so you will have to manage several reactions with that single one.

The new fusion condition is that you will have to pay a cost of EU and time every time you switch the recipe that's being crafted. Assuming you're using fusion power, the production of Europium and any other material should be batched between your usual rows of power generation. Perhaps you're overproducing power? In that case, you can use the pause to fuse some useful materials.

In time, you will be able to afford and use multiple fusion reactors. For now, this isn't the case.

Fusion is the lategame. It is not the entire lategame, but several tiers are effectively relying on it, even if new ways of generating power are being discovered (developed) over time. Whether you got here through focusing on power or products, you have surely felt the importance of that donut on your base, have you not? Let's just hope your power storage doesn't run out when you start relying on Mega Blast Furnace processing.

If you've looked at NEI enough, you might have discovered Force Plasma, or some of its crafting steps. This plasma is the end of the first of three fusion chains dedicated to power generation, although some of these special plasmas transform into useful materials in Plasma Turbines or Extreme Heat Exchangers, like Celestial Tungsten later on. There are three of these chains, and the build on top of one another: one for MK1 Reactors, another for MK2 and the last for MK3.

You can build these chains any time you like, and they offer more EU/t per Fusion Reactor than the Helium Plasma alternative, but it's unlikely you'll need them this early. They only become really useful later on, at the MK3 stage with bigger reactors and turbines. Despite the fact the three plasmas can be used for power, only the final one, Celestial Tungsten, might be powerful enough to be worthwhile for your central power generation.

At this point, why not? You should be in a better position to afford it, but there is the issue that t3 fusion unlocks an easier Americium recipe, which lets you craft a second t3 more easily. You might not want to wait that long, maybe you've been smelting a lot of ingots, or using World Accelerators?

Regardless, two Helium Plasma reactors will surely suffice for whatever it is you're doing. Tin Plasma is worth using, of course, but the Molecular Transformer recipe to convert Silver to Tin isn't available in the singleblock anymore, so you might want the easier option, since you're rocking two reactors and all. With the 2x overclock they still produce millions of EU/t with the right Plasma Turbines, assuming you have them ready.

If you want to continue expanding, you can look at the Mk2 fusion chain that ends at Runite Plasma. This process uses Force Plasma from the Mk1 fusion chain, so it needs those 5 fusion recipes, plus another 5. Despite being an extremely powerful powergen option, it's unlikely you need something in this scale right now. Keep in mind, however, that you might need it in UHV or UEV.

So many options for my next wand core! The six elemental options are icy, blazing, bone, obsidian, reed, and quartz. They are all pretty similar.

The last two options are more interesting. A transmutative wand has the same capacity while being cheaper to craft! It also has a nice ability that makes it easier to charge.

At last, the thaumium core creates a wand with a slightly higher capacity. But it is also more expensive to craft than the others. Depending on your discounts you might not be able to get it immediately and have to go for one of the other options first.

§3You only need to make one of the listed wand cores.
betterquesting:10.name:8: So many options for the core!

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
You probably have built a lot of Large Chemical Reactors by now. With the powerful 4/4 OC it is one of the strongest multiblocks there is. But what if even that is not enough to satisfy your chemical needs? You can't make it faster after using your best energy hatches available.

Fear not, we have a solution for you: The Mega Chemical Reactor. It lets you do 256 parallels for your LCR recipes! And you can still overclock after that if you provide enough power.

It only unlocks in LuV as it needs 7 Fusion Coil Blocks. Check with your hologram projector to see how it is built and what you need.

The glass tier limits the energy hatch tier that you can use. You can even use multiamp hatches from TecTech! If you want to use laser hatches however you need at least UV glass.

Silicon is needed in all boule (and thus wafers, chips, and circuits) creation. Silicon is therefore an §oincredibly important material§r.

With your new Electrolyzer you can obtain Raw Silicon Dust from many different sources. Alternatively, you can also centrifuge Redstone. You can also get it from Silicon Dioxide, by adding Magnesium Dust to it in a Chemical Reactor and then recycling it in an Electrolyzer, which also gives you a lot of bonus Oxygen.

However, the raw silicon dust you obtained is not pure enough! We will need to work on that. There are two reasonable options to do so. Let us look at the first one here. Don't worry, this is just a simple two step process. First let us start by reacting it with some chlorine in a chemical reactor.

As a second step, we combine the Tetrachloride with Sodium Dust. There we go! The Silicon Dust is now purified to solar grade!

The Chlorine and Sodium are §onot§r lost during this process. To recover them, just electrolyze the Salt you get at the end and send it back to the Chemical Reactors, for a complete loop that turns Raw Silicon into Solar Grade Silicon.

If you are salty about the ingredients needed to purify silicon, I got good news for you! You can recover all of the chlorine and sodium you used by electrolyzing the salt you got!

[note]You can also use zinc instead of sodium, the first reaction is longer but the recycling is much cheaper.[/note]

You can now make optical SMDs! They are required for all circuits beyond UEV.

Some of the materials are made in the ABS. Maybe it's time to add a few.

Smelting with the ferocity of the universe itself.

This unbelievable material seemed impossible to manipulate into a coil block form, even though its properties made this desirable. It is incredibly stable even at extreme temperatures, but this also made it unable to pack together for coils.

However, the situation changed when you thought about using something more intelligent. By integrating a Wetware or better UHV circuit, the Infinity Coil became a reality, controlled by the ever-watching eyes of the circuitry you've spent months to create. From now on, these eyes will watch over your multiblocks.

Provides 11701K heat. You could upgrade your EBF, though at this point it's more likely to be for your MBFs or your DTPF.

Forged from the blood of an ageless dragon, and melded together by the power of fusion beyond what you thought was the reality. No natural element, or combination of elements, could match up to this glowing orange material, not even the Awakened Draconium you got your hands on before.

What is this blood made of?

What truly happened inside that Mk4 Fusion Reactor? What §ois§r this material? It moves on its own, moving as if it is made of slime, however it is boiling to the touch. Despite moving as if it is soft and squishy, Hypogen is hard to the touch and is incredibly hard to cut or work. It feels out of this world, and it is obvious to you what needs to be done with it.

What were they feeding these dragons?

It absorbs and radiates energy without any effort, but it would be stupid to attempt making coils out of this without assistance. Wetware wasn't good enough anymore, and only the most advanced living circuit could withstand the erratic behavior Hypogen demonstrates.

Provides 12601K heat. Almost certainly, this will end up on your DTPF.

Beyond spacetime, beyond reality. You have peered into what never existed and brought into a fluid, and then a solid. It has been stabilized, against all odds. When you look at it, you think that you could hold the entire universe in your hand.

In the past, you were able to combine almost all materials into one, through an Eternal Singularity, an infinitely dense sample of the universe. However, automating this at the scale of the DTPF proved ridiculous, which would have stopped your progress altogether if not for the discovery of the Energized Tesseract. To physically manifest spacetime itself, you first needed to manifest the fourth spatial dimension, and that is what the Tesseract is: a 4-dimensional cube.

Cubes! Almost everything around you is made out of cubes. You have only glimpsed at the reality of the 4-dimensional world, but you have successfully used it to condensate spacetime, which can be arbitrarily molded into the complete Eternal mixture. Needless to say, living circuits will not suffice to maintain an infinitely dense, infinitely stable, multi-dimensional material.

Currently, the final upgrade with 13501K. This really makes your DTPF shine!

If you're familiar with Botania, you will notice that the overworld is noticeably void of magical flowers and mushrooms. Such pretty expressions of magic sadly require you to have leveled up on your magical skills. For now you will have to make do with what the world has to offer.

Look in deep caves in the Twilight Forest at low Y-levels for glimmering mushrooms. These are your starting ingredient and can be used instead of flower petals. Beware, unlike flowers you can't grow more just yet, so be careful what you use them for.

The first item you want to make is the Petal Apothecary. A mushroom is needed to anoint it and give it its restorative properties.

To operate it, fill it with a bucket of water to keep the plants hydrated. After that you can add the ingredients by dropping them on top.

Each craft requires some magical ingredients, but also one or more regular flowers from the world that can function as a stable base. Once you've added all the ingredients, finish the craft by adding a seed. Any vanilla seed will do.

The first magical flower you are able to make is the Pure Daisy. This flower can slowly enchant nearby stone and logs into their special Botania variants, which are used commonly as ingredients.

After placing the flower down, you can place down stone and/or wood in the 8 tiles horizontally surrounding it, and after some time they will be converted.

Now that you have livingrock, create your first mana pool. Chop some pieces into slabs with a saw to make the bottom, then stick them together with plates for the sides.

You lack the knowledge to make it effective, so sadly it won't be able to craft a lot as a result.
Now that you have discovered the power of the magically enchanted crucible, you can use that technology to make a better mana pool.

Some flowers are everywhere, and some are limited to specific biomes. If you don't want to walk long distances from home, you can call in some help.

Bees with the flower trait will slowly generate new flowers in its working area, including plenty that have been brought in from distant pastures.

Mana diamonds are magically enhanced diamonds, and they require more or less energy depending on the quality of the gem you're trying to enchant.

A completely full diluted pool is barely able to make a mana diamond out of an exquisite diamond. Once you upgrade the pool you can use regular diamonds - be it at a higher mana cost.

The next step is to make some catalysts. The Alchemical catalyst can use mana to change one item or block into a related item or block.

Put it under a filled mana pool, then try it out by making some prismarine.

The recipe will need to be researched in the Thaumonomicon.
betterquesting:10.name:8: A Glimpse Into A Watery Future

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
The infusion altar will allow you to make runes, which in turn gives you access to progressively more advanced flowers.

To operate the altar, drop the ingredients on top, whack it with a wand of the forest, and when it's done drop a livingrock block on top to complete the craft. You will additionally need a mana source, such as a mana spreader pointing at it.

To get some advanced tools and equipment you will need some terrasteel. This is done using a dedicated machine.

You'll need to lay out the blocks underneath the plate as described in the Lexica Botania. Then place a spark on top of the plate nearby a mana pool with a large stockpile of mana. Lastly you'll place a mana diamond, mana pearl, and mana steel onto the plate to begin the transformation.
Legends speak of a portal to a different realm filled with green energy.
Put the 4 pylons down and shift-right-click the terrasteel ingot on the beacon to summon the Gaia Guardian.

So the rumors about the elves are true. Well, §owere§r true. Some are still true. And what isn't true used to be true.

Turns out they have since been talking to a mysterious individual they call the §oDream Master§r. Apparently that sparked an industrial revolution among the Alfar. Sadly, that means that they now insist on receiving the latest fashion in machinery to fuel their ever-expanding factories, in exchange for the elven materials that are now rapidly going out of fashion.

Someone needs to have a word with this guy...
Go no further if you value your sanity.

These new hatches allow you to wirelessly store and receive energy from any location in any dimension. They can be placed in any existing multi block structure and will function as normal energy hatches. 

Additionally, the wireless covers can be used for singleblock machines such as a World Accelerator or a BioLab.

The wireless network can store a total of 2^(2^31) EU, far exceeding even a max tier LSC.

You can share a wireless network with others by adding them to your network with §5/gt global_energy_join §3user1§r §2user2§r. This will make §3user1§r use §2user2's§r energy when interacting with the global network. You can leave a network at any time by doing §5/gt global_energy_join§r §4your_name your_name§r.

You cannot connect wires to these blocks. These are also designed to be highly lag efficient, meaning EU is added at large intervals to prevent needless calculations from occurring. This will also save you some TPS lag from vast wire networks.

[note]If your calculator is giving up, 2^(2^31) is a number with 646,456,994 digits.[/note]
So you finally did it... but there's so much more to do. Onwards comrade!
Hope you have loads of transcendent metal ingots at the ready. :)

Breed an Industrious bee with a Heroic bee to obtain a Space bee. The temperature must be Icy.

Just one small step for you, but a giant leap for beekind.

[note]This is the starting point for many space-related bees. Check NEI to see what you can aim for.[/note]
Engineering beyond your comprehension. Destroying this strange higher dimensional object in a macerator is very easy though.

Now craft a Gaia Spirit ingot with your new Gaia Spirit from killing the Gaia guardian.

Put the 4 pylons down and shift-right-click the Gaia Spirit ingot on the beacon to summon a harder version of Gaia Guardian.

Pico circuits, a direct upgrade from Optical Mainframes, these UMV circuits will be required for a lot of future crafts.

[note]You will need a NAC to get started.[/note]

[warn]Rumor has it these circuits may not be around for much longer...[/warn]
Just a bit more.

Quantum Circuits, another upgrade of Optical Mainframes and Pico Circuits. These UXV circuits will be required for lots of future crafts.

[note]You will need your Pico Circuit NAC to get started.

Did you know all special circuits contribute to the calibration?[/note]

[warn]Rumor has it these circuits may not be around for much longer... 

Maybe do not trust rumors...[/warn]
Craft some runes, because why not?
This quest should never be complete which is useful to hide templates and other things.

For your first batch of Hypogen you will need some Dragonblood. Maybe you already have some lying around somewhere from killing the dragon a long time ago. You have 2 other options though. Bees and the DE Fusion Crafter.

For the bee path you have to go very deep into the breeding tree, but maybe you have already done that? Check the Bee Breeding tab either way.

In the DE Fusion Crafter you have 2 recipes. The better one uses an Infinity Egg from Witchery. Without any Witchery you can also just use a normal dragon egg for the weaker recipe.

Once you have a bit of Hypogen you can then use that as a starting point to make more in your DTPF without any Dragonblood. I don't know why it works that way, complain to Colen.

However, you will still need more Dragonblood eventually for UMV superconductors.

[note]There is actually another way to get Dragonblood which is similar to the DE Fusion Crafter recipes but in the mixer instead. It's even slower and less resource efficient. In particular, the dragon egg does not survive the process. So only use that if you are absolutely trying to avoid magic and bees.[/note]

[note]Just a reminder: a fluid task just needs you to have the fluid in some container in your inventory. (cell, universal cell, large cell, volumetric cell, etc.)[/note]

Let's make a brand new plastic! The trees that you found on Barnarda C have very interesting properties. Still, you can't just use the extracted radox substance raw. Some serious refining steps are in order!

§6You'll need it for a ton of stuff like UIV and UMV superconductors, UEV+ hatches, or parts of the Dyson Swarm.§r

Compared to the previous plastics, most of the steps required here are not chemical reactions. They are also very slow, so you might want to use a mega multiblock to help with that. This production line also underlines the necessity of large-scale plasma production. You will only need more going forward.

[note]Super Heavy Radox will be needed for Dimensionally Shifted Superfluid, so store some for later.[/note]

[note]The Heavy Radox you get as a byproduct can be used for MkV Naquadah Fuel.[/note]

Thanks to your help I have managed to create the ultimate energy source: An encased wormhole that drains energy from a synthesized pocket universe, to the point when it reaches heat death. I have no use for it, so you may have it. Thank you for making my dream come true!

If you've never used Botania before, you may be wondering about the purpose of all this effort. This isn't a simple question to answer, but one thing you can do that's quite useful right now is making yourself some manasteel.

Among its many uses, manasteel has one of the best, if not simply §othe§o §rbest, durabilities of materials available at LV, so it's perfect for all of your crafting tools.

If you have a particular dislike of Tinker's Construct, manasteel is a great material to make a Botania pickaxe out of too.
betterquesting:10.name:8: What Are All These Flowers Even For?

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
To use the power of magical flowers, you must understand how to generate and manipulate mana. This ethereal blue-ish substance is produced by generating flowers, when their requirements are met. Mana is not easily quantified, so you will have to do a lot of estimating if you want to use it efficiently.

Once you have chosen which flower you want to use to generate mana, you must plant it near a mana spreader. When the flower's conditions are fulfilled, it will begin to produce mana, and store it in the internal buffer of the nearest mana spreader. The mana spreader itself will automatically emit any mana it contains, provided it is aimed at a valid destination (such as a mana pool). You'll need a lot of these devices, so craft a pair for now.

Mana spreaders will aim towards you when you place them down. To change their direction, use a wand of the forest: while holding the wand, shift-right-click on the mana spreader, and then shift-right-click on the block you want it to aim at. This method of binding also works for other things, such as binding a flower to a specific mana spreader.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Moron's Manual For Mana Manufacture And Manipulation

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
The daybloom is an extremely simple generating flower. All you have to do is place it down, and it'll produce mana for free during the day. The downside of this arrangement is that dayblooms die after only an hour.

You can find Goldenrod flowers in Prairie biomes.

Make one, and I'll give you another.

Mana is blue. Water is also blue. There's a correlation there, and the hydroangea turns that correlation into causation. Place a water source block nearby, and the hydroangea will consume it to produce mana - until it dies after an hour.

This one can be a bit tricky to automate given the lack of naturally-regenerating source blocks.
Perhaps not the kind of "dark energy" you're familiar with, the nightshade produces mana at night. Like other passive generating flowers, it dies after an hour.

The endoflame burns combustible materials in order to produce mana. It can efficiently consume fuels with a burn time of up to 64000 per item (equivalent to four blocks of coal); any burn time beyond this will be wasted. Endoflames don't die like passive flowers do, and are simple to use, so it's a good idea to make several of them.

Functional flowers are a large part of Botania. Most of them have nuances to how they operate, and these are generally best explained in the Lexica Botania: a codex of all Botania knowledge. This questline will explain the basics, but be sure to keep a copy of the Lexica Botania on hand so you can easily reference the details.

Besides being a repository of useful information, the Lexica Botania has another function: if, while holding it, you look at any Botania block in the world, you can shift-right-click on that block to open up the relevant page.

Something else you'll want for functional flowers is a handful of redstone roots. Flowers which have a redstone root in their recipe have the ability to toggle whether they are active by applying a redstone signal. Make a few before you move on.

If you've made a ring of magnetization, you may be getting tired of having to take it off around various Botania systems that require items to be on the ground in order to interact with flowers. The solegnolia is your solution to that. Simply place one down anywhere you don't want items to be automatically put in your inventory, and the ring of magnetization will be disabled while you're in the vicinity of the solegnolia. It doesn't even require mana!
The dreadthorne is similar to the bellethorne, but it only kills adult animals. This is helpful for farming livestock, though it's only one aspect of a successful farm.

The bellethorne is a delightful little flower with an [warn]insatiable thirst for blood[/warn], though fortunately your blood doesn't count. When provided with a supply of mana, it will inflict damage on any living entities near it, with the exception of players. It's a good extra layer of defense to place at the entrances to your early-game bamboo fortress.
You'll need mana powder to proceed. Make four to start out with.

If you want anything better than an endoflame, you'll need a runic altar. Fortunately, most runes are easily crafted as soon as you can make the runic altar. Sinful runes, however, require titanium to make. For now, just make one of each of the elemental runes; that'll be enough to get you started.

Some flowers eat bees. Some eat leaves. Some eat slimes. This one eats everything (everything you can eat, anyway). The gourmaryllis is happiest when provided with a good variety of delicious meals, so I hope the HV-tier diet of canned sludge hasn't made you forget how to cook.

The Rosa Arcana transmutes experience into mana. A player standing near it will have their experience drained for this purpose. This process is unfortunately not very practical to automate, as the experience can only be extracted directly from a player or from orbs on the ground. It might be wise to place it somewhere you spend a lot of time.

Have you ever seen a slime and thought "I'd love to eat that"? The narslimmus has.

It needs to be planted somewhere slimes can naturally appear, but if you can find a good place for a narslimmus it'll consume those slimes and give you a good amount of mana in return.

The jaded amaranthus causes mystical flowers to grow all around it. Their vibrant petals can be used for magic, so you no longer have to go foraging for mushrooms.

There §ois§r another way of getting these, but you'll have to figure that one out for yourself.

The thermalily consumes lava, but it's not quite as simple as just constantly replenishing a lava pool. There's a cooldown that you'll have to account for. Even so, it's a fairly easy flower to automate if you have a good lava source.
The soarleander generates mana by consuming anything chicken-related, including entire chickens.
...there is no way a bee should be able to produce mana. The beegonia doesn't know this, and will gladly eat up all of your spare drones to help with filling your mana pools.
betterquesting:10.name:8: According To All Known Laws Of Mana Generation...

betterquesting:10.desc:8: Just try to dream of gold.

Well this is a bad idea, but since when has that stopped you before, golems with brains, what could go wrong?

§3You only need to make one of these golems.
betterquesting:10.name:8: Ignore the Glint in Their Eyes

betterquesting:10.desc:8:
Using a Chemical Reactor to create circuit boards has become quite inefficient... it's time for a proper solution! After some research you have found a more efficient method; a factory designed to print out circuit boards.

The PCB Factory is able to use a wide range of plastics to create circuit boards ready to be used. The printing mechanism overheats when it tries to overclock currently, so I will have to find a way to make that work later. Boards with neurons on them will also require a modification before they can be made, but that shouldn't be hard to achieve.

§2Trace size: the trace size represents the lines between components, which are needed to transmit the electrical signals on the circuit. One can make it smaller to slow down the machine, but use less resources, or make it bigger to make it faster, but use more resources.

§9Formulas:
- 10000/(TraceSize/100) Production
- RecipeDuration/TraceSize^2 Time§r

[note]Similar to the water line, additional modules of the PCB Factory can connect to one another using a Data Stick[/note]

With new technology comes the need for adaptation! In order to create §9Wetware§r & §cBioware§r boards you need a chamber that is capable of properly maintaining the neurons while they are installed to the board. Fortunately, the §5§lBio Chamber§r is a simple upgrade and doesn't require many resources. 

After its construction, you can link it to the PCB Factory by left-clicking the PCB Factory Controller using a Data Stick, and right-clicking that data stick onto the Bio Chamber Controller. One Bio Chamber can connect to any number of PCB Factories within a §216§r block radius.

[note]You can use any tier of glass.[/note]

Starting to hit the production limit of the PCB Factory? Let's install a §5§lCooling Tower§r; this will allow any PCB Factory within its range to overclock with §22x§r Speed in exchange for §c4x§r EU and §910L/s§r of §nDistilled Water§r while running.

You can connect this to the PCB Factory by first left-clicking the PCB Factory Controller and then right-clicking the Cooling Tower Controller. One Cooling Tower can connect to any number of PCB Factories within a §216§r block radius.

[note]The input hatch is placed in the bottom center of the Liquid Cooling Tower.[/note]

With the Nano Forge built, we can upgrade our production of circuit boards using Silver Nanites. Due to the nature of the nanites however, you will need both new structure casings and a special §5Nanite Containment Bus§r.

For the structure casings, you find that using infinity as a frame and enriched holmium as the protection layer works well. It can be allowed to let through nanites to go into the printer base so that extra material can be directly removed instead of trying to go slower.

With this new upgrade you can finally use §3Tier 2 recipes§r. Additionally, by placing extra nanites into the Nanite Containment Bus, you can boost your parallel amount by §2Amount^.75§r up to §2256§r parallels.

[note]P.S. For those who don't feel like doing math, that's §n1638§r nanites to reach the maximum parallel amount.[/note]

With your newfound ability to manipulate spacetime you have found a way to sustain cosmically low temperatures. It is now possible to make an even better cooling unit. A casing able to keep its room temperature very low and nanites which can transfer heat effectively because of their small bodies. You will still need coolant, though water won't cut it any longer given its high freezing point. If only there was some kind of super... coolant...

The §5Tier 2§r Coolant Tower now allows for a §24x§r Speed boost for the same §c4x§r EU cost, making it possible to speed through recipes much quicker. It requires §910 L/s§r of §nSuper Coolant§r to operate while running.

[warn]This upgrade is incompatible with its lower tier predecessor.[/warn]

Why use a small nozzle to print out the conductor on the board when you can just build it using nanites? Unfortunately, the Silver Nanite isn't rigid enough for that so a §6Gold Nanite§r will be needed... and so will new casings. Celestial tungsten should be a good candidate for a frame, and Quantum can be used for the protection for all these nanites flying around inside.

The structure will need to be bigger and taller to fit this more advanced technology, hopefully you prepared enough space!

[note]Works the same as the Tier 2, with the advantage of requiring less resource intensive Gold Nanites.[/note]

There must be a way to make a nano scale robots to work in a machine. Carbon ones can be made in an assembly line, but very inefficiently. There must be a better way.

What about a Nano Forge, able to cut up blocks into nano-thin sheets and then creating the first nanite, which helps create thousands of them in mere seconds.

[note]The Nano Forge is a big multiblock requiring lots of power over the course of a couple minutes. It is able to use TT energy hatches (including lasers). The controller must have a carbon nanite inside to make tier 1 recipes.[/note]

[note]Despite what NEI might claim there are no minimum voltages for the Nano Forge recipes. If you want to do a recipe you just have to achieve the minimum EU/t required, no matter the voltage[/note].

Metastable Oganesson is a very important endgame material that you will need for a variety of machines, like the MK5 Fusion Reactor and the NAC.

[note]You can't use it yet, but keep in mind that there is a much cheaper recipe unlocked in late UIV![/note]

A great source of silver.

Argentia leaves will 4x your silver ore.

You'll notice after processing your first Prismarine Precipitates you are left with a second §2Contaminated Prismarine Solution§r. You can also recycle this for added §3Prismarine Solution§o§r and §3Prismarine-Rich Nitrobenzene Solution§r. Again, technically optional, but highly recommended.

[warn]If you didn't setup the recycling for the Contaminated Hydrogen Peroxide then you'll want to now since this recycling actively produces it.[/warn]

The §1§lMatter Manipulator§r is an extremely powerful tool that you can use during your entire playthrough. It is essentially a survival version of world-edit that is custom made for the GTNH player's convenience.

As you might expect, the §1§lPrototype Matter Manipulator§r is the least powerful, most rudimentary version. You can only use the §5§lGeometry Mode§r to create and manipulate shapes for use in building. You will [warn]not[/warn]§r be able to remove blocks until you install an upgrade unlocked in EV.

You can find detailed information from the developer on: [url]https://github.com/GTNewHorizons/MatterManipulator/blob/master/README.md[/url]

But the best way to learn about it is to use it! Experiment with the UI and become familiar with how it works.

[note]Checkout the Building Better Bases tab for the complete Manipulator questline.[/note]

You didn't seriously think you only needed to do the Naquadah line in LuV did you? Well if so; better brace yourself for the Netherite line!

Don't panic, it's a relatively straight-forward line so long as you can wrap your head around minor processing loops and percent based output. Fortunately you have a quest book to guide you through your initial setup.

Be warned- you will need at least §2§lGrade 1 Purified Water§r and§5§l Naquadah Coils§r to make it through this entire line.

§3This questline will start you off with the three primary things you must prepare in order to begin:

§l- Milled Netherrack
- Nether Air
- Ancient Debris Collection§r

§3For at least one and likely two of those you will need to journey into the nether, so make sure you're prepared equipment wise!§r

[warn]If you already created the line and do not wish to complete the individual quests, hold one of these three item sets in your hand after completing this quest: [/warn]

§4§l- 1 Dense Netherite Plate
- 64 Intensely Bonded Netherite Nanoparticles
- 16 Netherite Ingots

Mining out large chunks of stone can be a huge pain when it comes to creating bases. Why not craft the excavator upgrade for your Prototype Matter Manipulator so that you have the ability to remove blocks quickly?

An armor set worthy of a God. These boots provide a permanent jump boost and increased running speed.

While wearing the complete set, you are completely unkillable.

Are you tired of making Energium Dust by mixing Ruby and Redstone Dust? This bee offers a way to acquire it directly - how convenient is that? To breed it, you'll need to place some Hot Coolant below the hive while inside a Boneyard found in the Nether.

Unlike its parents, this bee won't burn down your base—but it will set you on fire if you're not wearing your apiarist suit!

Remember when I mentioned that these could be used to create a more powerful ring? Well, the rumor is true.

Make 16 of each type of Master Sky Ring to continue down this path, but beware the journey that lies ahead!

[note]If you've already reached the end of this recipe line, just hold the ring and it will skip these quests![/note]

The Thaumium Boat is an upgraded version of your Greatwood Boat. The experience you have gained from manufacturing boats made of magical materials allows you to create a boat that can go even faster. Additionally, the Thaumium coating allows it to sail not only in rivers but also lava streams! Take it with you on your vacation in the Nether and enjoy.

At ZPM, you've almost reached the peak of personal defense technology. New augments await!

The living energy core will allow your armor to charge at ZPM voltage and equip tier 3 augments.

The frames in this tier provide 7 augment slots. Pushing the limits of modularity, every frame now has at least one prismatic slot.

Suck up liquids like never before! This module replaces the infinite fluid drilling rig, but has the convenience of being inside your space elevator. Look at the NEI recipes to see which fluids you can pump with this.

[note]Will require MK-II motors on Space Elevator to function.[/note]

§nApplied Energistics 2 is an integral part of GTNH gameplay. 
§r
AE2 is the primary networking and logistics management mod in GTNH for Items, Fluids, and Crafting. You will use it starting from EV and onward for most automations you perform. Given the sheer density of this modpack there are a variety of unique tools and features added specifically to aid in your adventure. Most of these tools are covered in this quest tab.

There is a lot to learn, but don't feel overburdened! Your abilities will continue to grow the more time you spend with it. There are a wide variety of helpful resources to take advantage of in addition to this book when it comes to learning:

§21. The Wiki: §r[url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Applied_Energistics_2[/url]

- The Wiki has a lot of great starter information on what various systems do. They also have a lot of machine specific automation tutorials so be sure to check the Wiki if you're struggling or want a point of reference.

§22. The Discord: §r[url]https://discord.gg/gtnh[/url]

- The Discord is full of experienced AE2ers', check out #ae2-help to find plenty of people who will take time to help you figure something out.

§23. Video Tutorials: §r[url]https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=LUYVmIAEC-I[/url]

- There are a lot of great GTNH content creators who make high quality video tutorials for this. Here is a link to AE2 Fundamentals by IX. There's an advanced version as well.
The MV Wiremill is twice as fast as the LV one but uses 4x the power.

One Essentia you might have a hard time gathering is Auram. Maybe you've gotten some from Ethereal Essence, which is dropped by the flying balls of light that rarely show up in the Nether, or some from Nodes. But that is hardly a good supply. The Aurelia plant can resolve this.

When a full moon is visible overhead, Aurelia flowers will open up their petals presumably to feed off of the light. Significant for you is that they will occasionally shed these petals, which can be collected off the ground as a dense source of Auram Essentia.

You should make sure the ground near the flower is level and clear, so you'll be able to collect the petals later. The flower itself is simply planted on grass, not farmland, so no need to have a water source nearby either.

[note]Gaia Wart is also a growable source of Auram Essentia. It has a quest in the Green Revolution quest tab.[/note]

A great source of manganese.

Pyrolusium leaves will 4x your manganese and tantalite ore.
No Description

Oh hey, don't void that stuff, centrifuge it into something useful? (◕‿↼)


Seriously though, as soon as you can: use these and some enriched fertilizer to breed Oil Berries in the MV Crop Breeder.

The immense heat of the God Forge and its modules allow for ideas themselves to be melted down.

Two clashing ideologies, forced to coexist. §3Hexanite§r is born.

A fusion of §dMagic§r and §6Technology§f§r, the ultimate concoction, a volatile one. Even the God Forge struggles to merge them perfectly. A mess of ideas needs a host, something familiar to bind them together.

§3§r[note]Redstone Plasma requires the God Forge to be melted, while Ichorium only needs a Fluid Extractor. You are sure to have lots of Ichorium Dust lying around from your Space Miners.

It is recommended to cast these materials in an Exo-Foundry, as the long wait times and high volume of use cannot be supported in a Mass Solidifier[/note]

If you improve your Thaumium to Thauminite, you can make this very stylish helmet! Also comes with a very useful 5% vis discount while equipped.

Maybe this new material is useful for wands too?

Interested in powerful, customizable armor that you can modify as you advance? Look no further than §6§r§l&z&zMechanical Armor§r!

In order to begin tinkering, you'll need a workspace for modifying modular equipment along with a set of Mechanical Armor. The armor is essentially useless on its own, but gains additional features through modification. Each piece of armor is composed of three parts:

§nAugments: §rAugments add a wide variety of useful features to the armor. Augments are categorized into one of three types: §6Protection§r, §aMovement§r, and §dUtility§r. Augments can only be inserted into slots corresponding to their category.

§nFrames:§r The armor's frame determines the protection value of the armor along with how many slots it contains for augments.

§nEnergy Cores:§r The energy core determines how much energy the armor stores, its charging tier, and which augments can be equipped.
No Description

Mix Samarium chloride dust with Salt. Electrolyze the result and the Samarium dust will be separated out.

Sodium and chlorine can also be fully recovered.

You also get some additional residue. It does not have any uses currently but might be useful in the future.
These are starting to get a little pricey...

Copper has managed to stay relevant into UIV by refusing to remain in one phase at a time.

You can hold the plates, but be warned: they may not stay in the same phase for long.

It's here that you might find yourself with some useful stuff alongside power. Xenon, which has become very useful in the EBF thanks to noble gas changes in its recipes, and Advanced Nitinol? If you don't already have a Quantum Anomaly setup for it, you can use this. Who knows what'll come in the future?

These recipes are the same 0.144 ratio ones that you've seen before and, since they're just before the final step, they will bottleneck you on the path to compact reactor setups. The one to focus on is Advanced Nitinol, which is the second last recipe, and where you'll need 9.216, or 10 Mk3 reactors to sustain a Celestial Tungsten compact at the end. If you build a compact here, however, you can feed 6 compacts as long as everything that comes before this is fast enough.

The MKII is the penultimate upgrade in the Matter Manipulator line. It is much more powerful, storing §210x§r the power, with a range of §2128 Blocks§r, and the ability to place §2256 Blocks/Second§r. In addition to all of the MKI features you now unlock §5§ltwo powerful new modes§r:

- §5§lCopy / Paste§r: Copy a selection of blocks and paste it as many times as you'd like. Works best with GT & AE2.

- §5§lMove§r: Similar to Copy / Paste, but will physically relocate something already built.

Here is a short list of things that are copied / moved with the MM, the more complete list is on the Readme, but this should give you a general idea of how versatile it is.

§3§lGregTech:§r
- Pipe/Cable connections
- Machine color
- Machine front & output directions
- Basic machine settings (auto outputs, etc)
- Hatch settings (sorting, stack limiting, etc)
- Multi machine settings (void protection, batch mode, etc)
- Multi rotation
- Covers
- Strong redstone output
- Custom names
- Ghost circuits
- Bus/hatch item/fluid lock
- Modes (for machines that use the new mode system)
- Data stick data
- TecTech machine input parameters
- ME output bus/hatch capacity

§3§lAE2:§r
- Any coloring
- The orientation
- The configuration
- The upgrades
- Custom names
- Any stored cells (will also automatically configure cells & install their upgrades)
- Any patterns (will encode but not decode patterns)
- Priority Settings
- P2P Settings
- OreDict / Regular Filter

§9§3§lAdvanced Copy Options:§r 

When in Copy / Paste mode, the radial menu has an §5§lAdvanced Options§r sub-menu with two powerful toggles:
  - §5§l§5§lLink to External Hubs§r: When copying wireless connectors that are linked to a hub outside of the copy region, the pasted connectors will stay linked to that original hub.
  - §5§lAuto-P2P Interfaces§r: Replaces ME Interfaces in the copied region with P2P ME tunnels, automatically placing matching tunnels at the source for seamless item routing.
The final energy hatch. You should make these wireless as soon as possible.
No Description

To complete this chain, you need to activate the Astral Titanium Plasma you have with a special material, also a GT++ one, called Titansteel. This is a considerable powersink, which is why the input amount is so low at 2L, and it forces you to dedicate an ABS at UV tier to feed one mk2 reactor running the Runite plasma recipe. If you decide to upscale this setup, the best option is to simply build a mega ABS, where you can also use EBF coils to save some EU, and in turn make the powergen chain more efficient.

Runite Plasma has a 350M fuel value, which leaves it free to run on Trinium XLs without penalty, whereas Tin Plasma has a 74.5% penalty on the same turbines due to having less than half the fuel value. If you want to upscale your plasma powergen to great numbers, this is an option, but the mk3 chain is probably the one to choose.

The same ratio of 0.144 to 1 reactors also applies here.

An enhanced version of the Diamond Shulker that allows you to see the contents within.

Has §n108§r slots.

[note]Can be dyed![/note]

Who knew that creating artificial solar systems would finally allow you to extract the core of a freshly dead star?

With your current crude casings, you can only accelerate the life of an artificial solar system to observe white dwarfs.

Perhaps this matter will help you push the process even further.

[note]This is one of the three EOH materials. Use it to upgrade your casings up to T4.[/note]

Are you sick and tired of having cables all around your base? Are you tired of having to upgrade your cables constantly to handle different amperage amounts? Are you a fan of lightning bolts zapping around your base?

Then this multiblock is for you, the Tesla Tower comes with high amperage output and full TecTech energy hatch support with this powerful multiblock.

To get started you will need to fill the tower with capacitors matching the tier of the Primary Tesla Windings within the capacitor bank. The Tesla Winding determines the tier of power that the tower transfers power at and the amount of capacitors determines the maximum amperage that can be output.

A total of 16 capacitors can be placed into one capacitor bank so you might need many banks depending on your power needs.

Once the tower is constructed click open the controller to configure the maximum transfer distance of the tower to fit the needs of your base. The range setting is currently buggy which means that at least for now you can do so without needing any plasmas. This option is called “Tesla Towers Transfer Radius Setting”.

Now that your tower is all configured how do you get power out of it to your machines? Well I am glad you asked. To get power to the machines of the base you will need to use the Tesla Coil Covers. Place them on the tops of your machines, energy hatches and even transformers to get power flowing from the tower. Energy hatches are a bit picky however and the hatch likes to be facing upwards to receive power.

[warn]Warning! The Tesla Tower will output only one tier of amp such as EV, IV etc. When upgrading the Primary Tesla Windings, please make sure to check that all of your coil covers and transceivers in the base can handle the upgraded power. Failure to do so will result in a machine explosion.[/warn]

[warn]Failure to turn off the controller before adjustment can also cause an explosion.[/warn]
A little faster couldn't hurt, right? This is the final version of the Striders augment.

This pack features many mods which add lots of new building blocks and/or QOL features which make building much easier.

This questline will go over a few of the major additions.

Sustainability. It's not the name of the game... but it could be!

If you've ever wanted to generate many chemicals from a single source, you've probably looked at Oil or Benzene. However, there's also the Algae Farm.

Each tier, starting from ULV (at 50s per batch) through IV (25s per batch), reduces the time it takes to produce Algae by about 5 seconds, and then beyond that each tier will cut the duration in half. The production time can also randomly double or triple, but this happens relatively rarely.

Each tier increase also adds to the amount of Algae you get in a single cycle, as well as the type of Algae produced. Each cycle gives out an exact amount as well as a bonus amount 10% of the time. The Algae Farm also accepts Compost, which you can make from the algae itself, to boost the multi's tier by one. This might be expensive at the start, but it's heavily recommended in most cases. You can get regular Algae and Green Algae starting at ULV; Brown Algae starts appearing at HV, Golden-Brown Algae at EV, and Red Algae at IV, though higher tier algae appears in very small quantities at first.

To find out more about the exact output quantities and timings, please see the wiki: [url]https://wiki.gtnewhorizons.com/wiki/Algae_Farm[/url]

The Algae can be used for various chemicals like Methane, Ammonia, Sulfuric Acid, Sodium Carbonate, Ethylene, Lithium Chloride, and even some power-generating fluids. You typically need a Chemical Plant for that. In IV tier you can also combine Green Algae with Glowstone to get Glowing Coral and make Sunnarium from that. If you're curious about all the processing chains, look them up on NEI: quests to cover them are coming up, possibly with more recipes that don't need the Chemical Plant.
Lazulia will produce Lapis Lazuli and Lapis Dust.

An armor set worthy of a God. These pants have no special effects on their own but are required to complete the full infinity set.

While wearing the complete set, you are completely unkillable.

Want even more speed on your wafer processing? Using Grade 2 Purified Water, made by ozonation, you can now reduce processing time by 50%. To run this machine, you will need to make large amounts of Ozone Gas by bombarding air with a strong laser. If you haven't already, you should definitely make the Hyper-Intensity Laser Engraver multiblock to speed up this process.

[note]This multiblock is very picky about where the ozone input hatch goes. If you can't figure out why it's not forming, chances are you forgot to place this hatch in the correct location. Use the hologram projector to see where it goes.[/note]

As you enter LuV, fewer mass processing multiblocks are available as you replace old setups with new systems and scale up the multiblocks you've already built - there are still some important upgrades in these higher tiers, though.

Definitely don't miss out on the Circuit Assembly Line or you'll be kicking yourself later.
This live root won't scream when you harvest it. At least, I don't think it will.

As an upgrade to the barrels, EFR also adds the ever-familiar shulker box! The shulker box allows you to comfortably tote around its contents. You can find the research for them in the New Horizons tab of the Thaumonomicon.

These have seven additional tiers much like the barrels and chests that give you additional storage space. 

You can dye any tier by shapelessly crafting them with a dye, and undye them by shapelessly crafting them alone. They §nwill§r retain their inventory. 

[note]There are many ways to obtain shulker shells:
1. Fighting Shulkers in the Twilight Forest Lich & Ghast Queen Towers.
2. Fighting Shulkers from the eggs you get from the Vending Machine.
3. Manually crafting the shells.[/note]

Have you made too many mistakes and researched yourself into a corner by getting too much warp with no way to get rid of it? Do you wish you could just start everything over? The [warn]Potion of Blissful Oblivion[/warn] is the solution you are looking for.

At the cost of your knowledge of [warn]all research, all discovered aspects, all knowledge points in the Research Table, and everything scanned with a Thaumometer[/warn], all of your warp will be removed. It won't do anything about warp from armor, so you might still get minor warp events if you're wearing any warpy armor. Be absolutely certain you know what you are doing before you drink this.

Keep in mind that there are better alternatives for dealing with warp (which you can see in the Adept Thaumaturgy tab). This is just the cheapest one.

[note]It's also a rather decent source of Strontio.[/note]

You're now getting into Magic Bees, and one of its mundane bee species is the Attuned species. These are scooped out of Deep Hives that you can find in the Overworld. These hives are a pain to find, so you should consider just buying hives with coins until you get a princess and a drone. However, if you are a real masochist or completionist try-hard, then here's some information about where they spawn:

* From Y=1 to Y=25
* In stone, surrounded on 5 sides. Not just vanilla stone.
* In biomes tagged with one or more of:
   * MOUNTAINS: Actual mountains may not count. It's the biome type that counts.
      * Example: Canyon.
   * HILLS: Again, actual hills don't count.
      * Example: Snowy Coniferous Forest.
   * MAGICAL: Unlike the others, they do have some ethereal aspect.
      * Examples: Magical Forest is obvious, but also Cherry Blossom Grove counts.
* Surrounded by a small redstone vein. This often fills any open space around them.

They also like to just kind of show up whatever-what-the-heck in other biomes. Our beekeeping intern found a Deep Hive in a Lush Desert:

Lush Desert [HOT, DRY, SAVANNA, LUSH, SANDY]

You can dump the biome data in NEI by clicking on the NEI options button (the wrench), then the Tools button, then the Data Dumps button, and finally the Dump button in the biomes category. This creates a "dumps" directory in the root folder of the modpack with a biome.csv inside of it. Any listed biome that has the tags of HILLS, MOUNTAINS, and/or MAGICAL can generate Deep Hives. You can feed these biomes into a Nature's Compass and see if there are any nearby.

Prospector's Scanners will pick up the little ore pockets for these (traces, small samples). If you had one of those end-game ones with a display, it would come up as a few red pixels. Larger ones are probably just regular ore veins. The ore finding wand doesn't do a good job from the surface. Chasing lava veins and tunnels helps. Ore veins filled with redstone will saturate either tool.

Of course, just buying hives is the low-effort way.

[note]Beekeeper's Notes:

If you get real bad luck and wind up with an ignoble princess, then just get a bunch of drones out of it and convert some other pristine princess afterwards. However, using base princesses will compel the bees to turn into the Common species. There are two choices:

1. Use an Alveary with an Alveary Stabilizer to block mutations.
2. Create a princess that doesn't line up with the Attuned species' breeding possibilities before starting.[/note]

To insert and extract many amps from your LSC, make these special hatches.

Some multiblocks can also accept multi-amp hatches.

The Mana Fountain allows for quick and seamless automation of Mana Pool recipes.

You can assemble the multiblock as specified in the Lexica Botania / NEI. After it's assembled, right clicking it using the Wand of the Forest will show you whether it's complete and the amount of internally stored mana.

You can send the controller mana directly by either using a spreader or a spark much like a Mana Pool. Technically you don't have to use the Mana Pool in the center of the multiblock for it to function, but it is placed conveniently so that you can (plus, it doesn't hurt to have an extra buffer).

Items are allowed to input from any side of the controller, but can only output from the bottom. For early automation, it's recommended to just use hoppers. Once you unlock AE2 however you can simply place an interface underneath the controller with the appropriate patterns and it should push and pull items automatically.

[warn]You cannot craft Alchemy or Conjuration recipes using this multiblock, those are separate multiblocks that you will unlock with more advanced robot arm technology.[/warn]

[note]This structure can absolutely wall-share. It has the perfect design to be able to share 4 different Mana Fountains between the center pool.[/note]

The Infinity Egg is the best power source available for the Witchery altar.

You can also use it to unlock more efficient recipes in the DEFC.

The §5§lSuperdense Casting Basin§r (SCB) module is one of the first three modules you unlock right away for use in the §nExo-Foundry§r.

The SCB adds §312§r parallels per voltage tier and reduces the minimum number of Foundry casings by §236§r, giving you space for more inputs. 

If this module is paired with the §5Streamlined Casters§r (SC) module, you will unlock "§6Optimum Production§r", a bonus giving §36§r extra parallels per voltage tier and a §275%§r speed increase.

Niobium-Titanium isn't used for much, but it can be used to make a decent LuV-capable cable. You'll also need it later to craft the IV Superconductor, the HV Field Generator, and a variety of other components.

If you find your pipe has thick red corners, then it means something is wrong. Either the network is out of power or you formed a junction with an Unrouted Transport Pipe.

When the system gets more complicated, the chances go up that something will go wrong. Have fun troubleshooting! :)

§2Fluorophlogopite§2§r is the industrial answer to Mica-based foils, and something you'll want to start investing in as higher tier coils cost increasingly more foil to make.

The recipe for making Raw Fluorophlogopite Dust is done in the MV mixer. While all of the new dusts involved may look a little daunting, they're not that bad. You will need the following:

- Some variant of quartz dust: Any one of Quartz Sand, Quartzite, Nether Quartz, or Certus Quartz
- Alumina
- Potassiumfluorosilicate, which is made in two steps by combining Rock Salt, Hydrofluoric Acid, and Raw Silicon
- Potassium Carbonate, made by combining Potassium Dust and Oxygen (or Potash to cover both) with Carbon Dioxide in a Chemical Reactor

The exact ratios of each ingredient depend on the form of quartz that you're using, as does the exact amount of raw dust that you get from the recipe.

[note]Technically, this process is entirely optional, but highly recommended. The raw dust is also used in ZPM, but Mica can be substituted for that use case if you would like.[/note]

A source of platinum.

Platina leaves will 4x your plat line ores.

[note]Using Platina will create a surplus of aqua regia if you just use it in your existing plat line, you'll need some extra infrastructure to handle the excess.[/note]

These Liliums aren't the most useful, but if you're wanting to build with say Tuff or Andesite this should ease your search for resources somewhat.

Remember that these crops can only be bred when their environmental requirements are met. In this case, use those stones from before as your sub-soil.

Now that storage is handled, you want to dive into the automation part?

A Mk1 Chassis can't hold enough modules for complex functions. We need a better one.

Chassis Mk2 can hold 2 modules. It should do for now.
The easy way to get some pollen, just right-click on leaves. The Pollen Collection Kits are one-time use though, so maybe make a few.
This block can be used to configure the Mothership's name and icon, who is allowed to land on it and who is allowed to access the Navigation Console and the Thrusters.

With that 31/31/31 seed now in hand you will (ideally) §lnever have to complete 
the entire statting process again. §r

Once replicated, you can cross this perfect seed with itself (keep them fertilized!) to access the pools that it has access to! §c§c§4§nThis is the intended path for early game crop discovery. §rWhile it is much more random than deterministic breeding, it will let you collect a wider range of species quicker.

Keep in mind that: when pool breeding occurs, the offspring has a chance to be any crop found within any of the pools shared by 2 or more of the parent crops.§lThe mutation selection occurs prior to the check for environment. §rIn practice this means that if you're searching for a specific species in say, the Food pool, it will take much longer to appear than one in the Reed pool because there are fewer alternative species. [warn]No matter the environment.[/warn]

Once you've gotten your hands on a solid number of species, deterministic breeding becomes a simpler and more effective method for obtaining new species.
It's like a golden goose but... not.

Most of the time you are requesting things because you need to craft something. So here is the Logistics Request Table.

This thing comes with a 3*3 crafting grid that you can load with a NEI recipe and request the recipe. There is also an inventory buffer that you can use to store items within.

These crops crystalize and produce their related crystals and dusts straight from the soil.

§4Most of these crops will need a sub-soil of their related material whether block or ore.

The peak of all Incenses.

§dPurpura§r will increase your Incense from §92400§r to §93500§r.

Now that storage spaces are organized and assigned, time to let the network sort the items for us.

There are 2 ways to insert items into the system

1. Use an extraction module to extract items into the system. It is slow, but everything that has a valid destination will be sent into the network.

2. Use a QuickSort module. It extracts a whole stack of items that has a valid destination. This module will ignore items that have no destinations other than the default route though...

It is your choice. Pick what you like.

Now that you have the core pieces of the NAC™ platform, it's time to decide what circuit you would like to make. The §5§nCrystal Package§r allows for the creation of Crystal Circuits much more efficiently than other methods. See the attached owner's manual for installation instructions.

§oIf you purchase in the next 72 hours, this package is 50% off! Please... make a NAC™ for crystal circuits, CALs aren't as good we promise...§r


§n§lUltra-high Energy Etching Array Owner's Manual:§r

The NAC™ will track the most recent 100,000 circuits crafted, and can be calibrated to a specific circuit type by reaching a certain percentage of circuits of this type. At 60% (60,000) crystal circuits crafted, the NAC™ will become "fully calibrated" to crystal circuits.

Once that has been met, the Laser Source Hatch on the Etching Array will provide two bonuses:
- The §nEU Cost§r will be divided by each amperage interval over 256A. Example - 1,024A will divide by 2, 4,096A will divide by 3, etc.
- The §nRecipe Duration§r will be divided by (hatch tier - 9). Example - UIV will divide by 2, UMV will divide by 3, etc.
All of the above could be useful for the production of certain drinks. But really all you'll be using them for is getting to the next crop,

These hold 8,388,608 units of essentia.

And can hold 48 types.
Very powerful.

It has 8 parallels and supports higher tiers of drones.

[note]You can obtain pure platinum group metals with this. It would be a nice boost if you haven't made the QFT for it yet.[/note]

The ME Fluid Infinity Water Storage provides §24.5P§r water directly to your AE system, That's the equivalent of 2.25 million reservoir hatches, all conveniently packaged into one drive. 
Might come in handy...

Once you can actually get your hands on some endstone, these babies will allow for a §olot §o§rof high level passive material production.

Since Enderbloom requires End Stone Lily to be bred deterministically and End Stone Lily requires Enderbloom for its deterministic mutation, you'll need to use your mastery of the mutation pools to obtain either of them.

[note]Tip #1: If you're lost and don't know what to do, remember that you can trigger pool mutation even when breeding 2 crops of the same species together.[/note]

[note]Tip #2: Also remember that crops require all their growth requirements to be met in order to breed, even when breeding via mutation pools.[/note]

[note]Tip #3: This requirement can actually be used to filter the outcome of a pool mutation so that only a subset of them may appear. Though this doesn't actually reduce number of crops that can be picked from the pools shared by the parents. (and therefore doesn't directly increase your chance of getting what you want).§r[/note]

[note]Tip #4: If you want to properly increase your chance of getting something through mutation pools, try lowering the number of shared pools between the parents.[/note]

Compartments are fancy chests with extra features that make them much easier to navigate.

Their inventory is split into different folders, which can be named and color-coded. They also come with a search feature that allows you to search for items in any of the compartment's folders.

The largest compartment can store up to 400 stacks of items.

[note]Place a compartment next to a crafting station for easy access to its entire storage space![/note]

The §5§lLarge Essentia Smeltery§r is the GT version of the Alchemical Furnace which supercedes the Advanced Alchemical Furnace and is extremely fast at melting down items into essentia.

Unlike its predecessor which required centi-vis alone for power, this will also require electricity. The amount of electricity required is specified by the tier of the Essentia Diffusion Cell and the amount of parallels the machine has.

Novice -> EV
Adept -> IV
Master -> LuV
Grandmaster -> ZPM

The amount of parallels made available to the machine is determined by both the Essentia Diffusion Cell tier and the length:
§3Parallels = (2^Tier * (Length-1))§r

As usage of the Forge continues, more data on graviton shards is gathered. It has been found that they can stabilize the outputs of the Forge, allowing for the direct extraction of molten material while it is still close to the heart of the star.
